News.title: Killers who refuse to attend sentencing will face being confined to their cells or lose social visits
News.content:
NO HIDING PLACE Killers who refuse to attend sentencing will face being confined to their cells or lose social visits







Next

MURDERERS who refuse to show up for sentence hearings could face cell confinement for weeks or lose visiting privileges.

It comes as several notorious killers avoided facing up to the judge, including Kyle Clifford, who murdered his ex, her mum and her sister.



While those who refuse to attend already face an extra two years, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has said it’s “little deterrent” to people serving long sentences.

Ministers have said the plans will allow crown courts to impose various penalties, including losing social rights and cell confinement.



Killers who disrupt their sentencing will face similar consequences.

Visits from inmates’ children will be exempt where it’s in the best interest of the child.

Eighteen to 20-year-olds will also only face up to 10 days’ confinement, with the removal of other privileges capped at 20 days.

The MoJ said no penalty can guarantee prisoners attend sentencing but the new rules will “strengthen the consequences”.

“Criminals should not be able to pick and choose when they face justice,” said prisons minister Catherine McKinnell.



“Refusing to turn up to sentencing is an insult to victims and their families, and offenders must face the consequences.”

Claire Waxman, the victims’ commissioner for England and Wales, also commended the move.



She said the news was a reflection of “the tireless efforts of victims’ families who refused to accept that offenders could simply opt out of facing justice”.

Ms Waxman added: “Having worked with the families of Sabina Nessa, Zara Aleena and Jan Mustafa, I know how offenders’ refusal to attend sentencing hearings compounds trauma and robs families of one of the very few moments of accountability in the justice process.

“Their determined campaigning, alongside that of Olivia Pratt-Korbel’s family, helped ensure that this harm could no longer be ignored.”

The plans will be introduced to parliament today and should come into effect next year.

News.title: Two men arrested after ‘rape and attempted rape’ of two women in UK city – as cops hunt third man
News.content:
'RAPE' HORROR Two men arrested after ‘rape and attempted rape’ of two women in UK city – as cops hunt third man







Next

TWO men have been arrested on suspicion of rape and attempted rape after two women were allegedly attacked in a busy city centre.

Police launched a probe after they were alerted to the two incidents in Conniburrow, Milton Keynes.

A woman in her 30s was allegedly attacked on a pedestrian bridge on Thursday, September 10.

The second incident reportedly saw a woman in her 50s attacked on Wednesday, September 23.





Thames Valley Police released images of a man they wished to speak to in connection with the alleged attacks.

A 22-year-old man and a 19-year-old man were subsequently arrested on suspicion of rape and attempted rape.

Both have since been released on bail pending further enquiries.

Thames Valley Police is now appealing for further information as a probe into the alleged attacks continues.



The force is keen to hear from anyone who lives in the Conniburrow, Bradwell, Bradwell Common, Linford Wood and Heelands areas.

Additionally the force is asking for any CCTV or dash cam footage of a man on a bicycle on Wednesday, September 23, between 8pm and 11pm.

Detective Inspector Graeme Williams said: “We appreciate that news of these incidents will have caused concern to local residents, and I would like to reassure you that we are following every line of enquiry available to us in order to bring whoever is responsible to justice.

“Both women are being supported by officers and we remain in contact with them.



“Based on the information available to us at the current time, we do not believe these incidents to be linked to any other offences in the area.

“Since these incidents were first reported to us we have been carrying out a range of comprehensive enquiries, including house to house and CCTV scoping in the area.

“In addition to the appeal we issued last week, which included an image of a man we would like to speak to in connection with these incidents, we would now like to hear from anyone with Ring Doorbell that may have captured him between the hours of 8pm and 11pm on 23 September.”

News.title: She ‘can’t speak English’ but binges Brit soaps…all the ways mum of Henry Nowak’s killer is ‘playing the system’ in jail
News.content:
Next

KIRAN Kaur was jailed for hiding the ceremonial blade her monster son used to kill student Henry Nowak in a random street attack after a night out.

Her vile acts helped son Vickrum Digwa, 23, lie to cops, claiming Henry had made racist remarks. The con saw the 18-year-old placed in handcuffs as he lay dying.





Her time in jail has seen her closely monitored by staff, who it appears she’s been rubbing up the wrong way with bizarre requests.

Sources said Indian national Kaur was “playing the system” in prison by demanding translators while she is assessed – but speaking English to other cons and watching British soap operas.

Kaur has been placed on an ACCT – Assessment Care in Custody and Teamwork – document which means guards have to check her regularly and keep notes on her wellbeing.

The Sun last week revealed that Kaur, 53, will be released from prison early and booted out of the UK in a move that left her “distraught”.





A source said: “Kaur is being monitored around the clock because she is upset about the deportation notice, and the fact it’s been revealed publicly.

“Staff hate having to open an ACCT on prisoners but they are duty-bound to do it.

“It means they have to check on her several times an hour and keep notes on how she is doing mentally.

“It is time-consuming and generally a bit of a pain.

“But this news has hit the prisoner extremely hard.

“She was hoping she would be eligible for early release under the government scheme.

“But she did not reckon on also being told she was likely to be expelled from the country.

“That has left her down in the dumps – not that anyone has much sympathy.

“The order would make seeing her sons extremely difficult, especially Vickrum Digwa who is in jail.

“But she is an Indian national and has committed a really serious offence.



“And the government is really cracking down on foreign offenders and she should have considered the consequences when she hid the murder weapon.

“She was not expecting this action and was really taken aback to receive the notice in jail.

“She can make representations to the Home Office and plead her case to stay – but is not likely to succeed.

“And that could mean being put on a plane to India on her own and without family when she comes out of jail.”

Kaur’s son Vickrum Digwa murdered Henry in Southampton last December as the first-year student walked home.

After the pair encountered each other, Digwa stabbed Henry with a large Sikh dagger he held in a sheath – before then claiming he was the victim of a racist attack as Henry lay dying.

Digwa and his brother Gurpreet, 27, lied that finance student Henry was drunk, had shouted slurs and attacked Digwa, knocking off his turban.

Police bodycam footage later showed officers siding with Digwa and arresting Henry as he repeatedly told them he has been stabbed saying: “I can’t breathe.”

After the attack, Kaur – who came to the UK 30 years ago when she married Digwa’s father Moga Singh, 53 – arrived and took the knife home and hid it in her son’s bedroom.

Digwa was caught on video telling his mother to remove the knife from the murder scene.



Kaur was arrested for assisting an offender when police finally realised what had happened.

Digwa was jailed in May for 21 years for Henry’s murder.

And when Kaur was caged for three years at Southampton Crown Court in July, Judge Wiliam Mousley KC blasted her actions.

He told her: “A responsible parent would have challenged their son over their actions and encouraged them to do the right thing.

“Instead, you took the knife home and put it with a larger collection of ceremonial and other weapons in your sons’ bedroom.

“That would have helped to conceal what it had been used for.

“This was because you wanted him to avoid being caught.”

He added: “You had a hard life in India although that improved when you married and came to the UK, nearly 30 years ago.

“You are embedded in your Sikh community but speak little English. You have a number of significant health problems.

“When you are released from prison, you may have to make very considerable changes to your way of life and living arrangements.



“The sentence is three years imprisonment.

“You will be entitled to release from prison when you have served a specified part of that term.”

The Home Office notice means Kaur – held on remand since December 2025 – could be removed to India by the end of the year.

The mother-of-five is eligible for freedom after serving as little as a third of her jail term under Labour’s scheme.

Her son Digwa is not eligible for early release as he is a killer.

Kaur is held at Bronzefield, where fellow inmates include baby killer ex-nurse Lucy Letby and Beinash Batool, who killed her 10-year-old daughter Sara Sharif.

Kaur is not on the same unit as that duo, but has been held alongside former X-Factor singer Gabrielle Carrington – accused of murdering influencer Klaudia Zakrzewska by running her over.

But – due to warped jail mentality – Kaur is said to be “respected” among fellow lags.

A source said: “She is quiet and keeps herself to herself, and is actually quite popular.

“Most prisoners in Bronzefield have respect for what she did which – in their view – was to stick up for a relative.



“They would see her actions as displaying family loyalty.

“And Kaur is fairly respectful to other so hasn’t really had any problems with other inmates.

“But staff think she is playing the game like she does a lot in jail so she gets an easier ride.

“They think she pretends she can’t speak English when it suits her.

“One minute she has a Punjabi translator over the phone, helping her while she is checked out by health professionals.

“The next thing you know she is watching a soap opera like Coronation Street in English on the telly.”

We told in August how Digwa had applied for video calls – known as Purple Visits – with his Mum.

But prison chiefs stepped in and blocked the calls fearing an outcry.

Asked about Kaur’s case, The Home Office has said it “will always seek to deport foreign criminals at the first opportunity”.

A spokesperson for Sodexo, which runs HMP Bronzefield said: “We do not comment on individuals.”

News.title: Boy, 16, fighting for life after ‘serious assault’ outside pub – as four arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR ATTACK Boy, 16, fighting for life after ‘serious assault’ outside pub – as four arrested







Next

TWO teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a 16-year-old boy was left fighting for his life after an alleged assault.

Officers scrambled to the scene after they were alerted to a boy reportedly being assaulted at The Lutine Bell pub in Everton.

A 16-year-old boy was found at the scene and rushed to hospital with chest and head injuries.

News.title: Woman, 36, dies after being found unresponsive in home – as cops probe ‘unexpected’ death
News.content:
DEATH RIDDLE Woman, 36, dies after being found unresponsive in home – as cops probe ‘unexpected’ death







Next

COPS are continuing to probe the “unexpected death” of a 36-year-old woman, as the mystery surrounding her final moments deepens.

Kelsey Smith was tragically found unresponsive at a property in Ashby Road in Watford back on September 28.



She was rushed to hospital after ambulance crews raised concerns about her welfare at around 1.40am.

Although sadly she died a short time later.



Officers say her death is not being treated as suspicious at this stage.

But detectives are now appealing for witnesses and information as they try to establish the full circumstances.



Hertfordshire Police say they are particularly keen to hear from anyone who saw or spoke to Kelsey in the days before she died.

Detective Inspector Tom Hassell said: “First and foremost, our thoughts remain with Kelsey and those who knew her at this incredibly difficult time.

“Understandably, we want to make sure we are giving them all the answers they need.

“We’re asking anyone who saw or spoke to Kelsey in the days leading up to her death, from Friday 18 September onwards, to please get in touch.



“Or if you have any other information which you think may be of importance, please contact us.”

Cops added that Kelsey’s family have asked that their privacy be respected at this time.

Anyone with information is asked to get in touch with cops, quoting ISR 39 of 28 September, 2026.

News.title: Vicious clashes erupt between cops and left-wing protesters in Spain – days after ‘apocalyptic’ riots rocked France
News.content:
Next

BRUTAL clashes erupted between cops and protesters in Spain just days after apocalyptic riots swept across France.

Twelve police officers and three protesters were injured after chaos broke out in A Coruña, a port city in Galicia, on Wednesday.



Around 100 people and several thousand demonstrators had gathered in María Pita Square to meet the leader of Spain’s right-wing Vox party.

But tensions boiled over by the end of Santiago Abascal’s speech with protesters launching eggs across the security cordon.



Shouts of “Galicia will be the tomb of fascism,” rippled across the crowd, met with a charge from police.

Two young people in the front row were injured, one of whom was arrested.



Another police charge tried to disperse the protesters, who started hurling stones from one of the square’s terraces.

Dramatic footage shows police in riot gear surrounded by a furious crowd, as hooded and masked protesters sling chairs at officers.



Separate footage shows a line of cops surging against a heaving group of demonstrators wildly waving flags and banners.

The protesters eventually retreated as a wall of police advanced towards the Church of San Jorge.

The three injured protesters were treated in the emergency room of the University Hospital Complex of A Coruña (CHUAC).

Cops arrested two people on suspicion of “assault and public disorder.”

Around 5,000 people had flocked to the square to reject the proposals of the Vox party in the run-up to the November 29 elections.



The A Coruña City Council condemned the outburst of violence.

“Any demand loses its legitimacy when violence is used, innocent people are attacked, and private property is damaged,” Mayor Inés Rey blasted.

But just hours later a second protest formed as crowds gathered to demand the release of those arrested.



More than 1,000 people clashed with riot police once again, lighting flares and forming barricades of burning furniture.

It comes after cars were set alight, shops were ransacked and a historic town hall was destroyed as hundreds of thousands took to the streets of France over the weekend.

The unrest spread from Paris to Limoges, Marseille and Lyon, forcing President Emmanuel Macron to appeal for calm.

At least 3,000 businesses were looted or damaged and more than 2,400 people were arrested.

Over the weekend, French president Emmanuel Macron blamed “agitators from far-Left fringe groups, joined by numerous criminals” for plunging his country into “unbridled violence”.



He made an impassioned plea “for unity” following chaos said to have involved up to 500,000 protesters.

The Gilet Jaunes – Yellow Vests – movement is meanwhile calling for another round of mass demonstrations on Saturday.

French police have already admitted that they “lost control” of major cities during a weekend of “apocalyptic rioting”.

“It was apocalyptic,” said a high-ranking officer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It follows almost five weeks of protests by school and university students against France’s crumbling education system.



They have now been joined by numerous other social groups, including the infamous Gilets Jaunes which brought chaos to France at the start of Macron’s time in office.

News.title: Putin ‘sends fishing boats to spy on Britain’ as tyrant’s loitering ships target critical undersea cables worth billions
News.content:
VLAD THREAT Putin ‘sends fishing boats to spy on Britain’ as tyrant’s loitering ships target critical undersea cables worth billions







Next

VLADIMIR Putin is deploying fishing trawlers to spy on the UK’s critical undersea cables, it is reported.

The bombshell revelation has sparked fears the Russian tyrant is mapping out Britain’s critical infrastructure to prepare for future attacks.



Nato has been tracking civilian vessels loitering in waters around Britain as they carry out espionage for the Kremlin, The Telegraph reports.

The outlet has analysed more than 500 cases of Russian trawlers lurking above vital communication cables linking the UK with Europe and the US.



Others have followed the cable routes – carrying billions of pounds of economic activity – for miles across the ocean.

Ministers have confirmed that Moscow is using “commercial proxies” to threaten the deep sea infrastructure.

A Russian attack on the network would paralyse the UK – disrupting hospitals, banks and the transport network.

Any assault would require accurate and specific knowledge of the cable’s exact position on the seabed.



The fresh analysis suggests Moscow has been carrying out subterfuge on an enormous scale, unchecked by the Royal Navy.

A Nato source told the outlet: “We’re absolutely aware of what Russian civilian fishing ships are up to and where …

“Some of these ships have never seen a single fish on their deck.”

Tracking shipping data across four years, The Telegraph found the most sustained activity occurred north of Scotland.

Here Russian fishing boats spent 337 hours over the Atlantic Crossing 1 telecommunications cable.



Europe has been on high alert for months after increasingly daring Russian underwater sabotage plots.

On December 25, 2024, an internet line connecting Finland to the Baltic states was cut by the rogue Eagle S tanker.

Hours later, the same ship’s anchor hit another four cables in rapid succession.



The vessel is believed to be part of Russia‘s shadow fleet – an armada of unmarked boats which allow Putin to dodge trade sanctions.

And British forces caught Russian subs training a secret weapon designed to disable critical undersea cables without leaving a trace this Spring.

The clandestine Russian operation was carried out by Moscow’s GUGI undersea warfare directorate near the remote Svalbard archipelago.

These strikes sit below the threshold of war but are designed to test the West and magnify Europe’s lack of a unified response, experts believe.

It comes as Western intelligence officials fear the Kremlin is ramping up sabotage operations in Europe and preparing for a conflict with NATO.



If Russia decides to attack, destroying subsea cables could be a critical part of that effort, officials warned.

Around £65billion of UK economic activity depends on undersea communications cables carrying data between Britain and the US.

They intersect with roughly 20,000 miles of subsea pipelines scattered around the world which also carry petroleum, crude oil and natural gas.

Every day, trillions of dollars worth of financial transactions as well as millions of barrels of oil and gas flow through these defenceless seabed pipes stitching the planet together.

Most are barely protected against foreign tyrants and dangerous global players – in some cases being so exposed even a fish could damage them.



The worst case scenario would be a simultaneous attack on multiple sections of the power cables such as in the Baltic Sea and North Atlantic Ocean.

This would plunge Europe into total panic as it would stop network operators from simply rerouting internet traffic to other cables.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In July 2022, Putin approved a maritime doctrine ordering Russian authorities to improve the “mobilised capabilities” of “fishing and special vessels”.

There is currently no law preventing Russian vessels from surveying the cables in international waters.

News.title: Navy has ‘lost its ability’ to fight beneath Arctic ice cap & is leaving seas to Russian subs, damning report warns
News.content:
Next

THE Navy has lost its ability to fight beneath the ice cap and is leaving the seas to Russian submarines, a damning report by MPs has warned.

Royal Navy crews need specialist training and subs with “hardened sails” to smash through the ice around the North Pole, like in the spy thriller Ice Station Zebra.



The skills were a Royal Navy staple until the late 1990s when it fell out of normal training cycle.

The last Navy exercise to smash through the ice was April 2018 and the last submarine fit to do it retired in 2024.



The lack of an under-ice capability was one of the “glaring gaps” in Britain’s High North defences identified by cross-party MPs.

Their report ‘Defence In The High North’ warned: “The UK has allowed its submarine under-ice capability to lapse just as the High North has become strategically more important.”

The report warned: “The lack of an under-ice capability allows Russia to leave its SSBNs [nuclear armed submarines] safe under the ice while its attack submarines surge forward to disrupt UK critical infrastructure, Nato sea lanes and allied [nuclear armed submarines] automatically putting the UK and Nato on the defensive.”

The Navy’s newer Astute class subs are still being “certified” for ice operations, MPs found.

It comes after The Sun revealed the Navy risks running out of captains due to record low numbers of offciers passing their “driving tests”.

And three more ships on the cutting board, bringing Labour’s scrap heap tally to 12.



As the ice caps melt the High North is increasingly contested. Russia wants access to military bases, undiscovered oil and gas fields and control of the merchant sea lanes linking Europe to Asia.

Labour’s Tan Dhesi MP, chair of the Defence Select Committee, said: “Russian submarine and sabotage forces in the High North pose direct risks to the North Atlantic and the UK, including the nuclear deterrent.

“Despite this, the Ministry of Defence has accepted a serious anti-submarine warfare gap.”

The report warned of chronic shortages of warships and submarines and cautioned against pretending that everything can be done by drones.

It said: “The MoD’s Hybrid Navy concept must not become a substitute for crewed capability before uncrewed systems have been proven in the specific conditions of the High North.”



It also warned against an over reliance on America after Donald Trump threatened Greenland and Canada, both essential High North Allies.

The report said: “Europe cannot count on the US returning to the European Arctic as the security partner and ally that the UK and Europe previously counted on.

The MoD said it was “clear-eyed about the threat Russia poses” and investing £1.8bn in Atlantic Bastion and subsea defences.

A spokesperson said: “We are leading allied activity across the High North, strengthening Nato’s northern flank and increasing our ability to respond rapidly to emerging threats.”

News.title: Cops issue update after police officer shot in the foot in Nottingham city centre
News.content:
Cops issue update after police officer shot in the foot in Nottingham city centre

The officer is now in hospital and detectives have been given more time to question suspects - but they have vowed their investigation is far from over

View 2 Images A police officer was shot in Nottingham on Sunday (Image: Joe Giddens/the Press Association)

The police officer shot in the foot in a British city on Sunday morning remains in hospital, their force have said in a new update issued on the probe.

The officer was shot in the foot in Nottingham city centre after approaching a man and a woman at a bus stop shortly before 5am, police previously said. The officer remains in hospital and is ‘in the expert care of medical professionals’, a new statement from Nottinghamshire Police issued at 10:35pm on Wednesday, October 21, said.

Detectives have also been given more time to question suspects by a court, it added. In total, seven people have been arrested — but the probe is far from over, according to Detective Chief Superintendent Richard Bull.

View 2 Images Forensic officers remained at the scene throughout Sunday (Image: Joe Giddens/the Press Association)

He said: "The investigation team continues to work tirelessly to establish exactly what happened before, during and after this appalling incident. I would like to thank them, along with colleagues from other police forces, for their continued support and assistance.

"It remains crucial that anyone with information about this incident comes forward and speaks to us.

"The injured officer was carrying out his duty to protect the public and it is truly abhorrent that this has happened to him. We continue to support him as he undergoes further treatment in hospital and are keeping him and his family fully informed of developments in the investigation.

"We would also like to stress that the officer has requested privacy at this time, and we ask that the media respects that wish."

A force spokesperson also thanked ‘everyone for their heartfelt messages of support and well wishes for the officer’. They also confirmed detectives have more time to question four people arrested hours after the shooting on Angel Row in the city centre.

Later that evening, cops stopped a vehicle in Radford and arrested its three occupants. Among them was a 27-year-old woman, arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

She is the suspect subject to a warrant allowing officers to question the suspect. The vehicle's two other occupants, a 24-year-old man and a 25-year-old woman, were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. Both have since been released on conditional bail pending further enquiries.

A 30-year-old man arrested in Bedfordshire during the early hours of Monday, October 19 was also questioned on suspicion of assisting an offender. He has since been recalled to prison for breaching the terms of his licence.

Meanwhile, a fifth arrest was made on Tuesday, October 20, when a 21-year-old woman was detained in south-east London on suspicion of assisting an offender. She has now been released on conditional bail pending further enquiries.

On Wednesday afternoon October 21, a 35-year-old man was arrested in Bulwell on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life and assisting an offender. A seventh person was then arrested during Wednesday evening when a 33-year-old female was detained in Aspley also on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life and assisting an offender. Both remain in custody.

Article continues below

Anyone with information who has not yet spoken to police is asked to call 101, quoting incident 106 of 18 October 2026. Information can also be passed anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: UK weather maps show 2C chill as Met Office forecast warns of 'chilly nights'
News.content:
UK weather maps show 2C chill as Met Office forecast warns of 'chilly nights'

Brits have been warned to brace for 'chilly nights' and cool conditions as weather forecasting models show daytime temperatures falling to 2C across parts of the UK

View 5 Images Minimum possible temperatures at 6am on November 1 (Image: WXCharts)

UK weather maps show temperatures could plummet to near freezing at the beginning of next month, with many Brits facing a cold snap.

‌



‌



The GFS weather model maps suggest temperatures will fall to just 1C in the Scottish Highlands at 6am on November 1, while other parts of southern and western coastal Scotland will remain slightly milder at around 3C.

‌



The map also shows part of England to be a chilly, with Cumbria and the North East expected to see 2C at 6am. As the day continues the overall pattern remains similar, with Scotland cooler than England.

‌



At 12pm, the cool temperatures are on the cards further south with parts of Manchester and Lancashire expected to sit at around 2/3C. In the south, the lower temperatures are forecast to be 7C, which will still feel crisp.

View 5 Images Minimum possible temperatures at midday on November 1 (Image: WXCharts)

Met Office weather maps show six counties facing snow on Friday – full list READ MORE :

By 6pm, most of the temperatures across the UK will slightly increase, however parts of the North West will remain at about 3C, the maps suggest.

‌



Throughout the day many areas are at risk of icy patches, including elevated inland locations in northern England and Scotland.

The mild conditions are expected to continue the following day, with overnight feeling fresh across the nation - even much of the south could drop to 4C.

‌



View 5 Images Minimum possible temperatures at 6pm on November 1 (Image: WXCharts)

On November 2 at 6am, the maps turn a light shade all over, forecasting cool conditions nationwide. Areas in the south and midlands will drop to 3C, with large part of Wales only reaching 4C.

‌



London is expected to be slightly warmer but will still feel very cold at 6C.

By midday these temperatures are not expected to increase, with many areas plummeting to cooler conditions.

‌



View 5 Images Minimum possible temperatures at 6am on November 2 (Image: WXCharts)

Areas surrounding Greater Manchester are likely to drop to 2C, according to the maps, with most of the midlands including Birmingham expected to drop to 3C.

‌



In London, the maps predict temperatures could fall to 6C. Parts of the south coast will also decrease to around 3C.

The Met Office's long range forecast for this period predicts 'chilly nights'.

‌



View 5 Images Minimum possible temperatures at midday on November 2

The forecast for October 26 to November 4 says: "Likely turning drier and calmer across the south and east bringing a greater chance of chilly nights and morning fog patches.

Article continues below

"A similar pattern then likely continuing during early November though with a chance that settled conditions may develop more widely for a time. Temperatures varying around average."

News.title: Sister of Stephen Hubbard held in Russian prison for years breaks silence after he's freed
News.content:
Sister of Stephen Hubbard held in Russian prison for years breaks silence after he's freed

Stephen Hubbard, a US citizen, was arrested by Russian officials while he lived in Ukraine as the Kremlin accused the 74-year-old of being a mercenary for Kyiv

View 2 Images (Image: Moscow City Court Press Service via AP)

The younger sister of the American prisoner Vladimir Putin freed after he spent years in a Russian jail has broken her silence on his release.

‌



‌



Stephen Hubbard was allowed out of prison on Wednesday, October 21, after spending more than four years behind bars. Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher, is now on his way back to the US.

‌



Now Hubbard has left Russian soil, he has had the chance to call his sister Patricia Hubbard Fox, who revealed what the pair talked about over the phone. She said: “That was awesome. He was just laughing. He said, ‘I can’t believe this is happening.’ He’s out of Russia territory. He is free, praise God. He really thought he was going to die in prison.”

‌



View 2 Images Trump said Hubbard was an 'innocent man' (Image: AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

President Donald Trump said he had asked Putin to free Hubbard during a phone call earlier this month. The US’ envoy in St. Petersburg, Steve Witkoff, also held talks with Putin about the war in Ukraine.

"He is the happiest man around," Trump said of Hubbard, describing the Michigan man as a "very high-quality, innocent man."

‌



Now Stephen is on his way home, Patricia said he suffered beatings and starvation while he was held captive. She said her brother was in perfect health when he was “kidnapped” in 2022 and accused of fighting alongside Ukrainian forces.

She added he now suffers from an enlarged heart and likely has post-traumatic stress disorder.

‌



Her brother was accused of signing a contract with the Ukrainian military and sentenced in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison during closed court proceedings. The US government under the Biden administration designated him as wrongfully detained, and his legal team has also disputed the Russian allegation, saying he was not involved in any military activity.

Hubbard, a US Air Force veteran, taught English overseas and retired in 2012 to Cyprus, where one of his sons is an Orthodox Christian priest. He later moved to Ukraine to be with a woman he had met, his lawyers said, and remained in the country after the relationship ended and was living there at the time of Russia ’s invasion.

Article continues below

Patricia also disputed the claim that her brother was a mercenary, saying he was used as “bait” in Putin’s war with Ukraine. She scolded the Russian premier: “Putin is as evil as they come.”

Patricia said her brother would probably come live with her in Colorado, and they both were looking forward to a family reunion — and sleeping somewhere comfortable. Patricia said she has slept on her couch for four years in solidarity with her brother “because I figured he didn’t have a bed. Why should I have a bed?”

News.title: Final moments of toddler, 1, captured on CCTV before tragic fatal police shooting
News.content:
Final moments of toddler, 1, captured on CCTV before tragic fatal police shooting

The footage shows the final moments before police shot and killed a one-year-old boy after an alleged shoplifting incident in Mississippi outside a Walmart store

View 4 Images Bodycam footage shows the final moments before the one-year-old was shot and killed

Bodycam footage shows the tragic final moments that led to the fatal police shooting of a one-year-old boy in a Mississippi car park.

‌



‌



The horrific events unfolded when police responded to an alleged shoplifting call on June 14 and opened fire on a vehicle after the child's mother allegedly tried to escape.. The incident took place outside a Walmart in Senatobia after Vellesiya Wiley and Latoya Ferrell were allegedly caught shoplifting.

‌



Kohen Wiley, Vellesiya's one-year-old son, was caught in the crossfire and sadly died.

‌



View 4 Images It has been confirmed the officers won't face any charges

The shooting triggered outrage, but the release of the bodycam footage comes as Mississippi Attorney Gerenal Lynn Fitch confirmed the officers who opened fire would not face any charges, with a review finding "the use of force was justified".

The footage, initially shared by Darkhorse Press, starts with a man running into the Walmart security office to warn the officers an active theft was in process.

‌



He can be heard saying: "Two women are running, two women are running."

View 4 Images Kohen Wiley, 1, was shot dead by officers in the incident

‌



Several officers sprinted into action, running to the car park and catching up with the vehicle as Wiley appeared to be attempting to get away.

The footage then shows several officers surrounding the vehicle ordering her to "stop the car". However, within seconds Ferrell, who was driving, accelerates towards the police and hits them with the vehicle.

‌



In the clip, a number of gunshots can be heard ringing out as she accelerated forward, and officials confirmed the one-year-old was shot dead.

Vellesiya claimed that the police were aware a baby was in the car as she raised Kohen in the air in the exchange. She said: “I raised my baby up, trying to show that he was in the car. So she [Ferrell] was backing up and she hit a car.”

‌



View 4 Images The driver was also airlifted to hospital after the shooting (Image: NBC News)

Her attorney, Ben Crump, said the two women deny the allegations they were shoplifting and neither have been charged with a crime in connection with the incident.

‌



The force used by the officers was determined as 'justified' but there was no further reasoning given.

Wiley added: “By the time I set my baby down, it was like three to four shots. One of the shots hit him in his ribcage and the other shot hit her in her arm and her thigh."

Article continues below

Baby Kohen was later pronounced dead at a local hospital as Ferrell airlifted to another hospital and was left in a critical condition, according to family members.

News.title: Tragedy as couple found dead at home nine years after children died in fire
News.content:
Tragedy as couple found dead at home nine years after children died in fire

Police are now probing how the two passed away - it is said they never got over the deaths of their young children in a refuge fire nine years ago which nearly killed their mother

View 3 Images Jamie McGinn and Bridgid "Biddy" O'Brien, who were found dead at their home in south County Dublin on Wednesday morning.

The bodies of a couple have tragically been found at home nine years after their two young children died in a horrific fire.

‌



‌



Bridgid 'Biddy' O’Brien, 45, and her partner Jamie McGinn, 38, were found dead at their home in Bray, Ireland, early on Wednesday morning. Their deaths are now being probed by Irish police, gardai, although it is not thought foul play had a role in their deaths.

‌



While Mr McGinn, who was found just outside the house, suffered visible injuries, the Irish Mirror reports there was no indication Ms O’Brien had sustained any injuries. Two full post-mortems are now set to take place and gardai hope that will help solve the mystery of how the couple died.

‌



The couple never got over the deaths of their children Jordan, four, and three-year-old Holly, who died in a fire that also killed their aunt and a young cousin in west Dublin in March 2017.

"It is another terrible tragedy for the family," a source said. A police spokesperson added : "Gardaí from the Serious Crime Unit, DMR East, continue to investigate all of the circumstances surrounding the discovery of two bodies at a residential property in Bray, Co. Dublin.

"Shortly after 8:00am, Gardaí were alerted following the discovery of the bodies of a male aged in his 30s and a female aged in her 40s at a residence on Old Connaught Avenue, Bray. Both individuals were pronounced deceased at the scene.

‌



"The bodies of both have been removed to the City Morgue at Whitehall where a post mortem examination will be completed by State Pathologist, Dr. Sally Anne Collis over the course of this evening and tomorrow. The results of the post mortem examination will assist Gardaí in determining the course of the investigation going forward."

And the force appealed for any witnesses to come forward.

‌



View 3 Images Police say a post mortem will help explain how the couple passed away

The statement continued: "The scene remains preserved for technical examination this evening, October 21, 2026. A Senior Investigating Officer (SIO) is leading the investigation from an incident room at Dun Laoghaire Garda Station.

‌



"Family Liaison Officers have been appointed to support the bereaved families. An Garda Síochána appeals to anyone with any information in relation to this incident to contact Dun Laoghaire Garda Station on (01) 666 5000, the Garda Confidential Line on 1800 666 111, or any Garda Station."

The couple were left devastated after the March 2017 blaze killed Jordan and Holly - and left Biddy fighting for her life. The tragedy happened when she brought her children to stay over with her sister Anne Marie O’Brien at a refuge in Clondalkin.

‌



A fire broke out at the refuge and claimed the lives of Biddy’s two children - as well Anne Marie, who was seven months pregnant, and her daughter Paris, aged two. Biddy, who was the only survivor of the blaze, spent several weeks in intensive care and only regained consciousness around a month after the disaster.

James then had to break the news to her that their children, as well as Anne Marie and little Paris had all perished in the fire. An inquest later heard that the fire was accidental, and was probably caused by a tea light or candle setting fire to a large TV screen.

‌



Friends paid tribute to the couple online on Wednesday.

View 3 Images Their deaths are now being investigated (Image: Getty Images)

‌



One said: "RIP Jamie and Biddy, sleep well mate, back with your babies now." Another said: "Can't believe this, rest in peace the both of you."

And another said: "Our hearts are shattered. Not a day went by without u calling into us for some lunch or dinner or a chat - how life can go on without that big laugh that helping hand around our home?

‌



"You left too soon, no chance of good bye.

"Hug and hold your babies, they deserve to have you back with them. We love you always miss you forever."

‌



The couple had both experienced substance abuse issues after the deaths of their children and Mr McGinn had become addicted to drugs. In February 2024, he was jailed for 18 months after he admitted possessing almost €200,000 worth of cocaine and cannabis - that he was holding for a drugs gang.

Dublin Circuit Criminal Court heard Mr McGinn took responsibility for the drugs. He was arrested and made admissions after the seizure the previous year. He told gardai that he had an €8,000 drug debt and he was holding the drugs to reduce his debt.

Article continues below

The court also heard his only other convictions were for road traffic offences.

News.title: Christa Pike's attorney issues new health update weeks after botched execution
News.content:
Christa Pike's attorney issues new health update weeks after botched execution

Christa Pike, 50, survived two massive doses of pentobarbital after the US state of Tennessee attempted to execute her - now just a few weeks on her attorney has issued an update on her health

View 4 Images Christa Pike continues to recover after her botched execution (Image: WVLT 8)

An attorney for Christa Pike, who was initially left unconscious and unable to communicate after surviving a botched execution, has issued an update on her condition weeks after her execution attempt left her unconscious and unable to communicate.

‌



‌



Christa Pike, 50, survived two massive doses of pentobarbital after the US state of Tennessee attempted to execute her for the brutal 1995 murder of classmate Colleen Slemmer.

‌



The lethal drugs failed to kill her, instead leaving her arms burned and blistered. Following the botched execution, Pike spent days unconscious and breathing through a ventilator in intensive care. Doctors feared she was brain-dead. But in a twist that shocked medics, she defied all odds to wake up on Tuesday and started talking.

‌



Christa was later released from the hospital and returned to prison, where she has continued receiving medical care. Her attorneys previously said she was struggling with confusion, memory issues and significant physical injuries.

View 4 Images Christa Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed Colleen Slemmer (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

911 call after Christa Pike failed lethal injection execution reveals confusion that delayed medical help READ MORE :

In the latest update her attorney has told TMZ she's continuing to improve physically and is now able to walk more on her own. The attorney says Christa's speech has also improved, and she's now able to communicate more clearly and form full sentences.

‌



However, her attorney says her cognitive and psychological functioning are still being monitored and it could take another month or longer before there's a clearer picture of any potential long-term effects from the ordeal.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



According to 911 dispatch recordings, it took 31 minutes for prison officials to confirm that a request for emergency medical assistance was legitimate after confusion between prison staff and first responders delayed the response.

After being rushed to hospital on September 30 one of Pike's lawyers, Randy Spivey, said that she suffered "extraordinary" swelling to her hands, which he described as looking like "if you tried to blow up a surgical glove".

‌



She remained shackled to her bed at the Tennessee hospital where she was taken after the execution.

The killer also woke up with a blood clot and pneumonia, and was unable to swallow, eat or move her badly swollen arms. "I don't know what function she will regain," he revealed in the days after the execution. "We do know that there is a long road ahead".

‌



Confusion that delayed medical help

View 4 Images Emergency vehicles leave Riverbend Maximum Security Institution after the execution of Christa Pike was halted (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

The audio captured from a series of 911 calls revealed emergency services were delayed over confusion among both prison officials and first responders. The recordings showed that minutes passed as the two camps tried to confirm whether the emergency request from the chamber was legitimate or not.

‌



The Nashville Department of Emergency Communications (DEC) released the transcript from the first call, which shows the moment officials detail the attempted execution. The transcript states: "We've been carrying out an execution tonight. We've administered 10 grams of pentobarbital. The person is not yet deceased. That started approximately 1 hour ago. And we're calling for an ambulance."

The dispatcher then asked the caller for a verification code, which they were unable to provide, prompting questions about whether the call was a "prank". One dispatcher says: "We are trying to find out if that is an actual thing that is happening and we need to send an ambulance and, or if you need police assistance or if this is someone that is just basically prank calling or, like, swatting us."

‌



A dispatcher later concludes the call was "false" and that medical assistance was not required at Riverbend, where Pike had sustained severe injuries to her arms. They say: “Per supervisors here at the DEC, we have been informed that it is a false call. There is no medical assistance needed at Riverbend prison.”

The confusion further continued when a dispatcher called back, saying they had received "a call about a failed execution at your guys' facility", adding they were calling to verify. They found a confused DEC employee on the other side, who asked: “Um, who called you?” After a short back and forth, the corrections employee says: "I’m being told that nobody from our facility called you, so there’s not really anything to speak of at the moment.”

‌



View 4 Images Pike's fate now remains unknown

What happens to Pike now?

It remains unclear whether Tennessee will try to execute her again. Her attorneys have said that they will urge Republican Gov. Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life in prison without parole.

Article continues below

“She should never be subjected to another execution attempt,” they said in the statement".

Lee has since postponed the state’s only other scheduled execution this year and ordered a review of why the execution failed. Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on whether a problem with the IV line caused the drug to pool in her tissue instead of entering her bloodstream.

News.title: Revolut and Lloyds down: Google Cloud outage hits banks as cards 'declined'
News.content:
A Google Cloud outage left Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC customers unable to make payments or transfer money for hours on Tuesday

A Google Cloud outage has disrupted a range of online services across the UK, leaving bank customers unable to make payments for hours.

The apps and websites of Revolut, HSBC, Rightmove, Royal Mail and Lloyds Banking Group brands Lloyds Bank, Bank of Scotland and Halifax were among those affected on Tuesday morning, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.

Revolut appeared to be down for thousands of customers, with many taking to social media to report that their cards were being declined and they could not access their accounts.

Google Cloud said the outage in its western Europe region was caused by a "power event" and had been "mitigated" by lunchtime on Tuesday. The companies mentioned have yet to confirm that their service disruptions were linked to the outage.

News.title: MI5 monitored NHS founder Nye Bevan for more than 20 years over 'Russia links'
News.content:
MI5 monitored NHS founder Nye Bevan for more than 20 years over 'Russia links'

Nye Bevan, one of the most important ministers of the post-war Labour government who spearheaded the creation of the NHS, was placed under regular surveillance by M15, files show

View 4 Images Nye Bevan, former Minister for Health and founder of the NHS (Image: Popperfoto via Getty Images)

Heroic National Health Service founder Nye Bevan was subject to monitoring by MI5 for more than two decades, according to newly-released official files.

‌



‌



Papers released to the National Archives show that the mastermind of the Labour movement, celebrated for founding the NHS, first came to the attention of the security service in the 1930s as a firebrand left-winger amid concern about his links with prominent communists. The monitoring continued even after he became a minister in the post-war Labour government, when he drove through the creation of the NHS in the teeth of bitter opposition from doctors.

‌



At one stage, the director general of MI5 became so concerned about his links to a known Russia spy that he went to see prime minister Clement Attlee in No 10 to warn him.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images He spearheaded the establishment of the NHS in 1948 (Image: Mirrorpix)

Proud relatives of NHS founder Nye Bevan issue heartfelt message over Tory cuts READ MORE :

However, some in the service questioned why they were taking an interest in his activities, given that everything he did was out in the open on the floor of the House of Commons.

‌



As a 13-year-old miner in the 1910s, he frequently witnessed serious accidents and saw co-workers suffer terrible illnesses from inhaling coal dust. But thanks to the Tredegar Workmen’s Medical Aid Society – the inspiration for what became the NHS – Mr Bevan observed ordinary people getting the medical care they needed. Decades later, as Minister of Health he was the chief architect of the NHS.

Reviewing the papers after his death in 1960, one MI5 officer noted: "Considering what a controversial character Nye Bevan was, the file is remarkably tame."

‌



View 4 Images A mural to the iconic founder at his hometown in Tredegar (Image: Jonathan Buckmaster)

The papers show that MI5 first opened a personal file on Mr Bevan - then the backbench Labour MP for Ebbw Vale in South Wales - in 1933. One of the first reports includes an account of a Canadian anti-Nazi rally which Mr Bevan addressed in Montreal in 1934.

‌



"Bevan has inherited the evangelical fervour of his Welsh forebears and knows how to use it in the Communist cause," it stated. "He pictured the overthrow of the Nazi regime as meaning the commencement of a united Europe under Soviet rule."

In 1943, Roger Hollis, a future director general, complied a summary of what they knew of Mr Bevan's activities up to that point.

‌



In 1933, he noted, the MP had been "in close touch" with Harry Pollitt, general secretary of the Communist Party of Great Britain, and others in the party who backed his plan to organise "workers' freedom groups" to defend against the "capitalists".

Against a background of mass unemployment and the Great Depression, he had been closely associated with the hunger marches of 1934, entertaining deputations of marchers in the House of Commons.

‌



View 4 Images M15 were watching his movements for years, records show (Image: Daily Mirror)

He soon fell out, however, with his communist allies, who complained he was not interested in workers' unity and was intent on building "a movement of his own" - now named The Sons of Freedom - with "all the elements of a fascist organisation".

‌



By 1936 they had patched up their differences sufficiently for Mr Bevan to support an application by the Communist Party to affiliate to the Labour Party.

With the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939 he was said to have adopted a policy of "war on two fronts" - attacking the Germans abroad and Neville Chamberlain's Conservative government at home.

‌



That continued with formation of Winston Churchill's coalition government - sharply criticising the prosecution of the war while accusing Labour ministers of "leaning too much to the right".

Although there is nothing in the files to indicate that MI5 ever tapped his phone or intercepted his mail, some wondered why they were bothering with him at all.

‌



"I do not think that Bevan's activities are a matter in which we, the security service, should be involved," one officer wrote in 1943. "In fact he makes exactly the same remarks in the Houses of Parliament pretty frequently, as any copy of Hansard will show, and it would not therefore be possible to do anything positive."

Nevertheless, the reporting continued after the war - albeit less frequently - when Mr Bevan was appointed minister of health in Mr Attlee's new government.

‌



In 1949, MI5 was becoming increasingly concerned about Mr Bevan's friendship with Wilfred Macartney, "an unsavoury, unscrupulous character" who had been convicted of spying for Russia in 1928.

Recordings of his conversations suggested he was passing on information obtained by Mr Bevan to Mr Pollitt, the Communist Party leader.

‌



In May of that year, the director general Sir Percy Sillitoe took the evidence to Mr Attlee - who dismissed Mr Macartney's claims as a "tissue of lies" but agreed to "warn Bevan about Macartney in general terms without, of course, making any allusion to the conversation".

One of the final reports dates from 1954 when Mr Bevan, by now back in opposition, was invited to meet the Soviet ambassador, Yakov Malik, over lunch at the Polish embassy in London.

‌



The event "went off very badly" in part because the Russian had difficulty in understanding Mr Bevan's Welsh accent leading to a bad-tempered misunderstanding.

"A great deal of drink was consumed, but the party broke up in a none too friendly atmosphere," the report stated.

Article continues below

The file was not finally closed however until 1975 - 15 years after Mr Bevan had died.

News.title: Criminals who skip sentencing will face solitary confinement or lose social visits
News.content:
Judges in England and Wales will be given stronger powers to block prison visits and keep offenders in their cells for weeks on end if they refuse to face their victims' families during sentencing.

The tougher sanctions, due to come into effect next year, build on an existing law that orders criminals to attend sentencing or face being fined or jailed for another two years for contempt of court.

The move is the latest bid to push killers to attend court, with the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) acknowledging that longer jail time alone is unlikely to deter them if they are already behind bars.

"Criminals should not be able to pick and choose when they face justice," Prisons Minister Catherine McKinnell said.

"Refusing to turn up to sentencing is an insult to victims and their families, and offenders must face the consequences", she added.

The new measures mean offenders could be confined to cells for up to three weeks, social visits could be banned for nearly a month and any prison privileges revoked for longer.

Judges will also be able to restrict social visits further to once every four weeks for almost three months for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing.

For criminals aged 18-20, similar restrictions could be handed down, but for shorter periods of time, the MoJ said.

However, visits from prisoners' children will be exempt from the new sanctions.

But Pia Sinha, the CEO of Prison Reform Trust, has called for evidence that sanctions will increase attendance and warned the measures will punish relatives of prisoners who "have committed no offence themselves".

The families of murdered primary school teacher Sabina Nessa, law graduate Zara Aleena and mother-of-three Jan Mustafa have previously advocated for changes to the laws.

All of their loved ones' killers did not attend their sentencing hearings.

Thomas Cashman, the gunman who murdered nine-year-old Olivia Pratt-Korbel, and triple crossbow and knife killer Kyle Clifford, also refused to face their punishment in court.

Victims' Commissioner for England and Wales, Claire Waxman OBE, said the announcement follows "tireless efforts of victims' families" not accepting offenders simply "opting out of facing justice".

She said it was "essential" the powers were used "consistently by courts and prisons, so families receive the justice and accountability they deserve".

News.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
News.content:
A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.

It will test multiple drugs simultaneously, starting with two repurposed medicines already used to treat type 2 diabetes and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

The study will examine whether the drugs can lessen symptoms such as memory and thinking problems, and help people maintain their quality of life.

Angela Bucksey, 67, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with Alzheimer's in January and is the first person to begin treatment on the trial, called AD-SMART.

"We have Alzheimer's in the family," she told the BBC.

"My mother had it and my aunts, so it was a disappointment rather than a shock when I was diagnosed because I knew it would restrict my life.

"But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me."

Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".

"Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back."

Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.

News.title: The real reasons US politicians are getting older
News.content:
Twenty-seven-year-old Republican Riley Owen is one of the few candidates from Gen Z - aged in their early teens to late 20s - from either party running for Congress on 3 November.

Owen is running in a newly created district in Utah that experts say may lean towards the Democrats. He has championed issues including paid maternity leave, restrictions on congressional stock trading and environmental action - all issues that may appeal to Democratic supporters.

When he was confirmed as his party's candidate in the state's 1st congressional district, he walked on stage to Billy Joel's We Didn't Start the Fire, and argued that his generation needed to help renew the American Dream.

The gerontocracy is "a bipartisan issue", he says. "We've got people who have become career politicians, and they spend their lives in Congress." He says this is indicative of a system that is not delivering for Americans.

Owen says the big challenge he faces is the fact that money really talks in US politics. Research suggests campaign donors tend to prefer incumbent candidates.

Indeed, the campaign of his rival Ben McAdams - a 51-year-old Democrat who has previously served in Congress - has so far raised much more cash than Owen's. By mid-October, McAdams had raised over $2.6m (Â£1.9m), compared with $150,000 raised by Owen, according to records on the Federal Election Commission website.

Owen argues that his generation is uniquely well-placed to understand contemporary political issues, such as the challenges posed by tech. He also disputes any suggestion that a younger candidate necessarily lacks relevant experience - pointing to his own background as a military officer and a White House policy analyst. "I think in politics, just like in industry, we need what's called disruptive innovation," he says.

The age of America's top politicians has long been a talking point. In 1984 Reagan - who was then America's oldest president at age 73 - deflected scrutiny with a quip about the "youth and inexperience" of his opponent Walter Mondale, who was a sprightly 56.

In the US, individual states also have their own legislatures, with a Senate and a House, where many politicians make their start. Many current members of Congress spent years in state politics before running for a seat in Washington

News.title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns
News.content:
The UK has "glaring gaps" in its ability to defend the Arctic region, leaving it vulnerable to potential Russian attacks, a report by MPs has warned.

The Commons Defence Committee said a shortage of Royal Navy warships and submarines was leaving the country's critical infrastructure in the High North, including undersea cables and energy supplies, exposed.

In the event of a conflict, the report added that Russia could threaten the UK's population, civilian and military infrastructure and vital supply routes across the Atlantic from the US.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) said it is "clear-eyed about the threat Russia posed" and is investing heavily to protect Britain's undersea cables.

Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer previously warned that Russia could attack Nato by the end of the decade.

The High North - which includes the Arctic circle and areas adjacent to it - has become central to the UK's defence concerns in recent years.

Earlier this year, the MoD said Russian submarine activity in the North Atlantic is now back to the same levels as the Cold War era.

In the new report, MPs highlighted a "shockingly low availability" of submarines and said there was a temporary loss in ability to operate them beneath Arctic ice.

"Russia can then use the ice to conceal and protect its own submarines while threatening Nato sea lanes, UK critical infrastructure and the UK's nuclear deterrent," it added.

Chair of the Defence Committee, Tan Dhesi, said: "This is a demanding, hostile environment, and one that our greatest adversary, Russia, is seeking to dominate for military advantage."

The work to address these gaps "cannot start soon enough," he added.

In light of uncertainty over US support for Nato, the report said the UK should consider whether the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force (Jef), a UK-led military coalition of northern European nations, should focus more on the High North.

An MoD spokesperson said the Jef was already "strengthening Nato's northern flank and increasing our ability to respond rapidly to emerging threats".

Conservative shadow minister for war readiness Stuart Anderson said: "If Nato could be at war with Russia as soon as 2030, as the former prime minister warned, that means time is just as important as money.

"To deter war we must be ready for it, that means spending money now, not kicking the can down the road until it's too late".

News.title: Dame Judi Dench: 'I can't do a play, a film or read any more'
News.content:
Dench also discussed meeting American actor Sidney Poitier, who became the first black man to win the Academy Award for best actor in 1964.

She was appearing in Amy's View in New York when Poitier came backstage after a performance. She recalled that director Richard Eyre was in her dressing room, giving her notes, when there was a knock at the door.

Dench said she felt as if she were in a wind tunnel when Poitier walked in, adding: "It was thrilling."

Asked what she had said to him, Dench replied: "Not much, a bit of an open mouth. So charming. Very tall."

The conversation then turned to Dench's love of Shakespeare. She recalled watching her brother play King Duncan in Macbeth when she was nine and said the moment sparked her passion for the playwright.

"He walked on and he said 'What bloody man is that?' I thought, 'oh my God, this is for me'. He said 'bloody', did you hear that?"

She also admitted to being " besotted" by Shakespeare's sonnets: "I just love them."

"It's the rhythm of it. It's the rhythm of your heart," she added, "it's the way he's summed up so simply the way that any of us feel about, well, anything."

News.title: The 'trillion pound' oil fund the government believes Britain could have built
News.content:
After a half-century wait, the United Kingdom now has an oil fund.

Chancellor John Healey announced the creation of an Energy Wealth Fund at the Jackdaw gas approval announcement on Wednesday, with Â£2bn of funding diverted from the existing National Wealth Fund.

A selection of energy exporting countries, mainly in the Gulf, but also including Norway, over the years have amassed multi-trillion funds using oil and gas revenues to create epic national piggy banks.

It has been a long-standing debate in UK economic policy circles. If neighbouring Norway has amassed a $2.4tn war chest from the same North Sea, where exactly did the UK's sovereign wealth fund go?

It is an apposite question on the week when the national debt also hit Â£3tn for the first time.

"The proceeds of this oil and gas coming ashore now can be invested for the future generations," the chancellor said.

"If we had done this when North Sea oil was first discovered in the 1980s, we'd have a British Sovereign Wealth Fund now that would be worth probably a trillion pounds."

On Wednesday, for the first time, Treasury officials actually calculated how much that missing British fund could have been worth.

The trillion pound number comes from internal Treasury modelling. The assumption was that the UK's historical North Sea receipts of Â£200bn had been invested, with no withdrawals and grown at a rate comparable to Norway's.

"Norway demonstrates the power of long-term investment: the government wants to learn from that principle, rather than copy its model wholesale," one insider told me.

It was a "missed opportunity" which "had we systematically invested those receipts, we could have built a huge national asset for future generations", they said.

News.title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds
News.content:
Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.

A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.

Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.

Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".

Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.

Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK:

AQA

Cambridge OCR

Pearson Edexcel

WJEC

CCEA

Qualifications Scotland

At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.

She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.

Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-Â­level Geology.

Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.

Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.

Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery. Franklin had died four years earlier.

Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.

The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.

"Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged."

The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".

They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.

Stephanie Buttigieg, one of the authors, said: "Relatable role models can help keep more girls in STEM by strengthening their sense of belonging in science and fostering positive attitudes towards scientific careers."

A spokeswoman for the Joint Council for Qualifications, which represents AQA, Cambridge OCR, CCEA, WJEC and Pearson, said: "Exam boards recognise that there is a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications, and this is an area they will be focusing on as these qualifications are reformed."

Qualifications Scotland said the Curriculum Improvement Cycle offered "an opportunity to consider gender representation within our future qualifications and assessments".

The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".

The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".

Additional reporting by Marthe de Ferrer and Rahib Khan

News.title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy
News.content:
Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices.

A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (Â£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

"The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices".

Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico". The company intends to appeal, a move Mahoney said will be successful.

The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety.

New Mexico's lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then still doing business as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

That firm utilised data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time.

New Mexico had also accused Meta of intentionally misleading the public on how it benefitted from content that included hate speech, and how such rules against it were enforced. The jury found the company had intentionally misled the public on those claims, too.

Meta disputed those accusations. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online," Mahoney added.

Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been.

They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly two million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data. A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times.

"For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," New Mexico Attorney General RaÃºl Torrez said on Wednesday.

"Today's result makes clear that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable."

The state lawyers sought up to $40bn in fines against Meta. Meta had argued anything beyond $3.4bn would be unconstitutional.

Judge Francis Mathew on Wednesday was direct in his decision to fine Meta an amount roughly equal to its profits each quarter.

He said Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations to the public about how their Facebook data was used and shared were "willful" and spanned "more than 11 years", stretching from 2010 to 2021.

Communications between senior executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, were "designed to mislead the public", Judge Mathew wrote in his order.

While the full amount of the penalty against Meta, based on thousands of violations of state law, was calculated as $219bn, Judge Mathew reduced the penalty to the $25bn fine.

It follows a $5bn fine levied by the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 against the company over its data privacy practices.

News.title: Burnham defends Jackdaw decision as Badenoch urges PM to overturn ban on new oil and gas licences
News.content:
The UK government has approved production from the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea amid intense debate about the project's environmental and economic impact.

Ministers said the first gas could be produced by the end of this month, helping heat millions of homes, and also announced the creation of a new energy wealth fund.

But environmental campaigners said the decision would hamper efforts to tackle climate change and make "no meaningful difference" to UK energy security.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused the prime minister of "dithering" on Jackdaw and said a ban on new oil and gas licences should be repealed - but Andy Burnham said her party had "messed up" the original decision.

Jackdaw is situated 150 miles (241km) east of Aberdeen and is operated by Adura, a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state energy firm Equinor.

A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, which is located off the coast of Shetland in the North Atlantic.

News.title: The four locations in the running to be UK City of Culture 2029
News.content:
Blackpool, Milton Keynes, Sheffield and Wrexham have been shortlisted to become the UK's City of Culture in 2029.

The winning location will be announced in May and will be the fifth holder of the title - following Derry-Londonderry, Hull, Coventry and Bradford.

A different location is given the City of Culture title every four years. Each shortlisted city will now receive at least Â£125,000 from the government to do further work on their bid.

The eventual winner will receive Â£10m to deliver a year of cultural events and activities drawing on its "local strengths and stories".

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said the shortlisted cities "have shown the pride that exists in their places with the incredible culture on their doorsteps".

Three of the contenders are in England and one in Wales. They were chosen from a longlist of nine, which also included Inverness, Ipswich, Middlesbrough, Portsmouth and Swindon.
