News.title: Jailed former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson being investigated over alleged rape inside Parliament
News.content:
Jailed former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Jeffrey Donaldson is being investigated by London police about an alleged rape of a woman inside the Houses of Parliament, the BBC can reveal.

The disgraced former MP has been accused of raping the woman in Parliament in 2016, at the very heart of the political establishment.

Last week Donaldson was sentenced to 15 years in prison for a series of child sex offences against two victims, including one count of rape, which took place between 1985 and 2008. He is seeking to appeal against his convictions.

It is understood the woman has been interviewed by Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) officers.

The PSNI has now shared her claims with the Metropolitan Police, as the alleged incident happened in London.

While not naming the former DUP leader, the Met has issued a statement confirming a 63-year-old man is being investigated.

It said: "On Tuesday 13 October, the Met received a report referred to us by the Police Service of Northern Ireland relating to an allegation of rape in 2016, by a man now aged 63.

"The allegation relates to one victim who is being supported by specialist officers.

"The investigation is in its early stages. No arrests have been made and enquiries are ongoing."

In July, the Belfast Telegraph first reported that a woman from Northern Ireland alleged she had been sexually assaulted by Donaldson in the DUP offices at Parliament in 2016.

She claimed that he attempted to get her to drink vodka shots in his office, before trying to kiss her and put his hand up her skirt.

On Saturday, the newspaper further reported that the Met was set to investigate and interview Donaldson about these accusations.

But in response to BBC questions it has now emerged the same woman has also alleged Donaldson raped her.

Concerns about the ex-DUP MP's behaviour in London were raised in a BBC NI Spotlight film, earlier this year.

A former senior PSNI detective told the programme he had seen Donaldson drunk in the Houses of Parliament.

Two other former senior PSNI detectives also reported seeing him going into a gay sauna not far from Parliament in 2006, the same year in which Donaldson described homosexuality as "sinful".

News.title: Aberfan disaster 'most tragic of days imaginable' says King on 60th anniversary
News.content:
The King has described the Aberfan disaster which killed 116 children and 28 adults as the "most tragic of days imaginable" on its 60th anniversary.

Pantglas Junior School and a number of nearby houses in the village near Merthyr Tydfil, south Wales, were catastrophically engulfed in coal slurry after the colliery spoil tip collapsed on 21 October 1966.

King Charles III, Queen Camilla and the Prince of Wales joined survivors and bereaved families on Wednesday and laid wreaths and a posy with the last surviving teacher in the Aberfan Memorial Garden, located on the site of the school.

The King also paid tribute to the community's strength, resilience and "unconquerable spirit".

Warning: This story contains upsetting details that some may find distressing

About half the children from the school died when excavated mining debris from the Merthyr Vale Colliery was dislodged, and 150,000 tonnes of coal waste came thundering down the hillside.

Emergency services, miners and people who rushed to the village began an around-the-clock battle to dig out those trapped by the debris.

News.title: Burnham proposes plan to cut standing charges from gas bills
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked ministers to develop a plan to remove standing charges from gas bills.

These are fixed daily fees that cover the costs of connecting to a supply. They vary by region and households must still pay them even when energy is not being used.

Industry body Energy UK said whether the proposed changes would make a difference to bills would depend on how or where the charges were reallocated on the bill.

But an influential research foundation argued it would be a progressive move that would help those on low-incomes and knock Â£27 off a typical annual bill.

During Prime Minister's Questions, Burnham said the "pragmatic decision" on giving the green light to the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea would allow the government to increase investment in renewables and "do more to help people with bills".

He said he had asked the Chancellor John Healey and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh "to look at whether we can remove standing charges from gas bills and to report back to this house at the earliest opportunity".

No details have been given on how removing standing charges would work in practice. But the suggestion has been made by research firm Nesta that they could be moved to the unit rate, external, so people pay for what they use.

This would probably benefit customers who don't use much gas, but heavy users could end up paying more.

For nearly two years, regulator Ofgem has run a series of consultations on standing charges, with a massive public response including vociferous opposition from low-energy users who can do nothing to cut standing charges.

Ofgem is running a pilot scheme on low standing charge tariffs, but is yet to draw any firm conclusions, suggesting there are no easy answers.

News.title: Teenage boy guilty of trying to murder girl, 15, in school
News.content:
A teenage boy who had a hatred of women and an "obsessive interest" in killers has been found guilty of the attempted murder of a girl at his school.

The boy dressed in black and wore a face mask before stabbing the 15-year-old victim in the back at Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich, in March.

Armed police were called to the school, which went into lockdown, and the attack was caught on CCTV.

The boy, who is 16 and cannot be named for legal reasons, wrote notes about hating women and had an "obsessive and dangerous interest in killers and killing", jurors at King's Lynn Crown Court were told. He will be sentenced on 18 December.

Jurors deliberated for just under four hours before delivering a majority verdict at the end of a trial which began two weeks ago.

The teenager "went to school not to learn, but to kill" while armed with a kitchen knife, the prosecution said.

The school went into lockdown after the attack and there was an armed police response, while the girl was taken to hospital with a minor injury.

News.title: Tributes paid to 'bravest' woman who died of 'stab wounds' after crash
News.content:
Tributes have been paid to a woman who crashed a car into a wall after allegedly being stabbed.

Eleanor Barnfield, 47, died in hospital after police were called to the crash in Bridgend on Monday, where they found she had "puncture wounds unrelated to the collision", which the BBC understands were sustained in a stabbing.

A 61-year-old man from Bridgend has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a "significant" police operation at a retirement housing complex, and remains in custody.

Eleanor, who worked for housing association Valleys to Coast which runs the complex, has been described by her family as the "kindest, most loving, bravest person in the world".

South Wales Police said Eleanor was taken to hospital after officers were called to the crash on Coity Road at about 12:40 BST on Monday, but later died.

Police were also called to nearby sheltered housing retirement complex, Ger-y-Nant, where the man was arrested.

Describing Eleanor, from North Cornelly, Bridgend, her family said: "She meant everything to us and will be forever loved and missed deeply by her devoted family and friends. She was our rock."

Jo Oak, chief executive of Valleys to Coast, added the organisation was "devastated by the tragic death of our colleague".

"Eleanor was a much-valued member of the Valleys to Coast team, and her loss has been deeply felt by everyone who knew and worked alongside her," she said.

"She made an important contribution to our organisation and to the communities we serve, and she will be remembered with great warmth and affection by her colleagues.

"Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with Eleanor's family and friends at this unimaginably difficult time."

Oak said the organisation would "continue to cooperate fully with South Wales Police".

Ch Supt Jason Rees said: "Our thoughts remain firmly with Eleanor's family. I want to assure the community that teams of detectives and specialist staff are investigating.

"We appreciate the patience and support of residents, especially those displaced following the incident. Local communities may notice an increased police presence as our investigation continues."

News.title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review
News.content:
The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.

Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".

She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review. This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.

"I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next â that is the job of education â to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world."

Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.

The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.

Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.

The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.

Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.

The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.

It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters.

The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.

Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.

He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools. This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges. We know that antisemitism crosses all boundaries."

Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.

Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.

"When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras. We have four full-time security staff. And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.

"We think about it a lot."

In response to the recommendations, the government will also encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.

The definition is supported by mainstream Jewish organisations and has been adopted by 47 countries, including the UK, as well as most British universities.

However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.

The Board of Deputies of British Jews said that adopting the IHRA definition would provide schools with a tool "to deepen understanding of contemporary antisemitism".

In a statement, a spokesperson told the BBC: "Treating antisemitism in schools as a safeguarding issue will have the benefit of creating an explicit duty on all schools to address this as they would any other threat to children's safety, and will strengthen accountability."

Rabbi Charley Baginksy and Rabbi Josh Levy, co-leads of the Movement for Progressive Judaism, said that the report "exposes serious failures in how schools recognise and respond to antisemitism".

They said: "Alongside that urgent question of how schools deal with hatred and educate about Jewish persecution, we also need to ensure they teach about Jewish creativity, music, literature, humour and the extraordinary pleasure of belonging to this diverse tradition."

Dan Green, Chief Executive of the Anne Frank Trust UK, said the review "confirms what we see in classrooms every day".

"Antisemitism in our schools is real, it is widespread, and too often it goes unrecognised and unchallenged."

"One-off assemblies are not enough, and neither is sitting pupils in front of a video. Young people need the space to ask difficult questions, challenge their own assumptions and understand that antisemitism did not start or end with the Holocaust."

The National Education Union raised concerns about creating a "hierarchy of racism" and adopting the IHRA definition.

It said the latter risked "blurring the line between antisemitism and legitimate criticism of the Israeli government and the genocide in Gaza".

The union welcomed a "strengthened focus on antisemitism" while underlining that "no form of racism should be minimised".

Recent figures from the Community Security Trust, an organisation which provides security advice and support to the Jewish community, showed a spike in antisemitic incidents at schools.

It found in the first half of 2026 that antisemitism in schools had reached the highest level ever recorded for the first six months of any year.

News.title: Keira Knightley’s awkward memory lapse leaves Bridgerton star Luke Thompson in stitches
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Luke Thompson had to remind Keira Knightley that they were in a film together after the actor forgot about it.

The pair were on the ITV show This Morning to talk about their new West End play, The Lives of Others, when Knightley insisted they had never worked together before.

“Well, do you not remember Misbehaviour?” Thompson turned to ask.

The Pride and Prejudice star took a second to think. “Oh no, you were in Misbehaviour, we have worked together!” she replied.

As they burst out laughing, Knightley tried to explain that it wasn’t entirely her fault for forgetting the Bridgerton star. “But that wasn’t fair, we didn’t really,” she said. “And I was early days pregnant so I don’t remember anything about that film. And he’s suddenly like, ‘You know we’ve worked together before?’ I was like, ‘Really?’”

open image in gallery Luke Thompson had to remind Keira Knightley that they had starred in a film together after the actor completely forgot about it ( YouTube/This Morning )

Thompson offered a little context to help Knightley’s case. “We were in the same film. Different days.”

“And again, I was like, under three months pregnant, so basically just vomiting everywhere, I don’t remember anyone on that film at all,” Knightley explained.

Misbehaviour, directed by Philippa Lowthorpe, is a comedy-drama based on the 1970 Miss World competition in London, when the newly formed Women’s Liberation Movement disrupted the live broadcast to protest against beauty pageants.

The film follows feminist activists Sally Alexander (Knightley) and Jo Robinson (Jessie Buckley) as they plan their protest, and tells the story of Miss Grenada Jennifer Hosten (Gugu Mbatha-Raw) becoming the first black woman to win the title. Thompson plays Peter Hain, the British politician who supports the protest.

open image in gallery Keira Knightley and Gugu Mbatha-Raw in ‘Misbehaviour’ ( Pathe )

Thompson has since become more recognisable as Benedict Bridgerton, the artistic second son of the Bridgerton family. The most recent season of the Netflix period drama follows his romance with Yerin Ha’s Sophie Baek.

He told This Morning that work on the fifth season had just been completed and “gone well”. “Now it will be about Francesca and Michaela but, obviously, Benedict is still around,” he said, referring to the sixth Bridgerton sibling’s romance with her late husband’s cousin Michaela Stirling.

Knightley is returning to Netflix with the second season of Black Doves, the spy thriller in which she plays Helen Webb, an undercover operative leading a double life as the wife of a politician. “It’s nice,” she said during the interview. “You’re a mum at home and then you get to go to work and be like, ‘Right. I get to beat everyone up, this is great!’”

open image in gallery The most recent season of the Netflix period drama follows Luke Thompson’s character romance with Yerin Ha’s Sophie Baek ( LIAM DANIEL/NETFLIX )

The Lives of Others is an adaptation of the Oscar-winning 2007 German film directed and adapted by Olivier Award-winner Robert Icke. The production also stars Stephen Dillane, best known for playing Stannis Baratheon in Game of Thrones.

Set in East Germany in 1984, the play follows playwright Georg Dreyman (Thompson) and his partner, actress Christa-Maria Sieland (Knightley), who are under surveillance by the Stasi, the country’s secret police. Dillane plays Gerd Wiesler, the officer assigned to monitor the couple whose observations begin to change his own perspective.

Asked whether the pair would try to trip each other up during performances, Thompson suggested they were already doing a fairly good job of that without any deliberate mischief.

“I think we already are. We’re trying to not trip ourselves up at the moment,” he said.

Knightley described the backstage scramble to make it on stage at the right moment, with the right costume and the right props. “There is lots of running around backstage trying to come in the right entrances and exits,” she said.

The Lives of Others is running at London’s Adelphi Theatre until 9 January 2027.

News.title: England are heavy favourites against France but must avoid ‘tripping up’ in pursuit of World Cup lifeline
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Just one game into the 2026 Rugby League World Cup and England are facing the prospect of an early exit. That’s how it goes sometimes.

Progression to the semi-final stage of the World Cup is now out of their hands due to a 30-12 loss to Tonga in their opening game and it leaves them vulnerable to being dumped out of the tournament even if they were to win their two remaining group matches.

That is down to the structure of the pools with Group B and Group C both featuring three teams but being collected as one full table of six. The teams in Group B (England, Samoa and Lebanon) each play the teams in Group C (Tonga, France and Papa New Guinea).

Samoa’s 78-4 hammering of France means that England need Tonga to beat them heavily and that they can then score more points than Samoa at the end of the three group games.

open image in gallery England were impressive in patches against Tonga but face an uphill battle to qualify for the semi-finals ( Getty )

open image in gallery AJ Brimson scored for England against Tonga despite eventually losing 30-12 ( Getty )

It leaves England head coach, Brian McDermott, in a tough spot. He must encourage constant attacking threat without leaving England vulnerable to being beaten. That’s not the most practical of positions to find yourself in.

Analysing the performance against Tonga and it’s clear that England made too many ball-handling errors and couldn’t capitalise at the end of sets. Still, there was encouragement to be found in England’s opening display with McDermott pleased at how his team played the type of style he wants to see.

“On occasions, I think we opened up in that first 20 and whether we went through the middle or went through the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position. We had some scrappy finishes to those good ball sets,” McDermott said.

“We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga and credit to Tonga as well. I thought they were terrific defensively in terms of breaching their line and cracking their line open. I thought we did that two or three times in that first half, but they came up with some try-saving tackles.

“The fact that we didn't score on the try-line doesn’t suggest that our game plan needs to change. We’ve just got to be more patient and knock off the ball as much as we can.”

McDermott’s comments would suggest a similar modus operandi for Saturday’s crunch clash against France. England had a clear plan against Tonga, which was to utilise second phase play and offload the ball. That created space and opportunity for them, but they struggled and lacked creativity inside the final 20 metres. A similar tactic, with fewer errors and more invention near the try line could be the key to striking gold asking a hurting French team.

France conceded 14 times against Samoa who, for most of the game, seemed far quicker and more able to physically assert themselves. France’s head coach Laurent Frayssinous reasoned afterwards that those differences were because Samoa’s players hail mostly from the NRL which he described as a “step up” from Super League where most of the French players ply their trade.

“The NRL keeps growing and keeps getting better every year,” Frayssinous said. “Watching NRL every year, it's at the top, at the top, at the top. A step up, step up, step up.

“Super League is [getting] better every year, but not as fast as the NRL. The smartness, the skill the guys have under pressure, the touches, week in, week out, that’s something we need to improve in Super League, simple as that.”

So how will France fare against an England squad also populated by Super League stars?

open image in gallery Samoa ran in 14 tries as they hammered France 78-4 in their World Cup opener ( Getty )

open image in gallery France struggled to keep Samoa at bay but can they improve against England on Saturday ( Getty )

Well, history is not on their side and recent matches have heavily swayed in favour of McDermott’s men with England securing a 40-8 victory away from home in 2024, a 64-0 win in 2023 and a 42-18 triumph when the two sides met at the 2022 World Cup.

That puts them as overwhelming favourites to win but the necessity to also accumulate a huge score and present themselves with World Cup lifeline could be see them overplay their hand. That is something McDermott has warned against.

“We know what’s in front of us now. We’ve got to win the next two games. We’ve got to improve on the things that we need to improve upon,” McDermott explained.

“I've just been said about not chasing points and not chasing scoreboards. We certainly don't want to trip ourselves up.”

England face France in Perth on Saturday 24 October with kick off at 7.35am GST.

News.title: Champions League power rankings: PSG remain top – but at what cost? Man United tumble
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Matchday three of the Champions League brought two battles of the heavyweights, but what did we learn from the early meetings between title contenders?

Paris Saint-Germain delivered a statement of their ambitions of winning a third consecutive European crown by inflicting a first defeat of the season on in-form Barcelona, but could be without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the remainder of their campaign after the star winger ruptured his ACL.

Arsenal rescued a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in an entertaining meeting of the champions of England and Germany, suggesting both could be bound for the latter stages of the competition once again, while Real Madrid, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Real Betis joined PSG in making it three wins from three.

Things got a whole lot worse for Manchester United, though, as Michael Carrick’s side stumbled to a 4-1 hammering at Champions League debutants Como in one of their heaviest-ever European defeats.

We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season.

Agree or disagree with our standings? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain

Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City, 4-2 v Barcelona

Fixtures: Villarreal (a), Roma (h), Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h)

Still the team to beat in the Champions League, but at what cost? PSG’s win over Barcelona came with the huge blow of losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured ACL. The Georgian winger was named the Champions League player of the season last campaign as PSG defended their crown but he faces a significant lay-off and may not play again this season, while Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos are likely to miss the next several weeks due to thigh injuries suffered in the same match. Kvaratskhelia scored 10 goals and assisted six in last season’s Champions League and Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions will not carry the same threat without him. PSG’s summer recruits Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts are now set to play an even greater role this season following the sale of Bradley Barcola to Liverpool.

open image in gallery Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s ACL injury took the shine off PSG’s win over Barcelona ( Getty )

↔️ 2. Barcelona

Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray, 2-4 v PSG

Fixtures: Aston Villa (h), Sabah (a), Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h)

Barcelona’s 11-match winning streak to start the season came to a halt at the Parc des Princes and raised the question that could well define their season in the Champions League. We know about their goalscoring – Hansi Flick’s side reached 50 in just 12 games this season – and the quality of their forward line led by Lamine Yamal and Raphinha. But whether the defence holds up come the knockout stages is another question. Conceding four against PSG, despite going into the 80th minute level with the hosts in Paris, suggests there is work to do against the very elite before Barcelona can think about winning a first Champions League crown since 2015.

open image in gallery Lamine Yamal scored a stunning individual goal in the Parc des Princes as Barcelona lost 4-2 ( AP )

↔️ 3. Arsenal

Results: 1-0 vs Napoli, 3-0 v Lille, 2-2 v Bayern Munich

Fixtures: Slavia Prague (a), Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h)

An entertaining draw at Bayern Munich, who have such a strong home record, gave a good account of whether Mikel Arteta’s side can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League. This has been a typically assured start from last season’s runners-up, who are determined to go one better after their heartbreaking defeat on penalties to PSG. Arsenal’s squad depth means the Gunners have a very good chance of finishing one of the top two spots in this season’s group phase but if there’s one area where Arteta’s side are short it’s attack, so Bukayo Saka’s injury is a further worry.

open image in gallery Declan Rice grabbed Arsenal’s late equaliser at the Allianz ( AP )

⬆️ 🟢 4. Bayern Munich

Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt, 3-3 v Viking, 2-2 v Arsenal

Fixtures: Atletico Madrid (a), Lille (a), Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h)

WIthout Michael Olise, Jamal Musiala and Luis Dias from the start against Arsenal, Harry Kane gave a timely reminder of his Ballon d’Or credentials as he produced a sublime all-round attacking display in the 2-2 draw at the Allianz. Certainly, if Kane continues his astonishing rate of goalscoring then Bayern will be there or thereabouts.

open image in gallery Harry Kane has now scored in 10 consecutive Champions League matches ( Getty )

⬇️ 🔴 5. Man City (-1 from 4)

Results: 2-0 v Porto, 2-4 v PSG, 5-1 v AEK Athens

Fixtures: Leipzig (a), Napoli (h), Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a)

No one knows what Manchester City’s season from here is going to look like. Could the Champions League become their top target if they are ruled out of the Premier League title race, for instance? No one knows. Still, there is quality and spirit throughout the team – as shown in a strong start domestically and in the second half of their 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

open image in gallery Phil Foden scored a hat-trick in the 5-1 win over AEK Athens ( AP )

↔️ 6. Real Madrid

Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan, 4-3 v Roma, 4-1 v RB Leipzig

Fixtures: AEK Athens (a), PSV (h), Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a)

Performances remain unconvincing but Real Madrid continue to find a way in the Champions League, with a couple of belting goals from Kylian Mbappe and Yann Diomande lighting up the 4-1 win over RB Leipzig. Somehow with maximum points, despite trailing Roma 3-1 at the Stadio Olimpico, and Inter and Leipzig spurning chances to take the lead at the Bernabeu, the 15-time Champions League winners still carry an aura in this competition and have so far offered a bit of a throwback to the days of Carlo Ancelotti.

open image in gallery Real Madrid are one of five teams with three wins from three ( Reuters )

↔️ 7. Liverpool

Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid, 6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal

Fixtures: Fenerbahce (a), Club Brugge (a), Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h)

Still sitting outside the top tier of contenders, you’d have to say it would be a surprise for Liverpool (or any of the teams below the Reds in these rankings) to win the Champions League in their first season under Andoni Iraola. But it has been a fine start in Europe for the Basque, with three consecutive wins to start the Champions League while managing to rotate his squad successfully. Alexis Mac Allister has been the star with key interventions against Atletico and Villarreal, but the likes of Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and Lewis Koumas have also benefited from Iraola’s rotation. The knockout rounds, where Liverpool have been knocked out by PSG in the last two seasons, already beckons.

open image in gallery Rio Ngumoha starred in Liverpool’s 4-3 win over Villarreal ( PA )

↔️ 8. Atletico Madrid

Results: 1-2 v Liverpool, 2-0 v Manchester United, 1-1 v Stuttgart

Fixtures: Bayern Munich (h), Viking (h), PSV (a), Bodo/Glimt (a), Fenerbahce (h)

Last season’s semi-finalists have the added motivation of hosting this season’s Champions League final at the Metropolitano in Madrid. Following the opening defeat at Anfield, Diego Simeone’s side clicked into form with six consecutive victories in all competitions until they were held to a 1-1 draw at Stuttgart. While it would be another colossal overachievement from Simeone to get Atleti into a third Champions League final of his 16-year reign, his side were impressive in beating Manchester United. You know what you’re going to get from a Simeone side in the Champions League but Alex Baena and Pablo Barrios have also added a touch of class into midfield, too.

open image in gallery Julian Alvarez was back among the goals in 10-man Atletico’s 1-1 draw at Stuttgart ( AP )

Results: 3-2 v Club Brugge, 6-0 v Fenerbahce, 3-1 v Viking

Fixtures: Barcelona (a), Galatasaray (a), PSG (h), Borussia Dortmund (h), Slavia Prague (a)

Unai Emery’s new-look Aston Villa side are finding their home and may have secured their qualification for the knockout stages already, ahead of a tough fixture list and games against Barcelona and PSG. Bright showings from the refreshed attacking line-up of Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson led to convincing Villa Park wins over Fenerbahce and Viking, with the Europa League winners retaining their identity under Emery despite the huge squad turnover in the summer.

After starting with back-to-back defeats, how badly Inter needed their late win over Shakhtar, which came after Alessandro Bastoni’s daft red card. News.title: Government urged to approve Rosebank oil and gas field after Jackdaw go-ahead
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Government has been urged to approve the Rosebank oil and gas field after Jackdaw was given the go-ahead on Wednesday.

Gas from the Jackdaw field will start flowing within weeks after Energy Security and Net Zero Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh backed the scheme.

She has now been urged to approve Rosebank, the largest untapped oil field in the North Sea, as a further sign of commitment to production.

The UK Government has approved plans to begin drilling in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea.

It comes as The Guardian and The Times reported that Ms Fahnbulleh is leaning towards rejecting Rosebank.

A Department for Energy Security and Net Zero spokesperson said it was “speculation”.

“As the Energy Secretary has said, each project will be assessed on its own merits,” the spokesperson added.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch called for Labour to repeal its ban on all new oil and gas licences.

“We have the resources, the expertise and the people,” she said.

“What we have lost is the confidence to make tough decisions.”

open image in gallery (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

US President Donald Trump, who has called for more drilling, said the UK should now go “full blast” in exploiting North Sea resources.

Responding to the news, Mr Trump said: “Great news for the wealth and prosperity of the United Kingdom, and the wonderful region of Aberdeen.

“The UK has started drilling in the North Sea, one of the greatest and most prosperous areas of OIL in the World.

“They should go FULL BLAST!!! This will make the UK very wealthy again. TAKE DOWN THE COSTLY AND RIDICULOUS WINDMILLS!”

The chief executive of Adura, the joint venture between Shell and Norway’s Equinor which is behind both schemes, also called for Rosebank to be approved.

open image in gallery Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh during a visit to Shell UK’s St Fergus Gas Terminal in Peterhead, Aberdeenshire on Wednesday (Paul Reid/PA) ( PA Wire )

Neil McCulloch said: “Jackdaw represents a significant prize in its own right: £2.1 billion of investment and enough gas to heat the equivalent of around 1.4 million UK homes at peak production.

“Our attention now turns to Rosebank.

“It follows Jackdaw in the regulatory process, but the case for approval is equally strong.

“We believe that applying the same rigorous, evidence-based approach can lead to a similarly positive decision.”

Approving Jackdaw has been sharply criticised by environmental campaigners who want to accelerate the shift away from fossil fuels.

Mr Burnham said the Government was taking a “pragmatic approach” to the North Sea but remained “committed to moving towards renewable energy” and reaching net zero emissions by 2050.

The approval of Jackdaw is expected to increase domestic gas production by around 6% at its peak, safeguard hundreds of jobs and provide an estimated £2.9 billion economic boost.

News.title: Sacha Baron Cohen defends reviving ‘problematic’ Ali G character: ‘That’s the reason I resurrected him’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Sacha Baron Cohen has defended bringing his comedic creation Ali G back for a new film after after 12 years, explaining that him being “outdated and problematic” is exactly why he’s needed today.

The comedian, who debuted Ali G on Channel 4’s The 11 O’Clock Show in 1998, is reprising the role in forthcoming film, Ali G: Who Iz I? , which arrives in cinemas later this week.

However, there have been calls to boycott the new film, with some considering Ali G – a stereotype of white, middle-class young men who adopt British Jamaican and hip-hop culture – to be an offensive character.

Responding to the controversy surrounding Ali G, Cohen defended his character in an essay for Time magazine, explaining that he has always intended his characters and comedy to “expose prejudice, bias and stupidity, though I realise not everyone sees them that way”.

open image in gallery Morgana Robinson and Sacha Baron Cohen in 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' ( PA )

“Ali G is a white imbecile – a delusional cultural appropriator – who steals the fashion and lyrics from his favorite gangsta rap and dancehall idols, from Compton to Kingston,” he wrote in a piece published on Tuesday (20 October).

“The joke is on him, and on the predominantly white male establishment who take him seriously enough to believe that HBO would hire the stupidest man in the world as an interview host. Like a good bouffon, he undermines that establishment—not the culture he loves and borrows from.”

“So why does my new movie bring back that phony and unfunny guy, which some have criticised as ‘microwaving a relic from a generation ago?’” he continued. “The fact that Ali G is outdated and problematic is the very reason I resurrected him.”

Cohen, who is also known for satirical characters by Kazakhstani TV presenter Borat, Australian fashion reporter Brüno and fictional dictator Admiral General Aladeen, added that the world that Ali G has returned to is “in many ways, worse than the one he left 20 years ago”.

“All the prejudices my characters are designed to expose haven’t just lingered – they’ve metastasized. They’re fueled by the greatest propaganda machine in history – social media – and now by its monstrous child, AI.”

Citing how political violence is on the rise, there’s been an “explosion of misogyny” and “intolerance and extremism have surged”, he hopes his new film will “sound the alarm”.

open image in gallery Cohen originated the role in 1998 ( Getty )

“It can remind people about the very real dangers of ludicrous lies – whether spread by a thin-­skinned authoritarian or an extremist with an online following. With the US midterm elections just weeks away, perhaps it encourages citizens to mobilise against these dangerous falsehoods – at the ballot box and beyond.”

Earlier this year, British news comparison site NewsCord launched a campaign calling for cinemas to boycott Ali G: Who Iz I?, claiming that 37,658 emails had been sent in support of it.

“Black British comedians called the character 'an alibi for racism' in 2000; Jeanette Winterson asked what separates it from the Black and White Minstrels; Kazakh and Arab organisations documented the harm of the catalogue behind it. Sony Pictures UK is selling it with the line ‘He iz back. We ain't liable,’” they wrote.

Cohen finished filming the Ali G follow-up in July this year, having filmed much of it in secret. It is also set to star comedian Morgana Robinson as Ali G’s girlfriend Julie and will mark Cohen’s directorial debut.

News.title: Tourist killed by roof debris while touring Frank Lloyd Wright's winter home
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A visitor from Brazil who was touring the Arizona desert home of famed architect Frank Lloyd Wright has died after he was hit by a piece of roof that blew off in high winds.

Witnesses say Rogério Renato Mateucci, 55, was struck on the head and died instantly Friday, according to police in Scottsdale, east of Phoenix.

Wind gusts of up to 38 mph (61 kph) were recorded at the Scottsdale Airport that day, according to the National Weather Service.

The designated UNESCO World Heritage site remained temporarily closed to the public on Wednesday.

The 1937 home and surrounding compound, called Taliesin West, have low-slung roofs and rock walls that appear to blend into the surrounding desert.

The property, which served as Wright's winter home as well as a “desert laboratory” for his students, draws up to 100,000 visitors a year, according to the Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation, its owner.

open image in gallery Frank Lloyd Wright House ( AP )

The foundation said in a statement following Mateucci's death that the property was closed to the public “until further notice.”

“The Foundation extends its deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of the individual who died Friday, October 16, following an accident at Taliesin West in Scottsdale, Arizona.

“The Scottsdale Police Department is aware of the incident, and no further details will be shared out of respect for privacy and to allow officials to complete their work.”

Sgt. Allison Sempsis, a Scottsdale police spokesperson, said the investigation doesn’t prevent the site from reopening.

A foundation spokesperson did not respond to an email Wednesday asking when tours would resume.

Mateucci worked as the senior administrator at the Pontifical Catholic University of Paraná, located in the Brazilian city of Curitiba. In a statement, the school said he was its rector and a lay member of the Catholic order of Marist priests and brothers. He was from the city of São Paulo.

The school said Mateucci was visiting the U.S. to attend an international program at Arizona State University.

News.title: Taiwan cancels over 100 flights as Super Typhoon Champi churns towards island with 140mph winds
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The strongest storm of the year weakened slightly on Thursday as it barrelled towards the Philippines, Taiwan, and China.

Super Typhoon Champi is now the equivalent of a Category 5 hurricane with maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 185mph, according to the US National Weather Service.

The typhoon was moving west-northwest across the Philippine Sea with sustained winds of 175mph on Wednesday evening.

It was expected to lose strength after turning northwest through Thursday but still remain “extremely powerful”, with typhoon-force winds extending up to 100 miles (160km) from its centre.

Champi developed into a tropical storm last week before rapidly strengthening to the equivalent of a Category 4 hurricane in less than 48 hours.

It swept northwest across the Pacific Ocean, passing within 10 miles (16km) of the US territory of Guam on Saturday.

The storm first attained the intensity of a Category 5 hurricane on 17 October, about six hours after passing Guam, with sustained winds of around 165mph. It subsequently weakened before regaining Category 5 intensity the following day. Now, it’s at the same intensity for the third time.

open image in gallery ( windy.com )

Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration issued a sea and land warning as Champi was expected to hit the island the hardest, on Friday and Saturday.

The storm is ⁠currently almost 250km ​southeast ⁠of Taiwan's northeastern county of Yilan, the CWA said. Its track shows it passing northeastern Taiwan, turning north towards the ⁠Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan.

The warnings are expected to be lifted on Saturday afternoon after the storm is projected to move away from Taiwan and towards Japan’s Kyushu island, according to forecaster Chang cheng-Chuan.

Airlines cancelled nearly 125 flights for Thursday, the transport ministry said, but the rail network was so far unaffected. The interior ministry said no area had been evacuated yet.

Authorities suspended ferry services and closed many tourist attractions as they stepped up disaster preparations. They also deployed additional water pumps in flood-prone areas and ordered checks of drainage systems and flood-control equipment.

President Lai Ching-te called for the public to get ready for the typhoon without delay and avoid going to ‌the mountains or the coast.

open image in gallery The eye of Champi swirls over the Philippine Sea on 21 October 2026 ( Reuters )

In eastern China, authorities are planning evacuations and urging residents in the path of the typhoon to prepare.

Although the Philippines and Taiwan did not predict a landfall, China’s National Meteorological Centre said Champi was expected to make landfall on the eastern coast of Taiwan around Saturday and again in the Chinese province of Fujian as a severe tropical storm.

The forecaster issued a blue typhoon warning for Champi, the lowest level in China’s four-tier system. But local authorities still drew up emergency evacuation plans for vulnerable communities in eastern Zhejiang province.

Champi was named Super Typhoon Rosal in the Philippines, becoming the Southeast Asian country’s 18th tropical cyclone of 2026.

The Philippine weather agency PAGASA said on Thursday the storm's centre was around 400km east of Basco, Batanes, in the northern Philippines.

It issued a warning for waves rising up to 12m along the northern and eastern coasts of Batanes and 9m around the Babuyan Islands.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there can only be one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

News.title: Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match
News.content:
There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

News.title: Ebola case confirmed in Nigeria as outbreak spreads through Africa
News.content:
African ministers have been called to an urgent health summit after Nigeria confirmed its first case in the outbreak of the deadly Ebola fever tearing through eastern Congo.

Confirmation of a case in Africa’s most populous nation came days after a cluster was detected in Kenya and has heightened questions about border screening checks designed to stop the virus spreading from its epicentre in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

With cases now found in West Africa, Central Africa and East Africa, the epidemic “has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the continent’s main public health body.

DRC has recorded close to 10,000 cases since an outbreak began in mid-May, with around half of them dying of the haemorrhagic fever.

The Nigeria case meant “Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa,” warned Dr Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

“The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level,” he said, convening an online summit for next week.

News.title: One billion children at risk from heatwaves, WHO warns
News.content:
More than one billion children are exposed to increasingly severe heat waves, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

1.5 billion children under one experienced a fivefold increase in the number of heat wave days in 2024 compared with the 1986 to 2005 baseline period, jumping from roughly four days per year to a high of over 20, says the health agency. And these periods of high temperature are becoming longer, more frequent and more severe, the WHO warns.

According to the Met Office, this summer was the hottest on record in the UK, with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Europe also saw record-breaking temperatures, and Asia and Africa both experienced their warmest July on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

Four UN agencies, including the WHO, the WMO, Unicef and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), have urged countries to monitor how extreme heat affects pregnant women, newborns and children.

The new framework tracks preterm birth, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health facility visits.

“Heat is already affecting our most vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, newborns and children. But what health systems do not count, they cannot respond to,” said Dr Pascale Allotey, director of WHO’s department of maternal and child health.

“By tracking outcomes such as preterm birth, child deaths and illnesses, and health-facility visits alongside heat exposure, countries can identify potential impacts and take action to protect women and children,” she said.

High temperatures are particularly dangerous for pregnant women because the body has to work much harder to cool both the mother and the baby.

Intense heat can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can restrict blood flow to the placenta and reduce the amount of oxygen and nutrients that reach the foetus. Heat can also put strain on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The odds of a preterm birth also increase by 26 per cent during heatwaves: for every one degree rise in heat exposure, the likelihood of giving birth early rise by roughly 4 per cent, according to a systematic review published in Nature Medicine.

The WHO has also urged countries to develop and implement tailored heat-health action plans that account for the needs of pregnant women, newborns and children, as well as strengthening early-warning systems to ensure timely action to heat risks, such as alert systems and personalised public messaging.

“As our world continues to heat up, it creates new risks for health, and older people, pregnant women, newborns and children are among those least able to escape them,” said Bruce Gordon, director of environment and climate change at the WHO.

“Our health systems need the data to recognise this reality and take action – from protecting people during heatwaves to embedding climate risk consideration into everyday health services,” he said.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Rio Ngumoha dazzles on coming-of-age night in Europe
News.content:
Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

News.title: Inflation jumps in run-up to Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
Inflation has jumped to its highest level in almost a year, underlining the challenges facing John Healey, the Chancellor, ahead of his first Budget next week.

The consumer prices index climbed from 3.1pc in August to 3.5pc in September, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

Inflation was ahead of the 3.4pc predicted by economists and is now at its highest level since October 2025.

The sharp rise was driven by soaring fuel costs as a result of the Iran war. The ONS said average petrol prices rose by 8.2p a litre in September and diesel by 10.7p. Both reached levels not seen since 2022, in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, said: “Rising inflation is turning the Budget into a perilous high-wire act for the Chancellor, increasing pressure for cost-of-living support while pushing up government borrowing costs, which is shrinking fiscal headroom and narrowing his policy options.”

Britain spent more money on debt interest last month than in any September on record, official figures show.

The UK’s debt servicing costs rose to £10.9bn in September, the highest total for the month since at least 1997, according to the ONS.

This burden helped to push national debt above £3 trillion for the first time.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said the unhappy milestone and the rise in inflation “show Labour has lost control of the economy”.

Public sector net debt has soared by 50pc since it first exceeded £2tn in June 2020.

Mr Healey insisted the British economy still had “momentum” and pointed to Wednesday morning’s approval of new drilling for gas in the North Sea as evidence of this.

He said: “We know that price rises from conflicts in the Middle East and Europe are hitting Britain and countries worldwide. Last week, the IMF said our UK fiscal discipline stands out with the lowest forecast deficit in the G7 by 2029.

“And today we’ve given the green light to getting North Sea gas from the Jackdaw field, investing the revenues in our clean energy future and supporting British workers.

“In my Budget next week, I will keep up this momentum. Maintaining our fiscal discipline and drive for growth in every postcode, while giving businesses and families some breathing space.”

September’s inflation figure is used for the annual uprating of welfare payments, with the state pension now in line to rise by almost £500 next year.

The figure is also used to calculate increases in business rates in England, with pubs, shops, offices and other hospitality businesses now facing a £1.1bn increase in the collective bill from April, according to tax firm Ryan.

News.title: England dealt harsh lesson in Pakistan collapse
News.content:
Brendon McCullum wants his team to learn how to adapt as they prepare for the World Cup and this was a lesson in how not to master a run chase.

Failing to overhaul 302 is not an embarrassment, but the way England threw away a good start with some brittle batting gives McCullum plenty to ponder.

Spin exposed familiar failings as left-armer Arafat Minhas added six for 40 to his 59 from 58 with the bat, but it was also short balls from the seamers that hurt England. A two-paced pitch made the back-of-a-length delivery tricky, as it had in the match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan on the same ground at the weekend, but England failed to find a way to adjust their tempo.

Ben Duckett, Joe Root and Sam Curran were all dismissed by seamers hitting the pitch hard and forcing them to play square while Arafat exposed limitations against spin. He bowled Harry Brook for five with a beauty that dipped and straightened as he mixed up his arm ball with consistent accuracy to deadly effect.

Sports.title: Can McLaren 'up their game' to respond to Red Bull threat?
Sports.content:
McLaren will introduce further upgrades at the United States Grand Prix as they bid to improve their car's performance and stave off a resurgent Red Bull in the standings over the remainder of the season.

The reigning world champions continue to sit third in the Constructors' Championship with six rounds to go but fell into the clutches of fourth-placed Red Bull over the first of the end-of-season triple headers.

While McLaren failed to score a podium across that run of races, Red Bull claimed four top-three finishes - including two wins for Max Verstappen - to cut what had been a 76-point deficit to their rivals to just seven points.

McLaren's official pre-Austin preview described the team's results over the last three events as falling "significantly short of expectations" and that their 33-point haul in that run was "significantly lower than anticipated".

McLaren now head to a Circuit of the Americas track in Austin this weekend that they are hoping will be more suited to the strengths of their car, which will be boosted by some further revisions.

Rob Marshall, McLaren's chief technical officer, said: "We're bringing a modest selection of upgrades for this event, aimed at improving some braking reliability and performance issues. We also have some small floor changes to test.

"We have all seen how difficult it is to predict the relative performance of the top teams over the last five or six races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fascinating insight into McLaren's communication between pit wall in Baku and McLaren's Technology Centre in Woking.

"Obviously, there are many factors in play here: cars being upgraded, cars suiting and drivers liking certain circuits among other factors. The last few races have not been great for us, but I think we're getting stronger again and Austin is probably a better circuit for our car.

"Practice will be important for correlating what we've seen in our development tools with the track.

"We are still learning how best to extract performance from this car. We have the full range of corner types here so getting the best balance for the whole lap will be our main focus."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McLaren team principal Andrea Stella reacts to the Sprint collision between Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri at the Singapore Grand Prix.

'They need to up their game'

McLaren's cause in Singapore was not helped by them losing eight points on the final lap of the Sprint when their cars collided after Lando Norris attempted an overtake on Oscar Piastri. Norris later apologised for the accident, admitting it was ill-advised move on his team-mate at such a late stage of the short-form race.

The world champion said in the team's Austin preview that "I take responsibility for my mistakes, and I learn from them".

McLaren now return to the scene of a previous high-profile incident in Austin from 2025, when both their drivers crashed out on the first lap of the Sprint in a chain reaction set off by Piastri colliding with Nico Hulkenberg, and have little room for any similar missed opportunities 12 months on.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris collide on the first corner after dramatic multi-car contact which forces both McLarens to retire at the US Grand Prix Sprint race!

Speaking on the post-Singapore GP edition of The F1 Show podcast, Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins said: "McLaren have had a few incidents through the year where they have not maximised their points.

"[In Singapore] Max Verstappen maximised the result, McLaren did not and there have been several weekends where McLaren did not maximise the result. This accident [in the Sprint] was a silly example of it.

"Arguably, I think if Hadjar hadn't missed three races when Liam Lawson was in that car Red Bull would be ahead of McLaren. And that's what McLaren know, that they have been saved I think, at this stage, because Hadjar wasn't in that car for three races and [Red Bull] weren't scoring the points that they could have done.

Image: McLaren have won the Constructors' Championship in each of the past two seasons but are in danger of finishing fourth this year

"But now Red Bull are on the up and they need to up their game if they are going to survive in that P3 position because it doesn't look like it at the moment."

Karun Chandhok added: "I think they probably know they now have the fourth-fastest car, which is a bit of a concern, and Red Bull are probably now the fastest if not second-fastest car for most tracks."

Sports.title: Alysson stars as Villa beat Viking to make it three wins from three in Europe
Sports.content:
Aston Villa made it three wins from three in the Champions League with a 3-1 win over Viking at Villa Park.

Ross Barkley headed Unai Emery's side in front midway through the first half and Emiliano Buendia's penalty made it two before the break. Alysson's run led to an own goal for the third with only Peter Christiansen's late volley taking Villa off top spot.

Bayern Munich struggled against the Norwegian champions last week but Villa were in control from the start despite a makeshift look to the side with Joao Gomes at right-back. The Brazilian had a cross deflected against the underside of the bar early in the game.

Image: Ross Barkley celebrates scoring Aston Villa's opening goal against Viking

Ibrahim Mbaye's corner from the other flank was nodded in by Barkley soon after before Buendia came close with two good headed chances. The Argentine made amends from the penalty spot when a VAR check ruled that Alysson had been clipped inside the box.

The young winger was the best player on the pitch, producing surely his best performance in a Villa shirt. He was instrumental in the third goal too, racing through from deep. Henrik Heggheim could only divert his cross past his own goalkeeper.

That was the goal that took Villa into top spot in this league phase. The crowd knew it too, chanting 'We are top of the league' afterwards. But Peter Christiansen's brilliant late volley - awarded after a VAR check - dropped them back to second behind PSG.

The tifo unveiled in the Holte End before kick-off pointed out that Villa have conquered before and are prepared for more. There are more fancied sides in this Champions League but few boast the clarity of purpose that Emery brings. Villa are building again.

Aston Villa's win in stats

Aston Villa are the second quickest team to record 20 wins in the European Cup (30 matches), behind only Real Madrid (29 matches).

Villa have won each of their last 12 major European home games, the joint-longest run by an English team this century.

Villa are the first Europa League holders to win their first three games of a Champions League campaign since Manchester United in 2017.

Buendia: Alysson was incredible

Emiliano Buendia speaking about Alysson to TNT Sports:

"He was incredible. He's showing his potential, his ability on the wing. Also Ibrahim Mbaye as well - their speed, their qualities. It's going to help the team a lot, so it's very important to have them and to try to help them to improve because they are young talents."

Emery: Some players did a step forward

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking in the press conference:

"We are delighted how we are responding in our demands, respecting the competition of the Champions League and respecting the opponent, and how we are improving things. Through those issues I think we played a good match, collectively, tactically, respecting them, following the plan we set on.

"Then, individually, the players showed their qualities. I think we did a good job and some players did a step forward in their confidence, feeling better, understanding everything tactically and playing their football."

Emery likely had his wingers in mind. When asked about Mbaye and Alysson, he replied: "It was a step forward for both players in our idea, so really happy." There was praise too for Alejandro Garnacho who "played his best minutes" in a late cameo off the bench.

Viking boss: They were all over us

Viking head coach Morten Jensen speaking in the press conference:

"The second half was much more like Viking wants to be. Maybe we had too much respect in the first half, they were all over us and we did not create much offensively, which is rare for Viking.

"I think we did a much better job by asking questions of Villa's midfield and their defence and ended up drawing the second half. That is something that we can build on for the future.

"It is the next level for us as a team and really great to see the team get a goal at Villa Park in front of over 2,000 Norwegian fans."

Image: Emi Buendia doubled Aston Villa's lead over Viking from the penalty spot

37 - GOAL! Buendia made it two from the penalty spot

62 - OWN GOAL! Heggheim turned in Alysson's cross

84 - GOAL! Christiansen's volley brings consolation

Sports.title: Fernandes criticises coaches, Carrick criticises players - but who was to blame?
Sports.content:
Who was to blame for Manchester United's miserable 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League?

Bruno Fernandes criticised the tactical plan of the Man Utd coaches.

Michael Carrick questioned the motivation of his players.

If only Man Utd's performance on the pitch in Italy was as forceful as the post-match interviews.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan reacts to Manchester United's embarrassing Champions League loss at Como

After losing at Atletico Madrid last time out in the Champions League, Lisandro Martinez hit out at the club's hierarchy, calling out technical director Jason Wilcox for failings in the transfer window.

This time captain Fernandes took aim at the club's coaching staff in a stinging take-down of their pressing plan.

Image: Bruno Fernandes during Man Utd's defeat to Como

Asked by TNT Sports about a lack of cohesion in United's work out of possession, Fernandes defended his team-mates and put the blame on Carrick and his coaches.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," he said.

Free pass? Como rack up big numbers vs Man Utd Como completed 594 passes, the most by a team in a Champions League game against Manchester United since Barcelona in April 2019 (725).

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

Was that tactical idea what cost Man Utd in Como? "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me," said Fernandes.
