"I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable - as they did to us."

A meeting between Carrick, Martinez and Wilcox repaired relations after the centre-back's comments in Madrid. But Carrick gave a blunt response in his post-match press conference on Wednesday when Fernandes' thoughts were put to him.

"We half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that," he said. "Whatever tactics you play, if you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson criticised Manchester United after they were thrashed 4-1 in the Champions League by Como

'Angry' Carrick: You can't choose when to give absolutely everything

Carrick is usually measured in front of the media but he made his feelings clear after the club's winless run stretched to seven games with this loss.

"I'm really angry," he said. "For us to play in that way is not acceptable."

Man Utd caught out early - again Manchester United are the first English team ever to concede inside the opening two minutes of back-to-back major European games (47 seconds vs Atletico Madrid, 118 seconds vs Como).

For all United did wrong in the game, it was the application of his players which was prominent in his post-match assessment.

"I'll definitely look at what we've done [as a coaching staff] or if it's the motivation and the intention and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football you have to bring," he said. "We didn't bring that today.

"You can't turn it on and off and you can't choose when you want to perform or when you don't want to perform or when you give absolutely everything or when you maybe don't," he told TNT Sports.

Manchester United

Bournemouth Sunday 25th October 12:30pm Kick off 2:00pm

Carrick, who apologised after the game to United's travelling support, later added in his press conference: "It wasn't just the goals. It was the manner we went about that was the difficult thing to watch. It's not about me right now. The results can come and go, but you've got to do it in a certain way. That wasn't it."

It's now two defeats in three Champions League games this season. Fernandes, Carrick and United will have to show the solutions to their problems at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, if their winless streak is to end in the Premier League this weekend.

Sports.title: Miserable Man Utd ripped apart by Como
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's Manchester United were ripped apart in a dreadful 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League, as their miserable run of results stretched to seven without a win.

The pressure continues to pile on Carrick and this United side as their start to the season lurches from bad to worse - and on Wednesday night they were humbled by a Como team that delivered more intensity and quality in Italy.

The first attribute should be a non-negotiable but, despite United's application being in the spotlight, they were once again outworked by their opposition. Static in midfield, allowing Como players to run off them, losing markers... this was a shocking show of United's big failings out of possession.

The tone was set just two minutes in when Man Utd went behind early on - again. They are the first English side to concede in back-to-back Champions League games so soon and never got to grips with Cesc Fabregas' impressively coached team.

Nico Paz brought the class for the hosts. The talented Argentina international stuck the opener into the top corner when Harry Maguire gave him too much space and then slotted in a third after catching Carlos Baleba in possession.

Paz set up another Como goal, too, playing in Tasos Douvikas, who ran away from a disoriented Matthijs de Ligt to find the net inside four minutes of the second half.

Image: Diogo Dalot during Man Utd's Champions League match with Como

This was De Ligt's first start in 325 days due to back problems and came due to a wider spate of injuries at the club. But excuses for this United performance may wear thin quickly for the travelling support who stood in the pouring rain to watch this dismantling.

United's own star, Bruno Fernandes, was anonymous again, with just one goal involvement now in his past nine appearances for the club. His head-shaking summed up the mood before a sweeping Como fourth, which saw unmarked centre-back Jacobo Ramon head in, underlining the vast gap between the sides on the night.

Joshua Zirkzee's injury-time goal was of little consolation. With just three points from their first three games, United have an uphill battle to make it out of the league phase in this competition. More immediately they are in desperate need of a better performance and win at home to Bournemouth on Sunday in the Premier League, live on Sky Sports.

Carrick 'really angry' with Man Utd performance

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick admits their performance was 'not acceptable' in their 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick:

"I'm really angry but you've got to move on and deal with what's next. At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before the next game to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everybody.

"It's not about playing for me - it's about playing for this club. My whole life's wrapped around it [Man Utd]. I genuinely give everything I possibly can. It's not about me, it's about what we all give."

Asked if all of the players give as much as he does, Carrick said: "I'd like to think so. I didn't like what I saw tonight though."

Analysis: No shock to see Man Utd beaten

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson criticised Manchester United after they were thrashed 4-1 in the Champions League by Como

Sky Sports' Paul Merson:

"They've got to start winning matches. The problem with Manchester United is we still live in the age of when it was [Wayne] Rooney, [Cristiano] Ronaldo and people like that.

"We're caught by the name - one of the biggest clubs in the world. But they're not one of the biggest teams in the world. They're far from it. Everybody judges them on when they had superstars.

"I don't see it as a shock. I look at their players and I don't go, 'oh this is a surprise'. I didn't expect them to beat Leeds. Absolutely not. I didn't expect them to beat Como. That's where they are.

"Rooney, Ronaldo, [Roy] Keane... they're a million miles away."

'Como defeat is one of Man Utd's worst ever in Europe'

'One of Man Utd's worst ever defeats in Europe'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan provides insight on three things we learned from Manchester United's embarrassing Champions League loss at Como

Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan in Como:

"Michael Carrick looked very angry. He's the first one to defend his players whenever he can.

"It was one of those games where you know from the first minutes that United weren't at it. The body language from some of those players... you could tell Carrick was frustrated.

"Let's not sugar coat it - this is one of their worst ever results in Europe.

"This was a pretty surprising and shocking performance, but I think it's been coming as well. My feeling is that watching this game has told us what we've been thinking about this Manchester United team.

"There will be speculation about how that changing room is feeling and whether Michael Carrick still has them on board. But tonight, it doesn't quite feel everyone is on board.

"Ultimately there's a lot more pressure on Carrick and his position at Manchester United."

Alarming stats for Man Utd

Manchester United are winless in seven consecutive games in all competitions (D3 L4) for the first time since a run of eight matches between November and December 2015.

Manchester United are the first English team to concede inside the opening two minutes of back-to-back major European games (47 seconds vs Atletico Madrid, 118 seconds vs Como).

Como completed 594 passes tonight, the most by a team in a Champions League game against Manchester United since Barcelona in April 2019 (725).

Key moments from Como...

2: BIG MISS! Diogo Dalot takes a Matheus Cunha cross down in the box but his left-foot shot flashes wide of the far post.

2: GOAL! Nico Paz curls Como's opener into the top corner after Harry Maguire gives him too much space. A similar chance to Dalot's - a different result!

17: WIDE! Harry Maguire heads wide from a Bryan Mbeumo cross.

39: BIG MISS! Tasos Douvikas blazes over after stepping into the United box, failing to capitalise on static defending.

41: OFFIDE! A let-off for Senne Lammens and Man Utd as an offside flag goes up against Douvikas after he is brought down in the box by the goalkeeper.

HT: SUBS! Michael Carrick makes two changes at the break with Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba sent on for Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha.

Image: Como players celebrate taking an early lead against Man Utd in the Champions League

49: GOAL! Man Utd concede at the start of the second half, too, as Paz plays in Douvikas, who runs off Matthijs de Ligt before firing in.

54: CLOSE! Lucas da Cunha blasts a left-foot shot wide from inside the box when he looked primed to add a third.

57: GOAL! Baleba makes an ill-advised turn in his own half with no cover behind him and Paz takes the ball and races in on goal to add a third.

64: CHANCES! But Amad can't connect with Fernandes' clipped pass into the box to pull one back for United. Moments later he sees a shot tipped over.

76: GOAL! Centre-back Jacobo Ramon heads in to finish off another sweeping Como move.

90+1: GOAL! Joshua Zirkzee is narrowly onside to grab a late goal for Man Utd, finding the net after controlling Amad's cross.

Man Utd's next fixtures...

Sports.title: ‘Angry’ Carrick on the brink as Fernandes hits out at Manchester United tactics
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick’s future as Manchester United manager is in the balance after a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday night.

Before Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford on Sunday his future may be discussed by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the co-owner who controls sporting policy.

On a torrid night an “angry” ­Carrick insisted afterwards that he had not given his position any thought and was forced to defend himself against Bruno Fernandes after his captain questioned the manager’s tactics of not pressing against Cesc Fàbregas’s team. Carrick also criticised his side for not running. The defeat by Como in the third Champions League group game leaves United with only two wins all season from 11 games. ­Carrick’s side are in 13th place in the Premier League and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup last month.

The 45-year-old was asked if he fears for his job. “Listen, I’ve not given my own position any thought,” he said. “[My thoughts are] for the supporters – I was one of them watching that and I wasn’t happy at all.”

Carrick was then asked if he could walk away following the latest defeat in Europe. “No. It’s not about me right now and my feelings in that regard,” the manager said. “It’s more of as a team and as a football club, what we want to look like, what we should look like. And as I said, the results can come and go at times, but you got to do it in a certain way. And that wasn’t it.”

700 United sup­porters travelled. At the end around 200 remained and Carrick went to ­apologise to them, noticeably ­ignoring his players. After United conceded Nico Paz’s second-minute goal, Carrick’s men were unable to mount any resistance. By 57 minutes Como led 3-0, due to Tasos Douvikas’s strike and Paz’s second, before Jacobo Ramón completed the scoring for the Italian side on 76 minutes. Joshua Zirkzee netted in added time for the visitors.

Fernandes openly challenged ­Carrick’s strategy during the match. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

The captain was asked if Carrick’s tactics were wrong. “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me,” he said. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with them, the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.”

Fernandes’s criticism was put to his manager after the match. “We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” Carrick said.

“Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Carrick was asked how he can raise the mood before Bournemouth’s visit.

“I’m bitterly disappointed, I’m frustrated; more than frustrated, I’m really angry. But you’ve got to move on. You got to deal with what’s next and see what that looks like.

“At this moment in time, there’s a lot to do before that next game to get the team ready because that was a difficult night for everyone. I have to apologise to the supporters.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
Sports.content:
It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own.

Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged.

Enter Kane. He wore his playmaker’s hat; some of his passing was sumptuous and it was his assist for Alphonso Davies that helped Bayern to draw level. He wore his finisher’s one, too, scoring from the penalty spot to put his team in charge. It meant he had scored in 10 consecutive Champions League games; one short of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record. There is a reason why Kane is the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday. He now has 16 goals against Arsenal; he has only scored more against one club – Leicester, against whom he has 20.

Rice loosened Bayern’s grip. It was a lovely goal from him and Arsenal even hinted at a late winner, Jurriën Timber drawing a tip over from Manuel Neuer in stoppage time. That would have been too much because Bayern shaded an absorbing tie in terms of clear chances created. But Arsenal made their point. They were value for it.

Arsenal knew they were inside a fortress. Bayern had not previously lost a Champions League group or league phase match at their own stadium since the 3-2 reverse against Manchester City in December 2013, 40 games ago. The following 39 featured 37 wins and two draws. Arteta’s players were not intimidated. They bristled with assurance at the outset and Rice rewarded their never-say-die spirit. Bayern had wanted revenge for their 3-1 defeat at the Emirates Stadium in the league stage last season. They did not get it.

Arteta’s idea was to go pretty much as strong as possible with his lineup. He made just two changes, Timber for Ben White and Noni Madueke for Eze, albeit the latter was not on the bench for long. Saka had tussled with Davies and it looked innocuous. The alarm bells rang when Saka grabbed his thigh and went to ground, waving his hand in the air.

View image in fullscreen Bukayo Saka receives treatment after going down injured early on. Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Was it possible for the Arsenal support to think that Bayern had been stripped of their fear factor in the line behind Kane? Michael Olise was suspended, Jamal Musiala was injured and Luis Díaz was a substitute. He came on in the 68th minute only to be forced off before the end. Bayern were without the midfielder Joshua Kimmich for personal reasons.

Arteta moved Madueke over to his more natural position on the right wing when he introduced Eze on the left and Bayern will still be wondering how the latter was afforded so much space up the inside channel on that flank to put Arsenal in front.

It was a fabulous ball from Martin Ødegaard, who was in the mood, full of sharp turns and urgency, and Eze had the time to let it bounce before shooting first time into the far corner. An offside flag killed the Arsenal celebrations and there was one of those weird waits before the video assistant referee ruled that Eze was in fact onside.

Kane was booed by the Arsenal fans. Of course he was. He dropped deep to link the play and there was a moment in the 17th minute when he started a move with a pass from inside his own penalty area. There was a glorious ping over Gabriel Magalhães, who was the last Arsenal defender, for Ismael Saibari on 23 minutes, although his teammate could not control, and Kane’s fingerprints were all over the equaliser. He was on halfway when he sculpted the low through ball for Davies which took Timber out of the equation. The Bayern winger’s finish was clinical.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane lashes in from the spot to put Bayern Munich 2-1 ahead. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

Bayern had other chances in the first half, none better than the one for Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, in the 21st minute. It was Kane who began the attack, taking a quick goal kick – yes, really – and Gnabry was the man over on the right when the Bayern forwards worked it that way. Gnabry’s shot was too close to David Raya. Kane also saw Ezri Konsa produce a fine block to keep him out.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It is never anything other than a pleasure to be at the Allianz for a showpiece match. All the staples were present and correct. The en masse scarf waving. The slightly slapstick oompah band notes. The fans at either end of the ground calling to each other. The non-stop drumbeat and songs from the Südkurve, who also bounced as one at times.

The pre-game surprise had been the sight of Vincent Kompany in the Bayern dugout; the manager made a Lazarus-like rise from his sickbed and the action after the restart kept the blood pumping. Arsenal thought they had gone back ahead when Bruno Guimarães rose to meet Rice’s corner only for Neuer to produce an extraordinary save.

The goalkeeper touched the ball up and on to the crossbar and away. Shades of Gordon Banks against Pelé. It was Raya’s turn next; his save to keep out Dayot Upamecano’s close-range header from Gnabry’s cross was of the highest order.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta applauds the travelling fans after the final whistle. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

It was interesting to watch Kane after the penalty was awarded for handball against Timber. Bayern had worked the ball back to their No 9 and, when he shot, Timber’s arm was outstretched. Kane went through his mental processes. He could see that Raya did not retreat to his line for what felt like an age. Kane delayed even longer. He was in total control. He stuttered before banging the ball hard into the right-hand corner.

Bayern were close to putting the game to bed. Konrad Laimer dragged narrowly past the far post when well-placed but it was Arsenal who produced the sucker punch. Eze was dangerous throughout. And when the opportunity knocked for Rice after a pass from the substitute Viktor Gyökeres, he made no mistake.

Sports.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
Sports.content:
For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read.

Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain.

“Collectively and individually we did a good job and some players also made a step forward in their confidence,” said Emery, who was pleased with Villa’s seriousness against opponents still finding their way in a first campaign at this level. “Each match has an objective to get better, to be consistent and be very demanding.”

The hard work had been done in an opening period whose scoreline hardly did justice to Villa’s total dominance. Viking had drawn at home with Bayern Munich in their previous game, a fact that would look more explicable when they emerged from their shell later, but were barely afforded a kick and looked vulnerable every time the ball was delivered from wide.

Nicolas Jackson, electric in the 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce, fluffed two free headers in the opening seven minutes and a similarly resounding win came to appear possible. Emery had made four changes but Villa, working the play smoothly from side to side, were a consistent threat and unfazed by opponents whose attacking ambition was initially minimal.

The breakthrough arrived after a spell of pressure sparked when a cross from João Gomes, the makeshift right-back, deflected on to the bar. Two corners later, an inswinger from the livewire 18-year-old Ibrahim Mbaye was met by Ross Barkley, who leapt highest to plant a firm header across Arild Østbø at the near post.

Barkley had scored twice in the previous week’s big win but the rest of the first half resembled a quest for Emiliano Buendía to put his mark on the scoresheet. Straight after the opener Buendía looped a header wide of the vacant goal after Østbø had parried from Alysson, who was a rangy threat throughout, and then he charged on to a clever John McGinn corner only to aim straight at the keeper.

View image in fullscreen Ross Barkley heads Aston Villa’s opener from Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

It was third time lucky when the VAR reviewed a needless challenge by the Viking captain Zlatko Tripic on Alysson, who had run into traffic in the box, and led the referee Sebastian Gishamer to award a penalty. Buendía rolled it in, his fourth goal in consecutive European games; 37 minutes had passed and Viking had still not produced a meaningful attack.

After the restart they showed some of the intensity and verve that had ruffled Bayern, the richly promising midfielder Tobias Moi warming Zion Suzuki’s midriff and seeing a goalbound effort blocked. Suzuki also beat away a Tripic drive. But Villa could now exploit space in behind and, after flashing an angled effort just wide, Alysson got away once again to create the third. This time his attempted centre snicked off Heggheim, who was desperately trying to recover, and gave Østbø no chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Now Villa were, as the home choirs gleefully announced, top of the league and they received further opportunities to hammer home the point. Alejandro Garnacho saw one of them saved by Østbø after a strong run but Viking remained a threat and Christiansen’s finish, emphatically converting Kristoffer Askildsen’s deep cross, was by some distance the best of the night.

“The second half was much more like the Viking we want to be,” said Morten Jensen, who co-manages the Norwegian champions alongside Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim. “Maybe we had too much respect for them in the first half, they were all over us.”

View image in fullscreen Emiliano Buendía calmly doubles Aston Villa’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Alex Livesey/AVFC/Getty Images

Nine points from nine, not to mention 12 consecutive home wins in Europe, mean Villa are flying. Sweeping Fenerbahce and Viking aside can “give us confidence and comfort for the next challenges,” Emery said. They will need plenty of it given a trip to Barcelona follows the relatively soft run presented so far. Maybe the peak is yet to come.

Sports.title: Champions League: Silva sparks Real Madrid’s demolition of Leipzig as Lask stun Sporting
Sports.content:
Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande among the goals for José Mourinho’s side.

Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval.

Mbappé bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on.

“We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible – we’ve won three and there are five to go,” Mbappé said. The France forward, who hopes to win the Ballon d’Or next week, has netted in each of Madrid’s Champions League matches this season and has 12 goals in 12 games.

“I’m doing well [but] I think I can do more,” he said. “I’m one of the few players who always has to demand more from himself ... right now it’s a good moment, but we have to keep going and I have to do more.”

Lask launched an impressive comeback at Sporting to earn their first Champions League win of the season. The Austrian champions went behind when Luis Suárez scored from the spot after five minutes, but equalised 10 minutes later through Christoph Lang.

The visitors then stunned the Estádio José Alvalade as Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek put them 3-1 up, the former rounding off a smart team move and the latter firing in at the near post. Suárez scored again for the hosts late on, but it was not enough.

View image in fullscreen Victor Osimhen, with Yunus Akgun on his shoulders, after rounding off Galatasaray’s 4-2 win at Lille. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Galatasaray swept past Lille at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, setting the tone with a goal after two minutes from Yunus Akgun.

Lille levelled the score via Soriba Diaoune, who then put them 2-1 up in the 39th minute. Aleksey Batrakov made it 2-2 just before half-time, however, before an own goal from Nabil Bentaleb and Victor Osimhen, in action against his former club, sealed a 4-2 victory.

Inter had Alessandro Bastoni sent off midway through the second half before Carlos Augusto’s late goal secured a 1-0 win at home to Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions got their first points of the league phase.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bastoni was sent off for two yellow cards in as many minutes, putting Inter on the back foot. Carlos Augusto saved the day in the 77th minute, capping a lightning-fast counterattack with a low finish.

View image in fullscreen Isco wheels away after netting from 12 yards to put Real Betis 1-0 up against Feyenoord. Photograph: Antonio Pozo/PRESSINPHOTO/Shutterstock

Real Betis, who beat Feyenoord 1-0 via a penalty kick from Isco, made it three from three in the Champions League to extend their strong start to the season.

Betis had the lion’s share of the chances, but only broke the deadlock when Jeremiah St Juste was adjudged to have handled in the box. Isco stepped up and fired low into the right-hand corner for what proved to be the winner.

Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0 at the Jan Breydel Stadium in a ruthless home performance. The Belgians went 1-0 up through Hans Vanaken in first-half stoppage time before Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs secured the win in the second half.

Sports.title: Paris Saint-Germain sparkle on the pitch while the city of light burns around them | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
PASSION!

GOOOOAL!

MVP!

The security deployment will be massive.

Those who sought to bring down the Republic will have to answer for it.

Tell you who would have loved this? Who would have been utterly engrossed scrolling the hashtag #Paris on Tuesday night as two things happened simultaneously, the harrowing of the Barcelona defence at the Parc des Princes, and the harrowing of Paris itself via tales of city-centre thuggery and end-of-days political doom‑mongering.

The big man, Guy Debord himself. The Society of the Spectacle, you say? Actually, I think we’re past that now. Hold the society bit. We’ll just take the spectacle.

The great Parisian Situationist philosopher wasn’t really one for managed fun. But it was impossible not to be bowled over by the extraordinary pre-match show for Paris Saint‑Germain versus Barcelona, Champions League Matchday Three.

The wild pyrotechnics, the plumes of smoke, the full-wrap light show, the lime-green robo‑text spelling out every player’s name on the pitch. Although not the Barcelona names, sadly, for anyone with an unrealised desire to see the words “ANTHONY GORDON” projected in vast letters for the delight of a shrieking crowd.

Admittedly, the Halloween‑themed tifo banner showing a masked Paris Saint-Germain serial killer-type literally butchering the Barcelona badge to death with his bloodied chainsaw was perhaps a bit much. As were the Barça Puta signs, which are now reportedly the subject of a complaint to Uefa.

But it was a wild and all‑consuming spectacle, annihilating every other impulse in your head to a green thought in a green shade. And in the process capturing the profound sense of cognitive dissonance in the city.

View image in fullscreen PSG fans light flares after their team took the lead against Barcelona. Photograph: Julien de Rosa/AFP/Getty Images

Just walking around the streets of central Paris earlier in the day generated its own mild whiplash. On the face of it this was still the same city of flâneurs and tourists and everyday bistro business, and not, repeat not, a civil war drama or some kind of emergent military caliphate.

But the sense of dread was also tangible. You still got the occasional crunch of glass underfoot. Here and there charred bikes and scooters had been politely piled to one side. Even close to the Parc, away from the main hotspots, shopkeepers could be seen emerging warily into their doorways at the sound of a police siren.

By Tuesday night, a total of 2,513 people had been taken into police custody after the events of the weekend. At least 420 rental bikes had been destroyed or maimed. Liberated high-value retail goods were already being sold on Vinted, a commendable show of entrepreneurial energy from the maligned younger generation.

Not that you’d suspect these two worlds had any kind of overlap, lost in the booming triumphalism around PSG’s 4–2 win, one of the most beautifully luminous football matches you’re ever likely to see. Or indeed reading the coverage of an event that seems to have been treated in France like its own clear, clean space, floating above the flames, all the chat about the brilliance of Monsieur Dynamite, Désiré Doué, the wonderful television audiences on Canal+ TV, the whole of European football “kneeling before the machine” (are we sure this isn’t to do with anarchic rejection of social control?). “Paris est insubmersible!” was the headline in Le Parisien. But is it?

Remember when football used to reflect the world? Or just provide clues, a commentary, some kind of metaphor? This is no longer the case. At a time when even the most thunderous of commentators is struggling to summarise all this in suitably trite and damning terms, it was hard to avoid the feeling Paris Saint-Germain, the pet power football project of the state of Qatar, expresses this dualism perfectly.

Sometimes you just have to let football tell you things. “People who want to cause trouble in the city centres next Saturday will be prevented,” Emmanuel Macron announced on Tuesday evening, speaking, as it happens, from Doha, where he met Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, ultimate owner of PSG.

View image in fullscreen Désiré Doué (left) with João Neves after scoring PSG’s first goal against Barcelona. Photograph: David Ramos/Uefa/Getty Images

Macron is said to be considering deploying the French military to keep the peace on the streets before the next planned protests, although even here he may have to ask Qatar’s permission if he wants to deploy any of the French troops currently deployed working its missile systems, or embedded in the Doha security services.

The key event Macron is tooling up for is this Saturday night, 24 October, the date the gilets jaunes social media feed has set for an even greater swell of disorder. And again this will be football adjacent, with PSG playing Lyon at home on Sunday, a top‑of‑the-table capital‑city clash played out against whatever wreckage is left, however many thousands of Dot bikes are savaged, whatever guerrilla skirmishes are still playing out in the Marais.

What does this really have to do with football and the Ici C’est Paris brand appropriated by a state outreach project? Well, what are these demonstrations anyway? There have been many theories put forward as to what exactly is happening here, what is the spark, the kindling, the fire behind this disorder. School protests were the original line. Others have now roped in some kind of nebulous omni-cause, Instagram-activism, perhaps even a barbarian takeover, the decline of the west, savagery at the gates, of the type Donald Trump pretends to see.

Do you need a single reason? Take a look around. Modern life is pretty alarming on a minute‑to‑minute basis. Disaffection, alienation, a sense of being transformed in real time into a passive economic consumer unit, a set of eyeballs, an avatar of consumption. French youth unemployment is close to 20%. Robots nobody wants are being lined up to take jobs that don’t exist. Why don’t these young people want to join a youth club? Why don’t they 

On the other hand, what is PSG in Paris, other than the perfect expression of this? It often seems to surprise people that celebrations of PSG victories end up with riots and burnt-out cars. But Paris is both a beautiful and deeply dysfunctional city, a place of make‑believe and deprivation, where the centre is a perfect, performative relic, the suburbs shunted out to the ring roads, a life lived inside a box, noses pressed up against the glass, peering through your binoculars at the city of someone else’s love.

Paris is the divide between overclass and churn expressed in a single city. It’s everything you might have had but never will. And PSG represent this like no other entity, a football club owned as an act of outreach by a staggeringly rich inherited monarchy, weaponised passion, borrowed culture, engineered spectacle, deeply cynical but also deeply seductive.

View image in fullscreen Damage after the riots in Place de la République. Photograph: Telmo Pinto/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Why are the Qataris splurging hundreds of millions into this project? Because they just really like high-pressing positional football? Qatar is the indentured labour state that employs Colin Kaepernick to promote its outreach projects. It will hymn its connections to the footballers of the banlieue, which is true and real and valuable, but not because of anything this political project wants or needs other than public relations.

It is in its own way a perfect human lab experiment, synthesised beauty, collectivism, with a cold, cold hand at its heart. And this is why there weren’t two versions of Paris in evidence on Tuesday night, just the same one, the dark side and the shiny side, an engine of the same divisions, the same kind of violence, right down to the sight of kids in PSG training gear dodging the police or taunting the barricades at the Place de la République.

And now we have Sunday night to come, more Ici C’est Paris, more PASSION. What kind of background will it be played out against? Does it matter under the lights? Will anyone notice?

Le Monde has described these events as a very basic test of the republic, its ability to bend, to remain essentially itself, the state’s willingness to pit itself against its own people. Football, as ever, holds these answers already. PSG’s Qatari owners have spent the past 15 years flaunting this city like a global luxury brand, extending its reach, creating its own ideal of conspicuous consumption, spectacle, triumph, son et lumière, bread and roses. As ever, if you want to know how and why, football has the answers.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo asked for punishment ‘without mitigation’, then fought to cut it
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo successfully fought to reduce his punishment for walking out on a Portugal training camp, after saying publicly that his sanction should be imposed “without mitigating circumstances”.

After leaving the training camp in Denmark last month, Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement on social media that he should be punished as the Portuguese Football Federation saw fit and that his role as captain constituted “an aggravating factor”.

However, during the disciplinary council’s inquiry the 41-year-old put forward several arguments for cutting his punishment, including his clean disciplinary record in recent seasons and his services to football.

Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension and a €255 (£215) fine, and the document accompanying the ruling reveals he presented three arguments in mitigation: his disciplinary record this season and in the previous three seasons; his services to football including recognition for sporting merit; and his contribution to establishing the facts of the case.

To support these arguments, Ronaldo listed the club titles he has won and his achievements with the national team: the 2016 European Championship and two Nations League titles. His individual awards were also highlighted, including the fact that the Al-Nassr forward has won the Ballon d’Or five times. Beyond his achievements on the pitch, he mentioned the honours he had received from senior state officials.

The decision-makers accepted Ronaldo’s arguments concerning his achievements and services to the country, using them to halve his suspension and fine. The punishment was then halved again because Ronaldo had accepted responsibility for his actions.

Ronaldo’s suspension will be served in a period during which there are no international matches. It is unclear whether he intends to return to the national team – or whether the head coach, Jorge Jesus, will select him again.

The account of events provides a clearer picture of the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the training camp. After head coach Jesus held a press conference in which he reiterated that he was in charge of the team and that no player would influence his selection decisions, Ronaldo requested a vehicle from the FPF and set off for Copenhagen airport.

During the journey, he called the Portuguese federation’s president, Pedro Proença, and told him he was “not in the right frame of mind” to remain with the team.

“The defendant [Ronaldo] did not inform or provide prior justification to the federation or the men’s national team officials regarding his intention to leave the stadium and the training camp,” the ruling states. It says that between 30 September and 4 October, Ronaldo missed more than 30 team activities, including travel, training sessions and meals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The federation says that Ronaldo’s promise on social media, after leaving the training camp, to tell his fans “the whole truth” brought further negative attention to the incident: “Given his prominence as a public figure on a global scale, the defendant could not have been unaware that his conduct, in the circumstances in which it occurred, would be subject to intense media scrutiny, as indeed it was.”

Ronaldo was therefore “expected to exercise particular caution in choosing the timing and manner in which he expressed his dissatisfaction with the manager’s decisions and conduct”. Instead, the player “further fuelled speculation and public curiosity by posting on Instagram on the very day he left Copenhagen, announcing that, ‘in due course’, he would tell ‘all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to his departure from the men’s senior national team’,” the inquiry concluded.

Portugal are scheduled to play Denmark again in their next game on 14 November in Braga.

Sports.title: Coach banned until 2048 for training children in DR Congo while suspended for sexual abuse
Sports.content:
A coach in the Democratic Republic of the Congo who was banned from football for 20 years by Fifa for sexual abuse of a minor has had his ban extended by five years to 2048 by the world governing body.

Jonathan Bukabakwa, known as Messi, has also been ordered to pay an additional fine of $15,000 (£11,200) after the Guardian revealed he had continued to work with young players despite his suspension.

The Congolese Association Football Federation (Fecofa) and Racing Club Baki, where Bukabakwa was coaching, have been fined $50,000 each by Fifa’s ethics committee for failing to comply with its decision to ban him for 20 years in 2023.

Quick Guide How do I 

Fecofa has also been instructed to introduce a “comprehensive education, compliance and monitoring programme for its officials, affiliated clubs and registered members” to try to ensure there is no repeat.

“The Congo DR Football Association, the club Racing Club Baki (formerly known as Esperanto FC), and the coach Jonathan Bukabakwa were found responsible for failing to comply with the decision rendered by the Fifa ethics committee on 18 October 2023,” said a Fifa statement.

Bukabakwa, who previously coached youth teams in the Limpopo and Malabo regions, was convicted of sexually abusing minors by authorities in the DRC and was released from prison last year. A Guardian investigation in August revealed there was video footage of him coaching young players at Esperanto in the Limete district of the capital, Kinshasa. Local sources confirmed he had regularly been seen taking charge of players on a school field.

Bukabakwa did not deny continuing to coach young players but claimed he had not been informed of his Fifa ban. He said he had not been questioned or received any communication from the governing body. He has denied the allegations against him.

The case has raised further questions about safeguarding in Congolese football and the ability of authorities to ensure that suspended individuals do not continue participating in the sport. Bukabakwa was provisionally suspended by Fecofa in November 2022 after media reports of alleged widespread sexual abuse in the DRC. Several other coaches were provisionally suspended at the time, although investigations into some of those other cases did not establish sufficient evidence for further action by Fecofa or Fifa.

Véron Mosengo-Omba, elected as Fecofa’s president in May, has promised to look into the previous cases once he has re-established a disciplinary committee. Fecofa was under a Fifa-appointed normalisation committee from 2023 until his election. “We will make sure that no one who is behaving like this will be involved in football in this country,” he said.

Sports.title: Sarina Wiegman signs contract extension to stay as England women head coach until 2029
Sports.content:
Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after the World Cup next summer and this extension gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row.

Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021, also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up.

“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” Wiegman said. “Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”

Quick Guide How do I 

England will reach the World Cup finals, to be held in Brazil in June and July, if they come through a two-leg playoff against Ukraine for which they are heavy favourites. “My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come,” Wiegman said.

This is Wiegman’s second contract extension with England and opens the possibility that she could coach Team GB at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles should the team qualify. Wiegman, who turns 57 next Monday, will continue to be assisted by Janneke Bijl, Arvid Smit and Darren Ward.

“Sarina is an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments and I am so happy to continue to work with her for the next Euro cycle,” the Football Association’s chief executive, Mark Bullingham, said.

Wiegman had refused to be drawn on questions over her future before England’s two games against Greece during the recent international break, but the Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh last week said “obviously I’d want her to stay” when asked about the head coach’s future.

“Sarina’s the boss, I would never ask her those questions, but I think everyone in England would love her to stay,” Walsh said. “I’ve played a lot of games for her and I really appreciate her as a manager.”

Sports.title: CHRIS WHEELER: Man United were insipid, lifeless and downright ugly in tame Como surrender. How much longer can Michael Carrick and his team sleepwalk through this wretched season?
Sports.content:
As the full-time whistle blew on one of Manchester United’s most embarrassing nights in Europe, Michael Carrick walked over alone to the few away fans still left at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium and held up his hands in apology. They had stood drenched for two hours, battered by the wind and rain that whipped off Lake Como. This has to be the most picturesque venues in the Champions League by some distance, but on a night like this it was downright ugly and so were United. Carrick’s apology was reminiscent of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s farewell game at Watford in November 2021, which also ended in a humbling 4-1 defeat. Solskjaer knew he was a dead man walking that day. If this proves to be Carrick’s last stand, what a lame surrender it was. How much longer can this go on? How much longer can United sleepwalk through this wretched season as Carrick continues to grasp hopelessly for positives? Statistically the fifth worst European defeat in United’s history was also Carrick’s fifth in 11 games this wretched season as they were torn apart by Como and the excellent Nico Paz. Manchester United were completely outplayed by Como as they lost 4-1 to the Italian side The dreadful result heaps further pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick This was an incredible night for Como, but one of the worst in United's European history This was meant to be the biggest game in Como’s history and they played like it. Cesc Fabregas’ team are a credit to the former Arsenal midfielder and it’s not by chance that they lie fifth in Serie A. But Manchester United coming to town is no longer what it was. This is a pathetic imitation of the teams that have represented this great club down the years. The 700 fans who made the journey to Lombardy stood in one of the areas of this stadium exposed to the elements beneath Giuseppe Terragni’s Monumento ai Caduti that sits at the head of the lake. It means monument to the fallen, and how much further can United keep falling from here? They were insipid. Lifeless. The confidence and self-belief has been sucked out of this team. It’s eight games since they last won, beating Sabah of Azerbaijan in this competition and recording their only clean sheet of the season. Como 4-1 Man United: MATCH FACTS Como 1907 (4-2-3-1): Butez 6; Couto 7 (Smolcic 80, 6), Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8 (Dossena 80, 6); Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8 Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76) Booked: Kempf Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Dalot 3, De Ligt 3 (Amass 79, 5), Maguire 4, Mazraoui 3; Mount 3, Santos 4 (Baleba 46, 5); Mbeumo 4 (Lacey 86), Tielemans 4, Cunha 3 (Amad 46, 6); Fernandes 4 (Zirkzee 67, 6) Goal: Zirkzee (90+1) Booked: Santos, Baleba, Lacey Manager: Michael Carrick 3 Referee: Sven Jablonski 6 Shortly after the half hour mark, their supporters broke into a chorus of ‘attack, attack, attack’ which is never a good sign for any United manager. From the chance that fell to Diogo Dalot in the opening seconds to Matheus Cunha’s tame effort on the stroke of half-time, they didn’t have another effort on goal in the first half. Yes, Carrick was without nine senior players, forcing him to put Matthijs De Ligt into the starting line-up without playing a minute of football in the last 325 days due to a back injury, and name Jack Fletcher and Tynan Thompson on the bench even though both players had featured in the UEFA Youth League defeat to Como earlier in the day. But that was no excuse for another performance that left you wondering just what these United players are doing on the training pitch all week – and what Carrick is saying to them. If there was concrete evidence that they simply aren’t learning or progressing, it came after two minutes here. A week after United conceded after 50 seconds to Atletico Madrid in Spain, they were behind again. No sooner had Dalot curled an effort wide after mistakenly creating the opportunity for himself by miscontrolling Cunha’s pass than Paz converted a similar chance at the other end. United had been warned about the gifted Argentine, but you wouldn’t have know it by the way Harry Maguire stood off the 22-year-old when he received a pass from Lucas Da Cunha inside the box. Paz looked up, picked his spot and guided the ball beyond Senne Lammens. He was simply too much for United to handle. Andrey Santos was booked for hacking him down with a crude challenge, Cunha resorted to similar tactics, and Lammens was relieved to see the offside flag go up after fouling Como’s No.10 in the box. Carrick made changes at half-time, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Cunha and Santos so that Bryan Mbeumo could play through the middle. He also asked his full-backs, Dalot and Mazraoui, to switch sides. Argentina wonderkid Nico Paz was Como's star as he scored twice and laid on an assist Paz put his side ahead in under two minutes after United's defence mistakenly stood off him United couldn't match Como's intensity and were insipid and error-ridden, which included Carlos Baleba giving the ball away for their second goal United were awful and Carrick even hooked captain Bruno Fernandes in the second half Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in added time but it was barely acknowledged It’s another sign of the growing crisis around Carrick that it only made things worse as United conceded another early goal. Martin Baturina had gone close twice before half-time, so it was no surprise to see him extend Como’s lead. Paz was the architect this time with a fine pass to Baturina who got away from De Ligt and powered a shot past Lammens. United were three down eight minutes later. Baleba gave the ball away to Paz close to halfway and no United player looked like getting near him as he surged downfield and finished clinically. Carrick’s misery was complete in the 76th minute when Jacobo Ramon got the fourth. It was a measure of the brimming confidence in Fabregas’ side that his centre-back felt able to charge forward in open play and meet a left-wing cross from substitute Kaiki Bruno. No-one had tracked Ramon and he beat Lammens with a thumping header. Carrick sent on teenagers Harry Amass and Shea Lacey which felt like a pathetically response to a pathetic performance, even though Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation from close-range in the 91st minute. The damage was done. As Carrick and his players flew home on Wednesday night, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the United board were left with a decision to make about where they go from here.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal: Gunners take huge step in the right direction, as Declan Rice earns point that means so much more in Mikel Arteta's bid to build dynasty
Sports.content:
A draw in Bavaria will not stand out in the list of achievements carved out stubbornly by Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal as he has taken them from nowhere to somewhere over the last six years or so. But the Arsenal manager will know what this night means, nevertheless. This is a season that must see Arsenal break fresh ground if they are to become the team we all feel they can be. They know they have questions to answer and they know what they are. They are about style and the ability to bring about repeat success. They are about building a domestic dynasty and winning things in Europe. At times Arsenal look to be quite close to that but at other times – such as in winning so drearily with one shot on target at Nottingham Forest on Sunday – they look to be rather too far away. So, yes, this felt like a big step in the right direction. An enterprising attacking performance – Arsenal could have scored four or five goals – against a team that hardly ever loses in its own stadium and then, a come from behind draw just when it seemed everything may be lost. The feeling the Arsenal team will have had when celebrating Declan Rice’s late equaliser down beneath their own fans here will have been one that should propel them forwards. Bayern are not used to teams doing that to them here and when the ball flew across Manuel Neuer and into the far corner you could feel the air being sucked out of this cavernous bowl and up into the night sky. Declan Rice smashed a powerful low effort to make it 2-2 late on against Bayern Munich Rice latched onto a through ball and his shot had too much for Manuel Neuer Harry Kane had put Bayern Munich in front from the penalty spot in the second half For Bayern had thrown their best at Arsenal here. Harry Kane had done so too. Arsenal had led midway through the first half through Eberechi Eze but as time wore on Bayern’s rapid counters threatened to become too much. Defeat beckoned. Kane – as irrepressibly as inspirational as ever – had supplied a world class assist for Alphonso Davies in the first half and then, on the hour, a penalty of his own. A loss here would have not been a disaster for Arsenal but it would have felt telling. It would have given their many critics further ammunition with which to do them down. Not good enough in Europe. Flat track bullies. Stuck in the mud. Not moving forwards. So it was a good night for Arsenal if not a perfect one. An injury to Bukayo Saka, for example, was not on Arteta’s wish list. He was clipped from behind in the tenth minute and went down holding the back of his knee. That was the end of his evening and the injury will be a worry. The only consolation to Arteta will have been that his replacement took his opportunity. This has not been a stellar season for Eze but you would not have known it watching him drive a pass from Martin Odegaard across Manuel Neuer and in to the far corner with his left foot in the 25th minute. The supply from Odegaard was exemplary but it needed a finish to match. At that point, Arsenal were worth the lead, even if Bayern had attacked on the counter to good effect. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya had to save sharply from Serge Gnabry after one such break while a lofted Kane pass a couple of minutes before Eze’s goal could have led to something had Ismael Saibari not applied such a clumsy touch. Arsenal, meanwhile, had their own moments to ponder. Twice from corners they had opportunities at the far post but Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes couldn’t take them. Alphonso Davies equalised for the German side with a tidy finish past David Raya Eberechi Eze fired a composed effort past Manuel Neuer to break the deadlock in Munich After a slow start, it had become a good game. Arsenal were purposeful and ambitious if a little too square across the back at times. Eventually, they were caught out. Kane’s pass inside Jurrien Timber from just inside the Arsenal half could not have been more geometrically perfect had he used a set square and Davies ran on to open his body and beat Raya quite comfortably. Kane’s goal – his 58th in the competition – was eventually to arrive on the hour and arrived after a spell of Bayern pressure. Before that, though, Arsenal had another couple of huge moments. Almost immediately after half-time, Neuer produced a stunning save to push a Gabriel header up on to the crossbar from another corner. At the other end Raya denied Dayot Upamecano in similarly brilliant fashion. It was an increasingly engaging game but one that Bayern were beginning to enjoy rather more. Their forays into the attacking third had become more regular and brought with them a greater menace. Kane, for his part, was showcasing his full repertoire, spending as much time in deep position as he was through the middle. There were concerning scenes for the Gunners when Saka limped off early on in the game This was a draw worth far more than the solitary point for Mikel Arteta's side But he was in the right place on the hour to meet a cross from Konrad Laimer and when his shot struck the sprawling Jurrien Timber on the arm a penalty was the only decision available. Kane took it and, after a little stutter, slotted it to Raya’s right with the keeper committed in the other direction. Bayern almost sealed the game soon after only for Laimer’s right foot shot to miss Raya’s right hand post. So Arsenal remained in it and – with Viktor Gyokeres on to change the shape of their attacks – they eventually took what they deserved. The move down the right side was slick and Rice’s finish – after a one-two with the big striker – was perfect, across Neuer with power. The celebrations that followed were about much more than a single Champions League point. NOW READ: Bayern Munich v Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?

Sports.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes questions Michael Carrick's tactics in wake of Champions League humiliation in Como - after boss was left 'angry' by team's display and apologised to supporters
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the club’s Champions League humiliation in Como. United were humbled 4-1 as their wretched season hit a new low and Carrick, who expressed his 'anger' at the performance, suffered his fifth defeat in 11 games. A week after Lisandro Martinez had taken aim at his Old Trafford bosses – and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular – Fernandes broke ranks to question why United were so passive again. He said: ‘It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.’ Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: ‘That's on the manager and staff to say, not me. ‘Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to. Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to hit out at manager Michael Carrick Fernandes expressed his frustration after Carrick's side were thrashed 4-1 by Como ‘A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide.’ Having conceded to Atletico after 50 seconds last week, United were behind within two minutes as Como star Nico Paz struck the first of his two goals. ‘It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early,’ said Fernandes. ‘Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way. ‘Conceding early makes us go into game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.’ Fernandes was surprisingly substituted by Carrick midway through the second half, and the United skipper shook his head in frustration as he made his way back to the dugout. Carrick refused to be drawn on Fernandes' post-match outburst but admitted he was left 'angry' by his team's performance in Italy. He said: 'I'm angry to be honest. My whole life is wrapped around this. I didn't like what I've seen tonight.' Carrick added: 'There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win.' On their performance more widely, the former United midfielder said: 'It was more than disappointing. I think everyone has to take responsibility for that. 'I'll 100 per cent take responsibility for the overall team and performance; that stops with me and I accept that. But as a supporter of this club for so long and I care so much about this club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable. 'A lot of it is the motivation, intensity and purpose you have to bring in a game of football and we didn't bring that today. You can't turn it on and off or choose when you perform or give absolutely everything. Until you do that you're not going to win enough football matches.' Fernandes was substituted in the second half and looked frustrated as he left the pitch Carrick apologised to United's travelling fans after the match and held his hands up in their direction having marched across the pitch, before he repeated this stance when speaking to the media. He added: 'I care an unbelievable amount about these supporters. They're the heartbeat of this football club and always will be. 'For them to travel, I have to apologise for the performance and everything they've done to get here tonight. To watch a performance like that I feel for them. There's no excuses for that and it's totally unacceptable.' NOW READ: Como 4-1 Manchester United PLAYER RATINGS: Which United stars were totally anonymous?

Sports.title: Ryan Bertrand unmasked as the face of AFC Wimbledon's previously secret prospective new investors - with plans to splash £87m
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea and England star Ryan Bertrand is the central figure behind a new investment group pitching to buy into AFC Wimbledon – with plans to pump £87million in to take the fan-owned club to the next level.

League One Wimbledon announced last week that they had identified a preferred investor in their effort to raise new capital, after admitting their ownership structure is 'not sustainable'.

The south-west London phoenix club, founded in 2002, rose from the ninth tier of English football to the third but narrowly escaped relegation in their tenth season in the summer, a year after announcing an operating loss of £600,000 and that projected finances 'will become very tight'.

Now, Daily Mail Sport can confirm Bertrand, 37, is the central football figure of the 'preferred investor' group – Sloane Street Capital (SSC), which is backed by British tech entrepreneur Omar Mir.

SSC plan to oversee football operations at Wimbledon with Bertrand in place as senior football adviser. They are offering £16m for 34 per cent of the shares in AFCW PLC and promise £71m of investment over five seasons while allowing fan ownership and control to continue by never gaining majority voting control.

'Wimbledon is a club with real football heritage,' Bertrand told Daily Mail Sport. 'There's the story of what happened before but what's happened since is truly unrivalled. This is not "The Ryan Bertrand Show". It's about more ideas and empowering the club by partnering with the fans.'

Ryan Bertrand is central to the preferred AFC Wimbledon investment offer (Source: Ryan Bertrand/Instagram)

Bertrand retired from football in 2024 and has been working in player representation and talent identification after selling the Fintech investment firm he co-founded. Sources close to the former left-back claim players he has identified for various clubs now have a market valuation of £332m.

A Champions League winner with Chelsea, he has long dreamed of entering football club ownership and held talks over a move to buy Charlton Athletic previously. This summer he completed an in-depth course at Harvard University on the Business of Entertainment, Media and Sports.

SSC's proposal is that £8m of the first £16m invested is in football operations and infrastructure. Bertrand believes his expertise can both unearth talented youngsters and help identify senior performance players with proven experience.

Mir, the backer behind the group's funding, is the Global Strategic Advisor to the Co-Founder/CEO of World Wide Technology, the largest privately-owned technology company in the US with $20billion (£15bn) in annual revenue, and an adviser to the King's Trust on AI and Advanced Technology. He is the group's sole funder.

Stuart Fiertz, co-founder of the investment manager Cheyne Capital, and football agent Oliver Ward complete the SSC group.

Mir owns 95 per cent of SSC and is its only funder. The other five per cent would be split equally on completion between Bertrand, Fiertz and Ward.

Bertrand, 37, retired from football in 2024 after playing for Chelsea, Southampton and Leicester

Wimbledon say they spoke to more than 20 interested parties and Bertrand's group emerged as the 'strongest fit'.

The offer will now move to a vote by the 6,266 members of The Dons Trust, which closes on November 17 with an announcement on the result a day later. For the vote to pass, at least 50 per cent of eligible members must vote, 75 per cent of votes cast must be in favour and 40 per cent of all eligible members must vote 'yes'.

Sports.title: England legend Sir James Anderson RETIRES from cricket at 44... after Lancashire tell him they will not give him a new contract for next summer
Sports.content:
Jimmy Anderson’s long career is finally at an end at the age of 44 after Lancashire declined to offer him a new contract for the 2027 season.

Anderson, who took a record 704 Test wickets for England and this summer collected 50 wickets for Lancashire at 17 each in division two of the county championship, was told earlier this week by the club’s new chief executive, Richard Kenyon, and their new director of cricket, Paul Farbrace, that his time at Old Trafford was over.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Anderson will not look to extend a county career that began in 2001, bringing to an end one of the modern game’s great fast-bowling stories. In all, he took 1,193 first-class wickets at 24 each, as well as 358 in one-day cricket and 71 in T20s.

Barring an unexpected late franchise detail, that appears to be it. Since Anderson has only ever played T20 cricket for England and Lancashire, and said he ‘hated every minute’ of his two-match stint with Manchester Originals in The Hundred in 2025, that seems unlikely.

He had been mulling over the possibility of captaining Lancashire next summer, having done the job in 2026, when they struggled for runs and finished second-bottom in the championship, ahead only of Gloucestershire. It was their worst finish since 1984.

James Anderson took 50 Championship wickets for Lancs at an average of 17.7 last season

Anderson was knighted by Princess Anne in 2025 for his services to cricket

Anderson took 704 Test wickets for England and celebrated winning the Ashes Down Under

Their on-field struggles were reflected by turmoil off the pitch, with chief executive Daniel Gidney stepping down after 14 years in charge, and Mark Chilton sacked as director of cricket.

Farbrace, once England’s assistant coach, has been brought in from Sussex to replace Chilton, and presented with a simple brief: to return Lancashire, who won the most recent of their nine championship titles in 2011, to the top flight.

Anderson had hoped to be part of that push under the new management, only to be told otherwise. The club’s fans may ask why they are getting rid of one of their two most successful bowlers from 2026 (George Balderson picked up 53 wickets at under 22 each), especially with only two others – Tom Bailey and Mitchell Stanley – taking more than 12.

But Farbrace and Kenyon, who left Nottinghamshire to move to the club he supported as a boy, are determined to start afresh in 2027, leaving Anderson to contemplate, at long last, a life outside the game.

Sports.title: Kyle Walker admits he will get rid of his 'four in a row' tattoo if Man City are stripped of their Premier League titles
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker has admitted he would probably wipe his 'four in a row' leg tattoo if Manchester City are stripped of their Premier League titles. The Man City legend won six league titles with the club and last year revealed his inked tribute to their record run of consecutive crowns between 2021 and 2024. Daily Mail Sport has reported that City are primed for a huge points reduction which would relegate them to the Championship after they were found guilty of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018. It remains to be seen whether the club will be stripped of their titles after they manipulated their financial accounts to the tune of £900million via 'sham' contracts. Asked by talkSPORT if he would get rid of his tattoo, Walker said: 'I'm probably going to have to do that. 'But you look at the likes of the great Man United squad, and they never managed to get four in a row. So there's only a select few of us that can say that we won four. Walker Walker says he will probably get rdid of his 'four in a row' tattoo if Manchester City are stripped of their Premier League titles The former England star revealed his tattoo - one of many that he has - last year 'I'll try and keep it on, but hopefully we don't get the things taken away.' He also said: 'As a player, all I can say is that all we did is go out and play our best football as a team and I will defend the players for the rest of my life. 'I feel that what we achieved in that space of time was probably incredible and probably won't be done ever again. 'From the outside looking in, it doesn't look great and we have to address that.' Walker was on the books with City for eight seasons, having joined from Tottenham for £45m in 2017, and was elected captain after winning the Treble with them in 2022/23. The right-back, who now plays for Burnley in the Championship, has previously admitted to talkSPORT that City's title-winners don't want to talk about the situation. 'It’s something we don’t want to talk about because we want to be looked upon as winning them trophies, winning them the right way,' he said earlier this month. City insist they are innocent and are appealing the verdict by an independent panel, which found them guilty of all the serious alleged financial breaches.
