In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'. It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee. The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club. As the Premier League note, this allowed City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend. Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'. The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'. It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018 when it won eight major trophies. Had City reported accurately 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'. The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker. Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'.

Sports.title: An evening with Saracens' 'wine consultant' Brendan Venter: His regret over title-change saga, the club's sacking of the player involved in melee with England cricketers - and plans to replace Owen Farrell and Co
Sports.content:
Brendan Venter, glass in hand, is holding court. Saracens’ ‘wine consultant’ is undoubtedly in his element as he paces around the home changing room at StoneX Stadium, discussing his favourite subject away from rugby. ‘The object of the evening is to have an adventure and to hopefully have some of you fall in love with wine,’ explains the knowledgeable South African, whose audience includes his players Owen Farrell, Ben Earl and George Martin and members of the media, including Daily Mail Sport. ‘Cabernet Sauvignon is the base of most Bordeaux wines,’ Venter continues. ‘In rugby terms, it’s the set-piece and defence of a team. The basics. If you don't have that, you have nothing. The Merlot is softer, more feministic. It's the attack. Cabernet Franc is the kicking – getting the team in the right areas. Then we have two others – Petit Verdot and Malbec. Those two are "the s*** people don’t see” – the things that keep groups and teams together.”’ Now back working in Prem Rugby for a second time, Venter, 56, is trying to perfect what he calls his ‘Saracens blend’. Saracens changed boss Brendan Venter’s job title to ‘head of rugby culture and wine consultant’ in a bid to ensure the eccentric South African could avoid undertaking media duties The Saracens director and the club have embraced the joke after coming under criticism His ideal recipe for success, as he outlines, is made crystal clear to the likes of Farrell and Co on a poster on the wall of the entrance of their home changing room at the StoneX. It was there where Venter and the Saracens hierarchy of owner Dominic Silvester, chairman Neil Golding and chief executive Ed Coetzee went on the charm offensive on Tuesday night. It has been a turbulent start to the season for the London club both on and off the field. Venter’s return to replace the immensely successful Mark McCall as director of rugby was then followed by the club being fined for his eagerness to avoid media duties. Saracens subsequently changed Venter’s job title, first to ‘head of rugby culture and wine consultant' and then 'head of culture and technical director’, prompting criticism that could easily have been avoided. Earlier this month, Saracens sacked academy prospect Totoa Auvaa for his part in a street fight in St Albans, just months after he’d been embroiled in a brawl with former England cricket captain Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson. On the field, Venter has seen his team suffer disappointing defeats to Sale and Connacht. Saracens have been inconsistent. But in Venter, they have a boss who isn’t for turning. He is sticking to his guns, even if he expresses remorse over how his temporary ‘wine consultant’ appointment was handled. ‘In retrospect, I would probably have done it differently,’ he says. ‘But my motive was not to be difficult and obnoxious.’

Your browser does not support iframes.

The South African hosted a dinner party in the home dressing room, with Owen Farrell, Ben Earl and George Martin and members of the media among the audience Spending time with Venter, two things quickly become clear. He is not deliberately obtuse, nor indeed rude. Also, he really loves wine. His passion for it burns brightly as he talks, engaging the room and pouring out eight red wine samples from a table stacked with bottles. They have all come from Golding’s cellar at a not-insignificant cost. ‘It is going to be a blind tasting,’ Venter says, before turning to Farrell. ‘Why do we taste wine blind, Owen? It’s because we are so subjective as human beings. We can't help it. ‘Wine is like rugby. You can get to know it, explore it. But you’re never going to beat it. There are always better winemakers and rugby coaches than you. I know I’ll never master either!’ Silvester, Golding and Coetzee clearly have faith in Venter’s rugby knowledge, even if the man himself admits he’ll never crack the sport’s code. Saracens’ inviting of members of the media to a wine tasting night in the club’s inner sanctum saw them lean into the ‘wine consultant’ controversy. No expense was spared. Fillet steak and chips was served, followed by lemon posset. All washed down with what felt like half of Golding’s collection of reds. Bizarrely, the evening took place on the same day Silvester released a strong statement criticising a national newspaper report and defending the work of Coetzee. It felt like the dreaded managerial vote of confidence. There have been many changes in the club’s backroom team and a new wave of players is now coming through to replace those who have been Saracens, England and Lions greats – the likes of Farrell, Maro Itoje and Jamie George. It is, undoubtedly, a new era at Saracens. Though, as ever, there is only one demand – to win. ‘We need to build again,’ Venter says. ‘We were so good for so long with superstars. They’re at the end of their time and we need a new group. They’re not going to fall from the air, so we need to develop them. Losses happen. We get on with it. Totoa’s thing was really well dealt with by Ed. ‘We saw the evidence. Totoa was wrong. We’d given him a chance. It was decisive. I actually think it was a victory for the club because Ed dealt with it really well. I don’t think he could have dealt with it better.’ Saracens recently sacked academy prospect Totoa Auvaa for his part in a street fight in St Albans, just months after he’d been embroiled in a brawl with Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson Farrell, Martin and Earl were given the licence to have a glass or two of red with the media, despite the season being in its early stages. Farrell says: ‘Mark was here for a long time and now we’re looking to see where we can take it next. Brendan set his stall out very clearly with a meeting. 'It was in there (the changing room) and we did the same thing with the wine tasting and then we went out to train! He’s been very clear and it’s about what we’re doing now – not about what’s been before. ‘Of course, it's feasible to compete again. We've got a great squad at the minute. We're doing things in a bit of a different way from what we've been used to. We feel like that will benefit us in the long run and we'll get up to speed pretty quickly.’ In Tomos Williams, Martin and Alfie Barbeary, Saracens have recruited well and they are still third in the PREM table ahead of Sunday’s derby with capital rivals Harlequins. That said, there has been significant turbulence at the club in the past month, some of it self-inflicted. ‘Losses happen,’ Venter says. ‘You either learn from a loss or you cry. When we played Sale, Alex Sanderson taught us a couple of lessons. Last weekend (Connacht and former England coach) Stuart Lancaster was cleverer than us. We are a good side and we should have won that game. ‘We’ll learn from it and that’s why it’s value. We don’t see the bigger picture in rugby today. The bigger picture is developing people over a longer period to try and win a Premiership. ‘The now is the result and when you get obsessed with only this, you’ll never have a vision of having a culture. It’s just so short-sighted.’ A new wave of players is coming through to replace those who have been Saracens, England and Lions greats – the likes of Farrell (above), Maro Itoje and Jamie George Venter’s planned rotation of his side and insistence on giving youth its chance is with the long-term success of Saracens in mind. He is certainly a fascinating character – methodical, intense, passionate. But, having sipped wine with him, I have to say not unlikeable. Many perceive him as gruff and antagonistic, a perception that has been accentuated by his reluctance to do interviews in the wake of past fines for comments made to the media. It prompts an obvious next question. Does Venter want to be liked? ‘I’m really good with that. I’m not on any social media,’ he says. ‘Someone told me there was a mean article about the club. But I don’t know that. I need to respect all human beings. ‘I'm quite thick-skinned. I do so few s*** things in my life. I just don’t do them. The analogy of the taxi driver is a great one. You can get cross with them, but it’s their job to drive fast and cut you up because they want to get to where they’re going as quickly as possible for their work. ‘It’s the media’s job to be inquisitive and find stories. I used to get cross with that. It’s the same with referees. But I looked at myself and I said: “I’m being affected. It’s stealing my joy.” I’m growing as a human being. There’s no animosity. I’m super relaxed, super easy.’ And with that, his hosting duties done, Venter puts on his overcoat and cap and heads off into the night. Whatever you think of him and his PREM return, one thing is for sure. With Venter around, things are never dull.

Sports.title: Where Jimmy Anderson ranks in England's top 10 greatest cricketers of all time, by LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Where Jimmy Anderson ranks in England's top 10 greatest cricketers of all time, by LAWRENCE BOOTH

Sir James Anderson is set to retire from cricket after Lancashire refused to offer him a new contract for 2027, ending a glittering and record-breaking career for one of England's finest ever players.

Anderson, 44, tops England's wickets list for Tests (704) and ODIs (269) after representing his country from 2002 to 2024.

But in light of his retirement, as revealed on Wednesday by Daily Mail Sport, where does the 'Burnley Express' rank in the all-time pantheon of great England cricketers?

Here, LAWRENCE BOOTH picks his top 10 men ever to pull on the shirt.

1. Ian Botham

Tests: 102, Runs: 5,200 at 33.54, Wickets: 383 at 28.4

If it weren’t enough that just two bowlers – Jimmy Anderson and Stuart Broad – took more Test wickets for England than Botham’s 383, he also scored 14 hundreds, and is synonymous with the most outrageous series of all time: the 1981 Ashes.

How good was he in his pomp? Put it this way: in the 1980 Jubilee Test against India in Mumbai, he took six for 58, then scored 114 out of 296, and finished with seven for 48 from 26 tireless overs.

He was England’s man mountain.

Ian Botham was England's man mountain - and a player who could win a series all by himself

2. Jack Hobbs

Tests: 61, Runs: 5,410 at 56.94

Long before Sachin Tendulkar became known as the ‘Little Master’, Hobbs was the original ‘Master’, an opening batsman of such skill and determination that he scored 12 hundreds against Australia, an Ashes record for England.

He scored roughly half his 199 first-class centuries after the age of 40, and was still playing Tests at 46. The Oval, where he scored a good chunk of the 43,554 first-class runs he made for Surrey, has suitably elegant gates named after him.

Jack Hobbs (left) walking out to bat for Surrey - he was cricket's original 'Master'

3. WG Grace

Tests: 22, Runs: 1,098 at 32.29, Wickets: 9 at 26.22

WG wasn’t everyone’s cup of tea: he employed gamesmanship before it was fashionable, and may have hoodwinked an umpire or two.

But, during a first-class career stretching from 1865 to 1908, he was England’s first sporting celebrity, and so far ahead of his cricketing peers as to render null and void the usual objection that he would have struggled in today’s game.

He played both forward and back at a time when batsmen did only one or the other, scored over 54,000 runs and took more than 2,800 wickets. A giant, no matter the era.

4. Joe Root

Tests: 169, Runs: 14,287 at 50.45, Wickets: 74 at 48.09

The only name on this list still playing, Root needs just 1,644 more runs to overtake Tendulkar and become Test cricket’s most prolific scorer of all time.

His 41 red-ball hundreds are eight more than anyone else has managed for England, and he averages over 50 in both Tests and one-day internationals.

Oh, and he’s just become captain again for the second time, answering England’s SOS after the chaotic retirement of Ben Stokes.

Joe Root's 41 Test hundreds are eight more than anyone else has managed for England, and he averages over 50 in both Tests and one-day internationals

5. James Anderson

Tests: 188, Wickets: 704 at 26.45

No fast bowler of any nation has more Test wickets than Anderson’s 704, and only two spinners – Muttiah Muralitharan and Shane Warne – are ahead of him on the list.

Other bowlers were faster, but few were more skilful at working out a batsman, then working him over. In Asia, he took 92 wickets at 27, settling the argument that he needed English conditions to thrive.

Now that he has called it a day, taking 1,193 first-class wickets with him, the leading current bowler is South Africa and Essex spinner Simon Harmer, with 1,068.

No fast bowler of any nation has more Test wickets than Jimmy Anderson’s 704, and only two spinners – Muttiah Muralitharan and Shane Warne – are ahead of him on the list

6. Walter Hammond

Tests: 85, Runs: 7,249 at 58.45, Wickets: 83 at 37.80

But for Don Bradman, Hammond would have been the undisputed No1 batsman in the world for the decade before the Second World War, and possibly for a few years after it.

His cover drive remains one of the great exclamation marks of English strokeplay, and he once averaged 563 in a two-match series in New Zealand.

On the 1928-29 Ashes tour, he scored four hundreds among his 905 runs – still an England record for a Test series.

But for Don Bradman, Walter Hammond (right) would have been the undisputed No1 batsman in the world for the decade before the Second World War, and possibly for a few years after it

7. Len Hutton

Tests: 79, Runs: 6,971 at 56.67

Hutton was the last England player to hold the individual Test record for runs in an innings, scoring 364 against Australia at the Oval in 1938, and one of only three English captains – along with Mike Brearley and Andrew Strauss – to win the Ashes both home and away.

As a Test opener he made 6,721 runs at 56: no one of any nationality has made more at a higher average.

Had World War Two not intervened, he would probably have broken all sorts of records, and he was not deterred by an injury in the gym which, after surgery, meant his left arm was two inches shorter than his right.

Len Hutton (right) walks out to bat against Australia at the Oval in 1938. He would go on to break the world record for most runs in a Test innings, with 364

8. SF Barnes

Tests: 27, Wickets: 189 at 16.43

Even now, well over 100 years since he signed off from Test cricket with a 14-wicket haul at Durban, Barnes’s figures take the breath away: 189 wickets at 16, including 49 at 10 in that final series in South Africa.

He was not fast, but deadly accurate, and he would snap at anyone who suggested he bowled cutters: ‘I spun it!’

He was an awkward customer, and preferred outsourcing himself to the highest bidders in the northern leagues rather than waste too much time in county cricket. But what a bowler.

9. Alastair Cook

Tests: 161, Runs: 12,472 at 45.35

It’s tempting to wonder how close Cook might have come to Tendulkar had he not quit Test cricket at the age of 33, especially after he signed off with scores of 71 and 147 against India at the Oval in 2018.

That left him with 12,472 Test runs, second in England’s pantheon and over 3,500 clear of third-placed Graham Gooch, once his mentor.

Cook’s talent lay in the marshalling of unglamorous resources: a strong back-foot game, a clip off the hip, and unbreakable concentration. His 766 runs at 127 helped England win in Australia in 2010-11 for the only time since the late 1980s.

Alastair Cook's 766 runs at 127 helped England win in Australia in 2010-11 for the only time since the late 1980s

Stuart Broad (right) sneaks into the top 10 – not only by sheer weight of numbers but also because he turned it on when it mattered

10. Stuart Broad

Tests: 167, Runs: 3,662 at 18.03, Wickets: 604 at 27.68

With apologies to Ken Barrington, Denis Compton and Fred Trueman, Broad sneaks into the top 10 – not only by sheer weight of numbers (only Anderson has more than his 604 Test wickets) but also because he turned it on when it mattered.

After announcing himself with an Ashes-clinching five-for at the Oval in 2009, his eight for 15 against Australia on his home ground at Trent Bridge in 2015 is arguably the most memorable spell of fast bowling in England’s Test history.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher calls Bruno Fernandes a DISGRACE for 'throwing Michael Carrick under the bus'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher calls Bruno Fernandes a DISGRACE for 'throwing Michael Carrick under the bus'

Jamie Carragher has launched a scathing attack on Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, branding the Portuguese a 'disgrace' for his post-match comments following the club's 4-1 defeat to Como

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher criticised Bruno Fernandes after his post-match remarks

Jamie Carragher has unleashed scathing criticism of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes - labelling the Portuguese midfielder a 'disgrace.' The former Liverpool defender defended embattled head coach Michael Carrick and commended the 45-year-old for responding to the skipper following their 4-1 hammering at the hands of Como.

‌



‌



Carragher suggested that Fernandes' explosive remarks came after he was left 'embarrassed' by his 66th-minute substitution during their humiliation in Northern Italy. Nico Paz shone brightest as his double inspired Cesc Fabregas' side to a memorable victory and intensified the scrutiny on the Premier League-winning midfielder.

‌



The United skipper joined Lisandro Martinez in delivering a shock statement during post-match media appearances. Fernandes directed criticism towards Carrick, pinning responsibility for the loss on Ruben Amorim's successor.

‌



Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer twist as Antonio Conte conditions emerge READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

In an impassioned outburst, the footballer-turned-pundit speaking on CBS Sports accused Fernandes of 'killing' his teammates and being the reason for United's inability to press collectively. He said: "No (not a good look). We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy and for Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really.

"When you think about last season he got Player of the Season, that was off the back of Michael Carrick becoming manager, he wouldn't have got that without Michael Carrick because he got put back in his rightful position and went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer."

‌



"But in terms of attitude, the way he goes about things, is not right at all. He's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed by the manager because he's been brought off. When he talks about pressing, man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press.

"Because he does things for the crowd, I commentate on games and he runs all over and plays like a kid in the schoolyard, he plays for the supporters, it looks like he's working hard, he's not, he's killing the team doing it. He's not playing in a successful era for Manchester United.

‌



Carragher continued: "Years ago, there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man United because he played for the club, he didn't throw the manager or the players under the bus.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes questioned Man United's coaching staff's decision

‌



"He kept fighting for Manchester United and watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace, calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch.

"Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should do."

‌



Carragher acknowledged that a change in the dugout is required at Old Trafford following the loss, which extended their winless run to seven matches. During his post-match media briefing, Carrick hit back at Fernandes by suggesting that 'if you don't run forward and back, you aren't going to win.'

The response earned praise for Carrick, with Carragher emerging as an unexpected supporter as he confessed to feeling sympathy for the manager.

‌



"Isn't it funny, how many managers has Bruno Fernandes had? So every single manager doesn't have a philosophy? How many managers are we on now? Five?" said the former Liverpool man.

‌



"It's an easy thing to say, Fabregas is the best new thing in managerial teams but Man United is rotten from top to bottom. Not just the manager, the whole club, who has got the answers?

"We comment on it all the time. Are we ever right really? No one else seems to. There's no doubt the manager needs to be changed now, this can't go on for a club of this stature but I'm glad Michael Carrick come out and said that about Michael Carrick. They don't run.

‌



"What he did last season, no one proclaims Michael Carrick is one of the greatest managers in Europe but what he did was come in and helped his own football club, he was out of work, come in and done amazing, the only reason they're in the Champions League is because of Carrick.

"He got them in there, the reason they got another £100m to £150m, no one thought they'd be there. I feel sorry for him a little bit. It's not working out and it needs to be changed.

"I'm delighted he brought him off and a pop back because that what they need some of them players."

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has commented on reports regarding one potential transfer target for the club as his coaching methods are compared to those of predecessor Arne Slot

‌

“And there has to be respect between clubs and well, if you’ll allow me, I don’t have my opinion, obviously, but I prefer not to comment, not about players who aren’t from Liverpool."

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer twist as Antonio Conte conditions emerge

Manchester United could look to strengthen a problem position at left-back, as Antonio Conte continues to be linked with the club

View 2 Images Lewis Hall is a long-term target of Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United's tough run of games continues against Bournemouth on Sunday, with Michael Carrick desperately needing three points. United have gone five games without a win in the Premier League, leaving them 13th in the table, closer to the relegation zone than the Champions League spots.

‌



‌



The pressure is on Carrick amid speculation he could be sacked if results don't improve, and soon. Ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash away to Como, he had to fend off questions about former United boss Erik ten Hag's recent comments about the club.

‌



The Dutchman accused United's ownership of broken promises and said there was a toxic atmosphere within the squad in a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic.

‌



Carrick has also had to contend with an injury crisis, which left him without nine first-team players for the game against Como. As United prepare for a return to Premier League action, here's a round-up of the latest news from Old Trafford…

Man Utd transfer plans being put in place as injury timeline emerges for Benjamin Sesko READ MORE :

United back in for Hall

United are reportedly ready to revive their interest in Newcastle's Lewis Hall. There was disappointment in the summer when the club failed to land a replacement - or at least an alternative - to Luke Shaw.

United wanted Hall but Newcastle were unwilling to sell and then tied the full-back to a new long-term contract, which appeared to make him unattainable. However, according to The i Paper, United will make a fresh bid to sign the 22-year-old, who, it is claimed, is open to moving to Old Trafford.

‌



The same report says United are interested in another left-back, Adrien Truffert, who is expected to leave Bournemouth next summer amid significant interest in the French defender.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Conte conditions

Antonio Conte, a contender to replace Carrick if United decide to make a change, has reportedly set out his conditions amid interest from Juventus. The Italians are the other club being linked with Conte, who is a free agent after leaving Napoli in the summer.

However, according to TMW Radio in Italy, Conte wants specific guarantees 'for the next few seasons' from Juve before returning to the Turin giants, whom he managed between 2011 and 2014. The report adds that if those assurances, which it hints are about rebuilding the squad, aren't met then he is likely to opt for United instead.

‌



Conte recently gave an interview in which he said he can see his next job being with a fallen giant, with United and Juve both falling into that category. He told The Athletic: "There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history.

View 2 Images Antonio Conte is ready for his next big job (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more. Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete."

Juve are currently managed by Luciano Spalletti, who, like Carrick, is under mounting pressure following Sunday's 3-0 home defeat to Lazio, which left them eighth in Serie A.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes comments in extraordinary press conference
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes comments in extraordinary press conference

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has responded to some veiled criticism from captain Bruno Fernandes in the wake of the Red Devils' humbling by Como

View 2 Images Carrick hit back at Fernandes in an extraordinary press conference (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick hit back at captain Bruno Fernandes after the Manchester United skipper blasted a 'decision from staff' following the Red Devils' lamentable defeat at Como.

‌



‌



United were hammered 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' side in a result that has plunged Carrick's future into doubt. His team have won just twice in 11 games so far this term.

‌



Fernandes said the coaching staff had opted not to adopt a man-to-man marking policy in the game, suggesting it contributed to the heavy defeat.

‌



"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave a bit of space in behind and then try to get the ball in the first moment to wait for them, to give them the ball," the Portuguese captain told TNT Sports.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"But sometimes when you give too much the ball [away] to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot which makes people get frustrated.

"And then, when we recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work."

‌



But Carrick has hit back, suggesting Fernandes' comments are not accurate. "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that," he said.

"And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

‌



Carrick took aim at his side's effort, while accepting the buck stops with him.

View 2 Images Fernandes had aimed a veiled dig at Carrick

‌



"We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure," he added.

"It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me.

‌



"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters.

"I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

Sports.title: Man City charges: Fresh investigation confirmed as EFL 'ready to agree' punishment
Sports.content:
All the latest news on Manchester City's guilty verdict ahead of their appeal hearing, with the club now expected to receive a 'huge points deduction' and a fine

At the end of September, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18. It was revealed that City had artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through so-called 'sham' sponsorship deals.

City, however, have vehemently denied any wrongdoing and submitted an appeal against the ruling on October 1. In an official statement, the club maintained they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and claim they possess "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their position.

Nevertheless, The Daily Mail have reported that the 'most likely' outcome is a three-pronged punishment for City, with the club expected to receive a 'points deduction which will guarantee relegation' and a 'huge fine'.

It's suggested that the sanction could include an additional points deduction that would virtually ensure City remain in the Championship for at least one further season, though the EFL would not be compelled to accept that penalty for one of their clubs. However, it's understood they would be prepared to agree to the points deduction.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes points finger at 'decision from Man Utd staff' after Como thrashing
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes points finger at 'decision from Man Utd staff' after Como thrashing

Manchester United were humiliated by Como in the Champions League, suffering back-to-back defeats in the competition

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes speaking to TNT Sports

Bruno Fernandes has questioned Manchester United's coaching staff's decision not to adopt a man-to-man pressing approach during their humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. Michael Carrick's side endured a nightmare start, conceding inside the opening two minutes before finding themselves 3-0 down before the hour mark.

‌



‌



Nico Paz struck twice, while Anastasios Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon also got on the scoresheet to pile further pressure on the Red Devils. Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute, but the damage had already been done.

‌



United's travelling supporters had seen enough by the 76th minute, with some spotted leaving the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium shortly after their side conceded a fourth goal. The emphatic victory will go down as a historic night for Cesc Fabregas' side, who secured their second win of the Champions League campaign in stunning fashion.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Erik ten Hag identifies the off-pitch area Man Utd lag behind rivals with INEOS dig READ MORE :

Carrick's men were dominated from start to finish, with the United boss going over to apologise to the travelling supporters immediately after full-time. Speaking after the match, Fernandes was asked about the lack of cohesion as a group after he also endured a tough evening, having been hooked after just 66 minutes.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave a bit of space in behind and then try to get the ball in the first moment to wait for them, to give them the ball," the Portuguese captain told TNT Sports.

‌



"But sometimes when you give too much the ball [away] to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot which makes people get frustrated. And then, when we recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work."

When asked whether the decision not to press had ultimately cost the team, the midfielder added: "That's on the manager and the staff to see. That's not on me, I just said that I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure.

‌



"Try to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable as they did to us. Their centre-back was coming to mark me all the way into my own half. I think sometimes we had to do that as a team and we were not really able to do it."

On the match, Fernandes reiterated: "Obviously it's not the first time, and I think again. we started with the wrong foot - they scored very early. Not much pressure on the ball, not really many good moments without the ball. It's many things not going our way.

‌



View 2 Images It was a tough night for Man United

"Conceding the goal very early, makes us feel going into the game already in a mood for defeat and it's very difficult to get out of that at the moment, without being ourselves and trying to push and be brave, trying to have the ball."

‌



Ahead of the match, Carrick faced questions about his future but insisted he had the full backing of the club's hierarchy.

"I don't need any reassurance," Carrick told a news conference on Tuesday. "It's pretty clear. I know the role, I know my responsibilities.

‌



"I don't need anyone else to tell me that or tell me when it's going well or when it needs to be better. I know that myself. I know the realities and I've got no problem with that.

"I know we've got to win football games for everything to flow and everything to fall into place. That's the great thing about it, you know? We can do something about it."

‌



Pressure is mounting with Carrick's future hanging in the balance after United managed just two wins across the Champions League and Premier League so far this season.

Sunday's home clash against Bournemouth now looms as a potentially defining moment for the under-fire manager.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr 'seriously considered' Arsenal transfer as agent lifts lid on failed move
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr 'seriously considered' Arsenal transfer as agent lifts lid on failed move

Vinicius Jr stalled on putting pen to paper on a new contract with Real Madrid which led to Arsenal making an approach for his services over the summer

View 2 Images Vinicius 'seriously considered' Arsenal's approach (Image: Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty Images)

Real Madrid superstar Vininicus Jr 'seriously considered' moving to Arsenal in the summer before penning a new deal with Los Blancos.

‌



‌



The Brazilian stalled on signing fresh terms at the Bernabeu leading Arsenal to make an approach for his services. But he eventually committed his future to Real with a new £480,000-a-week deal until 2032.

‌



His agent, Michael Yormark, has now revealed just how close Vinicius came to joining the Gunners. “You saw the news; Arsenal was very involved. They were very aggressive," he told SportsBoom.

‌



“But Vini’s heart is in Madrid, that’s where he’s always wanted to be, and that’s where he is, and that’s where he hopes to be for the rest of his career.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“I don’t think there was ever a question. Did he ever seriously consider Arsenal? I mean of course. When a team like Arsenal rolls out the red carpet for you and makes you feel really wanted, then obviously you have to listen.

“But he’s where he wants to be and we’re happy, he’s there. It’s not often that an athlete gets to start their professional journey at one team, and end it there as well.

‌



“He started his journey at 18, he’s 26 now. He’s already won so many trophies. To be at one club, the best club in the world, for your entire career, that would be very special.”

View 2 Images Vinicius penned a new deal with Los Blancos (Image: Getty )

‌



Yormark is the president of Roc Nation Sports International and Grant Veitch, a director with the same agency, added: "There were other opportunities that arose [for Vinicius to leave in the summer].

“But I think the level of comfort he has, and him already being a star at Real Madrid, it kept him there, and he wanted to stay.

Article continues below

“You can branch out, but I think the comfort level of him being there since such a young age and wanting to build up his reputation and wanting to continue that and win more titles with Real Madrid, that’s the main reason he’s stayed.”

Sports.title: John Gosden performs U-turn to rule Ombudsman out of Breeders' Cup Turf
Sports.content:
John Gosden performs U-turn to rule Ombudsman out of Breeders' Cup Turf

John Gosden has decided against running Ombudsman in the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland, opting instead for a tentative plan to target the Japan Cup in November after the horse's Champion Stakes win at Ascot

View 2 Images William Buick riding Ombudsman (all blue) to win the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

Ombudsman, brilliant winner of the Champion Stakes at Ascot, will not have his swansong at the Breeders' Cup after a U-turn by trainer John Gosden.

‌



‌



In the wake of the Godolphin horse's defeat of last year's world's best racehorse, Calandagan at Ascot, Gosden had indicated that Ombudsman would tackle 1m4f for the first time in the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland, before probably heading to stud next year.

‌



However, in an abrupt change of mind, the Newmarket trainer has now concluded that the race, 14 days after the Champion Stakes, will come too soon, and he is now floating the idea of a tilt at the Japan Cup instead.

‌



Gosden said: "It's very simple, the horse ran four days ago at Ascot and he would have to work tomorrow, get on a plane for a cross-Atlantic flight, quarantine and it's not fair to ask him to do that then ask him to run back within 14 days with a long journey in the middle.

"In fairness, we felt having discussed it with everyone, we shouldn't be trying to do that with him after he ran such a brilliant race in the Champion Stakes and we could consider the Japan Cup now.

‌



"There's plenty of time to that now in November, but to rush him over to America and put him through that we didn't think was in the best interests of the horse."

View 2 Images John Gosden: considering the Japan Cup for Ombudsman (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

Article continues below

He went on: "Japan would be a tentative plan and no more than that. It's the only other race this year he could really run in and an important international race, so to that extent it's a tentative plan.

"After that we're probably talking retirement and it would have been nice to go to America, we wanted to go and do it because we like the Breeders' Cup a lot, but the horse has to come first."

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
