Sports.title: Formula 1’s move to shorter grands prix in 2027 will not be permanent | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 will reinstate full grand prix distances in 2028 after shortening the races this year, the FIA has confirmed.

The championship announced last month it will cut 15 kilometres from the standard grand prix distance next year as a result of the new fuel flow limits which will come into force. Shortening the grand prix distances will reduce the number of components teams need to redesign next year.

The shortened distance of 290 kilometres will apply for all grands prix except Monaco, which has run to a shorter distance of 260km for many years and will continue to.

However the first edition of the 2027 Formula 1 Sporting Regulations published by the FIA notes the previous distance will apply again from 2028. “The distance of the race [i.e. grand prix], from the start signal referred to in Article B5.7.2 to the end-of-session signal referred to in Article B5.16.1, shall be equal to the least number of complete laps which exceed a distance of 305km,” it states.

Formula 1

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Fired On His Day Off: Bradley Shreds Shakur Stevenson Over Lost Zuffa Contract
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley pulled no punches on his channel when breaking down how Shakur Stevenson lost his Zuffa Boxing contract. According to Bradley, Shakur fumbled massive money because he failed to deliver the one matchup the promotion actually cared about: Devin Haney.

“Shakur and his team, they thought that they was going to pull off a lick,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “They was just like, ‘Oh yeah, we got these stupid people up here. They don’t know nothing about boxing.’”

Bradley believes Shakur and his handlers completely misread the room, assuming they were dealing with naive outsiders whom they could easily manipulate. In reality, Zuffa’s willingness to spend fifteen million dollars per fight was meant strictly for marquee events, not hand-picked opposition like Gary Antuanne Russell.

“The fight that Zuffa wanted was Haney-Shakur. Period,” Bradley said.

He also mocked how readily Zuffa allowed Shakur to leave his contract, imagining the company responding, “We good.”

“How big of a damn diva you got to be to get released on your contract?” Bradley asked.

Bradley highlighted the absurdity of the split, pointing out how rare it is for a fighter to get released from a massive deal without ever stepping into the ring. He called out Shakur’s team for managing his career poorly, arguing that letting an eight-figure bag slip away was inexcusable.

While Bradley noted that prolonged weight squabbles and promotional moves damaged the negotiations on both sides, he laid the ultimate fault on Shakur’s reluctance to take real risks.

“All this was done because you afraid to lose that O,” he said. “It’s about protecting that damn O, bro.”

Now planning to launch his own promotional outfit, Shakur faces a stark reality. Finding financial backers willing to offer that caliber of purse without top-tier opponents is nearly impossible. As Bradley put it, someone has to put up the money, and Zuffa was ready to do that, but Shakur was unwilling to fight the opponent required to earn it.

When an entity like Zuffa comes into boxing with massive venture backing, they aren’t paying a fighter $15 million a fight out of altruism—they are paying for immediate, marquee box-office events to establish their footprint.

Shakur made three miscalculated moves. For starters, treating Silicon Valley/UFC money like naive marks. Bradley’s phrase that they thought they could “pull off a lick” was dead-on.

Shakur’s camp operated like they could sign the deal, dictate terms from high above, and then demand eight-figure checks to fight safe stylistic matchups like Gary Antuanne Russell. They forgot that Zuffa’s entire business model is built on rigid control, star matchups, and high returns.

Then he got dragged into prolonged posturing over weight. The nine-month negotiation saga over whether they’d fight at 144, 145, or 147 pounds drained every ounce of momentum. By letting the fight stall over a couple of pounds, and then throwing Keyshawn Davis into the mandatory picture as an artificial wedge, they gave Devin and Bill Haney the opening to outmaneuver them entirely and do their own business with DAZN.

Prioritizing the “0” over generational exposure: At 27 or 28, in the prime of his physical career, Shakur had a direct pipeline to beat Haney, fight Ryan Garcia, and cement himself as the premier American star of this era. Instead, the hyper-defensive mindset inside the ring mirrored his mindset outside of it: risk minimization at all costs.

Getting released from an eight-figure contract without ever throwing a single punch under the banner, literally getting “fired on your day off” while only doing a broadcast stint, is almost unheard of at that level of boxing.

Betting on yourself only works if the market is willing to pay what you think you’re worth. Now Shakur is left trying to build his own promotional company in a landscape where broadcast money is tightening, and network buyers aren’t handing out $15 million paydays for sparring sessions.

Sports.title: Arnold Barboza Hints At Devin Haney Title Shot
Sports.content:
Arnold Barboza Jr. dropped word on social media that a massive welterweight title opportunity just landed in his lap on short notice. While he confirmed that 147 pounds is locked in with a belt on the line, he kept the identity of his opponent quiet for now.

Speculation immediately involved Devin Haney after Haney’s anticipated matchup with Shakur Stevenson fell apart. Barboza’s remarks point to a fast-developing opening, even if ink has not officially met paper yet.

“I got some news today. It’s a blessing. I don’t know how real it is, but it sounds pretty real. It might be a big fight sooner than expected,” Barboza said on social media. “I’ll be stepping in at the last minute on some s***, but I don’t know where it’s going to be at, but it’s soon.”

The tight calendar creates the biggest hurdle. Barboza appears fully ready to sign before even knowing the host city, but world championship bouts offer zero room for entering camp cold. Securing an unexpected offer represents one hurdle; having the necessary weeks to dial in a precise tactical blueprint presents an entirely separate challenge.

If Haney ends up standing across the ring, Barboza faces an elite defensive technician. Taking on Haney demands an answer for his distance control, lead hand control, and inside tie ups. Simply tracking him across the canvas without cutting the ring effectively will turn the contest into a frustrating chase.

“A lot sooner than expected. Not no next year fight. A couple of weeks soon. Yeah, I’m fighting at 147. Yeah, it’ll be for a belt. We got to go for legacy,” Barboza said.

Teofimo Lopez also figures heavily into Barboza’s long-range calculations. Barboza sees capturing a 147-pound crown as his quickest ticket to securing a second chance against Lopez after coming up short in their junior welterweight clash.

“It’s not a rematch with Teo. Not yet. I got to win this belt to rematch him,” Barboza admitted.

Holding a world title strap provides massive leverage at the negotiating table. The immediate task requires transforming the sudden opening into an executed contract, setting up a targeted training block, and verifying the sanctioning body timeline.

Sports.title: DAZN Team May Call Canelo-Mbilli From London
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli could fight in Riyadh on October 31, with DAZN’s broadcast team following the action from a studio in London. The potential arrangement adds another question to a card already approaching under difficult circumstances.

Dan Rafael reports that the team is likely to call the event remotely if it goes ahead. His report leaves both points conditional: the card proceeding and the commentators working outside Saudi Arabia.

“Per sources, if #CaneloMbilli goes forward Oct. 31 in Riyadh, the likelihood is that the DAZN broadcast team will not be ringside and will call the card remotely from a studio in London,” Rafael wrote on X.

DAZN’s likely move speaks for itself. Calling one of the year’s biggest fights from television monitors thousands of miles away suggests the broadcast team wants no part of the danger in Riyadh. Promotional talk about the event going ahead cannot erase the attacks on the city’s international airport.

It also creates an awkward contrast. Commentators would work from the safety of a London studio, while Canelo, Mbilli and the undercard fighters would be expected to fly to Riyadh, attend media events and fight. If the risk is enough to keep the broadcast team away, the fighters have every reason to question why they should be there.

The background explains everything. Dan Rafael reported earlier on missile strikes and drone activity aimed at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, even while noting Canelo planned to go ahead anyway. Those strikes turned travel safety and the host city into the dominant story leading up to the bout.

A London crew can watch the live monitors, but calling an event off a monitor is never the same. Commentators lose their direct line of sight between broadcast angles. They miss corner chaos, subtle crowd shifts, and whatever happens outside the camera frame, leaving them watching the exact same feed fans see on their couches.

That is a massive drop in quality for a pay-per-view centered on the sport’s biggest earner. Calling action from ringside lets commentators catch real impacts, subtle cornerman instructions, and shifts in body language that cameras and boom mics miss entirely.

Canelo is penciled in to challenge Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title. The sanctioning body still lists October 31 in Riyadh on DAZN.

The card needs an official word on how the broadcast will work. Rafael’s reporting suggests fight week will look bizarre, even if both guys walk to the ring on schedule.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Calls Sebastian Fundora Too Small
Sports.content:
Jaron Ennis laughed off Sebastian Fundora’s knockout claims, calling the towering champion “too small” to back up his words. Ennis is eyeing Fundora down the line, but he’s making sure business with Josh Kelly gets handled first.

That comment flips the script on Fundora. Opponents usually spend training camp obsessing over his massive reach, but Ennis seems far more eager to exploit openings than worry about incoming fire.

“He too small. He not big enough,” Ennis said to YSM Sports Media when told about Fundora’s knockout comments. “But we focused on Josh Kelly, and that’s the main focus, main target right now. We’ll talk about him later on.”

Ennis kept a close eye on Fundora’s clash with Ermal Hadribeaj, scouting for future business rather than just watching for fun.

“Definitely watching to pick him apart,” Ennis said. “Just to see what he got, and it’s what I’ve been knew.”

Fundora didn’t dial back his confidence at the post-fight presser either. When reporters brought up potential bouts with Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr., he insisted he’d halt both.

“If it was those guys, I’d still knock them out,” Fundora said. “These guys can’t hurt me.”

That confidence would face a different examination against Ennis. Choosing to fight inside is one thing against Hadribeaj; giving Ennis opportunities at close range would require Fundora to account for his speed and combinations.

Ennis even took a jab at the Hadribeaj stoppage, arguing the challenger beat the count right as the bell sounded. Regardless, he made it clear he wanted Fundora looking sharp so there are zero asterisks later.

“I don’t want nobody to say nothing,” Ennis said. “No excuses.”

Kelly is the obstacle between that talk and a possible Fundora fight. Ennis described him as a “sharp” and “smart” fighter. Beating him must come before Ennis can turn his confidence against Fundora into something more substantial.

Ennis is spotting the exact same tactical flaw everyone else saw against Hadribeaj: Fundora simply cannot resist fighting like a phone booth brawler. Calling a 6’6″ fighter with an 86-inch reach “too small” sounds bizarre on the surface, but Ennis is talking about physical density and ring presence, not height.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Claims Floyd Mayweather Title Fight Agreement
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia claims he and Floyd Mayweather have agreed to fight for the WBC welterweight title, putting a championship label on a matchup that looks more like a celebrity event than serious business at 147.

The selling point is obvious: Garcia gets a chance to put the first loss on Mayweather’s professional record. Whether beating a 49-year-old version of Floyd would prove much about Ryan’s ability is another question.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia posted on X. “But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight.”

Garcia added: “147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world. 50-0 vs The current champ.”

That is Garcia announcing an agreement. His post does not provide a date, venue, or broadcaster, and it does not establish that the WBC has approved Mayweather as a title challenger. Those details still need to follow before this can be treated as a confirmed championship fight.

As a commercial idea, it is easy to understand. Mayweather’s undefeated record gives the promotion something to sell beyond the usual exhibition routine. Ryan would be chasing the “0,” while Floyd would be selling the possibility that he can still beat a much younger champion.

As a title defense, it is a circus.

Mayweather’s reputation was earned against elite fighters over a long career. That reputation does not tell us what he can do at 49 against a current welterweight champion. Putting his record on the line would make the result official, but it would not turn back the clock.

Garcia would also leave himself open to an obvious criticism. Beat Floyd, and he has beaten a retired great approaching 50. Struggle with him, and the questions about Ryan become considerably louder.

There will be people willing to buy it. Two famous names and the possibility of Mayweather finally losing are enough to draw attention beyond boxing’s regular audience.

That is the appeal Garcia is selling. The WBC belt adds decoration, but the attraction is celebrity, money, and a famous unbeaten record.

Sanctioning this as an official WBC welterweight title defense would make a complete joke of the belt and freeze out actual contenders at 147. If two massive names want an unsanctioned exhibition to generate huge pay-per-view numbers, boxing fans understand the drill.

Celebrity events happen all the time now. Slapping an authentic world championship onto it crosses the line from entertainment into parody. Mayweather turns 50 next February and has not fought in a sanctioned professional bout since 2017. He is not ranked by the WBC.

Handing him an immediate shot at a real crown purely because of his fame insults every active fighter grinding through eliminators for a mandatory spot. For Garcia, putting the belt up brings zero boxing credit. If he blows out a 49-year-old retired legend, nobody takes it seriously as a legitimate championship victory.

If he looks bad or gets touched up by Floyd, critics will tear him apart. Keeping it as an exhibition protects the credibility of the sanctioning body, keeps the division moving, and lets fans enjoy the spectacle for what it really is. Turning it into an official title fight cheapens the entire sport.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Could Fight Four Times In 2027
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma could box four times in 2027, with promoter Frank Warren targeting a January return to give the heavyweight an early start on a busy year.

Warren wants at least three appearances, though fitting in a fourth will depend on the opposition. No opponent or venue has been announced for Itauma’s next fight.

“I would like him to have a minimum of three fights, maybe four if we can fit them in, depending on the opposition as well, of course,” Warren told BoxNation.

That last qualification leaves room for the schedule to change. Four fights would give Itauma regular work, but the value of that activity will come from who Warren puts in front of him. An opponent who makes him solve different problems could provide more than another quick finish.

Warren expects to reveal the next step shortly.

“I think we’ll be sometime next week, towards the end of next week, announcing something, but he’ll be fighting very early next year, probably in January,” he said.

January remains a target rather than a confirmed booking. Still, getting Itauma out that early would leave Warren enough room to spread three more appearances across the remainder of 2027, provided the fights and recovery periods allow it.

The opponent announcement will tell us more about the ambition behind that schedule. Warren offered no names and made no commitment to a world title fight during this interview. His comments were about getting Itauma into the ring regularly.

There is also a practical balance to find. As the opposition improves, fights can require longer preparation and leave less room for a quick turnaround. Warren’s preference for three, with four possible, gives him flexibility without committing Itauma to dates before the opponents are secured.

A busy calendar is a reasonable starting point. The next question is whether those appearances move Itauma closer to the heavyweights he eventually needs to beat.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol vs Callum Smith Gets DAZN Confirmation
Sports.content:
DAZN has officially confirmed its coverage of Dmitry Bivol’s December 12 title defense against Callum Smith in Yekaterinburg, Russia, where the Briton will challenge for the WBA, IBF and WBO light heavyweight belts.

The fight was announced on October 12, with DAZN already identified as the broadcaster. Wednesday’s promotional post provides the platform’s own confirmation, although it adds no new date, venue or opponent.

“An unmissable world title unification between Dmitry Bivol & Callum Smith lands on DAZN,” the broadcaster posted.

Bivol will defend his three belts at the UMMC Arena against Smith, who gets an opportunity to become a two-division world champion. Winning those titles requires solving a difficult boxing puzzle on the champion’s home turf.

Smith’s power gives him a threat if he can get close enough to use it. Bivol’s footwork and quick combinations can leave opponents losing rounds while trying to get into punching position. Smith cannot afford to follow him around without producing enough offense.

His prolonged absence has also taken some of the interest out of this fight. Smith’s February 2025 victory over Joshua Buatsi gave him something to build on, but fans will have waited almost 22 months to see him fight again by December 12.

That layoff was not entirely by choice. Smith was scheduled to defend his WBO interim title against David Morrell on April 18 in Liverpool before a training camp injury forced him out less than two weeks before the event. The fight never happened.

The injury explains the canceled return, but it cannot restore the attention lost during his absence. The Buatsi victory has faded into the background, leaving Smith without a recent performance to get fans talking about his chances against Bivol.

There is a sporting cost, too. Smith must find his timing against a champion who can score and move before an opponent gets his punches off. Spending several rounds settling in could leave the challenger chasing a substantial lead.

DAZN has confirmed where fans can watch. Smith’s task is to make this competitive after spending so long out of the ring.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Ready As Teofimo Lopez Deadline Hits Tomorrow
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall has made it known he is ready to get down to business with the October 22 deadline running out for talks on his ordered WBA welterweight title fight against Teofimo Lopez.

The British southpaw went onto social media while waiting to see if he lands his mandatory crack or gets hit with another postponement.

“READY FOR A FIGHT,” Catterall posted, tagging DAZN Boxing to make sure the network heard him loud and clear.

That puts Catterall’s stance out there in four words. He wants an official date on the calendar, yet the WBA process has not produced one.

Teofimo’s side has tried to get special permission to go after a different opponent, looking into a massive unification clash against Ryan Garcia for early 2027. Catterall stands as the main roadblock for that route because the WBA already issued the order for its super champion to face him next.

Catterall picked up the WBA regular title by beating Shakhram Giyasov back in May. Grabbing that strap put him in direct position for the bout he is trying to nail down right now. Five months have gone by, and he finds himself still stuck waiting for that mandatory pathway to deliver an actual ring return.

The deadline hits at the close of business Eastern Time on Thursday, October 22. It represents the conclusion of the official discussion window set up by the WBA, not an automatic guarantee that Teofimo gets stripped on the spot.

The pending appeal keeps Catterall hanging around for a ruling that will dictate who he faces and how quickly he gets back under the lights. He recently talked about his career being stalled out, and his latest message makes it obvious that no agreement came together behind closed doors.

There is a huge cash reason for Teofimo to chase Ryan Garcia instead. That matchup pulls in massive public interest compared to a mandatory chore against Catterall. Still, Catterall followed every single sanctioning body rule to earn his spot, and a giant commercial payday for the champion does nothing to restore the lost months Catterall spent on the shelf.

Ghana News.title: Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig: Spanish side maintain hundred percent start
Ghana News.content:
Bernardo Silva scored his first goal for Real Madrid as Jose Mourinho's side beat RB Leipzig to maintain their 100% start in the Champions League.

The midfielder, who joined from Manchester City in the summer, converted from close range to put the Spaniards in front two minutes before half-time.

Arda Guler bundled over the goalline for the second, while Kylian Mbappe scored his 12th goal in 12 games this season, and £120m summer signing Yan Diomande netted against his old club just before the end.

RB Leipzig looked the more dangerous side for much of the first half, but were made to rue missed chances as Thibaut Courtois denied both Christopher Nkunku and Romulo with smart saves.

Real improved and Bernardo forced the ball over the line after Guler's strike deflected off a defender and squirmed between the legs of goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt.

The Belgium goalkeeper did well to tip a stinging Federico Valverde effort past the post early in the second half, but was powerless to prevent Guler meeting Mbappe's header across the face of goal for a simple tap-in.

Frenchman Mbappe scooped a shot into the side netting from a Jude Bellingham cut-back as he looked for his customary goal, and he found it late on with a curling finish into the corner from the edge of the penalty area.

Tidiam Gomis finished off a neat move to pull a goal back for Leipzig, but two minutes later, Real substitute Diomande - who left the German side in the summer - rifled in a spectacular volley from outside the box.

After facing Barcelona in the first Clasico of the season on Sunday, 25 October (20:00 GMT), Jose Mourinho's men will travel to Greece to face AEK Athens on Wednesday, 4 November (17:45 GMT), while Leipzig will host Manchester City later that evening at 20:00 GMT.

Ghana News.title: Revenue, inflation and 2027 Budget in focus as IMF opens Ghana PCI review
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s fiscal performance, revenue mobilisation and preparations for the 2027 Budget are expected to dominate discussions as an International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission begins formal engagements with the government today.

JoyBusiness understands from sources familiar with the visit that the discussions will examine economic performance during the first nine months of the year and the policies needed to sustain recent gains.

The engagements are also expected to cover Ghana’s debt position, expenditure management for the remainder of the year and spending plans for 2027, as the government prepares to prioritise infrastructure investment in the upcoming budget.

On the monetary side, sources indicate that Ghana’s inflation-targeting framework, monetary policy and foreign exchange arrangements are likely to feature prominently.

The mission could also assess the Bank of Ghana’s financial position, international reserves and measures to safeguard the central bank’s independence.

Initial discussions are expected to involve officials from the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Ghana, with other key economic stakeholders likely to participate during the two-week visit.

Ghana’s PCI Programme and Mission Visit

The mission, led by Dr Ruben Atoyan, forms part of Ghana’s engagement with the IMF under the Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI), a non-financing framework intended to consolidate economic gains and sustain policy reforms.

The IMF Executive Board completed the sixth and final review of Ghana’s Extended Credit Facility arrangement on July 27, 2026, and considered the country’s request for a 36-month PCI.

Although the PCI does not provide direct IMF funding, its review process offers the government an opportunity to demonstrate progress on its policy commitments and reinforce confidence among investors and development partners.

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has previously described the framework as an anchor for Ghana’s next phase of reforms, aimed at strengthening economic resilience and supporting broad-based growth.

He said the programme would help preserve gains made under IMF-supported reforms while reinforcing policy credibility and investor confidence.

PCI Programme and What It Means for Ghana

The PCI allows countries to maintain close policy engagement with the IMF without receiving financing under the instrument.

It supports the design and implementation of economic reforms and helps signal policy credibility to development partners and private investors.

Its objectives include strengthening macroeconomic stability, addressing underlying economic imbalances and building resilience against shocks.

Although it provides no direct funding, the PCI requires policies that meet standards comparable to those under IMF lending arrangements. The IMF assesses performance through reviews on a fixed schedule, typically every six months.

The instrument requires IMF Executive Board approval, unlike a Staff-Monitored Programme, which is an informal arrangement between IMF staff and a member country.

Ghana News.title: Carrick’s job in jeopardy after Man United’s 4-1 Champions League humiliation at Como
Ghana News.content:
Manchester United suffered one of the worst European nights (4-1 defeat) in their history against Como to pile the pressure on beleaguered boss Michael Carrick.

Eight days after conceding in the first minute to Atletico Madrid, United's defences were breached after 118 seconds as brilliant Argentina playmaker Nico Paz scored the first of his double.

It meant United became the first English team in history to concede in the first two minutes of consecutive major European matches, something no-one at Old Trafford wants to be associated with.

When United last won the Champions League in 2008, Como were in Serie D. It is a measure of the different directions the respective clubs are heading in that this was about as comprehensive a victory and as one-sided a match as it is possible to imagine.

Paz scored twice, and set up Tasos Douvikas in between, before Jacobo Ramon powered home a header for number four.

At one stage it looked as if United may equal another unwanted record - their heaviest ever European defeat was a 5-0 loss to Portuguese side Sporting in 1964.

Skipper Bruno Fernandes was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half after Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos - £110m-worth of Ineos signings - were taken off at half-time.

Zirkzee beat the offside trap to calmly score a consolation from fellow substitute Amad Diallo's cross in stoppage time, but that did nothing to improve the mood.

Carrick seemed to ignore his players as he went to acknowledge the United fans, repeatedly holding his hands up in apology, in the manner of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer following the 4-1 defeat at Watford in November 2021 - which led to his dismissal 24 hours later.

Ghana News.title: Ghana targets first phase of AI facility within 24 months
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is targeting the completion of the first phase of a national computing facility within the next 24 months to provide researchers, universities and industry players with access to the computing capacity needed to advance artificial intelligence (AI) development.

The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Mr Samuel Nartey George, said the government was currently undertaking procurement processes with the Public Procurement Authority (PPA) to acquire the data centre infrastructure and related equipment for the project.

He said the facility would help reduce the reliance of Ghanaian researchers and businesses on computing services purchased from providers outside the country.

Speaking at the JoyNews Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, October 21, Mr George described the planned facility as an important first step in building the country’s capacity to develop and deploy AI technologies.

“We are currently going through procurement with PPA on getting a data centre, the computer infrastructure and all the various parts of it put together. 24 months from now, we should have phase one completed with serious computing infrastructure that we can then give to our researchers, our industry and our universities who are currently buying tokens outside the country and buying capacity outside the country,” he said.

The proposed facility is expected to provide computing resources for institutions and businesses working with AI, which often requires substantial processing power to train models, run applications and analyse large volumes of data.

Mr George said the project formed part of the foundational work needed to position Ghana for greater participation in the rapidly developing AI economy.

‘A long journey’

The minister cautioned against expecting the country to address all its AI infrastructure and development needs within the remaining period of the Mahama administration.

He said establishing the computing facility would be an initial milestone rather than a complete solution to the country’s AI ambitions.

His comments highlight the scale of the task facing Ghana as it seeks to build the infrastructure, skills and institutional capacity required to benefit from AI.

Access to computing power is one of the requirements for AI research and commercial development. However, the impact of the proposed facility will also depend on its capacity, affordability, reliability and accessibility to researchers, universities and businesses.

The government's 24-month target sets out a timeline for the first phase, while the minister's remarks indicate that further investment and sustained policy implementation will be needed to meet the country's broader AI ambitions.

Ghana News.title: Champions League: Declan Rice earns Arsenal draw at Bayern Munich
Ghana News.content:
Declan Rice scored a late equaliser as Arsenal and Bayern Munich played out an entertaining draw in the league phase of the Champions League in a game where Bukayo Saka limped off with injury.

Saka went down after just 10 minutes with a suspected thigh problem, after he attempted to play a pass without anyone around him.

Eberechi Eze replaced Saka and scored the opening goal of the game in the 35th minute, after he latched on to an excellent pass by Martin Odegaard, with the video assistant referee needing to intervene after the England international was initially flagged offside.

But Bayern Munich were behind for just 10 minutes, with Harry Kane picking the ball up in midfield and splitting the Arsenal backline with a pinpoint pass for Alphonso Davies to finish.

Kane, who had produced a number of eye-catching passes during the match, then put Bayern in front from the penalty spot.

The England captain's shot struck Jurrien Timber's hand inside the area and Kane sent David Raya the wrong way from 12 yards as he looked to have completed the turnaround.

Bayern piled the pressure on to Arsenal as they looked for a third goal but the Gunners held firm before Rice exchanged passes with substitute Viktor Gyokeres and drilled a low shot into the bottom corner to level the game.

The Gunners pushed for a winner and Jurrien Timber forced Manuel Neuer into an acrobatic stop before full-time.

Ghana News.title: Aston Villa maintain perfect Champions League start by beating Viking
Ghana News.content:
Aston Villa continued the impressive start to their Champions League campaign with a comfortable victory over Viking at Villa Park.

Villa made it three wins from three, following their 6-0 demolition of Fenerbahce, by easing past the Norwegian side who pushed Bayern Munich all the way to draw 3-3 in the last round of matches.

Unai Emery's side were on top from the start, Viking living dangerously on several occasions before Ross Barkley turned in Ibrahim Mbaye's corner at the near post after 23 minutes.

Villa continued to dominate and doubled their lead eight minutes before half-time, Emiliano Buendia scoring from the spot after Alysson was tripped by Zlatko Tripic, the decision given after a Video Assistant Referee (VAR) review.

Viking showed more attacking intent at the start of the second half, but Villa wrapped up another three points in the Champions League when the impressive Alysson's cross was turned into his own net by Henrik Heggheim after 62 minutes.

It paved the way for a comfortable conclusion as Villa closed out a victory that was another emphatic statement from the great European specialist Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho, who has struggled to make an impact at Villa since his loan move from Chelsea, emerged as a substitute to produce a lively cameo, almost getting on the scoresheet, only to see his shot saved by Viking keeper Arlid Ostbo.

Viking pulled a goal back with four minutes left, Peter Christiansen's acrobatic finish given by VAR after initially being ruled offside, but nothing could spoil another satisfying night for Emery, Villa's 12th consecutive home win in European competition.

Ghana News.title: Ghana reaffirms commitment to women’s economic empowerment at Addis Ababa dialogue
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to advancing women’s economic empowerment through inclusive policies, institutional reforms, and practical interventions that improve women’s access to finance, markets, and economic opportunities.

The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, gave the assurance during a closed-door Ministerial Policy Roundtable on Monday, October 19, 2026, at the Second Egumeni Dialogue on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Held under the theme “From Policy Commitments to Reforms: Creating an Enabling Environment for Women’s Economic Participation,” the roundtable focused on translating existing policies and legal frameworks into practical measures that enable women to participate meaningfully in economic activities.

Dr Lartey said the challenge was not always the absence of policies but whether institutions, budgets, financial systems and implementation arrangements were adequately structured to deliver tangible benefits.

She stressed that women’s economic empowerment must be treated as a macroeconomic and development priority because of its impact on household welfare, employment, productivity and national growth.

Highlighting Ghana’s interventions, she cited the National Gender Policy 2025–2034, implementation of the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121), and the proposed Women’s Development Bank as key measures to address structural barriers facing women.

She said expanding access to finance also required reviewing lending criteria, financial products and risk-assessment systems to make affordable financing more accessible, particularly to women operating businesses in the informal economy.

The Minister said the proposed Women’s Development Bank should form part of a broader financial inclusion strategy that links women entrepreneurs to business development services, markets, skills and technology.

Such support, she explained, would help women-owned businesses grow, improve productivity, create jobs and strengthen women’s economic independence.

She also called for stronger gender-responsive budgeting to ensure allocations for women’s economic empowerment are clearly identified, adequately resourced, and linked to measurable outcomes.

She emphasised the need for closer coordination among the Ministry of Finance, financial institutions, regulators, trade and industry institutions, local government and the private sector.

On regional trade, Dr Lartey urged stakeholders to help women-owned enterprises take advantage of opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

She highlighted the need to connect women entrepreneurs to export markets and buyers, improve access to product standards and certification, strengthen digital marketing and e-commerce skills, and expand access to trade information, logistics and export financing.

She reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to working with the African Union and other member states under the Women and Youth Financial and Economic Inclusion 2030 (WYFEI 2030) initiative to promote shared learning, strengthen accountability and accelerate reforms to advance women’s financial and economic empowerment across Africa.

Ghana News.title: Julius Debrah calls for integrated digital markets to boost African trade
Ghana News.content:
Chief of Staff Julius Debrah has called for greater integration of Africa’s digital markets to facilitate cross-border trade, strengthen economic cooperation and create new opportunities for businesses across the continent.

He said African countries must move beyond operating as disconnected markets by developing interoperable payment systems, trusted digital identities, compatible regulations and simpler processes for cross-border digital trade.

Speaking at Mobex Africa 2026, held under the theme “Resetting Africa’s Digital Identity and Sovereignty: From Promise to Practice,” Mr Debrah stressed that digital sovereignty must complement, rather than undermine, economic integration.

“Africa’s digital future cannot be built as 54 disconnected markets,” he said. “We need interoperable payment systems, trusted digital identities, compatible rules, and easier cross-border digital trade. Digital sovereignty and economic integration are partners, not rivals. We must be sovereign enough to protect our people and open enough to connect our markets.”

He said stronger digital links between African economies would enable countries to harness technology to create jobs, expand businesses and increase exports, positioning the continent to benefit more fully from the digital economy.

Mr Debrah also identified Ghana’s political stability, youthful population and growing innovation ecosystem as key advantages in building competitive technology companies. He said the country’s hosting of the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) offered an additional opportunity to expand its presence in regional and global markets.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: North Korea to resume propaganda broadcasts, South Korea urges dialogue
World.content:
North Korea has said it plans to resume broadcasting anti-South Korea propaganda along the armed border between the two countries, as Seoul urged Pyongyang to discuss easing tensions.

Kim Yo Jong, a senior North Korean official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Wednesday that North Korea will place loudspeakers along the entire border, following a visit with top military officials to fortifications along the contested frontier.

Kim warned Seoul of “the most horrible and distressing situation” if South Korea continued what Pyongyang calls interference in the North’s internal affairs.

She added in a follow-up statement on Thursday that North Korea would place “new counter means” on alert along the border, without elaborating, and have its loudspeakers on “standby” within days.

A landmine blast last month that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) between the two countries has ratcheted up tensions. Seoul accused North Korean troops of deliberately laying mines in the border zone as part of the North’s fortification work.

Kim had denied the allegation, calling the incident a South Korean fabrication. She said North Korean tactical units had taken up new positions, and accused South Korean troops of conducting warning broadcasts and firing warning shots at multiple locations near the border.

Seoul said the warning shots were fired as “legitimate and defensive measures”.

North Korea has been adding mines, barbed wire fences, anti-tank barriers and other fortifications to what is already one of the world’s most heavily armed borders.



South Korea’s Ministry of National Defence urged North Korea on Thursday to discuss measures to ease tension at the border and prevent any accidental military clash, its spokesperson said.

Pyongyang had cut off a military hotline with the South after declaring it would no longer seek dialogue or unification with what it called its “foe”.

Loudspeaker propaganda

Both North and South Korea have historically used loudspeakers to broadcast propaganda across the border, with South Korean broadcasts featuring K-pop music and news that have long irked Pyongyang and prompted tit-for-tat responses.

The two Koreas are separated by the DMZ, established after the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice.

North Korea has been reinforcing its side of the DMZ with mines, barriers and fencing since 2024 as it seeks to establish what it calls a permanent border with South Korea.

World.title: Brazil’s Bolsonaro challenges Lula to expand release of personal records
World.content:
Right-wing presidential candidate says he will release personal records if his opponent, President Lula, meets his conditions.

Brazilian right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has set out steep conditions for disclosing his personal records in response to a challenge from President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, his opponent in Sunday’s election run-off.

Bolsonaro’s campaign has said it will release the data Lula requested if the president expands his own pledge to disclose his personal records to include those of his advisers, security staff and records from companies held by Lula’s children.

Lula said on Tuesday that he would share his bank, tax and telephone records, along with those of his family, if Bolsonaro would agree to do the same.

His campaign submitted conditional authorisation to Brazil’s electoral court to release the president’s personal data.

Camilo Santana, a senator and representative of Lula’s campaign, told journalists that ⁠⁠Lula has agreed to Bolsonaro’s new demands, and the president’s would file an official response with the court on Thursday morning.

Corruption scandal

The call from Lula on Tuesday came as both campaigns try to navigate the fallout of an explosive corruption scandal involving disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro, which has implicated influential individuals and institutions across Brazil.

Bolsonaro, who narrowly leads Lula in the polls, is under investigation over alleged corruption and money laundering related to an investment he allegedly ⁠⁠sought from Vorcaro. He is also under investigation in a separate probe over alleged money laundering.

The presidential hopeful denies any wrongdoing.



Brazil’s president is also linked to a corruption scandal, via his son Fabio Luis Lula da Silva, a businessman, who is accused being investigated over allegations that he unlawfully helped another businessman to gain access to the government.

Lula’s eldest son is also being investigated over his links to a businessman detained under a pension fraud probe.

Lula’s son denies the allegations, and the president has said his ‌‌son ‌‌would be treated like any other citizen.

World.title: Australian TV reporter rescues man from sinking car
World.content:
NewsFeed Australian TV reporter rescues man from sinking car

An Australian television reporter and a bystander rescued a man from a car as it was engulfed by flood waters in Morayfield, Queensland. Will Murray, a journalist with Australia’s public broadcaster ABC, was reporting on flooding when a man became trapped in a four-wheel drive.

World.title: Trump administration seeks Supreme Court approval to build Big Bend wall
World.content:
The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to allow it to resume plans to build a border wall through the Big Bend region of West Texas, as part of its anti-immigration policy to strengthen security on the border with Mexico.

The Justice Department filed an emergency request on Wednesday asking the court to lift a federal judge’s injunction in a lower court that has halted construction while a lawsuit against the project, brought by an environmental group and other challengers, plays out.

The Department of Homeland Security plans include vehicle barriers, patrol roads, lighting and detection technology in and around Big Bend National Park.

Big Bend has about 805km (500 miles) of border, and, according to opponents of the project who have sued the administration, accounts for about 1 percent of migrant arrests.

Landscape, historic church

The lawsuit, filed by plaintiffs including the Center for Biological Diversity and a Big Bend-area river guide, seeks to preserve the landscape, protect a historic church, and challenge the federal government’s waivers of environmental and historical laws to fast-track the $1.7bn project.

Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and current Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who issued the waivers between February and July, found the region to be an “area of high illegal entry”, requiring additional barriers to control the border.



US District Judge Kathleen Cardone issued an injunction in El Paso on October 2 halting work “until and unless Defendants comply with all applicable laws,” she wrote in her order.

In a later opinion, the judge found that the waivers exceeded the authority of Noem and Mullin.

The Justice Department in its request urged the Supreme Court to pause or overturn Cardone’s injunction.

The Supreme Court has not yet responded to this appeal.

“Even assuming that the secretary’s waiver authority implicates a question of ‘vast economic and political significance,’ Congress did clearly authorize the secretary both to build border barriers and to waive legal requirements in order to facilitate their expeditious construction,” the Justice Department wrote.

In August, the administration paused construction in Big Bend after the project drew bipartisan criticism over its potential impact on the park’s landscape and wildlife.

World.title: Can Trump deport Congresswoman Ilhan Omar?
World.content:
NewsFeed Can Trump deport Congresswoman Ilhan Omar?

US President Donald Trump says Congresswoman Ilhan Omar could face jail or deportation as federal authorities investigate allegations surrounding her US citizenship. Omar denies wrongdoing and accuses the administration of political intimidation. With the midterm elections approaching, what could happen next? Al Jazeera’s Noor Wazwaz explains.

World.title: Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard after 4 years behind bars
World.content:
NewsFeed Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard after 4 years behind bars

US citizen Stephen Hubbard has been freed from a Russian prison, four years after being convicted of being a mercenary for Ukraine, a claim he denies. The 74-year-old’s release coincided with US envoy Steve Witkoff’s visit to Russia to try and get Moscow to rejoin peace talks.

World.title: Tigray resumes daily life amid fears of wider war
World.content:
Mekelle, Ethiopia- In Mekelle, shops are reopening, and banks are resuming services, but residents remain anxious about what comes next. Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters retook the Tigray regional capital on October 4, as renewed fighting raised fears that the region’s fragile recovery could be derailed once again.

Tigray, in northern Ethiopia, is still recovering from the 2020–2022 war between federal forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the region’s dominant political movement. For residents, the return of fighting has brought new uncertainty over jobs, education, security and the future.

Daily life resumes, but hardship remains.

Businesses and financial services are gradually reopening in Mekelle, but many households are struggling to afford necessities. Delayed salaries have left public employees struggling to cover food, rent and school costs, while years of conflict have depleted family savings.

“Things may be reopening, but that does not mean our problems are over. We still have expenses every day, and without our salaries, it is difficult to know how we will manage,” said Gebregziabher, a public servant in Mekelle.

The funding crisis has affected the wider public sector. In March, Tigray’s interim administration said it could no longer cover monthly salaries for about 137,000 civil servants because expected federal budget transfers had not arrived. In April, the regional finance bureau reported an 8.5-billion-birr (about $52,000) funding shortfall affecting salary payments and development projects.



For many residents, the reopening of businesses offers only a partial return to normality. Without reliable incomes and greater security, everyday expenses remain difficult to manage.

Students fear losing more time

For students in Tigray, renewed fighting has revived fears of another interruption to their education. Many already lost valuable study time during the previous war and worry about falling further behind.

In Adigrat, Shewit, a grade 10 student, said uncertainty about classes and security had left him worried about his future.

“I have already lost so much time because of the war. I am afraid that if our education is disrupted again, I will lose another year and fall further behind,” he said.

Some university students have left Tigray for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia’s capital, to seek transfers to other public universities. The Ministry of Education announced temporary placements at universities elsewhere in the country for students enrolled at institutions in Tigray. More than 5,000 returning students had applied by September 17–18, according to reporting on the ministry’s programme.

Abel, a third-year student at Axum University, travelled to Addis Ababa to request a transfer.

“I didn’t want to leave, but I also can’t keep putting my education on hold. I came to Addis to see if I can transfer to another university and continue my studies. I just want to finish what I started,” he said.

For students who have already lost years to conflict, the uncertainty means more than interrupted classes. It threatens to delay graduation and make an already difficult path to employment even harder.

Border communities fear a wider conflict

Near the Eritrean border, military movements and conflicting accounts of troop deployments have heightened fears that the fighting could spread beyond Tigray.

On October 8, The Associated Press reported claims by a commander allied with Ethiopia’s government that Eritrean troops had entered Adigrat earlier that week and Idaga Hamus the following day. The AP said it could not independently verify those accounts. The conflict-monitoring organisation ACLED separately reported Eritrean troops crossing the border at Zalambessa.

On October 13, Reuters reported that Ethiopian government forces had advanced into Zalambessa, citing people in contact with residents and other sources. The report said it remained unclear whether Eritrean troops or Tigrayan opposition fighters were still present in the town. The differing accounts underscored the difficulty of establishing control of individual towns as the fighting shifted.

The developments have unfolded amid worsening relations between Addis Ababa and Asmara. On October 8, Ethiopia’s foreign minister, Gedion Timothewos, accused Eritrea of sending troops as far as 60km (37 miles) into Ethiopian territory in several areas of Tigray and appealed to the United Nations Security Council to respond.



Eritrea has denied invading Ethiopian territory. Its government said Ethiopia’s accusations amounted to a declaration of war and called on the Security Council to take action against Ethiopia. The competing claims have raised fears that renewed fighting in Tigray could lead to a direct confrontation between the two neighbours.

Ethiopia and Eritrea fought on the same side during the 2020–2022 Tigray war, when Eritrean forces supported the federal government against the TPLF. Their deteriorating relations have added a regional dimension to the renewed conflict.

In Zalambessa, residents are watching developments with concern. One resident, who declined to be named, said the uncertainty made it difficult to know what to expect in the coming weeks.

An uncertain road ahead

On October 16, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced a six-month caretaker administration for Tigray, tasked with restoring public services, helping displaced people return and preparing the region for elections. The announcement followed the federal forces’ takeover of Mekelle and other major towns.
