He outlined four pillars: intelligence-led policing and early warning, stronger police-community partnerships, improved preparedness and coordinated response, and professionalism with respect for human rights.

And he had a warning for journalists too: “The need for speed in journalism must never displace the obligation to accuracy.” Sensational headlines, he said, can compromise rescue efforts and endanger children.

The $15 Billion Question: Where did the money go?

One of the most revealing sessions came from Hajia Halima Iliya, National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria during the panel discussion.

She took the audience back to the beginning how the Safe Schools Initiative was launched to enable victims to continue education unhindered, how persistent attacks forced Nigeria to sign the Safe Schools Declaration in 2019 alongside over 100 countries, mostly from the Sahel region and West Africa.

“There is more to what we are seeing which requires collective collaboration. Some of the actors are cross-border actors. They pass through the land, through the walls,” she said.

By 2021, the Ministry of Finance convened a high-level meeting with Defence, Police, DSS, Office of the National Security Adviser, Ministry of Education, NSCDC, governors, EU and World Bank. The verdict: Nigeria had no mid-term expenditure framework for school safety.

“Under my leadership, we developed a national plan on financing safe schools 2023-2026. By 2022, this document was developed and was launched. We started full implementation in 2023, with the Federal Government releasing N15 billion to the implementing regions,” she disclosed.

A database of vulnerable communities was built with CSOs, a National Safe Schools Response Centre established, and hunters, vigilante and forest guards trained within community ecosystems. Lagos and Jigawa, she said, have become champions.

“Over 4,000 students were trained across four states last year,” she said, with technology deployed to communities without network and hardware for the Police Schools Protection Squad.

Her plea: Governors must embed Safe Schools into annual budgets. Without a budget, there can be no sustainable protection.

Fencing, data and a weak justice system

The panel also brought the conversation down from policy to the school gate.

Comrade Hassan Akintoye, Chairman, NUT Lagos Wing, representing the NUT National President, was blunt: school threat has always been around, but today it is the magnitude that frightens. He listed what keeps schools unsafe: lack of fencing, inadequate data of students and teachers, and a weak justice system.

“If we can’t get crime offenders to book, then we can’t tackle insecurity,” he said. He asked EWAN to take this summit beyond journalists – to parents, students and teachers who live the danger daily.

Mr. Olushola Masheyi, President, ANCOPSS Lagos State, representing National President Dr. Robert Okorie, echoed the need for collaborative efforts and adequate data on school structures and stakeholders.

The school without a fence

Perhaps the most haunting illustration came from Motunrayo Alaka, Executive Director, Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism. She revealed that about 60% of Nigerian children attend low-cost private schools, many without perimeter fencing.

She referenced her DFID-supported work, Teaching in Distress, which documented how teachers in Borno State became farmers, displaced from attacked communities.

She cited reports from 2021: schools in Ekiti without fencing, a nationwide mapping of flashpoints, and Igangan in Oyo State where farmer-herder crisis threatened education.

Igangan, she noted, is more than 100km from Oriire –the site of the recent abduction but both share the same architecture: deep forests, porous communities. “If it happened in Igangan, then any other school that has similar architecture is also prone to an attack. If the community is unsafe, the schools are unsafe,” she said.

She told the story of a 57-year-old primary school in Ikorodu, Lagos, where she watched a journalist drive into the compound without any challenge. No fence, no gate, no check.

“That is the same way an attacker would have driven into that school,” she said. That report was done. Six months later, Lagos State renovated the school and built a fence. Journalism worked.

But she also flagged a different threat inside Lagos: students fighting after school with knives, sticks and stones – inter-school violence she witnessed herself living on the Island.

“These children, many of them, are very big hands for bandits,” she warned, urging journalists to learn what a standard school should look like – fencing, design, safety protocols – and to report the socio-economic conditions pushing children to carry knives to school.

Lagos says: Security starts from the community

Hon. Jamiu Alli-Balogun, Lagos Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, pushed back gently. Students fighting after school, he said, are products of environment, not the school. “The school does not create anything that is negative. It is the failure of our social system – parenting and the community,” he said.

He said Lagos has deliberately fenced schools even in interior areas, holds quarterly security reviews with principals, and has for almost six years permanently stationed four different security personnel, including MOPOL, in a riverine school accessible only through forest – a sign of commitment.

He described a security architecture where a text message triggers immediate response from the ministry and Lagos State Security Trust Fund.

“Security is also about welfare,” he added, citing housing loans and annual merit awards for teachers. “The best security system we can manage is from the community where the school is situated. We need the Baale, we need members of the community, we need political leaders,” he said.

Beyond the summit

As the summit ended, four new members were inducted into EWAN – a quiet but symbolic act that the circle of those holding power to account is widening.

World.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
World.content:
Atiku Abubakar

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers.

Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation.

In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case.

“Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said.

Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20.

“During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said.

He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response.

“Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said.

The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting.

“The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said.

Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression.

World.title: Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds
World.content:
CBN Governor, Yemi Cardoso

By Rosemary Iwunze

Insurance companies are now struggling to have access to the new capital they raised, amounting to about N300 billion under the just concluded recapitalization programme.

The funds were held in the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, pending verifications for illicit funds inflows.

Vanguard learnt that following suspicion of possible illicit sources of some of the new investments in the firms the apex imposed stricter capital verification regime, a development which has proved tough for most of the insurance firms to scale through.

It is further learnt that while the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has given approval for the apex bank to release the funds to the insurers, the affected firms are painstakingly going through the processes.

Speaking to journalist during the virtual press briefing on the outcome of the Insurers Committee meeting, Chairman of Nigeria Insurers Association, NIA, Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, stated that, the insurance sector regulator has done its part while operators are currently working on the CBN criteria to access the funds on or before the end of this month.

The insurers said they had planned to deploy the new capital in the third quarter of this year to boost their financial performance in 2026 while rewarding their investors with good returns in dividend for their support in the recapitalization program.

Recall that the 24 insurance companies had cumulatively raised N300 billion during the exercise, added to over N700 billion existing capital, taking the total industry capital to N1.079 trillion, post recapitalisation.

The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA), 2025, had stipulated that the underwriting firms and reinsurers who participated in the recapitalisation exercise that ended on July 31st, 2026 must keep their recapitalised funds in an escrow account with CBN.

Of the 50 firms that scaled through the recapitalisation hurdle, 24 of them raised fresh capital while 26 of them had earlier surpassed the minimum capital benchmark.

NIIRA had mandated life underwriters to recapitalise from N2billion to N10billion, non-life from N3billion to N15billion while reinsurers were required to upgrade from N10billion to N35billion.

The Commissioner for Insurance/CEO, NAICOM, Mr. Olusegun Omosehin, had earlier disclosed that the capital in the market has now risen to N1.079trillion, up from about N700billion before the exercise.

According to him, NAICOM now wants to allow operators access the recapitalisation funds, he promised that the regulator would monitor the operators to ensure that the funds fulfill its purpose and not mismanaged or divested into something else.

World.title: Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source
World.content:
File image.

By Omeiza Ajayi

Fresh facts emerged, yesterday, regarding the travel itinerary of the confirmed Ebola virus patient in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, revealing that the index case entered Nigeria aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight earlier this month.

Read Also: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria — WHO

A highly-placed aviation official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, as she was not authorised to brief the media on the matter, told Vanguard that the patient arrived in the country on October 3, 2026.

This is even as the Ugandan government asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the woman, the index case, insisting she didn’t pick the virus in its territory, since there is no Ebola case in Uganda.

According to the aviation official, the patient landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333.

The revelation provides critical details for contact-tracing, following an earlier official announcement by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, who confirmed the presence of the virus in the nation’s capital.

Pate had disclosed that the female patient had recently returned to Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda and subsequently spent several days receiving care at a private hospital in Abuja before the infection was formally diagnosed.

She has since been transferred to a designated isolation facility where she is currently receiving treatment.

In response, a multi-agency operation involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and the FCT Health and Environmental Services Secretariat has commenced extensive contact-tracing.

Public health authorities have so far identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare personnel, fellow hospital patients, caregivers and individuals connected to her travel route.

Consequently, the Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units across the country on high alert.

Vanguard News

World.title: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria —  WHO
World.content:
•Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source *Nigeria confirms first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain *Uganda seeks details of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case *Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG *Senate, Reps ask FG to make screening mandatory for passengers at all entry points, borders Urge govt to release emergency funds from service-wide votes to relevant agencies to curb disease *To immediately amend Quarantine Act of 1926

By Sola Ogundipe, Health Editor, Henry Umoru, Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Omeiza Ajayi, Luminous Jannamike & Gift Odekina

ABUJA — Fresh facts emerged yesterday regarding the travel itinerary of the confirmed Ebola virus patient in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, revealing that the index case entered Nigeria aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight earlier this month.

A highly-placed aviation official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, as she was not authorised to brief the media on the matter, told Vanguard that the patient arrived in the country on October 3, 2026.

This came on a day an emergency meeting of officials of the health ministry revealed the index case detected in the country carried the Bundibugyo strain of the virus which, according to the World Health Organisation, WHO, has no vaccine or specific treatment.

This is even as the Ugandan government asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the woman, the index case, insisting she didn’t pick the virus in its territory, since there is no Ebola case in Uganda.

Meanwhile, the two arms of the National Assembly, Senate and House of Representatives, have asked the Federal Government to urgently release money to relevant agencies to confront the disease.

According to the aviation official, the patient landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333.

The revelation provides critical details for contact-tracing, following an earlier official announcement by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, who confirmed the presence of the virus in the nation’s capital.

Pate had disclosed that the female patient had recently returned to Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda and subsequently spent several days receiving care at a private hospital in Abuja before the infection was formally diagnosed.

She has since been transferred to a designated isolation facility where she is currently receiving treatment.

In response, a multi-agency operation involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and the FCT Health and Environmental Services Secretariat has commenced extensive contact-tracing.

Public health authorities have so far identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare personnel, fellow hospital patients, caregivers and individuals connected to her travel route.

Consequently, the Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units across the country on high alert.

Nigeria confirms first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain

The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain, an emergency meeting on the issue was told yesterday.

“We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, Director of the Public Health Laboratory Service at NCDC, said yesterday.

The World Health Organization, WHO, which also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.

“This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said, adding the patient had deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”.

The official did not disclose the nationality of the diplomat.

In August, Uganda was declared officially Ebola-free by WHO after recording 20 cases, almost all people who had travelled from the DRC.

Uganda seeks details of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case

In a related development, Uganda has asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the index case in the country.

The Federal Government had confirmed on Tuesday that the woman recently arrived in Nigeria after travelling from Uganda.

But in a statement, Director-General of Health Services, Uganda Ministry of Health, Prof. Charles Olaro, said the information is required to guide further investigations and determine whether additional contact-tracing was necessary, even as he stressed that the woman’s transit through Uganda did not establish that she contracted the virus there.

The statement, issued in Kampala, said the Ministry of Health is awaiting further information from the Nigerian government to help establish the circumstances surrounding the infection, adding that it would strengthen screening and other public health measures at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies.

Preliminary information cited by the Ugandan authorities revealed that the woman, who travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business, transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms, but reportedly developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria, as the location where she contracted the virus remained under investigation.

The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: Ministry Calls for Calm and Vigilance” read: “The Ministry of Health has noted reports of a confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria involving a Nigerian woman who reportedly travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business.

“Preliminary information indicates that she transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms and developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria. Her transit through Uganda does not establish that she contracted the infection there. The location of exposure remains under investigation.

“The government of Nigeria is yet to provide detailed information on the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to guide further investigations and any necessary contact tracing.

“The ministry wishes to clarify that, as of the date of this statement, Uganda has no confirmed active Ebola cases.”

It said limited provisions had been maintained to facilitate humanitarian and diplomatic movements.

Senate asks FG to make screening mandatory for passengers at all international airports, others.

Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG

But the federal government said yesterday it was collaborating with Uganda to contain the risk of the disease outbreak, assuring Nigerians that public health authorities were coordinating response measures.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this while fielding questions from journalists after a meeting at the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Pate was asked to react to reports that Ugandan authorities had said there was no Ebola case in their country, despite reports that a Nigerian woman had contracted the virus in Uganda.

He said Nigeria was working with the East African country, while taking steps to contain the reported case and prevent further transmission.

“All I can tell you is that we are collaborating with our sister African nation of Uganda. What is important is that we have found this one case. We are doing contact tracing, and we are putting containment measures to ensure that it doesn’t go into our population,” the minister said.

Pate said Nigeria had competent public health institutions capable of responding to the situation, citing the country’s experience in managing the 2014 Ebola outbreak.

“We have done it in 2014, and we have good public health institutions,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but avoid panic, advising the public to rely on information from trusted public health authorities rather than circulate unverified reports.

“Nigerians should be reassured. We must be vigilant, but not panic, and people should respect public health information from trusted sources, and not spread misinformation and false rumours,” he said.

The minister assured Nigerians that the government would continue to provide updates as more information became available.

“We would be truthful to Nigerians with the information that we receive on a daily basis. I will be receiving a report. NCDC has an incident management system,” he added.

Make health screening compulsory at entry points — NASS

Meanwhile, the Senate and House of Representatives yesterday asked the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, National Centre for Disease Control, NCDC, and the Port Health Services, to make health screening compulsory for all arriving passengers at every international airport, seaport and designated land borders.

In the Senate chamber, senators asked that the screening should also involve temperature and symptom checks, with enhanced screening for anyone who had been in or transited an affected area in the past 21 days, regardless of nationality or county of departure.

Health officials are also to introduce exit screening for departing passengers during any declared emergency.

The Senate urged the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning to release emergency funds from the service-wide votes and make necessary funding available to the relevant agencies to curb the disease.

It also asked the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, and the Nigeria Immigration Service, NIS, to fully equip all entry points with trained port health officers, thermal scanners, protective equipment and isolation rooms, to ensure that isolation and treatment centres are ready in all 36 states and the FCT.

Resolutions of the Senate yesterday were sequel to a motion sponsored by Senator Francis Adedayo Faduyile (APC, Ondo South).

The Upper Chamber also urged the National Assembly to immediately, in conjunction with the Ministry of Health, repeal and re-enact the Quarantine Act of 1926 with a modern public health law consistent with the IHR (2005).

Recall that the Quarantine Act Cap Q2 LFN 2004 (originally enacted in 1926) is Nigeria’s primary legal framework for preventing the introduction and spread of dangerous infectious diseases.

In light of recent public health alerts, such as the 2026 Ebola surveillance, the Act empowers the President and governors to declare infected areas, enforce port/border controls, and mandate isolation or vaccination.

The Senate also called Nigerians to be conscious of this development and make adequate arrangements for hand sanitisers at event centres, institutions, private and public places.

However, the motion which mandated the committees on Health, Primary Healthca re, Development and Disease Control, Aviation, Interior and Appropriations to liaise with the relevant agencies, visit the principal entry points, and report back within four weeks for further legislative action, was unanimously rejected by senators.

The Senate mandated the Committee on Legislative Compliance to ensure implementation of these resolutions.

Earlier in his presentation, Senator Faduyile said: “The Senate: Notes that the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, declared in May 2026 and designated by the World Health Organization as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, now exceeds 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,400 deaths, making it the second largest Ebola outbreak in history, and that there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain.”

Reps demand urgent release of health funds, stronger emergency response

In the House of Representatives, lawmakers made similar demands as the senators, urging the Federal Government to strengthen Nigeria’s Ebola prevention and emergency response measures, following reports of a confirmed case in Abuja.

The lawmakers also called for the immediate release of outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies to enhance surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory testing and other measures aimed at preventing further transmission.

The resolutions followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Amobi Ogah, who represents Isuikwuato/Umunneochi federal constituency of Abia State, at plenary.

Moving the motion, Ogah described Ebola Virus Disease as a severe and potentially fatal infection requiring early detection, strict infection prevention and control, and coordinated public health intervention.

“It is extremely disturbing that yesterday (Tuesday), October 20, 2026, an Ebola Virus case was confirmed in a woman arriving from Uganda in Abuja who tested positive. Health authorities traced 44 contacts for isolation and further tests,” he said.

The lawmaker warned that delays in identifying suspected cases, conducting laboratory tests, isolating infected persons and tracing their contacts could increase the risk of transmission and place additional pressure on the country’s healthcare system.

Presided over by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu, the House unanimously adopted the motion and called on the Federal Government to immediately mobilise private, state and federal health agencies and place them on high alert to contain the reported outbreak.

The lawmakers specifically urged the Federal Ministry of Finance to release all outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies without further delay.

According to the House, the funding is critical to enable the agencies effectively discharge their responsibilities as the country intensifies surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory testing and other emergency response operations.

The House also urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to assess the additional resources required to strengthen Nigeria’s preparedness and response capacity, in line with prevailing epidemiological evidence and public health guidance.

Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn

Reacting to the development yesterday, former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers.

Atiku said government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment.

He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation.

In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case.

“Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said.

Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria early October, developed symptoms and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20.

“During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Our political differences will not diminish my affection for Kwankwaso — Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, on his 70th birthday, saying their political differences will not diminish his affection for the former Minister of Defence.

Tinubu, in a congratulatory message issued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, described Kwankwaso as a longtime friend and political associate whose contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development remain significant.

The President recalled that their relationship dated back to 1992, when both served in the National Assembly, with Kwankwaso in the House of Representatives and Tinubu in the Senate.

He said their political association continued in 1999 when they both emerged as governors of their respective states.

“As members of the Class of ’99 Governors, we both played pivotal roles in laying the foundation for the democracy the nation enjoys today,” Tinubu said.

According to him, their political paths later diverged because of different political choices before they came together in 2013 to form the All Progressives Congress.

“Since then, history and service have kept us intertwined,” he added.

Tinubu acknowledged Kwankwaso’s contributions to Kano State and Nigeria, citing his service as a two-term governor, Minister of Defence, senator representing Kano Central Senatorial District and presidential candidate.

He also noted Kwankwaso’s current role as a presidential running mate, describing him as an influential figure and progressive politician.

The President said their membership of different political parties and participation on competing platforms in the January 2027 election would not affect his personal regard for the former Kano governor.

“That we are in different political parties and competing on different platforms in the January 2027 election will not remove my affection for Senator Kwankwaso,” he said.

Tinubu wished Kwankwaso good health, personal fulfilment and many more years of active participation in Nigeria’s democratic process as he marked the milestone.

World.title: Over 100 Ogun students hospitalised after suspected gas emissions
World.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

More than 100 students from several secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo areas of Ogun State were reportedly hospitalised on Wednesday following another suspected gas emission that left students and staff struggling to breathe, with some fainting.

The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention.

Among the schools reportedly affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye.

A video circulating on social media showed some students fainting and being rushed for medical attention as panic spread across the affected communities.

The incident has renewed concerns over recurring gaseous emissions in parts of Ijebu land, with residents and school authorities calling on the state government to establish the source and prevent further exposure.

A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident began at about 10 a.m., when students and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties.

“The students and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and had to be rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said.

According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close for the day at about 11 a.m. as the situation worsened.

“Some of the schools in Ago-Iwoye had to close for the day when the situation became frightening and unbearable. The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode,” the teacher added.

The teacher said parents who heard about the incident rushed to their children’s schools to take them home amid fears for their safety.

The teacher further claimed that similar emissions had occurred since April, sending hundreds of students to hospitals during previous incidents.

“We are all worried about our health and the safety of our students. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas emission. The government needs to act quickly before the situation gets worse,” the teacher said.

Wednesday’s incident was reportedly the fourth occurrence of gaseous emissions disrupting school activities in Ijebu land since April 2026.

The first reported incident in April affected about 40 students, while more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure in May. Another 69 students were reportedly hospitalised on June 1.

Schools affected in previous incidents included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin.

The repeated incidents have heightened concerns about the safety of students and staff, particularly as some of the affected schools appear to have experienced multiple occurrences.

Government investigates suspected emissions

Following previous incidents, Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, said the state government was working with relevant agencies and experts to determine the cause of the emissions.

The governor said the Ministries of Environment and Health were collaborating with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority and the Department of Geology at Olabisi Onabanjo University to investigate the phenomenon.

Abiodun, who spoke on the matter in June, said gas analysers had been installed in affected schools to establish the nature and concentration of the emissions.

“Twice now, we have recorded cases of pollution in this school and some neighbouring schools. What is interesting is that the gas pollution occurred at about the same time in the affected schools — about three schools altogether — and this has happened on two separate occasions,” the governor said.

He added that the gas detected during the investigation had been identified as methane.

“Following the first occurrence, we installed gas analysers across the schools to determine the nature and concentration of the gas, which has now been confirmed to be methane,” he said.

According to the governor, preliminary findings suggested that geological factors, including fault lines, could be responsible for the emissions.

“Preliminary findings suggest there may be geological factors involved, possibly fault lines common to these locations, which could be responsible for the emissions. We are awaiting the final report from the professionals handling the investigation,” Abiodun said.

When contacted on Wednesday, the state Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said the government was monitoring the situation.

“We are on top of the situation,” he said.

Also speaking on the latest incident, Kehinde Bello, Senior Special Assistant to the governor and General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, said the emissions were linked to underground gas occurrences previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April.

Bello, who visited affected areas in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo to assess the situation, said the government was working towards finding a lasting solution.

He said investigations had indicated that the phenomenon could be a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak.

Bello urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention.

He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks.

However, the precise source of the emissions and the reasons for their recurrence remain unclear, with residents awaiting the outcome of the investigation.

As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were reportedly attending to affected students at general hospitals and other healthcare facilities.

The latest incident has intensified calls for a conclusive investigation and effective preventive measures to protect students and staff from further exposure.

World.title: Senate rejects NMDPRA’s PMS import records, summons agency heads
World.content:
Senate

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Public Accounts has rejected the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL).

The committee, chaired by Senator Ahmed Wadada Dankwambo, resolved on Wednesday to summon the heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) to explain the discrepancies and reconcile the conflicting records.

The decision followed the NMDPRA’s response to queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023.

Appearing before the committee, the NMDPRA’s Authority Chief Executive, Mallam Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, was represented by Deputy Director Uzoamaka Ugwu-Ojobe, who maintained that the authority’s records were credible despite the differences.

She told the committee that NMDPRA recorded 3.29 billion litres of PMS imports in 2022 and 6.02 billion litres in 2023, compared with the 6.27 billion litres and 3.88 billion litres reported by NNPCL for the respective years.

“The slight disparities are being looked into for possible reconciliation,” she said.

However, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, rejected the description of the differences as slight, noting that the figures showed substantial variations that required serious investigation.

“The disparities in records of PMS importation between NMDPRA and NNPCL in 2022 and 2023, as stated in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report of 2021 to 2023, are too wide to be described as slight or being looked into without the seriousness required,” he said.

Similarly, Senator Dayo Faduyile, representing Ondo South, said the discrepancies raised concerns about the reliability of the records submitted by the two agencies.

He said the differences left room for questions about what might have gone wrong in the reporting of petroleum imports.

Senator Anietan Bassey, representing Akwa Ibom North-East, called for a thorough investigation, insisting that Nigerians must not be shortchanged because of discrepancies in official records.

“Mr Chairman and very distinguished colleagues, these questionable records of volume of PMS importation by the two agencies must be thoroughly investigated to save Nigerians from being yearly shortchanged and expose those milking the country dry,” he said.

In his remarks, Dankwambo said the committee would convene a meeting involving the three agencies to establish the reasons for the conflicting figures.

“In view of the unacceptability of presentations made by the representative of NMDPRA on queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023, specifically on volume of PMS imported within the years under review, this committee resolved to summon heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and NEITI for reasons behind the wide disparities,” he said.

The committee is expected to use the meeting to seek explanations for the discrepancies and determine whether the records can be reconciled.

World.title: FG, States, Agencies Rally Nigerians in Early Fight against Ebola
World.content:
• Keyamo puts 44 contacts on ‘no-fly’ list

•Atiku demands accountability on N10bn preparedness fund

Emmanuel Addeh, Olawale Ajimotokan, Michael Olugbode, Sunday Aborisade, Juliet Akoje in Abuja and Ayodeji Ake in Lagos





The federal government, state governments, the National Assembly and public health institutions yesterday intensified efforts to prevent the spread of Ebola in Nigeria, mobilising health workers, strengthening disease surveillance and urging Nigerians to adopt precautionary measures following confirmation of an imported case in Abuja.

The response came as the Senate and House of Representatives called for the immediate release of emergency funds to strengthen the country’s preparedness, while the West African Health Organisation (WAHO) stepped up regional surveillance and coordination.

Besides, the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) urged persons suspected of infection to stay away from congregational prayers pending medical assessment.

In the same vein, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has demanded accountability for the N10 billion reportedly approved for Ebola preparedness, questioning how much had been released and how the money had been spent.

Health authorities have identified 44 contacts linked to the confirmed case and are tracing them for monitoring and appropriate medical intervention, as public health officials warn that early detection, contact tracing and strict infection prevention measures are critical to preventing further transmission.

Also, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) yesterday convened its first Incident Management Meeting following the official declaration of the outbreak, bringing together its leadership and key partners to coordinate response activities.

The development has prompted heightened vigilance across states, with Niger State placing public and private health facilities on alert and directing them to report suspected cases immediately.

Medical experts have also urged Nigerians to avoid unnecessary physical contact, practise regular handwashing and seek prompt medical attention if they develop symptoms or suspect exposure.

FG Assures Nigerians of Containment Strategies

The Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness, Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats yesterday evening assured Nigerians it can handle Ebola disease recently discovered in the country.

Chairman of the Task Force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said this while speaking to newsmen after the group’s emergency meeting at the State House, Abuja.

Gbajabiamila said the Task Force has been working behind the scenes since it was inaugurated in June this year adding that this informed why it was easy to detect the index case discovered yesterday.

“It’s very important to note this. Since the issue of Ebola came up in June, there have been about 44, 000 flights in and out of Nigeria. So, it’s because of what the Ministry of Health, the task force and all the agencies have been doing. All hands have been on deck.

“The passenger with the disease showed no symptoms, which came four days after the woman got into Abuja, and it was the identification process and the protocols that were put in place that enabled the quick identification. That also speaks to the country’s capacity and ability to deal with this disease as best as we can,” he added.

He assured Nigerians that the Task Force would strengthen whatever needed strengthening, the protocols, and ensure more rigorous enforcement moving forward.

“The Task Force is on top of it. NCDC is on top of it; everyone is on deck. We must build community trust and avoid panic, but it’s also important to state clearly that this is a collaborative effort between the government and the people,” he stated.

Also speaking, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate, said Nigeria has competent health authorities, including private hospital operators and agencies, Immigration, Aviation, Interior, and subnational actors, who have put surveillance systems in place across the country, ready to respond.

“We have been conducting contact tracing diligently and isolating those contacts of the index imported case in this country. We will continue to do that, and we want to reassure Nigerians that the federal government, alongside its technical partners, the World Health Organisation, the Africa Centre for Disease Control, and our own Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, have activated the incident management system across the various pillars.

“They are working day and night diligently, and our hospital capabilities are also activated, such that we can aim to contain this case, as has been the case in other countries, but we will not relent. Our population should respect public health directives.

“Most of our states have adequate response plans. We have the resources, and we’re mobilising those capabilities. And we’re also confident that if we continue on this path, we should be able to dent this outbreak,” he stated.

He further urged citizens to avoid misinformation while combating the virus.

“The key also for the population is to avoid spreading misinformation or baseless rumours, which can cause unnecessary panic. The Task Force leadership has met. WHO and Africa CDC are working closely with the team.

“In addition to our exceptional public health physicians who had successfully tamed this virus in 2014, and had contributed to other countries, we are confident that if we continue in this direction, we will emerge from this crisis in a much stronger place,” Pate assured.

Senate Demands Immediate Release of Emergency Funds

The Senate yesterday called on the federal government to release emergency funds from the Service Wide Vote to strengthen Nigeria’s disease surveillance and response system, following confirmation of the Ebola case in Abuja.

The upper chamber, however, rejected a proposal for relevant Senate committees to visit major international entry points to assess the country’s preparedness, after Senate President Godswill Akpabio questioned the necessity of the exercise and raised concerns about exposing lawmakers to possible infection.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Francis Faduyile, representing Ondo South, who called for mandatory health screening at international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases.

Faduyile, a professor of medicine, warned that Nigeria could not afford to take chances with its public health infrastructure, particularly as the strain responsible for the outbreak had no approved vaccine.

He urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, NCDC and Port Health Services to enforce compulsory screening for international arrivals, including health declaration forms, temperature checks and symptom assessments.

He also advocated enhanced screening for travellers who had visited or transited through affected areas within the preceding 21 days, irrespective of their nationality or country of departure.

The senator called for the provision of trained port health officers, thermal scanners, personal protective equipment and properly equipped isolation rooms at entry points, while urging the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria and the Nigeria Immigration Service to ensure that adequate personnel and facilities were available.

He further recommended the establishment of functional isolation and treatment centres in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, alongside stronger contact tracing and surveillance mechanisms.

Faduyile also called for a review of the Quarantine Act of 1926 to bring the legislation in line with contemporary public health realities and the International Health Regulations.

He proposed that Senate committees on Health, Primary Healthcare, Development and Disease Control, Aviation, Interior, and Appropriations visit major entry points and submit a report within four weeks.

However, Akpabio opposed the proposed visits, questioning whether lawmakers needed to travel to the entry points when the immediate priority was to strengthen the agencies responsible for disease surveillance and control.

The Senate President subsequently put the proposal to a vote, with the majority of lawmakers rejecting the visits while retaining support for measures to strengthen the country’s response.

Contributing to the debate, Senator Ekong Sampson, representing Akwa Ibom South, stressed the need to strengthen Nigeria’s health system to protect citizens against Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases.

Senator Sadiq Umar, representing Kwara North, called for the deployment of appropriate technology to improve contact tracing, while Senator Adamu Aliero, representing Kebbi Central, urged the federal government to release emergency resources without waiting for previously approved budgetary allocations to become available.

Senator Tahir Monguno, representing Borno North, also supported calls to amend the Quarantine Act.

House Seeks Strategic Action

The House of Representatives has called on the federal government to immediately mobilise public and private health agencies across the country and place them on high alert following a reported Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) case involving a woman who arrived in Abuja from Uganda.

The call followed a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Hon. Amobi Ogah on October 21, 2026 seeking stronger preventive and emergency medical measures to curb the spread of the disease in Nigeria.

Ogah expressed concern over the reported case which he said was confirmed on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 involving a woman who arrived from Uganda and tested positive for the virus in Abuja.

The lawmakers noted that Ebola Virus Disease is a severe and potentially fatal infectious disease that requires prompt detection, effective infection prevention and control measures and coordinated public health interventions to prevent transmission and save lives.

They warned that delays in identifying suspected cases, conducting appropriate laboratory investigations, isolating confirmed cases, tracing contacts and providing timely medical care could increase the risk of transmission and place additional pressure on Nigeria’s healthcare system.

The House further expressed concern that inadequate public awareness, insufficient infection prevention and control supplies, gaps in healthcare workers’ preparedness and limited emergency response capacity could undermine efforts to prevent and contain the outbreak.

It emphasised the critical roles of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, state ministries of health, port health authorities and other relevant stakeholders in strengthening the country’s epidemic preparedness and response mechanisms.

The lawmaker also acknowledged the importance of collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO) and other relevant international and regional public health institutions to ensure that Nigeria’s preventive and emergency response measures are guided by current scientific evidence and international health regulations.

Consequently, the House resolved to mandate the federal government to immediately mobilise all relevant private, state and federal health agencies and place them on high alert to contain the disease.

It also urged the federal government, through the Ministry of Finance, to urgently release all outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies to enable them to effectively discharge their responsibilities.

In another resolution, the lawmakers urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to immediately assess the funding expected to be released in order to strengthen Nigeria’s preparedness and response capacity against the disease, in line with current epidemiological evidence and public health guidance.

Atiku Demands Accountability for N10bn Fund

Former Vice President Atiku has demanded a detailed account of the N10 billion approved for Ebola preparedness, alleging that Nigeria’s response to the confirmed case has exposed gaps in surveillance, emergency funding and the protection of healthcare workers.

In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku called on President Bola Tinubu’s administration to disclose how much of the announced funding had been released, the dates of disbursement, contracts awarded, beneficiaries and items delivered.

“Ebola is a grave public health threat. Nigerians deserve urgent action, competent leadership and the truth,” he said. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered,” Atiku added.

He argued that announcing emergency funding was insufficient without verifiable evidence of disbursement and utilisation, calling for a formal audit to establish how the money had been spent.

The former vice president also questioned the timeline of the reported case, alleging that the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, while the government publicly confirmed the case on October 20.

He demanded explanations about the handling of the 44 contacts reportedly associated with the case and alleged that private healthcare workers lacked adequate protective equipment.

Atiku also questioned the leadership structure of the response, recalling that Tinubu announced a Presidential Task Force chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, in June.

He maintained that medical experts, including epidemiologists, doctors and public health professionals, should lead the technical response, with the authority and resources required to manage the outbreak.

The former vice president further alleged that the Minister of Health’s planned press conference was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and participating in voting. He warned that the outbreak could worsen economic pressures if the response disrupted movement, livelihoods and commercial activities.

WAHO, NCDC Step Up Surveillance

The West African Health Organisation (WAHO) has intensified regional disease surveillance and coordination among West African countries following the confirmation of the imported Ebola case in Abuja, amid concerns about possible cross-border transmission.

The ECOWAS health institution disclosed that Nigerian authorities confirmed the case on October 20, involving a woman who had recently arrived from Uganda.

According to WAHO, the patient developed symptoms on October 7 and received treatment at a private health facility in Abuja on October 11, before laboratory tests confirmed the infection on October 20.

The organisation said it was monitoring the situation in collaboration with the NCDC, national health authorities and regional epidemiological surveillance mechanisms.

As part of the response, WAHO yesterday held a briefing with directors of the National Public Health Institutes of ECOWAS member states to reinforce regional vigilance and coordination.

It stressed that early detection, prompt notification of suspected cases, effective epidemiological surveillance and coordination among health services were critical to containing epidemic-prone diseases.

The organisation advised the public to wash their hands frequently with soap and clean water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers.

It also urged Nigerians to avoid direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of sick or deceased persons, as well as contaminated clothing, bedding and personal belongings.

WAHO warned against handling the bodies of people who died from suspected causes, recommending that safe and dignified burials be conducted by trained teams.

It further advised against handling or consuming bushmeat and cautioned against contact with sick or dead animals, including bats and primates, urging people to ensure that meat was thoroughly cooked.

People experiencing symptoms consistent with Ebola, including sudden fever, severe fatigue, body aches, vomiting, diarrhoea or bleeding, were advised to contact or seek assistance from a health facility immediately.

WAHO also urged travellers to avoid non-essential journeys to affected areas and comply with official health guidance where travel was unavoidable.

Warning against misinformation during public health emergencies, the organisation urged Nigerians to rely on official sources and refrain from circulating rumours or unverified reports.

It reaffirmed its commitment to working with the health ministries of ECOWAS member states and technical and financial partners to strengthen regional health security.

The organisation said its specialised Regional Centre for Surveillance and Disease Control, based in Abuja, would continue monitoring developments and sharing relevant information in coordination with the appropriate health authorities.

Besides, the NCDC yesterday convened its first Incident Management Meeting following the official declaration of the outbreak in Nigeria.

The meeting brought together the agency’s leadership and key partners to align response efforts as the Incident Action Plan was being finalised.

NCDC teams were also conducting case management and response activities, with emphasis on enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and coordinated risk communication.

The measures are intended to strengthen the detection and management of suspected cases, identify people who may have been exposed to the virus and limit potential transmission. The agency reaffirmed its commitment to a timely, coordinated and evidence-based response, stressing the importance of collaboration among stakeholders.

WHO Urges Nigeria, Others to Strengthen Measures

The World Health Organisation (WHO), has advised countries in Africa to strengthen control measures, including case investigation, contact tracing, infection prevention and control. This followed reported import of Ebola into Nigeria’s federal capital territory, Abuja.

WHO said it was working closely with, “partners and health authorities to strengthen control measures, including case investigation, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and provision of essential supplies including personal protective equipment for health workers.

In a statement, the organisation urged all countries in the region to sustain a high level of readiness as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to evolve.

“Kenya has reported nine cases linked to an imported case in recent weeks. Countries should maintain strong disease surveillance and rapid alert investigation, ensure laboratories can safely test suspected cases, keep rapid response and clinical teams ready for immediate activation, reinforce infection prevention and control in both public and private health facilities, and pre-position essential supplies, while actively engaging with communities.

“They should also heighten monitoring at points of entry, with response plans in place. Sustained readiness is essential to detect cases early, prevent onward transmission and protect health workers and communities.

“WHO advises against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries, and continues to closely monitor and, where necessary, verify travel and trade measures in relation to this event.

“WHO risk assessment is being regularly reassessed, to incorporate the latest developments related to this event.”

NSCIA Bars Suspected Ebola Carriers from Prayers

The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) has urged persons suspected of Ebola infection to refrain from attending congregational prayers pending medical assessment, as part of measures to prevent the spread of the disease.

The council, under the leadership of its President General and Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, made the call in a public health advisory issued yesterday following the reported laboratory confirmation of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory.

In the advisory signed by the NSCIA Secretary General, Prof. Is-haq Oloyede, the council urged Muslims to comply with medical guidance and prioritise the preservation of life.

It called on chief imams, Islamic scholars, state councils for Islamic affairs and Muslim organisations to intensify public awareness through Friday sermons, religious gatherings and community engagements.

The council also advised anyone experiencing symptoms associated with Ebola, particularly following possible exposure, to seek prompt medical attention and avoid close contact with others while awaiting professional guidance.

It warned that Ebola could spread through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of infected persons who had developed symptoms, contaminated materials or the bodies of people who had died from the disease.

The NSCIA identified fever, severe headache, weakness, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in some cases, unexplained bleeding as symptoms requiring attention.

It urged Nigerians to wash their hands regularly, avoid contact with suspected cases and promptly report suspected infections to the appropriate health authorities.

The council also called on the federal and state governments to strengthen disease surveillance, contact tracing, public enlightenment and healthcare facility preparedness, while ensuring adequate protection for health workers and timely dissemination of accurate information.

Emphasising the religious basis for the measures, the NSCIA said the preservation of life, known in Islamic jurisprudence as Hifz al-Nafs, was one of the fundamental objectives of Islamic law.

It referenced Qur’an 2:195, which cautions against throwing oneself into destruction, and recalled the Prophet Muhammad’s guidance on precautions during infectious disease outbreaks.

The council urged the public to avoid spreading unverified information and to refrain from stigmatising affected individuals and their families.

It reaffirmed its readiness to mobilise mosques, Islamic organisations and community leaders nationwide to support public health education and disease prevention.

The NSCIA urged Nigerians to remain calm and act responsibly, stressing that faith, prayer and appropriate medical care were complementary in responding to public health emergencies.

Expert Urges Nigerians to Avoid Physical Contact

President of the Academy of Medical Sciences, Prof. Oladapo Ashiru, yesterday urged Nigerians to avoid handshakes and hugs, maintain strict personal hygiene and promptly report suspected cases to prevent the spread of Ebola.

Ashiru made the call during an interview with Arise News, where he described the situation as serious but manageable, stressing that public awareness, early detection and strict adherence to infection prevention measures would be critical to containing the threat.

He recalled Nigeria’s successful response to the 2014 Ebola outbreak in Lagos, saying the country could draw on that experience to prevent further transmission.

“It can be managed. And the way we manage this depends on how we respond to this situation,” he said. “We successfully managed this in 2014 when there was an index case in Lagos, and it was critically managed and contained,” he added.

Ashiru said the circumstances surrounding the current infection, including whether it occurred during transit or originated from Uganda, remained unclear. “Right now, we have one case confirmed in Abuja. Whether in transit or from Uganda, we don’t know,” he said.

He explained that Ebola differed from COVID-19 because it was not airborne and was primarily transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of an infected person.

“In the case of Ebola, the difference between Ebola and COVID-19 is that Ebola is not airborne, whereas COVID-19 is airborne,” he said.

He identified contact with the bodily fluids or secretions of an infected person, particularly after symptoms developed, as a major route of transmission. “The major way you can get it is by contacting the body fluid or secretions of somebody showing the signs of Ebola,” he said.

The medical expert advised Nigerians to suspend customary greetings involving physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, while preventive measures were strengthened.

“This is a time for Nigerians, as the Academy of Medical Sciences has stressed, to refrain from shaking hands and hugging,” he said.

The expert urged public and private hospitals, clinics and other healthcare facilities to strengthen surveillance and remain alert to patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of Ebola.

He said healthcare providers must act promptly when they encounter a patient with fever or other symptoms that raise suspicion of infection.

“The private clinics must be on high alert in terms of once you recognise a case with fever or you suspect it, you have to be proactive in suspecting such cases,” he said.

Ashiru particularly cautioned health workers about the risks associated with removing personal protective equipment after attending to suspected or confirmed cases.

Niger Ramps Up Surveillance

The Niger State Government has placed public health organisations across the state on heightened alert following confirmation of the Ebola case in Abuja.

The government said the measures were precautionary and intended to strengthen surveillance, early detection and rapid response capacity, particularly because of the frequent movement of people and volume of trade between Niger State and neighbouring Abuja.

The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Murtala Bagana, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists in Minna yesterday, reassuring residents that no Ebola case had been detected in the state.

He said the state government was collaborating with the NCDC, the World Health Organisation and other international partners to strengthen preparedness and ensure a coordinated response.

According to him, public and private health facilities across the state had been directed to report any suspected case immediately.

Bagana said Local Government Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers and response teams had been deployed to strengthen contact tracing, clinical assessment and safe referral protocols.

He added that infection prevention and control measures had been reinforced across health centres to protect frontline workers and patients.

The commissioner appealed to residents to remain calm, avoid panic and observe basic hygiene, particularly frequent handwashing with soap and water or alcohol-based hand sanitisers.

He also advised residents to avoid direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of anyone exhibiting symptoms and warned against spreading unverified rumours or stigmatising individuals being assessed by public health officials.

Bagana stressed that living in or travelling to Niger State did not, in itself, constitute exposure to the virus.

He advised anyone exhibiting symptoms or suspecting possible exposure to isolate themselves and contact public health authorities through designated emergency hotlines before visiting a medical facility.

The state government said the heightened alert was intended to ensure that suspected infections could be identified promptly and referred for appropriate medical assessment, while surveillance and response systems remained on standby.

World.title: Mbah Backs Tinubu on Fuel Subsidy Removal, Says a Return Inconceivable
World.content:
• Maintains subsidy return will create panic among investors

• Insists he has delivered good governance to Enugu

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has doubled down in his support for the removal of fuel subsidy by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying it was undebatable and inconceivable for anyone to imagine a return to the old order.

Mbah spoke at the “Meet the Candidates” town hall meeting organised by Afia TV in Enugu yesterday, where he also said that his administration had delivered good governance to the people of the state across all sectors.

He described it as a pathetic misconception of the country’s situation and the direction it was headed for anyone to talk about the reintroduction of fuel subsidy.

“If you reintroduce fuel subsidy today, we will lose ten times whatever we are currently trying to gain in terms of the removal of subsidy. The poverty rate that you are going to experience will be very high because the naira would be automatically devalued.

“We cannot go back to subsidy. And I do not think it is in the interest of the country for us to even debate that.

“Again, we should not even debate it because we do not want to send a signal to prospective investors that we are contemplating it. That would take us back. It is going to create panic in the system. It is going to get investors to pull back.

“Those that are coming in today to invest in that sector will become jittery. So, it is not even a subject to debate. It is something that we have moved on from, and we should be thinking about how to ensure that the natural benefits cascade to the households, create jobs and generate wealth for our people,” he said.

He said the nation should focus on how to further encourage private capital to flow, noting the growth the nation had experienced in the stock exchange space.

He added that Tinubu’s policies had stabilised the macro indicators, thus encouraging foreign direct investment.

“You can see quite a lot of funds coming into our country, not just portfolio investments, but also direct investments. It is also going to strengthen because the macro indicators are right,” he stated.

Mbah maintained that whereas fuel subsidy removal enables the government to target the less privileged, fuel subsidy as earlier practised benefited the rich more.

“By the way, I do not think the subsidy we practised before the President removed it was even the right one for the country because even the people we were looking at benefiting from it were only insignificantly benefiting from it. It was largely beneficial to our wealthy folks.

“But now, you can almost notice that the government is doing that in targeting the poor, using proceeds from subsidy removal. The government is aggressive on cash transfers. There is also the programme where the government is targeting 1,000 persons per ward across the entire country to be able to provide seed capital for them to become productive,” he added.

Meanwhile, on his stewardship so far, Mbah said his administration had kept faith with the people of Enugu State, delivering good governance across all sectors in line with his campaign manifesto.

He said the people of the state only needed to imagine where the state was before his inauguration as governor and where it is currently headed.

“Let us imagine the Enugu we knew four years ago. Let us just imagine an Enugu without Hotel Presidential. Let us imagine an Enugu without the International Conference Centre. Let us imagine an Enugu without Enugu Air. Let us imagine Enugu without the transport terminals, the 268 Smart Green Schools, 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres.

“You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the International Hospital. You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the CNG buses, the Nigergas. I think the list is endless.

“But I even think that we can stretch that imagination further because the work ahead will be more profound. Just imagine an Enugu where our children are receiving education that prepares them for the world because they have been imbued with evolving 21st-century skills. Imagine again an Enugu where you do not have any part of the city with an unpaved road.

“Also, imagine an Enugu in four years’ time that generates 660 megawatts of electricity; where we are able to provide 24-hour power supply; where you cannot come into your house and have the light off; and where people can run their businesses for a whole week without worrying about the cost of diesel.

“Just imagine an Enugu where you generate electricity and the people of Enugu are buying that at 120 naira because they own the coal that feeds the power plant.

“Imagine an Enugu where you now have to ride, not just on our CNG buses, but you have the monorail that can take you from point A to point B. Imagine an Enugu where you can fly from here to the United Kingdom, to the United States and other parts of the world,” he stressed.

Mbah urged the people to keep faith with the journey of greatness, growth and development, defending the gains of his first term and guaranteeing the promises of his second term by working for his re-election.

“If these imaginations capture our fancy, then we have a duty to fight for it. We do have a duty to continue to make sure that the bar does not come down and that the standard we have set in Enugu is sustained,” he noted.

World.title: Fertiliser Summit: Experts Proffer Measures to Boost Food Security
World.content:
Agricultural experts, researchers and policymakers have called for greater investment in soil intelligence, digital technology and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations to improve farm productivity and strengthen food security in Nigeria.

The call was made at the 2026 Nigeria Fertiliser Summit on Phosphorus and Food Security, held in Abuja, where more than 280 participants from across the agricultural sector examined ways to improve nutrient management and ensure farmers obtain better returns from fertiliser application.

The summit was organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University, in partnership with the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) and the Fertiliser and Inputs Support Services Department of the federal ministry of agriculture and food security.

Speaking at the opening session, the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Aliyu Abdullahi, represented by the Director of Agricultural Land and Climate Change Management Services in the ministry, Mr Oshadiya Olanipekun, emphasised the importance of soil data, soil testing and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations in improving farmers’ productivity.

He also acknowledged the contribution of the Regional Hub for Fertiliser and Soil Health for West Africa and the Sahel, noting that collaboration with the initiative would enable Nigeria to benefit from regional expertise and technical support for site-specific fertiliser recommendations.

Similarly, the Vice Chancellor of Obafemi Awolowo University, Prof. A.S. Bamire, said improving agricultural productivity required more than increased fertiliser application, stressing the importance of responsible nutrient management, research, innovation and stronger partnerships.

A member of IAR&T and one of the summit organisers, Prof. Vincent Aduramigba-Modupe, said agricultural transformation depended on applying the appropriate nutrients in the right quantities and under suitable conditions.

“Improving crop productivity is not only about applying fertilizer. It is about ensuring the right nutrient is applied in the right amount, at the right place, and under the right conditions,” he said.

Participants identified soil intelligence as a critical component of efforts to improve fertiliser-use efficiency, highlighting the importance of digital soil maps, soil information systems, laboratory services, site-specific nutrient recommendations and digital advisory tools.

A visiting scientist with the Regional Hub and Professor of Soil Science at Bayero University, Kano, Prof. Jibrin Mohammed Jibrin, described soil intelligence as fundamental to achieving food security.

“The basis of food production and food security is the soil. You need healthy soil to produce well and feed the nation with nutritious food. To do that, you need soil intelligence,” he said.

Presentations by the Regional Hub highlighted ongoing efforts to strengthen evidence-based nutrient management in Nigeria and across West Africa through digital soil mapping, support for national soil information systems, laboratory assessments and the validation of fertiliser recommendations tailored to specific soils and crops.

The Hub’s Senior Agronomist, Dr Bello Shehu, said improving phosphorus management required a better understanding of the nutrient needs of different soils and crops.

“It is about understanding what different soils and crops need and ensuring that farmers have access to the right products and the right advice,” he said.

The summit also underscored the need for stronger coordination among stakeholders to address fragmented approaches to soil health and fertiliser management.

Participants noted that although several initiatives were already underway, improved collaboration was necessary to prevent duplication, align priorities and accelerate implementation.

They highlighted the roles of technical working groups, the Coalition of the Willing and Nigeria’s National Technical Team, which serves as an interface between the country and the Regional Hub, helping to align national priorities with regional expertise and support.

“If we want to achieve our goals, we have to work together. Too many initiatives have been implemented in silos. Real progress will come when stakeholders align, collaborate and follow through on agreed actions,” Jibrin said.

The summit further highlighted the Regional Hub’s role as a technical resource and coordination platform supporting fertiliser and soil-health priorities across West Africa and the Sahel.

The Hub works with a consortium comprising the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, the International Fertiliser Development Center, OCP Africa, the International Soil Reference and Information Centre, the African Plant Nutrition Institute and Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, alongside national technical teams, country focal points and research institutions across the region.

In a goodwill message, the incoming Director of the Regional Hub, Bastiaan Huesken, said the initiative was established to help countries translate scientific evidence into practical solutions for farmers.

“The Hub was created to turn soil data into recommendations, and recommendations into products and advice that farmers can use,” he said.

World.title: Akume: North-south Power Rotation Good for National Unity
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja





The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, has urged political stakeholders to respect the North-south power rotation arrangement, saying the principle is essential to Nigeria’s national stability, fairness and democratic consolidation.
