He made this known yesterday in Abuja when he received a delegation from the Order of the Knights of St. Mulumba (KSM), Nigeria, led by its Supreme Knight, Sir Steve Adehi.

Akume said the arrangement, which emerged from consultations among political leaders ahead of the return to civilian rule in 1999, remained an important framework for promoting national cohesion and ensuring equitable distribution of political power between the two regions.

The SGF recalled that political leaders, who met in Kaduna in 1999 had agreed that presidential power should alternate between the North and the South in eight-year cycles, beginning with the South, as part of efforts to address concerns about political exclusion and strengthen national unity.

He explained that the arrangement was conceived to promote political balance, build mutual trust and safeguard the country’s territorial integrity by ensuring that neither region felt permanently excluded from the nation’s highest political office.

Akume insisted that power rotation should not be regarded as a temporary political convenience but as a fundamental political understanding anchored on fairness, mutual respect and national stability.

He also expressed concern over attempts by Northern aspirants to contest the presidency before the completion of the South’s current eight-year cycle, insisting that the established sequence should be respected.

According to him, following the eight-year administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari, the current presidential tenure held by a Southerner should be allowed to run its course in accordance with the principle of alternating power between the two regions.

He argued that respecting the arrangement would reinforce confidence in the democratic process and help sustain the understanding among Nigeria’s diverse political and regional interests.

Akume further emphasised the need for greater collaboration among the federal, state and local governments to address the country’s economic and social challenges, noting that ongoing reforms and development initiatives should be assessed against both immediate economic realities and long-term national objectives.

He commended the Order of the Knights of St. Mulumba for its charitable interventions aimed at improving the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians.

Earlier, Adehi said the organisation had undertaken several humanitarian initiatives, including supporting medical treatment for patients, assisting inmates with outstanding financial obligations to facilitate their release from correctional facilities, providing boreholes, renovating schools and supporting hospitals.

He explained that the interventions were informed by the recognition that the government alone could not address the numerous social and economic challenges facing the country.

He also urged greater collaboration between government and private organisations through philanthropy, partnerships and community-based initiatives to alleviate poverty and improve living conditions

Umahi Seeks Support for Tinubu’s Second Term Bid, Cites Infrastructure Drive

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The Minister of Works, David Umahi, has urged Nigerians to support President Bola Tinubu’s second term bid, arguing that continuity in leadership would sustain the administration’s infrastructure drive and consolidate the gains of its economic reforms.

Umahi made the call at a town hall meeting in Kano, ahead of the commissioning of major road projects in the state, including outstanding works on Section I, Lot 1 (Zaria-Kano) of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Expressway, the ministry said in a statement.

The minister, who also called for the re-election of Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, said the federal government’s infrastructure investments and difficult economic decisions were laying the foundation for sustainable growth and prosperity.

“The worst is over. The darkest part of the morning is the dawn. We are moving into prosperity as a result of the hard decisions occasioned by the reforms,” he said.

He identified the removal of petroleum subsidy and other economic policy changes as necessary measures to reposition the Nigerian economy, urging citizens to remain patient as the benefits of the reforms increasingly translated into development projects across the country.

Umahi also dismissed the perception that the South-east was opposed to Tinubu’s administration, reaffirming the region’s commitment to national unity and calling for support for the president’s second-term ambition.

The minister commended Yusuf for his leadership, particularly his efforts to promote peace, unity and inclusive governance, while praising the state’s environmental sanitation standards.

“I am yet to see another state that is beating Kano in cleanliness. In all the streets we passed through, you could pick a pin,” Umahi said.

He attributed the level of cleanliness to purposeful leadership and the effective use of public resources, adding that Kano’s example reflected the standard of environmental responsibility and governance Nigerians deserved.

Umahi also praised the governor for bringing together political leaders, former governors, prominent indigenes and other stakeholders, describing the gesture as evidence of mutual respect and a commitment to the collective progress of the state.

He urged Kano residents to support Yusuf’s second-term bid, arguing that continuity would help sustain the governor’s development initiatives and strengthen the state’s contribution to national progress.

The minister further advocated greater representation of engineers in leadership positions, saying their technical expertise, professional training and problem-solving abilities could improve governance and infrastructure delivery.

He expressed appreciation for the peaceful atmosphere and unity he witnessed in Kano, noting that the experience had positively influenced his perception of the state and prompted him to reconsider his departure date.

Earlier, Yusuf commended the federal government for its infrastructure investments, particularly the road projects expected to improve transportation, connectivity and economic activities in Kano and the wider North-west region.

The governor described the scheduled commissioning of outstanding works on the Zaria-Kano section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Expressway as a significant milestone in the country’s infrastructure development.

He thanked Tinubu for the interventions and other support extended to Kano State, expressing optimism that the commissioning ceremony would be successful.

The Federal Ministry of Works said it remained committed to delivering durable, safe and quality road infrastructure across the country under the federal government’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

World.title: Tinubu Felicitates Kwankwaso at 70, Says He’s a Friend and Progressive Politician
World.content:
• Hails his contributions to nation, as Obi, NDC vow to rescue Nigeria, celebrate ally

Deji Elumoye and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja





President Bola Tinubu has rejoiced with the vice presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, on his 70th birthday, describing him as his friend and progressive politician.

Tinubu acknowledged the contributions of Kwankwaso, whom he described as an influential figure, in different capacities, as ex-governor of Kano State, and ex-defence minister and former Senator.

Tinubu, in a seven-paragraph tribute, stated, “My warm congratulations to my friend, Dr Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, former Governor of Kano State, one-time Minister of Defence and former Senator representing Kano Central Senatorial District, on his 70th birthday on October 21, 2026.

“Senator Kwankwaso and I have longstanding association, dating back to our time in the National Assembly in 1992, he in the House of Representatives and I in the Senate, and later in 1999 when we both emerged as governors of our respective states.

“As members of the Class of ‘99 Governors, we both played pivotal roles in laying the foundation for the democracy the nation enjoys today.

“Shaped by different political choices, our political paths differed until we coalesced in 2013 to form the All Progressives Congress. Since then, history and service have kept us intertwined.

“I must acknowledge Senator Kwankwaso’s immense contributions to Kano State and Nigeria as a two-term Governor, former Minister of Defence, former Senator, former presidential candidate, and now a presidential running mate.

“Senator Kwankwaso remains an influential figure and a progressive politician. That we are in different political parties and competing on different platforms in the January 2027 election will not remove my affection for Senator Kwankwaso.

“As the former governor marks this milestone, I wish him good health, personal fulfilment, and many more years of engagement in the nation’s democratic process.”

Obi, NDC Celebrate Kwankwaso, Vow to Rescue Nigeria from APC in 2027 Elections

Presidential candidate of NDC, Peter Obi, and the party’s leadership celebrated Kwankwaso on his 70th birthday, describing him as an experienced public servant and a key partner in their quest to transform Nigeria.

In a separate birthday tribute, Obi expressed confidence in his partnership with the former Kano State governor, saying their shared commitment to national development could help rescue the country from the consequences of poor governance.

NDC also praised Kwankwaso’s record in public service, citing his experience in the legislature, the executive arm of government, and Kano State politics as important assets to the party’s presidential ticket ahead of the 2027 general election.

Obi said their relationship had deepened through conversations and a shared determination to build a country that offers opportunities to all Nigerians.

He stated, “With the passage of time, I have come to appreciate the bond between us deeply, the many conversations we have shared, and the common commitment to Nigeria that continues to shape our service.

“As you mark your 70th birthday on October 21, I honour not only an accomplished public servant but also a very dear elder brother, friend, and partner whose life has been dedicated to serving our people.”

Obi said Kwankwaso’s career had taken him through the legislature, the Federal Executive Council, the governorship of Kano State, and other responsibilities in national public life.

According to Obi, those experiences represent decades of engagement with the Nigerian people and provide a foundation for continued service to the country.

The NDC presidential candidate said, “Turning seventy is not merely a significant milestone; it is a moment to look back with gratitude on a life devoted to service, the wisdom gained through experience, and the opportunities that remain ahead.

“As we continue to hope for and work toward a better Nigeria, I remain grateful for our partnership, and for our shared conviction that our nation can become a place where no child is deprived of opportunity, no family is left in poverty, and every Nigerian can live with dignity, security, and hope.

“My dear brother, may God bless you with renewed strength, good health, wisdom, and many more productive years. May the years ahead be filled with peace, fulfilment, and the satisfaction of seeing the values we cherish take firmer root across our nation.”

In its statement, NDC, through its National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses, congratulated Kwankwaso on behalf of the party’s National Executive Committee, National Working Committee, members, and supporters in Nigeria and the diaspora.

The party described the former Kano State governor as a symbol of courage, progressive politics, and people-centred leadership.

It said his record in Kano State and his service at the national level had established him as an influential figure in Nigerian politics.

“At 70, you remain a towering symbol of courage, selfless service, progressive politics, and people-centered leadership,” the party said.

NDC recalled Kwankwaso’s tenure as governor of Kano State, where he promoted the Kwankwasiyya political philosophy, and his service as a senator, minister, and national political leader.

It stated that his experience and grassroots support had strengthened the party’s presidential ticket, which pairs him with Obi.

“As our vice presidential candidate, you have brought uncommon energy, loyalty, capacity, and grassroots appeal to the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) ticket,” the statement said.

The party added that Kwankwaso remained a dependable partner in its campaign to build a new Nigeria that works for all citizens.

World.title: Senate Mourns Uduaghan, Recalls Role in Niger Delta Amnesty, Regional Integration
World.content:
• Akpabio, Oshiomhole, Nwoko, others highlight his legacy

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja





Senate, yesterday, paid tribute to former governor of Delta State, Emmanuel Uduaghan, recalling his contributions to peace-building in the Niger Delta, regional economic integration, and the development of healthcare and infrastructure during his eight-year administration.

President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, highlighted Uduaghan’s role in the BRACED Commission, a regional development initiative involving Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Edo and Delta states, as well as his participation in efforts by South-south governors to address militancy in the Niger Delta.

Akpabio said the former governor worked with other governors in the region and the administration of former President Umaru Yar’Adua towards the amnesty initiative that helped restore relative peace in the oil-producing communities.

The senate’s tributes followed a motion by Senator Joel-Onowakpo Thomas (Delta South) and co-sponsored by Senators Ned Nwoko (Delta North), Ede Dafinone (Delta Central), and Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan (Kogi Central), following the death of the former governor on October 19. He was 71.

Lawmakers who contributed to the debate highlighted Uduaghan’s record in healthcare delivery, education, transportation, and economic diversification, describing his years in public service as significant to the development of Delta State and the wider South-south region.

Moving the motion, Thomas described the deceased as a distinguished medical practitioner, statesman, and public servant whose eight years as governor left an imprint on the political, social, and economic development of Delta State.

Thomas said Uduaghan’s medical background shaped his administration’s emphasis on healthcare, particularly through programmes that provided free medical services to pregnant women, nursing mothers and children under five.

He also cited investments in the Delta State University Teaching Hospital, Oghara, and initiatives aimed at improving education, including the rehabilitation of public schools, the Edu-My-Child programme, scholarships, and assistance for students taking public examinations.

On infrastructure, the senator listed road construction, transportation projects, and the development of Asaba International Airport among the major initiatives undertaken during Uduaghan’s administration.

He added that the former governor’s Delta Beyond Oil agenda sought to reduce the state’s dependence on crude oil revenue by encouraging agriculture, tourism and the growth of small and medium-scale enterprises.

Contributing to the debate, Dafinone said the late governor’s legacy should be assessed by the lives he touched through public service.

“Public service is marked by the number of lives touched in service, and there is no doubt that in his eight years as governor, his position as Secretary to the State Government and Commissioner for Health, our late governor touched very many lives,” he said.

Former Edo State governor and senator for Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, highlighted Uduaghan’s contribution to regional integration through the BRACED Commission.

Oshiomhole said the initiative was designed to move the six South-south states beyond periodic meetings towards a coordinated development framework that could harness the region’s natural resources and human capital.

He recalled that Uduaghan provided logistical support for the establishment of a secretariat to coordinate the commission’s activities.

Oshiomhole stated, “Emmanuel Uduaghan was not lost in the Itsekiri people. He may have been born as an Itsekiri man by accident of birth, but actually, he was a proud son of Delta, and he deployed all he had to upgrade the living standard of Delta.”

Nwoko, in his contribution, recalled discussions with Uduaghan about the development of Asaba International Airport during his time in the House of Representatives between 1999 and 2003.

He said the proposal initially encountered opposition from the administration of former Governor James Ibori, which argued that Delta State already had an airport at Osubi, near Warri.

Nwoko’s account highlighted the policy discussions that preceded the development of the Asaba airport, which subsequently became an important transportation facility for the state.

Senator Francis Faduyile, a medical doctor representing Ondo South, described Uduaghan as a role model whose professional background informed his commitment to improving healthcare delivery.

Faduyile recalled the former governor’s interventions in the health sector and his participation in a National Health Summit organised by the Nigerian Medical Association.

Akpoti-Uduaghan, who described the deceased as her in-law, spoke of his compassion, gentleness, and willingness to offer counsel and support to members of his family.

“He is a father figure to many, and to me, he goes beyond being an in-law,” she said.

At the end of the deliberations, the senate observed a minute’s silence in honour of the former governor and extended its condolences to his family and the people of Delta State.

Born on October 22, 1954, in Abigborodo, Warri North Local Government Area of Delta State, Uduaghan trained as a medical doctor at the University of Benin before entering public service.

He served as Delta State Commissioner for Health in 1999, Secretary to the State Government from 2003 to 2007, and governor from May 29, 2007 to May 29, 2015.

World.title: Shettima, Akpabio, Daniel, Mimiko, Hamzat, Adeyeye, Others Mourn Fasoranti
World.content:
• Hail his legacy of democratic struggle

•Nigeria lost a century of wisdom, principled leadership, says vice president

•Ex-Ondo gov grieves over Uduaghan

Deji Elumoye, Sunday Aborisade in Abuja, James Sowole in Abeokuta and Fidelis David in Akure





Vice President Kashim Shettima has expressed sorrow over the passing of Leader of Afenifere, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, describing his departure as the end of a remarkable chapter in Nigeria’s political and democratic history.

Mourning, too, President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, paid glowing tributes to Pa Fasoranti, describing him as a patriot, whose contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development would endure beyond his lifetime.

In the same spirit, former governor of Ogun State, Otunba Gbenga Daniel, expressed sorrow over the passing of the Afenifere national leader, describing his death at the age of 100 as a monumental loss to Yorubaland and Nigeria.

Former governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, said the death of Pa Fasoranti marked the end of an era of principle, integrity, and selfless service in Nigeria’s political history,

Lagos State Deputy Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, who expressed sorrow over Pa Fasoranti’s death, said he was a respected voice in the nation’s political arena.

Similarly, Chairman of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA’23), Senator Dayo Adeyeye, hailed the legacy of the deceased, especially his support for President Bola Tinubu in 2023.

At the same time, Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, mourned the elder statesman’s passing, describing him as a towering figure whose legacy would inspire generations.

The vice president, in a condolence message, said the late patriarch, who passed on at the age of 100 belonged to a generation of leaders, who understood that public service was a lifelong obligation to society.

He said Fasoranti’s century-long journey reflected the struggles, sacrifices, and aspirations that shaped modern Nigeria.

Shettima extended his sympathies to the Fasoranti family, the leadership and members of Afenifere, the government and people of Ondo State, and the entire Yoruba nation.

He stated, “There are men who live through history, and there are those whose lives become part of history itself. Pa Reuben Fasoranti belonged to the latter. For a hundred years, he witnessed the changing fortunes of our nation, yet remained steadfast in his convictions and commitment to the common good.

“Baba’s passing reminds us that the true measure of a life is neither the number of years lived nor the offices occupied, but the values transmitted, the people inspired and the institutions strengthened along the way.”

The vice president described the late elder statesman as a custodian of political memory whose contributions to education, democratic governance, and progressive politics transcended regional boundaries.

Shettima stated that while Pa Fasoranti’s longevity was extraordinary, his passing would remain deeply painful to those who knew him as a father, grandfather, mentor, and trusted counsellor.

He said, “Even a hundred years cannot exhaust the love of a family or prepare the heart for the final departure of a cherished patriarch. Those who loved Baba will miss the familiar voice, the reassuring presence and the wisdom that no public tribute can fully capture.

“Yet, there is consolation in knowing that a life devoted to service does not end with its final breath. It continues in the character of those it shaped, the convictions it inspired and the memories that give succeeding generations a sense of belonging.”

The vice president said Pa Fasoranti’s legacy should encourage Nigerians to preserve the values of dialogue, mutual respect, and responsible citizenship, particularly in moments of political disagreement.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the late patriarch’s soul and divine comfort for his family and all who mourn him.

Godswill Akpabio

Akpabio, in a condolence message, said Nigeria had lost a distinguished elder statesman whose life exemplified integrity, courage, selflessness, and an unwavering commitment to public service.

He described the late Afenifere leader’s death as a profound loss to his family, the Yoruba nation, and the country, stating that Fasoranti belonged to a generation of Nigerians whose contributions helped shape the country’s political and democratic evolution.

The senate president said Fasoranti’s influence transcended ethnic and political boundaries, adding that his commitment to democratic ideals, social justice, and principled leadership remains relevant to Nigeria’s quest for national progress.

He stated, “Pa Reuben Fasoranti was one of those rare elder statesmen whose lives embodied the wisdom of experience and the strength of conviction.

“His passing is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family and the Yoruba people, but also to the entire Nigerian nation.

“At 100, Baba Fasoranti leaves behind an enduring legacy of service, courage and fidelity to his convictions.

“His life reminds us that true leadership is measured not merely by the positions we occupy, but by the values we uphold, the people we serve and the positive impact we leave on society.”

Akpabio added that the late Afenifere leader’s century-long life was a testament to the enduring value of service and fidelity to personal convictions

Gbenga Daniel

Daniel, who had long regarded the centenarian as a father figure and moral compass, stated that Baba Fasoranti lived a century defined by integrity, courage, and unwavering service to the progressive cause.

Reflecting on their personal bond, Daniel recalled his visit to Pa Fasoranti’s residence in 2019 to commiserate with him over the tragic murder of his daughter, Funke Olakunrin, where he praised the nonagenarian for his resilience and for continuing to provide much-needed leadership for the Yoruba race despite personal grief.

Describing him as one of the few remaining leaders truly passionate about national existence, Daniel also remembered Pa Fasoranti as the embodiment of the Omoluabi ethos.

Olusegun Mimiko

Mimiko said Pa Fasoranti’s passing marked the end of an era of principle, integrity and selfless service in Nigeria’s political history,

Mimiko, who described Fasoranti as more than an elder statesman, said he was a custodian of political tradition and a devoted disciple of the late nationalist leader, Chief Obafemi Awolowo.

He said Fasoranti’s life embodied discipline, integrity, courage and service, adding that his record as an educationist, administrator, politician, Afenifere leader and pro-democracy activist distinguished him across generations.

Mimiko, who governed Ondo State between 2009 and 2017, recalled that Fasoranti served as Commissioner for Finance under the administration of the late Governor Michael Ajasin, describing the period as a defining expression of his commitment to public probity and responsible governance.

According to him, the late elder statesman’s leadership of Afenifere reflected his conviction that politics must be anchored on principle and directed towards the welfare of the people, with particular emphasis on social justice, good governance, federalism, and the advancement of the Yoruba nation within a united Nigeria.

Mimiko said, “Never for once were personal ambition or greed markers of his leadership philosophy or direction; it was all about fidelity to principle and an abiding concern for the future of the nation.

“For us in Ondo State, his passing is a profound loss. We have lost a father figure whose long life connected our political present to some of the most consequential chapters of our collective history.”

In a separate condolence message, Mimiko also mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, describing him as a gentleman, a compassionate medical doctor, and a detribalised statesman whose contributions to governance left enduring footprints in Delta State and Nigeria.

Mimiko said Uduaghan served with “uncommon grace, humility and calmness even in crisis”, describing him as a bridge-builder who maintained relationships across political divides.

Obafemi Hamzat

Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, expressed sorrow over the passing of Pa Fasoranti, describing the revered National Leader of Afenifere as a respected voice in the nation.

In a condolence message, Hamzat, on behalf of his family, extended heartfelt sympathies to the Fasoranti family, the government and people of Ondo State, and the entire Yoruba nation over the loss of the elder statesman.

He described Pa Fasoranti as a distinguished educator, principled leader, and respected voice in Nigeria’s socio-political landscape, whose life was devoted to the pursuit of justice, fairness, and the preservation of Yoruba values within a united Nigeria.

According to him, Pa Fasoranti’s leadership of Afenifere reflected his unwavering commitment to the dignity, rights and aspirations of the Yoruba people.

His courage, wisdom and steadfast adherence to principle earned him the respect of generations, making him a father figure, counsellor and custodian of enduring values in Yoruba leadership, Hamzat said.

He added, “Pa Fasoranti lived a remarkable century of service to his people and humanity. His life was defined by integrity, conviction and an enduring commitment to justice. He was a voice of wisdom whose counsel and principles will continue to inspire generations to come.”

He stated that the late elder statesman’s passing represented a profound loss not only to his immediate family and Ondo State but also to the Yoruba nation and Nigeria as a whole, stating that his legacy of selfless service and principled leadership would remain a source of inspiration.

Dayo Adeyeye

Adeyeye described Fasoranti as a towering figure in the Yoruba socio-political movement and a custodian of the political tradition established by Awolowo.

In a statement announcing the death, SWAGA’23, the political movement that campaigned for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2023 general election, said it received the news with deep sadness and submission to the will of God.

The group described Fasoranti as “the last of the great titans of the Awo tradition”, stating that his life and political involvement provided a link between Nigeria’s First Republic and the present democratic dispensation.

SWAGA’23 recalled the late elder statesman’s support for Tinubu’s presidential ambition during the build-up to the 2023 general election, saying his endorsement provided significant moral encouragement to the movement.

The group said it would remain grateful for Fasoranti’s support at a time when Tinubu’s ambition required what it described as the moral authority and guidance of the Yoruba race.

Ayodele Olawande

Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, mourned the elder statesman’s passing, describing him as a towering figure whose legacy would inspire generations.

Olawande said Fasoranti’s death was not merely a personal loss to his family and associates but also a defining moment for Ondo State and the Yoruba nation, given his contributions to education, public service and socio-political development.

The minister said the late elder statesman devoted his life to causes that transcended personal interests, demonstrating that the true value of leadership lay in its positive impact on society rather than the number of years spent in office.

He stated that Fasoranti’s commitment to justice, accountability, and good governance offered important lessons for contemporary leaders, particularly at a time when the country needed public officials prepared to place the collective interest above personal considerations.

Olawande urged young Nigerians to draw inspiration from the deceased’s dedication to service and community development, stressing that the values he represented would remain relevant to efforts to build a fairer society.

Ooye Development Initiative

Ooye Development Initiative (ODI) described the passage of Pa Fasoranti, as “irreparable” and a sad day for the Akure kingdom.

ODI, a sociocultural umbrella body of Akure sons and daughters, is a group that actively engages in community advocacy, cultural preservation, and governance accountability in the state.

The group made the statement after a visit to the family house of Pa Fasoranti to commiserate with his family on the exit of the Yoruba leader.

In a release by its President, Mr. Tokunbo Jegede, the group said rare persons it called “avatars”, like Fasoranti, live with a people once in multiple generations. It maintained that Akure was fortunate to have been favoured by God to play host to such in Fasoranti for 100 years.

The statement said, “For us, it is like the sun setting at noon for the people of Akure Kingdom. Though Papa Fasoranti left this world at a desirable age, having lived to attain the advanced age of a centenary, Akure could not have had enough of his imperishable imprints on the sands of time.”

ODI recalled Pa Fasoranti’s “single-handed” role of placing Akure on the maps of the world, through his invaluable contributions to its development and advancement, since 1951 when he graduated from the University of Ibadan.

ODI said, “Chief Fasoranti made Akure Kingdom proud, brought the world’s attention to its people and promoted the values of Omoluabi which the forebears of the people established as the irreducible minimum of the people’s ethos in their relationship with humanity.”

The group also said towards Pa Fasoranti’s twilight of existence on earth, he bequeathed to the people of Akure the dividends of his national honour and respect through the bestowal of the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Akure (FUTHAT) project which President Bola Tinubu gave Akure people in recognition of Fasoranti’s invaluable contributions to mankind.

It stated, “We will miss our father and leader; Akure will forever honour him among its pantheon of leaders; Ondo State will forever miss him; Yorubaland will remember him alongside leaders like Obafemi Awolowo, Adekunle Ajasin and the likes; and Nigeria will never ever forget a first class patriot, for whom materialism was immaterial and one who worshiped humanity with his incredible existence.”

World.title: 2027: Matawalle Gifts Vehicles to Eight Zamfara Lawmakers Who Returned to APC
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent





Minister of State for Defence, Dr. Bello Matawalle, has donated vehicles to eight members of Zamfara State House of Assembly, who recently returned to All Progressives Congress (APC).

The vehicles, according to Matawalle, were meant to facilitate the lawmakers’ return to Zamfara State and enable them to resume full political engagements in their constituencies.

The gesture came ahead of the 2027 general election and was seen as part of efforts to strengthen the party’s structure at the grassroots in the state.

It was gathered that the intervention followed President Bola Tinubu’s directive, urging the lawmakers to return to the state and work towards strengthening unity and cohesion within the Zamfara APC.

Matawalle, a former governor of Zamfara State, was said to have ordered the immediate release of the vehicles to ease the transportation challenges of the lawmakers and support their political activities.

Presenting the vehicles on behalf of the minister, Managing Director of the Nigerian Agricultural Insurance Corporation (NAIC), Mr. Yazid Shehu Danfulani, described the gesture as consistent with Matawalle’s commitment to unity and understanding among stakeholders.

Danfulani said the minister has remained committed to ensuring political stability and cohesion within the APC family in Zamfara State.

He stated that the donation of the vehicles was aimed at empowering the lawmakers to reconnect with their constituents and mobilise support for the party.

Party stakeholders in Zamfara viewed the gesture as part of ongoing efforts to consolidate the reconciliation process between the lawmakers and the minister.

They said the move would further deepen trust and reinforce the renewed unity within the state chapter of APC after months of internal disagreements.

Speaking on behalf of his colleagues, Hon. Aliyu Kagara thanked Matawalle for the gesture and assured of their loyalty to the party.

Kagara promised that the lawmakers would work assiduously for the success of Tinubu and APC in the forthcoming elections.

World.title: BUSINESS INSIGHTS: Are Cape Town CIDs Worth the Extra Bill?
World.content:
Forget squabbles over bin etiquette and neighbours hammering away at 7am. There’s a new controversy causing no shortage of drama in some Cape Town neighbourhood Facebook groups, WhatsApp chats and probably a few complex braais: the unassuming-sounding City Improvement District (CID).

For the uninitiated, a City Improvement District (CID) is a defined area where ratepayers collectively fund extra services to tackle neighbourhood problems that existing structures like private security and volunteer-led neighbourhood watch groups don’t have the capacity to address.

That can mean 24/7 security patrols and camera monitoring, dedicated cleaning teams, maintenance of public spaces and social outreach to homeless residents.



The idea is not to replace municipal services, but to add a locally managed layer of support where residents feel existing services are falling short.

Importantly, CIDs are community-initiated rather than imposed by the City or Ward Councillor. In residential areas, at least 60% of property owners must support the business plan before an application can proceed, with one vote attached to each registered property.

The argument for: somebody is actually doing something

Cape Town already has 55 established CIDs across the metro, ranging from the CBD and Sea Point to Camps Bay, Pinelands and Somerset West.



And they largely seem to be working. In just three months between February and April this year, the Cape Town Central City Improvement District reported 1,205 crime-prevention initiatives, 461 arrests carried out with law-enforcement agencies and hundreds of road and urban-management interventions.

It also contributed to the removal of over 298 tonnes of litter and illegally dumped waste from the CBD streets.

It is not difficult to understand why CIDs attract passionate supporters. For homeowners worried about crime, dirty streets and neglected public spaces, the appeal is immediate: more visible security, more cleaning and more consistent attention to the spaces outside their front door.



These are the kinds of issues residents experience every day, and where even relatively small improvements can change how safe and liveable a neighbourhood feels.

And from a property valuation perspective, there is an obvious argument that cleaner, safer and better-managed neighbourhoods make an area more desirable to live in and invest in.

Then comes the bill

The controversy starts with how the CID bill is split.



Cape Town CIDs are funded through additional rates paid by property owners within the district. The amount is linked to municipal property valuations, meaning someone with a more valuable home generally contributes more towards the same neighbourhood intervention.

Once Council approves the CID, payment becomes compulsory for liable owners.

There are exemptions for qualifying pensioners, indigent owners and certain other categories, but that does not solve the problem for every homeowner who may be asset-rich and cash-poor.



How much homeowners end up paying also depends on what kind of neighbourhood they live in. Mixed-use districts have commercial property owners contributing alongside residents.

A tourism-heavy precinct like De Waterkant which is packed with hotels, restaurants, offices and shops therefore has a very different funding base from a predominantly residential neighbourhood like Vredehoek with only a handful of businesses.

So pointing to a successful CBD or tourism precinct and saying “look how well the CID works there” is not always a like-for-like comparison.



But what am I already paying rates for?

This is probably the strongest objection. Cape Town homeowners already pay some of the highest municipal rates in the country, so being asked to contribute even more towards security, cleaning and maintenance can understandably feel like paying twice for services residents believe local government should already be providing.

However, the City’s position is clear: CIDs are supposed to fund supplementary services and cannot be used as an excuse to reduce ordinary municipal service levels.

On paper, that distinction makes sense. In practice, residents who support CIDs often do so precisely because they feel ordinary service delivery is not enough.



There is also a fairness question. A homeowner who bought in the City Bowl 25 years ago may now sit on a highly valued property without having anything close to the disposable income of a newer buyer. Property value and monthly cash flow are not the same thing.

Joburg shows the other side

CIDs are not a Cape Town novelty. As of 2026, it’s estimated that there are almost 60 CIDs across Gauteng metros, with areas like Gandhi Square and Jewel City showing visible improvements in cleaning, security and public-space management.

But Joburg’s CIDs also expose the risk at the heart of the model. Where municipal delivery deteriorates badly enough, CIDs can shift from supplementing government to filling gaps the municipality should arguably be handling itself.



And that’s why this debate is so hard to settle.

The real question is not whether CIDs are good or bad. It is whether your CID, at your cost, delivers enough value to justify making that extra charge compulsory for everyone. Like any property-related cost, the numbers still have to stack up.

World.title: SAFA paying for Jordaan’s fraud and corruption court case
World.content:
Following last weekend’s Nationaal Executive Commitee (NEC) meeting, SAFA confirmed their stand on the Danny Jordaan case.

The FA further committed to interdece in the criminal hearing at the Palm Ridge Magristrate’s Court. They will defend the newly re-elected president and other officials against the fraud and corruption wrongdoing.

SAFA ANNOUNCE DECISION ON DANNY JORDAAN’S CASE

Jordaan, the Chief Financial Officer Gronie Hluyo, Grit Communications Director Trevor Neethling and former CEO Russel Paul are involved. They’ve been asked to address allegations on theft, corruption and fraud.



SAFA insists that it never laid a criminal complaint against its president or the other officials involved in the case.

“The Association has never lodged a complaint with the SAPS, the Hawks or any other authority,” SAFA said in its statement.

The federation state they were not a complainant in the proceedings, as mentioned in a letter written by CEO Lydia Monyepao in December 2024.

According to the statement, the complainants are disgruntled former SAFA NEC members and employees who brought the matter in their personal capacities.

The assiciation further highlighted its audit history during the period under investigation by the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA).

“It is worth adding that SAFA received unqualified audits for the period of this investigation by the National Prosecuting Authority and the subsequent audit period to date,” the association said.



Despite the ongoing criminal proceedings, SAFA has resolved to pay all legal costs incurred by Jordaan and Hluyo, including expenses already incurred.

SAFA TO DEFEND ITS PRESIDENT

The NEC has also resolved to submit a detailed written statement to the court refuting allegations of wrongdoing against Jordaan, Hluyo and former acting CEO Russel Paul.

Furthermore, SAFA intends to take civil action against individuals it believes have damaged the association’s reputation or brought its officials into disrepute.

“SAFA shall also institute civil action against any person or persons who have brought SAFA into disrepute or damaged the name of SAFA and its officials,” the statement read.

The association will also appoint an attorney and Senior Counsel to attend future court proceedings on a watching brief.

World.title: Aden McCarthy makes Kaizer Chiefs admission after scoring against Dortmund
World.content:
Sabah FK defender Aden McCarthy described Kaizer Chiefs as a massive team and thanked South African fans for the support he continues to receive.

The 22-year-old scored during his team’s 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, continuing to make a name for himself on Europe’s biggest stage.

Speaking to a journalist after the match, the former Kaizer Chiefs defender was asked about the supporters cheering him on following another impressive performance in the competition.



“The best country in the world. You know, it’s my home, where I come from. I come from a massive team with a massive supporting group, you know. From home, that’s how I always know my people to be. I notice everything. I love my country and the people there. Ja, I appreciate all the support,” McCarthy said.

McCarthy has impressed since leaving Kaizer Chiefs in June, with his performances helping Sabah FK progress through the UEFA Champions League qualifying rounds and into the competition’s main phase.

The young defender has continued to attract attention with his displays against some of Europe’s biggest clubs. He previously impressed against Manchester United at Old Trafford before scoring against Borussia Dortmund.

His latest goal further underlined his progress since leaving Naturena, as he continues to represent South Africa on the European stage.

McCarthy spent two seasons with Kaizer Chiefs, scoring once from 24 appearances. He has one cap for Bafana Bafana, which he earned in 2025.

Will McCarthy move to a bigger team next season?

World.title: Bad news for Kaizer Chiefs! Three key players to miss Red Arrows clash
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will be without several players when they face Red Arrows in the second leg of their CAF Confederation Cup tie on Friday evening.

Amakhosi head into the encounter trailing 1-0 following their defeat in the first leg in Zambia. They must win by at least two clear goals to secure qualification for the group stages.

Langelihle Phili, who joined Chiefs from Stellenbosch FC, remains sidelined as he continues his recovery from an injury sustained in August.



The Soweto giants are also still without Khanyisa Mayo, who picked up an injury during pre-season.

Kaizer Chiefs have two attackers out

Meanwhile, Thabiso Monyane is expected to miss Friday’s encounter after coming off during last weekend’s match against Red Arrows.

There is, however, some positive news for Chiefs, with goalkeeper Brandon Petersen expected to be fit for the clash. Despite his expected availability, Renaldo Leaner is tipped to start between the posts.



Red Arrows head coach Chisi Mbewe was confident that his side would beat Kaizer Chiefs to advance to the next round.

“I can assure you that this time around, Red Arrows is qualifying for the group stage, he said as per KickOff.

“On a scale of one to ten? I would say eight out of ten.



“We’re only maybe disappointed on the part where we created a lot of chances but only managed to convert one goal.”

Kaizer Chiefs will need a strong performance at home to overturn the first-leg deficit and keep their hopes of reaching the CAF Confederation Cup group stages alive.

Failure to reach the next round will put more pressure on head coach Fernando Da Cruz.



Will Amakhosi advance?

World.title: Here are the Nelson Mandela Bay mayoral candidates for the 2026 polls
World.content:
Some of the mayoral candidates for the Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality. Images: X/DA/EFF/ACDP/COSATU and MK Party

With South Africans set to head to the polls on 4 November, political parties are putting forward their candidates to lead Nelson Mandela Bay, a metropolitan municipality that has experienced coalition instability and ongoing service-delivery challenges.

The Democratic Alliance (DA), Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) and several smaller parties have identified candidates for the mayoral race. However, the African National Congress (ANC) has decided not to publicly announce its preferred mayoral candidate ahead of the elections.

DA: Retief Odendaal



The DA has selected incumbent Nelson Mandela Bay Mayor Retief Odendaal as its mayoral candidate.

Odendaal has been campaigning on issues affecting the metro, including municipal finances, service delivery, water and electricity provision, and corruption.

🚨Crime has left too many families living in fear. Residents should not have to accept unsafe streets and failing law enforcement as the new normal.



DA Mayoral Candidate Retief Odendaal says enough is enough. It's time to take back Nelson Mandela Bay and restore law and order.… pic.twitter.com/hWarBqEJEE  July 14, 2026

EFF: Sinawo Thambo

The EFF has selected its national spokesperson, Sinawo Thambo, to contest the Nelson Mandela Bay mayoral position.

The party is among the political formations seeking to challenge the DA and ANC for control of the metro.



Today, EFF Mayoral candidate for Nelson Mandela Municipality, Commissar Sinawo Thambo continues the campaign trail in Govan Mbeki, Alex Matikinca and champion Galela, engaging residents through door-to-door visits and community meeting.#VoteEFF pic.twitter.com/4s4kyPEwcU — EFF Eastern Cape (@EFFEASTERNCAPE_) October 20, 2026

MK Party: Mvuleni Mapu

The MK Party has put forward Mvuleni Mapu as its mayoral candidate in Nelson Mandela Bay and once served as the acting city manager in the metro.



The party is also contesting council seats as it seeks to expand its presence in local government.

MKP Nelson Mandela Bay Mayoral Candidate Cde Mvuleni Mapu outlined plans to improve service delivery, upgrade water infrastructure, attract investment and create sustainable jobs through community-based cooperatives.#DumelaMoagisane #SizothathaOmaspala #MasibuyeleBantwini pic.twitter.com/9K2XdGwr52 — uMkhonto WeSizwe Party (Official) (@MkhontoweSizwex) October 20, 2026

SACP: Zanoxolo Wayile



Former Nelson Mandela Bay mayor Zanoxolo Wayile is contesting the elections as the South African Communist Party’s mayoral candidate.

Wayile served as mayor from 2009 to 2013 before being recalled by the ANC and moving to Parliament. He stepped aside from the Nelson Mandela Bay Civil Society Coalition to pursue his political ambitions, with the coalition saying the move was intended to preserve its non-partisan character.

Congratulations to Xolani Tshayana our Education Officer at VW who graduated with BCom Honours in Labor Relations; Zanoxolo Wayile retired HOD for Education & Innocent Ndiki, Health & Safety Coordinator for NUMSA who graduated with Post Grad Diploma in Labour Law from NMU✨️ pic.twitter.com/0urD8AezeN  April 23, 2025

ACDP: Lance Grootboom

The African Christian Democratic Party has named Lance Grootboom as its candidate for the mayoral position. He has served as the MMC for Health and Energy in the metro municipality.

ACDP Nelson Mandela Bay mayoral candidate, Lance Grootboom says the party's focus is on strong leadership and appointing competent, capable leaders to key positions in the metro. Tune in to #eNCA, on #DStv403. pic.twitter.com/D45cDucSpO  September 27, 2026

Patriotic Alliance: Bradley Murray

The Patriotic Alliance has put forward Bradley Murray as its mayoral candidate. He previously served as the MMC for Roads and Transport.

PA regional leader Bradley Murray and the party's mayoral candidate in the Bay has officially welcomed everyone to the event #PA2026 pic.twitter.com/qVKoegJoWf  May 17, 2025

The ANC has not publicly identified its preferred mayoral candidate for Nelson Mandela Bay ahead of the elections.

The party previously shortlisted several potential candidates, including incumbent mayor Babalwa Lobishe, former ANC Youth League leader Andile Lungisa, Xolani Vela and Ntombi Nama. However, the ANC later decided against announcing its preferred mayoral candidates before the elections, citing concerns about internal divisions and the limited time remaining for campaigning.

Lungisa’s position on the ANC’s proportional representation candidate list also became the subject of a legal dispute. The Johannesburg High Court ruled that his removal from the list was unlawful and directed the party to reinstate him on its internal list. This ruling concerned his position on the candidate list and should not be taken as confirmation that he has been publicly named as the party’s mayoral candidate.

World.title: Leanne Manas: ‘It’s absolutely frightening’
World.content:
Leanne Manas has disputed viral claims that she quit SABC 2’s Morning Live. The breakfast TV show anchor made headlines this week over a TikTok account’s unverified claims.

LEANNE MANAS SHUTS DOWN FAKE NEWS

After trending on social media over the last week, Leanne Manas addressed rampant speculation about her “departure” from Morning Live.

She said live on air from the SABC studios: “I’m still here and proudly so with the Morning Live team.



“Please disregard those conflicting reports. There is so much disinformation out there, it’s absolutely frightening…It’s crazy!”

On her Facebook account, Leanne Manas emphasised that the viral videos circulating on TikTok were untrue.

She shared: “Not going to waste too much time on the fake news doing the rounds about me, but just to clear things up…



“I have absolutely NOT resigned from the SABC! I’m very much still part of the public broadcaster and will be back on your screens tomorrow after a beautiful week off!

“And while I’m at it, every TikTok account claiming to be me is FAKE. I have never posted a single thing on that platform”.

On its official platform, the SABC also distanced itself from the viral posts.



It shared: “SABC News wishes to clarify that reports circulating on social media regarding Morning Live Anchor Leanne Manas’ alleged resignation from the organisation are false.

“We encourage the public to refrain from sharing unverified information and to rely on credible sources and verified accounts for accurate updates”.

OVER TWO DECADES ON MORNING LIVE

Leanne Manas joined Morning Live in 2004 as co-anchor alongside her late colleague, Vuyo Mbuli.



She shared on her Instagram account: “The nerves got the better of me, but as I walked onto that set, I was welcomed by the friendliest SABC crew who embraced me from the moment I arrived. Sitting next to the formidable Vuyo Mbuli, I realised I was going to be okay.

“In fact, I was better than okay; I was on top of the world. Something snapped inside of me that day, and the passion for what I do grew so strong that I knew this was what I wanted my career to be for as long as I possibly could”.

In 2024, she marked her 20th anniversary of helming the breakfast show.



“It certainly hasn’t been easy, but it has been a privilege and honour”, she added.

In June, Leanne Manas took a short break from Morning Live to recover from ankle ligament reconstruction surgery. She returned a few weeks later.

World.title: Police hunt caller behind false bomb threat at King Phalo Airport
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - Police are hunting for the person responsible for a false bomb threat involving a commercial aircraft at King Phalo Airport in the Eastern Cape on Wednesday.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) confirmed that the threat was a false alarm after a thorough investigation.

The KuGompo Explosives Unit responded after an anonymous caller allegedly contacted the airport’s passenger information desk, claiming that a bomb had been placed on an aircraft.

The call, made from an unknown number, prompted airport officials to alert police.

READ | Bomb threat at King Phalo International Airport

Following a briefing by airport security, Bomb Disposal Unit members activated a multidisciplinary response.

As a precaution, all passengers, pilots and cabin crew safely disembarked while security personnel searched the aircraft and luggage.

No explosives, explosive devices, suspicious objects or hazardous materials were found. The scene was declared safe and handed back to airport security.

A criminal case has been opened. The incident has been registered as a contravention of Section 27(1A)(a) of the Explosives Act 26 of 1956.

Police have warned that making a false bomb threat is a serious criminal offence that can carry a prison sentence of up to 10 years.

World.title: IEC turns to TikTok to help keep voters informed
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The IEC is turning to social media to encourage voter participation ahead of the Local Government Elections.

But the spread of misinformation on these platforms poses a challenge to efforts to keep voters informed.

TikTok Southern Africa is partnering with the Electoral Commission to help combat disinformation and protect the integrity of the elections.

"The in-app election centre actually plays a critical role in ensuring that we are able to expeditiously review and identify content that could potentially mislead our users on our platform and undermine the integrity of the elections," said TikTok Southern Africa's Tholoana Ncheke-Mahlaela.

"What we also do is we label content. So whether it is AI-generated content, we label that content so that our viewers or rather our users, know what it is that they're interacting with.

"And we also indicate by label whether or not a piece of video has been, or rather is, unverifiable."

Also read: IEC receives more than 700 complaints over election-related content

World.title: Malema brands Eastern Cape a province of 'zeros'
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - The Eastern Cape is the country’s worst-run province, according to EFF leader Julius Malema.

He has warned that residents will continue to suffer under ANC rule, promising better support for the elderly under an EFF-led government.

Malema was addressing thousands of supporters in KuGompo City as part of the party’s Local Government Elections campaign.

Malema began his KuGompo City visit in Bhongweni, where residents’ homes were demolished amid allegations of illegal land invasions.

The party's commander-in-chief says that if the EFF ran Buffalo City Metro, they would offer more support to the elderly.

"There are two reasons why the elderly of the Eastern Cape remain loyal to the ANC. They are loyal because of Nelson Mandela and the legacy he left behind. They also have this misconception that without the ANC they will not be given social grants," he said.

"We, as the EFF, say that they will be provided more than what they are given."

Malema wrapped up his visit in Duncan Village, where he again criticised Eastern Cape Premier Oscar Mabuyane.

"They call it a province of heroes, but to me, as long as you don't deliver to people, it is a province of zeros, a province of Oscar Mabuyane, a domkop of note and who has got no idea of what he's doing," Malema told supporters.

The Economic Freedom Fighters leader now heads to Mangaung on Thursday to canvass for votes ahead of the 4 November polls.

World.title: Soweto teacher accused of raping Gr 4 pupil hands himself over
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A teacher accused of raping a Grade 4 pupil at Busisiwe Primary School in Soweto has handed himself over to police.

He is expected to appear in the Protea Magistrate’s Court.

Gauteng education officials visited the school as angry parents protested outside, demanding the teacher’s removal.

The teacher has since been placed on precautionary suspension.

World.title: New video evidence expected in AKA and Tibz murder trial
World.content:
DURBAN - The State is expected to present new video evidence on Thursday in the murder trial of South African rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes and his friend, Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane.

The defence received the three-hour-long footage on Wednesday, ahead of its expected presentation in court on Thursday. However, it remains unclear what the footage contains.

Earlier in the trial, the State presented CCTV footage showing a man believed to be one of the accused allegedly following Forbes and his entourage at King Shaka International Airport.

READ | AKA murder trial hears surveillance analyst was threatened

Seven men stand accused of the 2023 murders of Forbes and Motsoane, who were shot dead outside a restaurant on Durban’s Florida Road.

The trial continues on Thursday, with the State expected to present the latest video evidence.

World.title: Man Utd humiliated as Arsenal deny Bayern in Champions League
World.content:
LONDON - Manchester United were hammered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday as the pressure increased on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick, while a late Declan Rice equaliser earned Arsenal a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

Elsewhere, Real Madrid thumped RB Leipzig 4-1 and there were also notable victories for Inter Milan, Aston Villa and Real Betis.

The most remarkable scoreline, though, came in driving rain on the banks of Lake Como, where United suffered their joint-heaviest loss in the Champions League in the last 30 years.

Nico Paz scored twice for Cesc Fabregas's Como, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon getting their other goals. This was a second 4-1 home win in this season's competition for the tournament debutants.

Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back at the death for United, but they are now seven games without a win in all competitions.

The Red Devils have just one win in the Premier League this season and have now suffered back-to-back losses in Europe. Carrick's position risks becoming untenable.

"I have not given my own position any thought," Carrick said.

"For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all," he admitted.

Last season's beaten finalists Arsenal have seven points from a possible nine after Rice struck in the 82nd minute to earn a draw in Munich.

World.title: X Community Notes 'failed' to flag US election falsehoods, study says
World.content:
WASHINGTON - A crowd-sourced verification system used by Elon Musk's X failed to flag a vast majority of false claims related to the US midterm elections -- including those promoted by the billionaire -- a study said.

Community Notes, which allows users to contribute notes that add context or corrections to posts, was introduced by X in late 2022 and the same model is increasingly being adopted by other tech platforms.

But researchers have repeatedly questioned its effectiveness in combating misinformation.

NewsGuard, a US watchdog that rates the credibility of news and information sites, identified dozens of posts on X that advanced false claims related to the elections, including bogus allegations of election fraud.

Only 13 of those posts were tagged with Community Notes.

"X's crowdsourced fact-checking program failed to flag 93.1 percent of false claims related to the US midterm elections," NewsGuard said.

"The uncorrected X posts have drawn millions of interactions ahead of the November 3 midterm elections."

The falsehoods included a post by a conservative commentator claiming that New York and California had made it illegal for voters to show -- and officials to ask for -- their voter ID. No such rule exists in either Democratic stronghold.

Musk has often promoted Community Notes, calling it "awesome" and asserting that all users, including himself, were subject to being corrected by the crowd-sourced model.

NewsGuard, however, said that Musk, who has 241.5 million followers on X, has advanced at least four false claims related to the midterm elections, none of which carried Community Notes.

X did not respond to AFP's request for comment.

Studies have shown Community Notes can work to dispel some falsehoods, like vaccine misinformation, but researchers have long cautioned that it works best for topics where there is broad consensus.

Some researchers have also cautioned that Community Notes users can be motivated to target political opponents by partisan beliefs.

Tech platforms increasingly view the community-driven model as an alternative to professional fact-checking.

Last year, Meta ended its third-party fact-checking program in the United States, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg saying it had led to "too much censorship." Professional fact-checkers vehemently reject the claim.

Last month, Meta said it had begun testing its own version of Community Notes in 16 Spanish-speaking countries in Latin America, in a step toward replacing its fact-checking program.

Meta gave no timeline for when the change will become official.

Meta's Oversight Board, a quasi-independent body the company funds to review its moderation decisions, said Community Notes was not an adequate replacement for fact-checking.

AFP currently works in 26 languages with Meta's global fact-checking program, including in Latin America.

World.title: Canadian publisher says novelist Orelien used AI to write novel
World.content:
MONTREAL - The publisher of top-selling Haitian-Canadian writer Thelyson Orelien said it had confirmed that he used artificial intelligence to help write his novel "It Was Either That or Die."

Orelien has denied allegations that he used AI on his breakthrough novel and, last week, Canadian publisher Boreal said it was standing by the 38-year-old writer.

But on Wednesday, Boreal said it had conducted a further investigation into the allegations.

"New information, confirmed over the past few days, indicates that artificial intelligence was used in the writing process" of the novel, a Boreal statement said.

The publisher announced it was "ending its professional relationship" with Orelien.

Boreal said it did not know the extent of AI's use in the writing process "and we will likely never have a definitive answer."

It said it gathered all the working versions of the novel and hired an outside party to analyze the various drafts.

"The results obtained this week revealed traces of AI tags in the metadata of certain documents," Boreal said.

Before conducting this analysis, the publisher said it had tried to work with Orelien to gather the evidence necessary to prove his innocence.

That effort was inconclusive, and Orelien "subsequently announced that he would not provide any further information," the publisher said.

The novel about migration, known by its original French title "C'etait ca ou mourir," had been scheduled for translation in more than 20 countries.

- 'Slander and heresy' -

The book was shrouded in suspicion and withdrawn from the shortlist for France's top book prize, the Goncourt, after tests with AI detector Pangram indicated a 100-percent probability it contained computer-generated text.

In a statement to AFP earlier this month, Orelien called the allegations "slander and heresy."

"Here and there I did use tools for research, particularly for foreign idioms," he said in a statement sent exclusively to AFP.

"But not a single sentence in this book was created by a machine, nor the meaning or the structure of a story that comes from my gut."

He stood firm on Wednesday, telling the French newspaper Liberation he used AI "in the creative process" for "historical research."

"I've explained everything to those close to me, but at the moment I don't think my words count for anything," he said, adding that what he is currently experiencing has "gone way too far."

Orelien said he started writing the book in late 2017 "on the corner of a table" and completed a first draft in 2019 of more than 300 pages, several years before the advent of AI services such as ChatGPT.

The author fled his native Haiti following a 2010 earthquake that struck the Caribbean island, already ravaged by poverty and unrest.

In response to separate allegations of plagiarism, Orelien admitted to making "unacceptable mistakes" in the past in his writing, without mentioning specifics.

"I was just over 20, I was probably a little too impatient, without really understanding how much I still had to learn. I wanted to write, I was reading a lot," he wrote.

"But admiring someone does not give you the right to take, to claim as mine texts that are not my own."

World.title: Super coalition: Gachagua and Sifuna court Uhuru, Kalonzo in plot to deny Ruto 'tutam'
World.content:
DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua hosts Edwin Sifuna and Linda Mwananchi leaders at his Wamunyoro residence on October 20, 2026. [Linda Mwananchi, X]

A powerful political wave is expected to sweep across the country from this weekend, when Rigathi Gachagua’s Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) and Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi outfit hold their first joint rally in Nyahururu.

Fresh details emerging from a meeting held at Wamunyoro on Tuesday indicate that a series of joint meetings between the two camps will continue in the coming weeks.

World.title: Drama in church after Mudavadi, Wetang'ula walk out as Sifuna speaks
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula join mourners at the late Burudi Nabwera's memorial in Nairobi. [Edwin Sifuna, X]

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula walked out of the requiem mass of former lawmaker Burudi Nabwera after Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna was invited to address mourners.

In a clip that has since gone viral, the two senior government officials are seen walking towards the entrance of Friends Church in Lang'ata on Wednesday, the venue for the memorial service, while Sifuna took the stage.

Sifuna appeared to acknowledge the departure with a "this is Nairobi" quip that drew laughter from mourners.

The incident appears to lay bare the deepening political divisions ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The two leaders’ departure came as Sifuna used the funeral gathering to condemn tribal politics, lament the breakdown of political friendships and pledge to restore the spirit of national unity that defined Kenya at independence.

“At the beginning of this country, when we got independence, we were all Kenyans; there was nothing like tribalism and everyone of us should be available to all of us to sell our policies,” he said.

The senator appeared to take a swipe at those seeking to restrict political associations along regional lines, saying leaders were being judged based on whom they were seen with.

“Some people saw me somewhere with someone and somehow they are telling us that there is a region in this country where none of us is supposed to associate with,” Sifuna said.

The sentiments appeared to castigate government leaders who he said "are not happy" with his association with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

This happened just hours after he met the Democracy for the Citizens (DCP) party leader at his Wamunyoro home in Nyeri on Tuesday, in the company of other Linda Mwananchi movement leaders.

He pledged that, in honour of Nabwera, he would work towards reviving the spirit of unity that characterised the country at independence in 1963.

“I want to make assurance here, in honour of Burudi Nabwera, we will restore that feeling that was there at the beginning of our country in 1963, that all of us, irrespective of our tribe, are Kenyans and we all belong to this society,” he said.

Sifuna, also used the opportunity to woo the Nabwera's nephew, Nabii Nabwera, who is Lugari MP, with whom they have "shared a long political history."

Sifuna also expressed regret that political divisions had separated him from Nabii, whom he described as a friend with whom they journeyed together in ODM.

“Our politics is so petty that being seen with some of us, you are branded and told you are hanging out with Sifuna; you are now a bad person,” he said.

“I miss Nabii Nabwera. You know the things we have done together. You know the journey we have walked together in ODM. I want you by my side on this journey towards the presidency,” he said.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
