World.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
World.content:
Alice Weidel (center) said the European Union is not a group of sovereign states any more Image: Ann-Krisitn Wenzel/dpa/picture alliance

Alice Weidel, the co-leader of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, has presented her party's proposals for a European Union that she said was "in severe need of reform" during a visit to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, saying they rested on three core pillars.

"We would like to rebuild and reform the European Union," she said. "We would like to found the European Union on three major principles: the first one is subsidiarity, the second one is responsibility, and the third one is sovereignty."

On subsidiarity — the idea that power should reside as close to the grassroots level as possible as much as possible — she said it was important to put the "competences" on the "lowest level of decision-making," saying "we don't want the state, or the [European] Commission — that is not elected — to intrude and disturb your private life in decision-making."

"I'm an economist, and for me, the European Union is not a group of sovereign states any more," Weidel said. She said that in sovereign states' parliaments, leaders were elected, "and so the decision-making on the sovereign level should be made in the national parliaments and not here, to be very clear."

This is already the case in the vast majority of core EU public policy areas. National governments decide foreign and defense issues, finance and health policy, education policy and much more. The notable exceptions Weidel objects to are fiscal policy and the primacy of EU law, but only after sovereign member states agree to them.

She said the European Commission was not elected but had a "legislative right of initiative," saying this was a "huge disturbance of checks and balances" and of a "democratic decision-making process."

Weidel accused the EU of failing to follow its own rules, for instance on sovereign debt and whether the European Central Bank should or can guarantee it, citing issues like this as questions of responsibility.

Finally, she reiterated her desire for "sovereign states to protect their borders," saying that "if the European Union is not capable of protecting our borders, the outer borders ... then it is a decision of the sovereign states to protect our national borders."

"If Schengen is over, if Schengen doesn't work, then we need to get out of Schengen and protect our borders," she said of the open-border zone within much of the EU.

She said that if the EU fails to protect the bloc's external borders, "we should have a veto right to opt out of this chaos."

While the EU maintains a border management agency, Frontex, national authorities are responsible for the external borders of the Schengen zone and the EU.

World.title: Milei agita la campaña con insultos a Sánchez y abrazos a Ayuso
World.content:
Cuando se confirmó que Javier Milei volvía a España pero esta vez en plena precampaña electoral, el equipo de campaña del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, no daba crédito. Parecía un regalo perfecto. Y lo fue. Hasta el alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, del PP, admitió que el viaje era un caramelo para el presidente. “Pedro Sánchez será el primero que esté muy feliz por la propaganda que le ha dado Milei hoy, estoy seguro”, llegó a decir el regidor.

Conscientes de esa realidad, el PP buscó un perfil bajo ante la visita y Vox actuó de manera atípica. Pero como siempre se saltó esa estrategia Isabel Díaz Ayuso, que intentó disimular, recibiendo a Milei sin convocar a los medios y sin intervenciones públicas, al contrario que otras veces, pero al final le dio al argentino la imagen que buscaba: un abrazo entusiasta y una foto de apoyo muy poco después de que el mandatario insultara a Sánchez llamándolo “dictador” y “ladrón”.

Más extraño fue aún el comportamiento de Vox, el gran aliado español de Milei. Santiago Abascal no recibió al argentino, algo inédito en todos los viajes anteriores, donde siempre lo habían utilizado un referente y estrella de sus actos. Abascal alegó que estaba de campaña fuera de Madrid, pero la visita se conocía hace tiempo.

Javier Milei, presidente de Argentina, en el Foro Nueva Economía en Madrid este miércoles. Samuel Sánchez

Pero después, el líder de Vox llamó al argentino por videoconferencia mientras estaba en la sede de la Fundación Disenso reunido con sus colaboradores, y ahí se vio la enorme sintonía entre ambos. Los dos parecían competir para ver quién insulta mejor a Sánchez. “No hay nada más divertido que patear culos zurdos”, le dice el argentino. “Me han presentado por tus insultos a Sánchez. ¿Pero qué insultos? Si le ha llamado dictador, igual que yo”, contesta el español. ”También le he llamado ladrón”, compite el argentino.

Efectivamente, aunque la expectativa de la campaña progresista era alta, Milei la superó con creces. Primero insultó a Sánchez, al que además de llamar dictador pidió “echar a patadas“ delante del presidente del Senado y de varios empresarios españoles, después insultó a la prensa, como suele hacer en Argentina, pero esta vez directamente con una periodista española de la Cadena SER, a la que llamó “corta intelectual y miserable política” simplemente por preguntarle si había incomodidad en el PP y Vox por su visita. Y más tarde trató de reivindicar su política económica en contraste con la española.

La presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, abraza al presidente de la República Argentina, Javier Milei, este miércoles en Madrid. COMUNIDAD DE MADRID PRENSA (EFE)

Sánchez aprovechó ese guante para atacar a Milei por sus datos económicos y los contrastó con los españoles. Según explicó, con Milei se ha alcanzado un récord de economía sumergida en Argentina, con 11 millones de trabajadores en negro, y por tanto sin derechos y sin cotizar, mientras España ha llegado a 22,6 millones afiliados con Sánchez en el Gobierno. Además, dijo, Milei ha reducido el salario mínimo un 40% mientras España lo ha aumentado un 66%.

Sánchez usó los recortes de Milei como ejemplo de lo que harán Feijóo y Abascal si llegan a La Moncloa. Aunque ninguno de los dos se reunió con el argentino, él sí pidió el voto para los dos, citándolos expresamente. En un momento en que la campaña tanto del PSOE como del Frente Amplio está explotando al máximo los mensajes confusos del PP y Vox sobre una posible reforma de las pensiones, Milei ayuda también a esta estrategia porque su ajuste, del que presume, ha recaído especialmente sobre los pensionistas argentinos y sobre los empleados públicos de este país.

El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo (i) y el presidente de la Junta de Andalucía, Juanma Moreno Bonilla (d), este miércoles en Sevilla. PACO PUENTES

Por eso Feijóo huyó de cualquier encuentro e incluso de una mínima mención, mientras el argentino, que claramente tenía ganas de entrar en la campaña española, lo citó para mostrar sus simpatías no solo hacia Vox sino también hacia el PP.

Sánchez está volcado en la estrategia de movilizar a los progresistas con el miedo a un Gobierno PP-Vox, y Milei es una mina para consolidar esa idea. En el PP creen que eso ya no tiene ni de lejos el efecto que tuvo en 2023, pero por si acaso intentan no mezclarse mucho con el argentino.

El PSOE llevaba varios días preparando un momento políticamente muy importante para su campaña. Ya dos días antes de la llegada a Madrid del argentino, Óscar Puente calentaba motores del plato fuerte de la semana para la campaña socialista. Puente dio las gracias a Milei por la visita, porque así los españoles pueden comprobar los resultados de su motosierra, y este miércoles dio un dato: desde que Sánchez gobierna, los argentinos en España han pasado de 250.000 a 500.000, dijo, “incluidos los 100.000 que han llegado desde que gobierna Milei”.

El PSOE exhibe una lona en su sede de Ferraz durante la visita a España del presidente argentino, Javier Milei, este miércoles. Álvaro García

El PSOE tenía tan claro que el argentino era un regalo que incluso puso una enorme lona en su sede con un “Milei, los zurdos y las zurdas te dan la bienvenida a España, el país que más crece de Europa”. Y Sánchez grabó un vídeo con un mensaje claro contra Milei: “Sí, soy zurdo, y a mucha honra”. Zurdo es la manera argentina de llamar a las personas de izquierdas, y Milei lo usa de forma despectiva.

El resultado final de la visita, desde el punto de vista de la campaña, es de nuevo una polarización cada vez más fuerte entre el PSOE y Vox, que no renegó de Milei con ese extraño vídeo, mientras el PP queda desperfilado y de nuevo incómodo ya no solo con Milei sino también con Ayuso, que siempre va por libre y rompe la estrategia de la dirección nacional.

Para Sánchez, el único problema de esta visita de Milei es que esté tan lejos de las elecciones, porque su efecto se diluirá, y que no tenga previsto hacer otra en la última semana de la campaña. Si la cúpula del PSOE pudiera controlar la agenda de Milei, lo traería a España cada semana hasta las elecciones.

World.title: Un negocio con muy buen olfato
World.content:
Más de la mitad de los hogares españoles cuenta con una mascota, un indicativo de la pujanza de un sector que mueve a 15.121 empresas, da trabajo a 91.700 personas y que trata de atender el creciente interés de los dueños por la calidad de vida de sus perros y gatos

Los nuevos hábitos de vida de los animales de compañía ya no caben en una tienda de mascotas tradicional... Se extienden por las clínicas veterinarias, los laboratorios farmacéuticos, las carnicerías, incluso por las guarderías y los salones de belleza. Cada vez más propietarios, o tutores, como prefieren llamarlos en el sector, tratan a sus perros y gatos como miembros de la familia y ya no buscan únicamente cubrir las necesidades básicas, sino mejorar su bienestar. Y esto se traduce en un auge del sector, explica Kike Domingo, fundador de Wild Balance y uno de los protagonistas de este capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen. Su compañía, que comenzó en 2020 con un pequeño local cerca de la estación de Joaquín Sorolla, en Valencia, se ha especializado en hamburguesas para perros que siguen la dieta BARF (por sus siglas en inglés, biologically appropriate raw food, que significa alimento crudo biológicamente apropiado), un modelo de nutrición a partir de ingredientes frescos y crudos.

La revolución en el cuidado animal ha comenzado por la alimentación. El pienso común ha dado paso a otros que no tienen saborizantes ni colorantes artificiales, con conceptos como el NøPienso®, de la propia Wild Balance, producto en el que se observan a simple vista los ingredientes, como la carne y las verduras, y a dietas alternativas sin cereales, hipoalergénicas o que replican la de los humanos. Y recientemente se ha extendido al campo de la cosmética, para incluir productos ecológicos y con formulaciones más respetuosas con las mascotas, señala Alba Ciordia, fundadora de The Doog Life, marca ecológica que comercializa champús, dentífricos, espumas de limpieza en seco y suplementos alimenticios para perros y gatos, quien comparte protagonismo con Domingo en el pódcast de Banco Sabadell.

Cuenta Ciordia que se inició en el sector gracias a una de sus dos perritas, Claire, a la que los productos convencionales le producían reacciones cutáneas debido a la presencia de determinados ingredientes sintéticos. Encontrar alternativas no era sencillo. Por eso, Ciordia se formó en campos como la nutrición para perros y gatos y la fitoaromaterapia, un tipo de tratamientos complementarios a partir de aceites esenciales y extractos vegetales. Con ese conocimiento se embarcó en el desarrollo de soluciones junto a laboratorios especializados. Lo que comenzó como una búsqueda personal terminó por convertirse en una marca que hoy comercializa más de 30 referencias.

La conversación entre los empresarios sirve como hilo conductor para explicar un sector que hoy representa el 0,38% del producto interior bruto (PIB) español, cuenta con 15.121 empresas y da trabajo a 91.700 personas, de acuerdo a las estimaciones de la Asociación Española de la Industria y el Comercio del Sector del Animal de Compañía (AEDPAC). Su secretario general, Ignasi Solana, celebra, en conversación telefónica, el éxito de esta industria que, según él “aún se encuentra dando sus primeros pasos”.

“El subsector de la alimentación natural y de los cuidados naturales ha crecido mucho más rápido que el resto” Kike Domingo, fundador de Wild Balance, acerca del auge de las alternativas a las dietas habituales para perros y gatos

Las fortalezas Una industria que se expande y encuentra nuevos modelos de negocio

Un sector en expansión. El negocio del cuidado de los animales de compañía crece cada año, de acuerdo con el Informe sectorial 2026 de la Asociación Madrileña de Veterinarios de Animales de Compañía, que analiza su evolución a nivel nacional. La facturación de las clínicas veterinarias, los laboratorios farmacéuticos y los fabricantes de alimentación aumentó un 7,4% en 2025 respecto al año anterior. Una cifra similar a la que ofrece el informe Pet-money: la economía de las mascotas y su impacto en el hogar español, de EAE Business School, que cuantifica la expansión en el 8,3%. Además, el sector exporta cada año más, en 2025, el 30% del valor del mercado de la producción de alimentos fue a Europa, Magreb, América y Sudeste Asiático, destaca Santiago de Andrés, secretario general de la Asociación de Fabricante de Alimentos para Animales de Compañía (ANFAAC).

Basado en productos de primera necesidad. Se caracteriza por una demanda constante en artículos de alimentación y atención sanitaria, lo que genera actividades con ingresos recurrentes, como las suscripciones de alimentación para recibir la comida de la mascota en casa, los planes veterinarios y los seguros.

Diversificado y con enorme potencial para la innovación y la especialización. El sector se expande continuamente hacia nuevos modelos de negocio como la cosmética canina y felina, el ocio y los viajes. También está abierto al desarrollo de productos nuevos en campos como la nutrición especializada, la telemedicina y los dispositivos inteligentes.

Con consumidores que buscan lo mejor para los animales a su cargo. La cesta de la compra para perros y gatos cada vez se parece más a la de los humanos. A veces, incluso, la supera en calidad en determinados artículos, especialmente en los alimentos, explica Ignasi Solana, de AEDPAC. “El ejemplo más claro es que los responsables de perros y gatos apuestan por comida de marca antes que por las genéricas, conocidas como marcas blancas, porque la asocian a mayor calidad. Es un fenómeno que se extiende a otros campos como la cosmética y que nosotros denominamos como premiumización”, indica para describir la estrategia comercial que consiste en ofrecer productos o servicios que son percibidos por su presentación o su precio como de mayor calidad.

“Hay un potencial muy grande de dispositivos inteligentes para la prevención que buscan detectar cambios en la salud del animal y que ayudan al veterinario” Alba Ciordia, fundadora de The Doog Life, sobre las posibilidades de innovación dentro de la industria

Los desafios El reto de luchar contra la pseudociencia y multiplicar los espacios para mascotas

Luchar contra la desinformación. Internet y, en especial, las redes sociales han multiplicado la información que reciben los propietarios o tutores, lo que puede generar confusión y dificulta la capacidad para distinguir los contenidos basados en evidencia científica, en publicidad, en opinión o en pseudociencia. Santiago de Andrés, de ANFAAC, señala que aún hay margen de mejora en la comunicación entre veterinarios y tutores, con datos precisos y basados en ciencia.

Atender a la sostenibilidad. La fabricación de alimentos implica un gran consumo de recursos a través de la producción ganadera. Además, genera gran cantidad de emisiones contaminantes. Los piensos, aperitivos y productos de higiene requieren de envases plásticos muchas veces difíciles de reciclar. La industria ya trabaja en proteínas alternativas y en el aprovechamiento de productos de la industria alimentaria para desarrollar formulaciones de menor impacto. Igualmente, investiga nuevos métodos de almacenamiento y distribución de los productos que permitan reciclar y reutilizar envases.

Potenciar la digitalización. La modernización del sector requiere un avance en dos de sus patas, señala Solana, de Aedpac. Por un lado, las tiendas de artículos para mascotas, como las pajarerías, habitualmente negocios familiares, están hoy en manos de la segunda o la tercera generación de comerciantes que afrontan paulatinamente la digitalización de sus sistemas y el desarrollo de sus comercios electrónicos. Por otro, la irrupción de la telemedicina y los dispositivos inteligentes abren nuevas oportunidades en el sector sanitario, pero requieren de grandes inversiones.

Contribuir a la creación de espacios adaptados a las mascotas. En España, señala Solana, aún hay mucho recorrido para convertir los lugares públicos en sitios propicios para el acceso con animales de compañía. La Ley de Bienestar Animal establece que hoteles, bares y restaurantes, entre otros establecimientos, pueden permitir su entrada y, en caso de no admitirlos, han de indicarlo en el exterior de manera visible. Solana es uno de los promotores del certificado ITVET, un protocolo de inspección técnica organizado por una empresa privada que acredita las buenas prácticas para facilitar la presencia y el tránsito de animales de compañía en instalaciones que se definen como pet-friendly (aptas para mascotas).

“Europa es mucho más ‘pet friendly’ en general que España” Kike Domingo, fundador de Wild Balance, sobre la presencia de animales de compañía en comercios y en el transporte público

World.title: Mi vecina es morosa y ocupa la vivienda de su madre fallecida. ¿A quién reclamamos la deuda?
World.content:
Pregunta. Tenemos una vecina morosa que acumula una deuda de más de 6.000 euros. Los propietarios murieron y la casa está habitada por la hija y la familia de esta. No se adjudicaron la herencia. La hija y los dos hijos mayores de edad trabajan, mientras que el el marido cobra una pensión no contributiva. ¿Cómo podríamos cobrar la deuda? ¿Se podría hacer alguna anotación de la deuda en la finca? F.J. Callejón

Respuesta. Cuando los propietarios de la vivienda han fallecido y los herederos no han aceptado ni rechazado la herencia, los bienes forman una herencia yacente. Las reclamaciones judiciales por impago de cuotas comunitarias deben dirigirse contra la herencia yacente y los herederos desconocidos o potenciales.

Respecto a la ocupación de la vivienda por parte de la hija con su familia, con carácter general, el Tribunal Supremo y las Audiencias Provinciales determinan que no se puede condenar al pago de cuotas comunitarias a un heredero si no se acredita que ha aceptado la herencia, bien de forma expresa o tácitamente. El uso de la vivienda puede ser indicio de aceptación tácita de la herencia, pero esto debe ser valorado y declarado en el procedimiento judicial correspondiente. Por ejemplo, la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid considera que el uso y disfrute de los bienes de la herencia podría constituir un acto de aceptación tácita de la misma (artículo 999 del Código Civil). Si formalmente no se considera aceptada la herencia, la deuda recae sobre la herencia yacente (el patrimonio del fallecido que aún no tiene titular adjudicado). Si se considera aceptada la herencia, entonces el heredero responde de las deudas de la comunidad de forma solidaria con su propio patrimonio.

Respecto a la anotación de la deuda sobre la finca, no se trata de una cuestión sencilla. Para que el Registro de la Propiedad y el juzgado permita una anotación preventiva de embargo sobre los bienes, es necesario acreditar el título sucesorio e identificar quiénes son los herederos concretos titulares de esos derechos.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Health insurance could cost you €177 more next year
World.content:
Healthcare premiums are set for their biggest rise in 15 years after insurer DSW announced its premium will go up by €14.75 a month in 2027.

The basic insurance package, which is compulsory for everyone, will cost €173.50 per month, or €2,082 a year.

DSW is traditionally the first Dutch health insurer to publish its rates for the following year, but all companies tend to follow a similar line because the content of the basic package is prescribed by law.

The rise of 9.3% is the largest in percentage terms since 2011, when premiums went up by 10%.

“In the eight years I have worked here I have never seen such a big increase,” Aad de Groot, chair of DSW’s board of directors, told broadcaster NOS.

It is also more than the €12.50 estimated by the health ministry in its budget calculations for next year. The maximum health benefit (zorgtoeslag) is going up by €11 a month for people earning the minimum wage, meaning low earners will have to pay more out of their own pockets for health cover.

The excess, or deductible, on health insurance is also going up for the first time in a decade. From January patients will have to pay the first €400 for treatment covered by the basic plan, up from the current level of €385.

De Groot said the government had not taken into account cuts to mental health care, hospital care and care at home in its calculations. “The effect is that the state is paying less but individuals are paying more through their premiums,” he said.

People whose earnings are just above the threshold for government support will be hit hardest, he added. Some 200,000 people have fallen behind on their insurance payments, according to the CAK, the government agency that handles healthcare bills, up from 172,000 in 2022.

“We see a growing group of people who are struggling to pay their premiums,” De Groot said. “It is a painful increase, but we have no option but to do this.”

Insurers must publish their rates by November 12, after which Dutch residents have until the end of the year to decide whether to switch to a different insurer for 2027.

World.title: European Commission investigates Booking over scams
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The European Commission has launched an investigation into whether Amsterdam-based travel site Booking.com has breached data protection laws by not cracking down on fake adverts.

The Brussels-based commission will also consider whether the company told site users which adverts had been ranked higher in search results because their owners had paid more, as is required under transparency rules.

In a third branch of the investigation, Booking.com is accused of exposing users to phishing scams by hackers who gained access to the company’s reservation and guest data.

Booking.com could be hit with fines amounting to 6% of its turnover if the commission decides it has breached the rules and refuses to change its policies.

The number of scams reported on the website increased by 500% between 2022 and 2024, with fraud totalling €4.2 billion in 2024 alone.

Henna Virkkunen, European commissioner for tech sovereignty, said: “Europeans should be able to book their holidays without fear of being scammed.”

In a statement, Booking.com said it was “cooperating fully” with the investigation, adding: “security, trust and the protection of personal information are top priorities.”

“We remain committed to working with relevant governments, regulators, law enforcement and industry partners to combat cybercrime and online fraud and protect travellers and partners,” the company said.

World.title: Feyenoord second best to Betis as Isco is on the spot for CL win
World.content:
Feyenoord endured a frustrating evening in Spain as a penalty by Real Betis’s outstanding player, Isco, secured a 1-0 win for the La Liga side.

The Rotterdammers were second best for most of the game, but held out until the 59th minute, when Abde Ezzalzouli’s cross hit the arm of Jeremiah St. Juste in front of goal.

Isco, who was at the heart of Betis’s attacks all evening, grabbed the ball and gave Tjark Ernst no chance from the penalty spot.

Ernst had made good saves from former AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and Marc Batra to keep Feyenoord in the game in the first half, but Feyenoord had the best chance of the opening period when Gjivai Zechiël shot over the bar from close range.

The visitors had a claim for a penalty of their own turned down in the 68th minute when Givairo Read claimed he had been pushed by Ezzalzouli, but referee Simone Sozza waved the appeals away.

The result leaves Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side in 26th place in the Champions League table, with Internazionale up next in De Kuip on November 3.

World.title: Some important websites remain down after emergency shutdowns
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Websites in the Netherlands are coming back online following emergency shutdowns. This follows the discovery of vulnerabilities in the programming language on which many government, hospital and news sites are built, including Dutch News.

The organisation behind PHP, one of the world’s most widely used programming languages, said on Tuesday it would patch two flaws in its code.

The announcement prompted hackers to search for the holes and begin trying to attack sites, which US cyber security firm Cloudflare said on Wednesday it was noticing and defending against.

Sites were then swiftly taken down, including the government’s digital ID system DigiD and its online services portal MijnOverheid, the website of parliament, the umbrella organisation for the water boards, and a tool used by local councils for storing documents and scheduling meetings.

Some important sites, like anonymous crime reporting site Meld Misdaad Anoniem and domestic safety reporting network Veilig Thuis, were still offline on Thursday morning.

Disruptions

Dutch media companies were hit – RTL’s news website and app went down, and broadcaster NPO shut down the system used to upload content to its streaming services.

Several hospitals also took their websites down, as well as charities such as KWF cancer fund and the Dutch Heart Foundation.

Schiphol airport’s app stopped showing live flight information, and benefits agency UWV took a tool people use to report sick or recovered offline.

The problem was not limited to the Netherlands – the Flemish, German, French and Finnish governments all took websites offline.

What happened

Two critical flaws in PHP’s programming language were discovered in August using AI models from OpenAI and Google.

Google-owned cybersecurity firm Wiz, one of the firms that reported the flaws to PHP, said that the vulnerabilities in PHP had existed for over a decade, and said they ranked “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history”.

PHP built fixes for the vulnerabilities into an update and said all companies using its code should install the update immediately. Prime minister Rob Jetten reiterated this call on social media.

Justice minister David van Weel said the fact that so many websites had been taken offline as a precaution “has an impact on our digital society”.

“Fortunately, there are currently no indications that the vulnerabilities are being actively exploited,” Van Weel stated through his spokesperson.

The National Cyber Security Centre said it had not seen any active hacks, and the PHP Foundation told news agency ANP it also had no indication of breaches.

World.title: Dutch workers more likely to stay on after state retirement age
World.content:
The number of Dutch workers who stay in work beyond the statutory retirement age has increased by more 50% in eight years, according to latest figures from the statistics agency CBS.

In the second quarter of this year 152,000 people in work were over the age of 67, representing 1.7% of the working population.

In the first quarter of 2018 1.2% of workers were beyond the retirement age, which was then 66, equivalent to 96,000 people.

Men are more likely than women to keep going to work after drawing their pension, the figures show. In June 2.3% of men over 67 were working, compared to 1.1% of women.

The figures also revealed large differences between sectors, with 4.3% of people working in real estate after their 67th birthday compared to 0.6% of civil servants.

A study by the demographic institute NIDI in 2023 found that most people who kept working in retirement did so because they enjoyed their job or to feel useful. Just 10% said the need to earn money was a significant factor.

The Netherlands has the latest retirement age in the European Union, along with Denmark, Sweden, Italy and Greece. The state pension age is due to increase to 67 years and three months in 2028.

World.title: Minister refuses inquiry into abuse at youth home in Spain
World.content:
Long-term care minister Mirjan Sterk has refused to launch an independent investigation into a Dutch youth care scheme in which children are sent abroad, despite revelations about exploitation and harsh treatment.

An investigation by news programme Nieuwsuur found that the “family home” in the Valencia region, which has been running for over 20 years, subjected children living there to cruel physical and psychological punishments.

Sending troubled teenagers abroad is a long-standing practice in Dutch youth care, meant to remove them from difficult environments in the Netherlands. Huize Soria alone received tens of millions of euros in taxpayers’ money over 20 years, according to the investigation.

Reporters found that the Dutch owners of Huize Soria, the Valencia institution, were forcing children their to work long hours. When they misbehaved, they were deprived of food, sleep and access to a toilet.

Some were made to stand stress positions for long periods, others said. Contact with relatives in the Netherlands was restricted, sometimes for months at a time.

Experts described the conditions as “torture”. Huize Soria was ordered to close down in September after evidence of abuse was first uncovered.

Sterk, from the centrist Christian Democrat CDA, has urged youth care organisations to stop placing Dutch children abroad where possible said there was no need for her to order an investigation.

In a letter to parliament, she said it was up to local councils, child protection agencies and care providers who placed the children to make sure the home met the rules.

She also said she did not know which organisations had sent children to Huize Soria, apart from one child protection agency, because there is no central record.

MPs from across the political spectrum said that was exactly why an investigation was needed. Far-right JA21 MP Ingrid Coenradie said refusing one was “running away from your responsibilities”.

World.title: Nearly half of Dutch MPs use AI to write speeches in parliament
World.content:
Nearly half of Dutch MPs used artificial intelligence to help write speeches and statements delivered in parliament, according to an investigation based on the AI detection tool Pangram.

A scan of debates and committee hearings revealed that 68 of the 150 MPs from across the political spectrum used AI at least once. Most of the members admitted using artificial intelligence tools when asked by De Groene Amsterdammer and investigations website Investico.

The real number is likely to be higher because only contributions that were found to be more than 50% AI generated were included in the results.

Top of the list was former Pro MP Esmah Lahlah, who is now a member of Amsterdam city council’s executive after leaving parliament in June. The analysis found evidence of AI in her contributions to four debates on poverty and the law on jobseekers.

Lahlah said she sometimes used AI to summarise conversations she had with people during working visits. “Sometimes it was hard to condense those stories into a few minutes’ speaking time, so I used AI,” she said.

Most MPs wrote their own material for big set-piece debates such as the recent debate on the king’s speech, known as the Algemene Politieke Beschouwingen, which kicks off the parliamentary year. But more than half of contributions to committee hearings showed evidence of AI use, the analysis found.

“Rolled out by Chat”

Other frequent users included Rachel van Meetelen of the far-right PVV, who said she used it to make her statements more concise and effective. “I would never say anything in Parliament I didn’t support,” she said.

The heaviest users were right-wing parties such as Gidi Markuszower’s DNA group of former PVV MPs. Only the Socialists (SP), the animal rights party PvdD and Volt showed no use of AI at all.

Harmen Krul of the centre-right CDA also said he used AI to edit his speeches, but not generate content. “I would be dismayed if this created the impression that my contributions were rolled out by Chat,” he said.

Last month an analysis of 28,000 questions in parliament by national broadcaster NOS, again using Pangram, found that around a quarter showed stylistic features of AI.

Prime minister Rob Jetten also had to admit that he used AI to write social media posts, including personal reflections on sensitive subjects such as the mistreatment of Moluccan war veterans who came to the Netherlands in the 1950s.

He defended the practice at the time, saying: “Like three-quarters of Dutch people I sometimes use AI to make things better.”

Some MPs also dismissed the concerns raised by the latest analysis. Henk Vermeer, leader of the farmers’ party BBB, said AI was useful for small parties, after Pangram detected traces in 30% of speeches by his three MPs. “We also use calculators, mobile phones and even coffee makers,” he said.

World.title: Man arrested over discovery of woman’s remains in suitcase
World.content:

A 23-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the discovery of a woman’s body in a suitcase in Amsterdam.

The victim, 29-year-old Hajar, went missing on October 4 after she was seen cycling away from the Rai area towards Buitenveldert on a bicycle with an unknown man.

Her remains were found on Saturday in a suitcase that had been dumped in the Amsteldijk. The discovery was made nearly two weeks after she disappeared and two days after police issued an appeal for information about her whereabouts.

The suspect, a Somali national of no fixed abode, was arrested on Monday evening in connection with an assault on another man in Koggeland, Noord-Holland.

According to Dutch media reports the victim of the assault was the man’s foster father, who needed hospital treatment for injuries. The suspect had lived in foster care until he was 16 years old.

He had earlier been questioned as a witness about Hajar’s disappearance after camera footage showed him with her at the Rai on October 4.

“Further inquiries led to him being identified as a suspect,” René Beukelaer, head of the prosecution service in Amsterdam told a press conference on Tuesday.

Murder of Lisa

City mayor Femke Halsema acknowledged that the death of Hajar would revive questions about women’s safety, following the murder of a 17-year-old girl, Lisa, on a cycle path in August last year. A 22-year-old asylum seeker, Chris Jude, believed to be from Nigeria, has since admitted killing her.

“It is just 14 months since the Amsterdam authorities had to inquire about the dreadful murder of a 17-year-old girl,” Halsema said.

“The fear, anger and outrage that it stirred up in our society have not been quelled, and it pains me hugely to have to sit here again, knowing that this will cause more fear for women in this city and across the Netherlands.”

Peter Holla, Amsterdam’s chief of police, said the suspect was initially treated as a witness because “there were no signs in the camera footage that he was a suspect or there was a threatening situation.”

Outstanding questions

He said police were still appealing for information from the public to answer outstanding questions, such as where Hajar was killed.

The suspect has lived in the Netherlands since the age of six and has permanent residency. He is being held in solitary detention, with contact restricted to his lawyer.

Beukelaer added there was no indication that the suspect and Hajar knew each other.

Holla said Hajar was reported missing by a family member on October 4 who said she had left home with a suitcase. The search was classed as “urgent” the following day.

Public appeal

“It was not clear at that time whether we were dealing with a crime,” Holla said.

Her photograph was circulated to the public on October 13, along with details of when she was last seen at Rai.

The family told police Hajar had spent periods of time away from home before, but always returned, Holla said.

At the start of the press conference, Halsema extended her sympathies to Hajar’s family and close friends.

“For nearly two weeks they lived between hope and fear,” she said. “A few days ago the worst possible scenario was confirmed: the 29-year-old Hajar had been violently deprived of her life.

“I ask everyone to respect the peace and anonymity of the family.”

World.title: Court acquits Polish soldier who accidentally shot Syrian refugee at Belarus border
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish soldier who accidentally shot a Syrian refugee who had entered Poland over the border from Belarus has been acquitted of negligent use of a weapon. The Syrian man had been seeking 50,000 zloty (€11,500) in compensation from the soldier. The verdict was welcomed by defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, whose ministry had supported the soldier’s legal defence. ❗Podporucznik Wojska Polskiego został dziś uniewinniony przez Wojskowy Sąd Garnizonowy w Warszawie. Nie udowodniono mu żadnych zaniedbań w czasie służby na granicy z Białorusią. W listopadzie 2023 r. przypadkowo postrzelił on migranta. Od początku zapewniliśmy mu pomoc prawną… pic.twitter.com/RS2p2WsQ7Z — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) October 21, 2026 The incident in question took place in November 2023 in Poland’s northeastern Podlasie province. The soldier, named only as Adam Ł. under Polish privacy law and who holds the rank of second lieutenant, had only recently received his first posting to the border, reports legal news service Prawo.pl. Since 2021, Belarus has been encouraging, assisting and in some cases coercing tens of thousands of migrants, mainly from Asia and Africa, to try to cross into Poland. Among those who make it over the border, most head westwards to Germany, while some have sought to claim international protection in Poland. In response, Poland has posted thousands of soldiers to the border, where they provide support to the border guard and police. Officers have at times faced violence from migrants trying to cross. In one case, in June 2023, a Polish soldier died after being stabbed. Poland has named a Moroccan man, Mohamed Addamrou, as the suspect in the 2024 murder of a Polish soldier, Mateusz Sitek, who was fatally stabbed while trying to stop a group of migrants from forcing their way through the border from Belarus to Poland https://t.co/mw8JuOPwcE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 10, 2026 A few months after that tragedy, Adam Ł. took part in an operation to apprehend a group of migrants who had crossed from Belarus and were around 2 kilometres from the border. After the soldiers called on the migrants to stop, one of them, a 23-year-old Syrian man, began to flee. As Adam Ł. chased him, the soldier slipped and fell, resulting in his gun, a PM-98 Glauberyt submachine gun, accidentally discharging two rounds. One bullet hit the Syrian man in the back, close to his spine. The soldier immediately began providing him with first aid, before the Syrian was taken to hospital. He was discharged a few weeks later and, in May 2024, was granted asylum in Poland. Initially, when it appeared possible that the Syrian could suffer partial paralysis, military prosecutors considered charging Adam Ł. with negligent use of a weapon resulting in serious injury, a crime carrying a prison sentence of up to eight years. In the end, that was downgraded to a lower charge of negligent use of a weapon causing impairment or a health disorder, which is punishable by up to three years in prison. The defence ministry provided the soldier with legal counsel from a special team set up in 2024 to defend military personnel. They advised him not to plead guilty. Eventually, prosecutors asked only that the court impose an indemnity of 2,000 zloty on Adam Ł., to be paid to the Syrian. The Syrian’s lawyer, meanwhile, sought 50,000 zloty for his client. The president has signed into law new rules removing criminal liability from officers who use firearms while serving on the border. The measures were passed in response to a surge in aggression from some migrants seeking to cross the border from Belarus https://t.co/sBMaoYhoCw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 16, 2024 In a ruling announced on Wednesday, a military court in Warsaw fully acquitted Adam Ł. Judge Michał Żak said that it remained unclear how the incident unfolded. He also pointed to expert evidence commissioned by the court that found the soldier’s gun could have had defects that caused it to fire when it hit the ground. Those doubts, and a lack of convincing evidence to support the prosecutor’s version of events, meant the charge of negligence could not be proven, found Żak. The verdict can still be appealed. The Syrian’s lawyer said they would wait for the judge’s full written justification before deciding whether to appeal. Kosiniak-Kamysz, meanwhile, welcomed the ruling in a social media post. “From the very beginning, we provided him with legal assistance,” wrote the defence minister. “A soldier who carries out his duties cannot be left alone, even in a difficult situation.” In May this year, another soldier was acquitted over an incident in which he fired shots towards a group of migrants who had illegally crossed the Belarussian border. The judge found that, in fact, the soldier had been fulfilling his obligation to defend the Polish border. A Polish soldier who fired shots towards migrants who had illegally crossed the border from Belarus has been acquitted of abusing his powers and threatening the lives of others The military judge found he had been fulfilling his duty to protect the border https://t.co/ugxq5tkdFV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 27, 2026 In 2024, Poland’s government introduced a new law making it easier for soldiers and other uniformed officers serving at the border to use firearms. They now no longer face criminal liability for employing their weapons in certain cases. Since then, the government has also further strengthened physical border barriers and banned asylum claims by migrants who cross irregularly from Belarus. That has been followed by a significant drop in attempted crossings by migrants from Belarus: in the first half of this year, only 250 attempts were recorded, down from 15,500 in the same period of 2025 – a 98% drop. Poland also now claims to have a 100% success rate in apprehending those who do manage to cross. World.title: Poland condemns Ukrainian region for honouring figures associated with WWII massacres of Poles
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has condemned a decision by the Lviv region in Ukraine to declare 2027 a year honouring the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which led the massacre of Poles during World War Two, and one of its leaders, Roman Shukhevych. The Polish foreign ministry called the decision “contrary to European values,” and warned it could undermine recent progress made between the two countries toward reconciliation over their difficult shared history. Decyzja Lwowskiej Rady Obwodowej, by 2027 rok był rokiem UPA i Szuchewycza, jest nieakceptowalna. Taka decyzja nie buduje wzajemnego zaufania między narodami, lecz wzmacnia podziały. Konieczne jest odcięcie się władz Ukrainy od tego stanowiska. — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) October 20, 2026 On Tuesday, the Lviv regional council adopted resolutions proclaiming 2027 the year of the UPA, of Shukhevych, and of Oleh Olzhych, a poet and leading figure in the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN). Sviatoslav Sheremeta, chair of the region’s committee on culture, said the decisions will pave the way for “large-scale events” to commemorate the UPA, Shukhevych and Olzhych. “This is our history, our heroes, and we must duly honour their memory,” he added, quoted by local news service Sokal Voice. The OUN was a nationalist organisation that sought Ukrainian independence. The UPA, a partisan formation, emerged in 1942 from a more radical faction of the OUN, with Shukhevych serving as its military commander. While the UPA is still remembered positively by some in Ukraine for its role in fighting against Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is associated with the Volhynia massacres, in which the UPA led the slaughter of around 100,000 Poles, mostly women and children. Poland has previously condemned official commemorations in Ukraine of Shukhevych and other figures associated with the UPA. This year, President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to name a military unit after the “heroes of the UPA” triggered a diplomatic crisis. The resolutions adopted by the Lviv region on Tuesday likewise prompted a swift response from Warsaw. “Glorifying the UPA and criminal figures is contrary to European values ​​and the strategic and good-neighbourly nature of relations between Poland and Ukraine,” foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór told news website Wirtualna Polska. “Shukhevych is a criminal stained with the blood of thousands of innocent victims, people who were murdered simply because they were Poles,” he added, also noting that the UPA’s victims included Jews, Czechs, Armenians and Ukrainians themselves. The European Parliament has criticised Ukraine's @ZelenskyyUa for naming a military unit after a group that massacred Poles during WWII, calling it an "unprovoked escalation" that is “not in line with European values” and "disregards Polish sensitivities" https://t.co/54rbPSrs9S — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 8, 2026 Wewiór warned that, while the Ukrainian and Polish governments have recently made progress towards reconciliation over historical issues, “irresponsible local activists are damaging these relations by honouring people clearly responsible for crimes and collaborating with the Nazis”. On Wednesday, Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski announced that he had signed a motion to place Sheremeta, who has led the efforts to commemorate the UPA and Shukhevych in Lviv, on Poland’s “list of undesirable persons”. Meanwhile, Poland’s deputy prime minister and defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, described Lviv’s actions as “unacceptable” and called on the Ukrainian national authorities to distance themselves from the decision. Podpisałem wniosek o wpisanie na listę osób niepożądanych w RP radnego obwodu lwowskiego S. Szeremeta, rekonstruktora Galizien Waffen-SS, autora pomysłu ustanowienia 2027 rokiem R.Szuchewycza, dowódcy UPA, który wydawał rozkazy wysiedlania i mordowania Polaków.… — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) October 21, 2026 Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN) also condemned the resolutions. It called Shukhevych “an architect of the genocide in Volhynia” as well as the “co-founder of collaborationist units operating alongside Germany”. It quoted an order issued by Shukhevych in which he wrote: “Cut them down to the last man. Burn villages inhabited exclusively by Poles; in mixed villages, eliminate only the Polish population.” However, the IPN noted that Olzhych – whom Lviv is also honouring next year – was the head of a group that condemned the crimes committed by the more radical faction of the OUN. The Lviv Regional Council has designated 2027 in the Lviv region as the Year of Roman Shukhevych, an architect of the genocide in Volhynia, the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), and Oleh Olzhych, a leader of the OUN-M. Among those being commemorated, Roman Shukhevych stands out as… pic.twitter.com/Bge2muwjHz — Institute of National Remembrance (@ipngovpl_eng) October 21, 2026 Polish leaders have previously warned that the honouring of the UPA and figures associated with it would harm Ukraine’s chances of joining the European Union. Poland, like all other member states, can veto accession. However, there have also been recent signs of progress on issues of historical memory. Last year, in a diplomatic breakthrough, Ukraine lifted a ban on exhuming the remains of Volhynia massacre victims on its territory. In July, as part of efforts to calm tensions following his decision to name a unit after the UPA, Zelensky promised that Ukraine would approve more exhumations. This month, the head of the IPN and its Ukrainian counterpart held their first meeting since 2018. World.title: Parliament approves liberalisation of Poland’s abortion laws
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government’s majority in parliament has approved two bills that would liberalise Poland’s strict abortion laws. One would reverse the 2020 constitutional court ruling introducing a near-total ban on abortion; the other would decriminalise providing help to women in obtaining unlawful abortions. However, it appears likely that both measures will be vetoed by President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition. His chief of staff reiterated on Tuesday that Nawrocki “supports the protection of life from conception to natural death”. Mamy to! Sejm przyjął dwa projekty: dekryminalizujący pomocnictwo w aborcji i przywracający aborcyjny kompromis. To niezbędne minimum i pierwszy krok. Jesteśmy to winni kobietom. pic.twitter.com/1yLyfuFCQC — Aleksandra LEO (@AleksandraLeo) October 20, 2026 When Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, took power in December 2023 from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, it pledged to soften abortion laws. However, since then, it has failed to do so, largely due to disputes between more conservative and liberal elements within the coalition. But now, a year ahead of parliamentary elections, that has changed, with the more powerful lower-house Sejm pushing through two abortion bills on Tuesday. One would once again allow abortions to be carried out in cases where a severe foetal abnormality is diagnosed. That would reverse a ruling by the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) in 2020 outlawing such abortions, which the TK found contravened various constitutional principles, including the right to life. That judgement, which went into force in January 2021, means that abortion is currently only allowed in two cases: when a pregnancy results from a crime (such as rape or incest) or when it threatens the mother’s life or health. In Europe, only Malta has a stricter abortion law. The ruling was issued when the TK was stacked with PiS-appointed judges – including three who had been illegitimately appointed – and regarded as being under the control of the then-ruling party. It prompted the largest protests Poland has witnessed since the communist era. In the Sejm vote on Tuesday, 233 MPs were in favour of the new bill, with 203 opposed. Support came from parties in Tusk’s coalition, as well as the small left-wing Together (Razem). Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) and The Left (Lewica), one of its coalition partners, have previously expressed support for an even greater liberalisation of the law, allowing abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy. However, all of their MPs voted in favour of the compromise option on the table. Meanwhile, five MPs from the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), the most conservative element of the coalition, joined with the right-wing and far-right opposition in voting against the bill. In a separate vote, the Sejm also approved a bill that would decriminalise the act of helping a woman obtain an unlawful abortion. Currently, that is an offence that carries a prison sentence of up to three years. A previous attempt to pass such a bill was defeated in 2024, after most PSL MPs joined with the opposition to block it. That prompted Tusk to declare that abortion reform would be impossible during the current parliamentary term. However, on Tuesday, 217 MPs voted in favour and 213 against, meaning the bill was approved. A total of 27 MPs failed to attend the vote, including 10 from PiS, among them party leader Jarosław Kaczyński. If they had participated, the bill would likely have been rejected. All MPs from KO, The Left and Razem voted in favour of the bill, as did almost all from the centrist Poland 2050. However, 14 PSL MPs joined with the opposition in voting against it, including PSL’s leader, deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Both the bills approved by the Sejm now pass to the upper-house Senate, which can propose amendments but not block the passage of legislation. Tusk’s coalition has an even larger majority in the Senate than the Sejm. Once final versions of the bills are approved by parliament, they pass to the president, who can sign them into law, veto them, or ask the TK to assess whether they comply with the constitution. Given that Nawrocki is aligned with the right-wing opposition, has vetoed a record number of government bills, and has declared his opposition to abortion, it appears very unlikely that he will sign either bill into law. President Nawrocki joined thousands of people on the National March of Life, Poland’s largest annual anti-abortion event, which is held under the patronage of the Catholic church https://t.co/8BQEVUoMZn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 20, 2026 Speaking to broadcaster Polsat on Tuesday evening after the Sejm votes, the president’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, said that Nawrocki would wait to see what the legislation looked like by the time it reached him. However, Bogucki noted that, “during his campaign, the president said he supported the protection of life from conception to natural death”. Bogucki also pointed to the fact that the TK, even before PiS was in power, had been “very clear” on “protection of life”. He also suggested that abortion was now suddenly back on the table because Tusk wants to “rehash ideological issues in order to cover up his incompetence in matters he should actually be dealing with”. .@BoguckiZbigniew o stanowisku prezydenta ws. aborcji ⬇️ 🗨️ Pan prezydent w tej kampanii mówił, że jest za ochroną życia od poczęcia do naturalnej śmierci@GoscWydarzen 🎙️ @mtejchmanhttps://t.co/ZJ4gKAPywM — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) October 20, 2026 A further complication is the fact that the TK is currently in crisis. The government does not recognise any of its rulings (including the 2020 abortion ruling) due to the continued presence of judges illegitimately appointed under PiS. Meanwhile, Nawrocki and the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, have refused to accept five new TK judges appointed by the Sejm this year. Opinion polling has consistently shown that a majority of Poles want to liberalise the abortion law. World.title: Polish leaders condemn Hegseth’s “scandalous” remarks downplaying role of US allies in Afghanistan
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Leading figures from Poland’s ruling coalition have hit back at US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth over his recent remarks downplaying the contribution of America’s allies during the war in Afghanistan. The speaker of parliament, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, called the comments “scandalous”, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk read out a message sent to him by a Polish army medic who was serving in Afghanistan when the last of 44 Polish soldiers who died there was declared dead. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Chciałbym, żeby te słowa dotarły do naszych sojuszników, żeby już nigdy więcej nikt nie lekceważył wysiłku naszych żołnierzy. pic.twitter.com/gGJkh4Gnft — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) October 20, 2026 The controversy stemmed from a speech the US defence secretary gave to US military cadets in Tennessee on Saturday. Hegseth referred to his time serving as a US Army officer in Afghanistan, where he recalled that the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) headquarters had flags from over 50 countries. “Except,” Hegseth said, “there were maybe five [countries] that contributed. It was actually closer to one or two that actually, by the end, were involved in kinetic operations. In fact, the patch ‘ISAF’ – we joked that it meant ‘I Saw Americans Fighting.'” The comments earned quick reproach from Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, who aimed a message at Hegseth on social media, saying: “Tell that to the families of 44 Polish soldiers who died securing the tough Ghazni province.” Tell that, Mr @SecWar, to the families of 44 Polish soldiers who died securing the tough Ghazni province. https://t.co/vm4TM0sMJO — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) October 18, 2026 On Tuesday, the remarks earned even stronger reproach from Czarzasty, who is the speaker of the Sejm, the more powerful lower house of parliament, and the leader of The Left (Lewica), one of the groups that forms Poland’s ruling coalition. At a press conference, Czarzasty said that Hegseth’s “scandalous” comments are “harmful to the families of Polish soldiers and to Polish national pride”. He also criticised President Karol Nawrocki – an opponent of the government and conservative ally of Donald Trump – for not condemning Hegseth’s remarks. It is “an insult to Polish soldiers” that Nawrocki, who serves as commander-in-chief, “is unable to stand up for their dignity and the dignity of those who died”, declared Czarzasty. To skandaliczne, że prezydent Polski boi się potępić polityków amerykańskich za brak szacunku do polskich żołnierzy, którzy zginęli w Afganistanie. pic.twitter.com/uyv54yDvrI — Włodzimierz Czarzasty 📚📖 (@wlodekczarzasty) October 20, 2026 Later on Tuesday, Tusk read out to his cabinet a text message he said he had received from a former military medic, whom he did not name. “Please stand up for soldiers, I beg you,” wrote the medic. “During my tour in Afghanistan, we confirmed the death of the last Polish casualty, a platoon sergeant whose wife was pregnant in Poland at the time.” “I received a medal from the Americans for helping them, for treating Americans. I didn’t have to do that. We treated them with our own Polish medicines,” they added. Tusk then added his own remarks, stating: “I would like these words to reach our allies. So that no one will ever again downplay the efforts of our soldiers. Wherever our allies, including our closest ally, the Americans, have needed our participation, Polish soldiers stood shoulder to shoulder with them.” Tusk also referenced Nawrocki’s silence on the matter. “Frankly, I was also counting on the president speaking out on this matter. But it seems I miscalculated.” Tusk is the first European head of government to directly criticise Hegseth’s remarks, although a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham did say on Monday that it was “wrong to diminish the role” of British personnel, 457 of whom died in Afghanistan. Of the 3,621 coalition deaths during the war in Afghanistan, around two thirds were Americans (2,461). The rest came from 31 different countries, with Poland’s 44 fatalities the seventh most of any nation. Hegseth’s remarks are not the first time that the Trump administration has caused anger in Poland by downplaying allies’ role in Afghanistan. In January, Trump himself suggested that other countries had “stayed a little back, a little off the front lines”. That prompted General Roman Polko, who commanded Poland’s GROM special forces unit in Iraq and Afghanistan, to call the US president “a coward who has never been on the front lines”. The former commander of Poland's special forces in Iraq and Afghanistan has condemned Donald Trump for questioning the contribution of America's allies "This is the cynicism of a coward who hasn’t been on the front lines himself," said General @PolkoRoman https://t.co/kElkAO5qX4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 23, 2026 The Polish government has also clashed with the US on other issues. In January, Tusk joined other European leaders in calling for Greenland’s sovereignty to be respected, following Trump’s calls for the island to be brought under US control. The following month, Tusk declared that Poland would not be a “vassal” of the US and suggested that Nawrocki wanted Poland to be too subservient to Washington. Czarzasty has twice this year clashed with the US ambassador over critical remarks he made towards Trump. However, at the same time, the Polish government has sought to maintain positive relations with Washington, given the United States’ role as Poland’s most important security partner. In June, Poland formally requested that the US establish a new permanent military base on its territory. Hegseth himself has praised Poland, calling it a “model ally” last year. The US State Department this month also announced that it was pushing for Poland to be allowed to join the G20 “as soon as possible”, pointing to its “growing leadership position in the international arena”. On Monday afternoon, following media reports of the arrest, a spokesman for the military police confirmed that they had detained a 31-year-old man of Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, who holds the rank of senior private reserve. The suspect, who had at the time been undertaking a course at the Military Medical Academy (WAM) in Łódź, is being held on suspicion of declaring readiness to act for the benefit of a foreign intelligence service against Poland. That crime is punishable by up to eight years in prison. W dniu 16 października 2026 r. żołnierze z Oddziału Żandarmerii Wojskowej w Łodzi, zgodnie z postanowieniem Prokuratora Działu do Spraw Wojskowych Prokuratury Rejonowej Łódź-Polesie w Łodzi, dokonali zatrzymania mężczyzny w wieku 31 lat, obywatelstwa polskiego i ukraińskiego, w… pic.twitter.com/MLpqzfT4iO — Żandarmeria Wojskowa (@Zandarmeria) October 19, 2026 The Polish authorities have not revealed which foreign intelligence service the suspect – who has been placed in detention for three months – is believed to be associated with. Speaking later to reporters, deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk said that the man had “clearly shown himself to be someone who is conducting reconnaissance of certain types of military installations belonging to the Polish armed forces”. He also revealed that the suspect had recently obtained Polish citizenship. While the authorities have not released further information, Rzeczpospolita, a leading newspaper, reported earlier on Monday that the suspect, whom it named as Vasiliy, had been found in possession of several different phones, documents, and a large amount of money and gold. Poland has recently seen a number of high-profile cases of individuals charged – and in some cases convicted – of spying on behalf of Russia and Belarus. Poland’s security services recently revealed that the number of espionage cases they launched last year was more than double the figure for 2024. Over those two years combined, there were more investigations than in the previous three decades. This month, a former Polish soldier was sentenced to five and a half years for spying on behalf of Russia. The tasks assigned to him included reconnaissance of Rzeszów-Jasionka airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky while he travelled through Poland. A Polish man has been sentenced to five and a half years in prison for spying on behalf of Russia. He was tasked with reconnaissance of Rzeszów-Jasionka airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate @ZelenskyyUa while he travelled through Poland https://t.co/WCmhyHG1Kp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 8, 2026 In July, a Russian married couple who had been studying in Poland were jailed for spying on behalf of Moscow and involvement in a plot to send a parcel bomb. In April, prosecutors charged a soldier from Poland’s Territorial Defence Force (WOT) with seeking to spy on behalf of Russia. The following month, three Polish citizens were charged with working on behalf of Russian intelligence to spread disinformation and conduct reconnaissance of NATO troops. In December last year, a Russian national was charged with running an espionage and sabotage network in Poland on behalf of Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB). The agents he oversaw were mainly Ukrainians and Belarusians, as have been many others convicted of conducting Russian hybrid activities in Poland. Poland has detained and expelled 15 Russians and Belarusians who tried to take part in youth world karate championships that were taking place in the Polish city of Bielsko-Biała. “Eleven Belarusian citizens and four Russians entered the country on tourist visas, which was inconsistent with the declared purpose of their stay in Poland,” said border guard spokesman Szymon Mościcki. After being detained, they received orders to leave the country within eight days, which is “the shortest possible deadline”, he added, quoted by broadcaster TVP. Piętnastu obywateli Rosji i Białorusi zostało zatrzymanych przez Straż Graniczną. Przyjechali do Polski na wizach turystycznych, choć prawdopodobnie zamierzali wziąć udział w mistrzostwach świata w karate. Otrzymali decyzje nakazujące opuszczenie kraju.https://t.co/czcjQKZ2kw — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 19, 2026 The announcement came one day after the karate world championships in the cadet, junior and U-21 categories had finished in Bielsko-Biała. In early October, Russia’s TASS news agency had reported that some of the country’s junior karatekas, as competitors are known, had planned to compete in the tournament. The World Karate Federation (WKF) allows Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete under a neutral banner. However, Poland has a strict policy of not allowing Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete in tournaments on its territory. This year, it banned them from taking part in a World Cup ski jumping event. It was also removed as host of two European junior weightlifting championships for banning Russian and Belarusian athletes. On 15 October, the day after the championships in Bielsko-Biała had started, TASS reported that none of the Russian athletes had been allowed to register by the Polish organisers. Paweł Połtorzecki, president of the Polish Karate Union (PUK), confirmed that, despite PUK warning them not to come, Russian and Belarusian athletes had sought to take part, prompting the organisers to ask the border guard to conduct an inspection. “The first sign was the appearance of a Russian at the refereeing course,” he revealed, quoted by TVP. “That’s when the first detention occurred.” Gazeta Wyborcza, a leading Polish daily, reports that the Russian karatekas had obtained tourist visas from other countries in the European Schengen area, of which Poland is part. Poland itself does not issue tourist visas to Russians. Poland has been removed as the host of two European junior weightlifting championships after refusing to allow Russian athletes to take part The European Weightlifting Federation says it "does not accept discrimination based on geopolitical circumstances" https://t.co/j7PfiTHZ1M — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2026 Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has been one of Kyiv’s closest allies, providing military and humanitarian support while also pressing for tougher international sanctions against Moscow. Meanwhile, Poland has become the primary target in Europe for sabotage operations carried out by operatives working on behalf of Russia, including arson attacks and an attempt to derail a train. Russia has also repeatedly violated Polish airspace with drones, missiles and, most recently, a helicopter. In response to Russia’s aggressive actions, Poland has successively shut down all Russian consulates on its territory. Moscow responded by likewise closing all Polish consulates that it previously hosted. In January, Russia warned its citizens against travelling to Poland due to “Russophobia”. World.title: Poland breaks up international criminal group accused of laundering €77 million
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland says it has broken up an international criminal group responsible for laundering an estimated 337 million zloty (€77 million) by using currency exchange offices to illegally process money obtained from internet scams. Nine suspects – eight Ukrainians and one Belarusian – have been detained in a series of raids, which also resulted in the seizure of gold and cash worth over 1 million zloty. Służby rozbiły międzynarodową grupę zajmującą się praniem pieniędzy z oszustw inwestycyjnych i kryptowalut. Zatrzymano 9 osób, a skala transakcji przekroczyła 337 mln zł. Zabezpieczono złoto i gotówkę wartą ponad 1 mln zł. @Straz_Graniczna @PolicjaCBZC @ABW_GOV_PL pic.twitter.com/g2NQoqaPvP — Marcin Kierwiński (@MKierwinski) October 19, 2026 The accused – four women and five men aged between 26 and 53 – were arrested in Łódź, Warsaw and Małopolska province, announced Krzysztof Kopania, spokesman for the Łódź regional prosecutor’s office, which is leading the investigation. The detainees are four female cashiers, three men running the exchange offices, and two couriers used to transport money. All have been charged with participating in an organised criminal group and money laundering. They could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. Prosecutors say that the gang, which operated in the cities of Warsaw, Lublin, Wrocław, Katowice and Gdańsk, collected money that had been obtained through internet fraud and transported it to cryptocurrency exchanges. It was then processed without complying with anti-money laundering procedures. Proceeds were then transferred to bank accounts, sent abroad by car, or concealed in fictitious purchases of gold. Most money was ultimately invested in cryptocurrencies. “The scale of the operation was enormous,” said Kopania. “It is estimated that between February 2025 and July 2026, members of the group took steps to conceal the origins of approximately 337 million zloty.” The ringleader was a 34-year-old Ukrainian national who made the key decisions and oversaw the domestic and international channelling of funds obtained from illegal sources, according to the Internal Security Agency (ABW) and border guard, which were also involved in the operation. Seven of the accused have been placed in pre-trial detention for three (or in one case two) months, while two have been bailed and ordered not to leave Poland. World.title: Lithuania says Ukrainian drone that struck car entered its airspace from Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This article has been updated to include a statement from Poland’s defence ministry issued on Monday afternoon. Lithuania says there is “no doubt” that a Ukrainian drone which exploded on its territory on Sunday, hitting a moving car, entered its airspace from Poland. However, Poland has so far said that there is no confirmation of an object crossing the border. Meanwhile, Ukraine has apologised for the incident, saying that Russian electronic warfare had diverted the drone’s path during an operation against military targets in Russia. Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and EU. This morning, NATO fighter jets stationed at Šiauliai Air Base scrambled once again after an unidentified object entered Lithuanian airspace. What appears to be a drone exploded… — Gitanas Nausėda (@GitanasNauseda) October 18, 2026 On Sunday morning, Lithuania confirmed that a drone had entered its airspace and exploded, causing damage to a moving vehicle. NATO jets were scrambled in response to the incursion but were not able to visually identify the object. President Gitanas Nausėda said that the incident was further evidence that “Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and [the] EU”. Meanwhile, Lithuanian defence minister Robertas Kaunas revealed that preliminary information indicated the drone had entered from Polish airspace. “I have already contacted the Polish defence minister and asked Poland to join the investigation so that we can look into this incident together,” said Kaunas, quoted by broadcaster LRT. However, a spokesman for Poland’s defence ministry, Janusz Sejmej, told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) on Sunday that “there is no confirmation [from our radar systems] of [an object] crossing the border from Poland to Lithuania”. Polsat, a leading Polish broadcaster, cited unnamed sources at Poland’s defence ministry saying that they believed the drone in fact took off from within Lithuanian territory, around 30 kilometres from the Polish border, and then flew deep into the country. In response, Deividas Matulionis, an advisor to the Lithuanian president, told the Baltic News Service (BNS) on Monday that “I can say very unequivocally we have credible evidence that the drone crossed the Polish border”. Later, the country’s prime minister, Mindaugas Sinkevičius, said that “there is no doubt that it entered…from the Polish side”. He also confirmed that the evidence indicates the drone “is of Ukrainian origin”. We regret the incident that occurred this morning in Lithuanian airspace, which may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones during an operation against legitimate military targets in Russia. We apologise for any disruption, risks, and concern this may have… — Heorhii Tykhyi (@SpoxUkraineMFA) October 18, 2026 Those remarks followed a statement on Sunday afternoon from Heorhii Tykhyi, the spokesman for Ukraine’s foreign ministry, who appeared to confirm that the drone was Ukrainian. “We regret the incident that occurred this morning in Lithuanian airspace, which may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones during an operation against legitimate military targets in Russia,” wrote Tykhyi. “We apologise for any disruption, risks, and concern this may have caused.” The spokesman said that Ukraine would “share all relevant information with our Lithuanian partners to establish the full circumstances of the incident”. However, he gave no further information on what type of drone was involved, where it was launched from, and what its target was. Lithuania borders Belarus, an ally of Russia, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, as well as Poland and Latvia. In March and May this year, a number of Ukrainian drones aimed at targets in Russia entered the airspaces of NATO members Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Finland, likely due to Russian electronic jamming. On Monday afternoon, Poland’s defence ministry issued a statement “strongly refuting” media reports suggesting that sources within the ministry had identified the drone as having taken off within Lithuania itself. It added that the ministry, in cooperation with its Lithuanian partners, was still “conducting a detailed analysis” of what had taken place.
