World.title: Carney says Trump's tariffs hurt Americans as U.S. Embassy alleges Canadian interference
World.content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs have driven up costs for American families and upended a decades-old trade relationship as he unveiled a multibillion-dollar plan to shield Canada's manufacturing heartland from the trade war.

Also Read | Trump again targets offshore wind, risking deal to speed approvals of new energy projects

Mr. Carney on Wednesday (October 22, 2026) also said he spoke with Mr. Trump for “quite some time” about issues including trade, as the U.S. Embassy in Canada accused Canadian politicians of seeking to influence American politics ahead of next month's midterm elections.

Mr. Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford rejected suggestions of improper interference.

Mr. Trump has openly said he wants automakers to move production from Canada to the U.S., threatening an industry deeply integrated across the border for decades.

"US tariffs have upended a trade bargain that's existed for decades,” Mr. Carney said. “They've raised costs for American families while putting Ontario workers and businesses at a disadvantage and under a cloud of uncertainty.”

Mr. Carney said an integrated North American auto industry would benefit both countries but acknowledged that it may no longer be a priority for Washington. “Their approach has changed,” he said. “So must ours.”

Mr. Carney said the conversation covered Iran, the West Asia and some trade issues. They discussed Ukraine days earlier. He did not indicate a breakthrough but said Canada remains ready to negotiate.

Trade negotiations collapsed in August after the countries appeared close to a deal. Mr. Trump subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion in Canadian goods, prompting Canadian retaliation.

Ford: No going back in Canada-U.S. relations

"It's clear that Canada's relationship with the United States has changed permanently,” Ford said. “No matter what happens in the midterms, no matter who sits in the White House, we're not going back to the way things were.”

Trump's trade war and repeated threats to make Canada the 51st U.S. state have fuelled a surge in Canadian nationalism.

Mr. Carney has made reducing Canada's dependence on the United States a priority, setting a goal of doubling exports to other markets over the next decade.

Mr. Carney and Ford announced the 8.7 billion Canadian dollar ($6.2 billion) plan to support steelmakers, automakers and critical mineral development in Ontario, Canada's manufacturing heartland.

The plan includes 5.2 billion Canadian dollars ($3.7 billion) over five years for steelmakers and 2.5 billion Canadian dollars ($1.8 billion) for automakers, including 1.5 billion Canadian dollar ($1.1 billion) from Ottawa.

The announcement comes as U.S.-owned steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs announced layoffs at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant, highlighting the toll of Trump's tariffs on Canadian manufacturing.

U.S. Embassy alleges Canadian interference in American politics

Also Wednesday, the U.S. Embassy issued a fact sheet accusing Canadian politicians of seeking to interfere in American elections.

The statement singled out Industry Minister Melanie Joly for discussing retaliatory tariffs targeting Republican states and Ford for airing a U.S.  featuring former President Ronald Reagan criticising tariffs.

Mr. Trump abruptly cancelled trade talks with Canada after the ad aired during the World Series in October 2025.

The Embassy also cited 11 Canadians charged with illegally voting in U.S. elections between 2012 and 2026, without linking the cases to Canada's government.

The administration has launched a whole-of-government effort to investigate and prosecute noncitizen voting, something election experts and administrators characterise as a comparatively small issue.

The Department of Justice says that since the start of 2026 it has arrested more than 200 people for illegally voting as noncitizens in past elections, a vanishingly small number compared to the country's tens of millions of regular voters.

"The items featured in the US embassy's fact sheet are not genuine examples of foreign interference and the implicit assumption that Canada could significantly alter the outcome of the midterms is absurd,” said Daniel Béland, a political science professor at McGill University in Montreal.

“Accusing Canada of foreign interference ahead of the midterms could pave the way to Blame Canada' rhetoric after the electoral results are in.”

Mr. Carney said Canada was responding to US tariffs, while Ford denied any interest in interfering in American elections.

Mr. Carney said Canadian auto exports to the US have fallen more than 10%, while U.S. exports to Canada have dropped more than 20%.

“Tariffs make both our industries weaker and reduce choice for our families,” Mr. Carney said.

World.title: Shivamogga Jamboo Savari: Scary scenes as howdah elephant Somanna runs amok
World.content:
The Jamboo Savari procession, held as part of the Dasara celebrations in Shivamogga on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), witnessed scary scenes, when the elephant carrying the howdah with the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari ran helter-skelter within minutes of the procession kicking off, leaving the public, elephant caretakers, and the police personnel in shock.

Somanna, the elephant from the Sakrebailu camp which was carrying the howdah for the first time during the Dasara procession, had moved about 500 metres from the Kote Anjaneya Swamy temple on Kote Road when it suddenly turned back. Another elephant, Bahaddur, followed, triggering chaos and confusion among the crowd.

Also read: Mysuru Dasara: The Howdah Bearers | Infographics

Somanna, the elephant carrying the howdah with the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari, ran helter-skelter along Kote Anjaneya Swamy Temple Road in Shivamogga within minutes of the Jamboo Savari procession beginning, causing chaos and tension. The howdah fell off the elephant, leaving its caretakers and Shivamogga City Corporation staff in shock. 📸 S.K. Dinesh — The Hindu (@the_hindu) October 21, 2026

Caretakers and Shivamogga City Corporation staff ran behind the animals to stop them. Somanna ran towards a corner, the howdah slipped off, and the elephant hit a couple of cars and two-wheelers.

The city corporation had brought three elephants, Sagar, Bahadur, and Somanna, from the Sakrebailu camp for the procession. Sagar had carried the howdah for the last six years, but Somanna was chosen for the task on Wednesday morning.

The caretakers eventually brought the animals under control. By then, the howdah had fallen and the staff had carried the idol of Chamundeshwari away from the scene.

Superintendent of Police B. Nikhil told reporters that the procession would continue as scheduled, without elephants. “The elephant carrying the howdah ran backwards, creating chaos and tension. Another elephant also followed. A couple of vehicles were damaged. There were no casualties,” he said.

He appealed to the public to take part in the procession to Allama Prabhu Park as per the schedule.

DCF reaction

Prasanna Krishna Patagar, Deputy Conservator of Forests (Wildlife), told The Hindu that the elephant was probably frightened by the huge crowd and suddenly moved backwards.

“For the first time, Somanna was carrying the howdah. Last year, Sagar handled the responsibility. During the rehearsal, however, we noticed that Somanna’s performance was better, and the mahouts and caretakers felt the same. Hence, he was chosen to carry the howdah,” he said.

After the elephant moved backwards and ran helter-skelter, the staff and veterinarians brought it under control. “The animal was sedated to bring it under control. Now it is calm,” he said.

The elephants are expected to be taken back to the camp on Thursday (October 22, 2026).

First exposure

Somanna, a 36-year-old elephant, carried the howdah during the Dasara festival for the first time. In fact, he had no previous experience of taking part in the event. Last year, three elephants, Sagar, Bahaddur and Balanna, took part in the Dasara procession. This time, Somanna replaced Balanna.

Officials believe that Somanna, carrying the howdah for the first time, was frightened by the large crowd along the procession route. Apart from the rehearsal, he had hardly been exposed to such a large gathering.

Past incident

The incident reminded residents of Shivamogga of the 2023 Dasara celebrations in the city. Nethravathi, one of the elephants chosen for the procession that year, gave birth to a female calf hours before the procession was to begin. Officials and caretakers had no idea that she was pregnant, and she had taken part in the rehearsals for three days. The administration then resolved not to involve elephants in the procession.

The development had angered many animal lovers and wildlife activists.

World.title: CII urges exporters, MSMEs to tap opportunities under India-New Zealand FTA
World.content:
Domestic exporters, including MSMEs, should engage with New Zealand buyers, check product-specific rules of origin and leverage schemes such as the Export Promotion Mission to maximise the benefits from the recently implemented bilateral free trade agreement, Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) Sanjay Budhia said on Thursday (October 22, 2026).

Mr. Budhia, the Chairman of the CII National Committee on Exports and Managing Director of Patton International Ltd., said New Zealand can also serve as a gateway to the wider Oceania and Pacific Island markets.

On October 20, the two countries implemented a free trade agreement to boost trade and investment ties.

"I urge exporters, especially MSMEs, to move early, engage with New Zealand buyers, check product-specific rules of origin, and make full use of schemes such as the Export Promotion Mission. New Zealand can also serve as a gateway to the wider Oceania and Pacific Island markets," he said.

The pact, Mr. Budhia said, gives Indian exporters duty-free access across all tariff lines in New Zealand, with tariffs of up to 10% on engineering goods, textiles, leather and footwear now at zero.

The agreement is set to benefit a wide range of industries — including engineering goods, chemicals, plastics, electronics, pharmaceuticals, and processed foods — alongside labour-intensive sectors like textiles and leather.

He added that streamlined SPS and TBT (Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures and Technical Barriers to Trade) procedures, electronic certification, and acceptance of GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices) and GCP (Good Clinical Practice) inspection reports will also help reduce compliance costs.

World.title: How Tamil actor M.R. Radha got away with staging a ‘banned’ play in 1959
World.content:
On April 25, 1959, the Madras Government issued an order banning popular actor M.R. Radha’s Tamil play Thooku Medai. It was bannedon the ground that it deliberately intended to outrage the religious feelings of a class of citizens of India and also on the ground that it is indecent, scurrilous and obscene.

Subsequently, Radha submitted the script of another drama Kathal Bali to the Madras Commissioner of Police and obtained a licence to perform the play. He then staged the play at the Theagaraja College Open Air Theatre in Washermenpet on July 19, 1959.

World.title: Sub-Inspector suspended for slapping female dancer and brandishing pistol to crowd in Bihar
World.content:
The Bihar Police sub-inspector accused of assaulting a female dancer and brandishing his pistol in Begusarai was suspended after the video of the incident went viral on social media.

In the video, SI Anil Kumar Singh, posted at the Mufassil Police Station, is seen climbing the stage and slapping a female performer. When people protested, the SI drew his pistol and fired into the air to intimidate the crowd.

The incident took place on Tuesday (October 20, 2026), during a jagran (devotional night-long event) held at ‘Sarvajanik Durga Sthan in Panagachhi’, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Mufassil police station. During the event, local police personnel were also deployed to maintain law and order and ensure security arrangements.

The SI deputed there tried to shut down the programme and even “assaulted” the event organiser, after which the locals became angry, and a scuffle broke out among some people in the crowd.

The locals present over there asked why he had raised his hand against a woman and slapped her. Faced with protests from the angry crowd, the sub-inspector (SI) drew his service pistol and also used abusive language. He even threatened the people with dire consequences.

Taking cognizance of a video circulating on social media platforms (Facebook and Instagram), the Superintendent of Police (SP), Maneesh Kumar Begusarai, has initiated disciplinary action.

A press statement on October 21, 2026, from the office of the Begusarai Superintendent of Police (SP) stated that a preliminary review of the viral video indicates that the methods used by SI Anil Kumar Singh—who was deputed at the site—to maintain law and order were flawed and his conduct has tarnished the image of the police force.

The statement further stated, “The Superintendent of Police, Begusarai, has placed SI Anil Kumar Singh under suspension with immediate effect; he will be entitled to a subsistence allowance during this period. His headquarters during the suspension will be the Police Lines, Begusarai.”

The Begusarai SP has directed the Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO), Sadar-01, to conduct an impartial and thorough investigation into the video and to submit a formal report within the stipulated time frame.

World.title: IJCCI felicitates winners of intercollegiate competitions
World.content:
The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a prize distribution ceremony for the India-Japan intercollegiate competitions’26 in the city on Wednesday.

Around 20 colleges participated in the essay-writing and speech competitions. “Both our competitions attracted more than 110 participants from city colleges. This encouraging response demonstrates the enthusiasm of students to explore international themes, understand another culture and engage with the growing relationship between India and Japan,” said S. Padmanabhan, president of IJCCI.

N. Ravi, Director, Kasturi and Sons Limited, said that India-Japan relations across many facets, including political, strategic, trade and investments, and culture, have been growing stronger over the years. He also described how the relationship had moved from a global partnership to a strategic global partnership.

“Japanese investments, the working of Japanese companies and assistance have greatly enhanced India’s technological, scientific and digital capabilities, improved competitiveness and enhanced skill levels,” said Mr. Ravi. “Over 665 student and faculty exchange programmes, technical cooperation and collaboration, and research programmes have been established between more than 128 universities in Japan and 257 universities in India,” he added.

Chief guest Takahashi Muneo, Consul-General, Consulate General of Japan, said that young Indians are not only the future of India-Japan relations but also the bridge that connects the two countries. “Japan has many opportunities for young Indians especially in areas such as engineering, IT, manufacturing and healthcare,” added him.

Avantika Chandrasekar of the University of Madras secured first place in the speech competition and Nedhiya Fathima S. of Velammal Engineering College won the first place in the essay-writing competition. The judges, K. Sivaramakrishnan and Sridhar Krishnaswamy, also spoke at the event.

World.title: In Israel, Eisenkot tries quiet appeal to oust Netanyahu
World.content:
Gadi Eisenkot, the man who could unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, almost always dresses in plain black, speaks halting English and, reflecting the military culture that shapes him, responds in interviews in bullet-point lists.

For some voters, the 66-year-old Mr. Eisenkot's lack of charisma may be one of his greatest assets.

Serious and unassuming, Mr. Eisenkot is in many ways the opposite of Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest serving Prime Minister, who has flawless American-accented English and is ever ready with headline-grabbing soundbites on U.S. television or social media.

Mr. Eisenkot, the military chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, has vowed to unite Israelis after the divisive tenure of Mr. Netanyahu, who has moved the country sharply to the right.

"There is a large camp in Israel whose main goal in the coming election is just for things to be calmer," said Tal Elovits, a researcher at the Molad think tank.

"The middle class," he said, "is looking for someone who will look responsible, boring. I think Mr. Eisenkot has that appeal."

Mr. Eisenkot, who is neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu in polls, has promised to try to restore the international image of Israel, badly strained after three years of war in Gaza and violence in the occupied West Bank.

Mr. Eisenkot has vowed to crack down on West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity and recently beat up an American journalist and a French mayor, decrying the incidents as "Jewish terror" abetted by Mr. Netanyahu's government.

But the military man is no peacenik. He has even sought to play to the right of Mr. Netanyahu by vowing no Palestinian state, replaying clips from an earlier political era in which the long-serving Prime Minister begrudgingly voiced openness to the idea under U.S. pressure.

Commanding the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah, Mr. Eisenkot devised the so-called "Dahiya doctrine", named after a Beirut suburb, in which Israel vowed massive force against civilian infrastructure in areas populated by the Lebanese militants.

Israel has adopted the doctrine again in Gaza, causing destruction that critics say amount to war crimes, an assertion disputed by Israel.

Working-class roots

Mr. Eisenkot has garnered broad public sympathy after his son Gal and two nephews were killed fighting in Gaza.

His working-class roots constitute another element of his appeal. He would be the first Prime Minister who is Sephardic, Jews who trace their recent origins to the West Asia and North Africa.

Unlike Mr. Netanyahu, who comes from an elite family and whose father was a prominent professor in the United States, Mr. Eisenkot is the son of Moroccan Jews, and grew up on Israel's geographic periphery.

His background came into the spotlight when a senior commentator on the pro-Netanyahu Channel 14 television station described Mr. Eisenkot as "a monkey" controlled by "Ashkenazi elitists". He was referring to Jews of European descent who have historically dominated Israel's political and economic institutions.

While the term is not necessarily a racial slur in Hebrew and can mean a "fall guy" taking the blame on behalf of others, the remark drew widespread condemnation from opposition politicians and from Mr. Netanyahu himself.

Mr. Eisenkot swiftly sought to turn the episode to his advantage.

His campaign erected billboards denouncing discrimination against the Sephardim, and his party accused Mr. Netanyahu of sidelining Sephardic members of the Likud by limiting their media appearances during the campaign.

Limited change on security

In a pair of weekend appearances, Mr. Eisenkot went from meeting LGBTQ activists, promising the community greater protection in a forum at a hip cafe, to meeting religious Jews to whom he defended Israeli control over the West Bank.

"Israeli settlement (of the West Bank) is a value, on condition that it serves the interests of the state of Israel, and it's done according to the law," he told representatives of the Religious Zionist movement on Sunday (October 18, 2026).

He appeared to be rejecting the establishment of unauthorised settlement outposts, which have fuelled a recent rise in violence against Palestinians.

On Gaza, he has vowed to end Hamas rule within 18 months. Last week he said this could be achieved either through the implementation of U.S. President Donald Trump's ceasefire plan, which envisages Hamas's gradual disarmament and a transfer of power, or through "creative operations" aimed at destroying the movement's military wing.

Addressing a key source of resentment among Israelis following three years of war, Mr. Eisenkot has promised to curb exemptions from military service for religious students.

He promised a "universal national service law" requiring ultra-Orthodox Jews and Arab citizens to perform either military or civil service.

He has sought to appeal to centrist and liberal voters by pledging to "protect judicial independence, the rule of law, minority rights and a free press".

World.title: Anthropic PB admits to having an Indian subsidiary, contradicts earlier stand in court
World.content:
A legal dispute over the use of the name ‘Anthropic’ has taken a new turn after US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic PBC acknowledged in the Belagavi Commercial Court that a wholly owned subsidiary operates in India.

Belagavi-based Anthropic Softwares Private Limited has claimed to have registered the name of the company and brand much before the US-based firm, and has challenged the use of the company’s name by the American entity.

“In a written statement filed in the court, the company stated that Irina Ghose is the managing director of the India entity. This development raises questions about corporate conduct and the positions taken during the proceedings,” said Mohammad Ayyaz Mulla, Managing Director of Belagavi-based Anthropic Softwares Private Limited.

“For over 10 months, Anthropic India Private Limited resisted being impleaded in the case, maintaining that it was a separate legal entity and disputing the existence of a cause of action against it. More significantly, in an objection supported by an affidavit on oath, its Managing Director, Irina Ghose, denied that Anthropic India was directly or indirectly promoting Anthropic PBC’s business, calling the allegation baseless and requiring strict proof.

“Anthropic PBC’s subsequent written statement refers to its wholly owned Indian subsidiary and identifies Ms. Ghose as its managing director. We want to ask whether these positions, considered together, reflected the transparency and professional ethics expected of a global technology company. He said the court should examine whether procedural objections were being used to delay consideration of the core dispute over prior use of the ‘Anthropic’ name.”

Mr. Mulla alleged that repeated misdirected emails intended for Anthropic PBC had reached his company despite regular notifications, creating business disruption, brand confusion, and potential data-security risk, including the possibility of sensitive communications reaching unintended recipients. He said the continuing problem raised serious questions about whether customer confidentiality and corrective action were receiving adequate attention. He urged the US company to demonstrate its belief in corporate ethics through its behaviour.

World.title: PTI leadership ‘turns on itself’ after protest debacle
World.content:
Salman Akram Raja

• Raja ‘rebukes’ move by KP lawmakers to nominate Gandapur as interim KP president

• Ex-CM fires back, demands apology from secy gen over ‘name-calling’

PESHAWAR: The debacle that befell the PTI’s recent protest march has led to serious fissures within the core committee, with demands emerging from within for chan­ges at the leadership level that can steer the party out of its current crisis.

The bad blood became public on Wednesday as two senior party leaders — Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur — traded accusations of betraying the party cause.

Meanwhile, a woman parliamentarian from Peshawar echoed the sentiments of many within the core committee when she demanded accountability over the failure of the party’s much-touted protest march, which resulted in the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, and created more problems for their jailed leader, Imran Khan.

The Salman Akram-Ali Amin spat on X (formerly Twitter) followed reports that a group of lawmakers from the KP Assembly had met to endorse the latter’s nomination as acting provincial president in place of MNA Junaid Akbar, who has been missing since the imposition of governor’s rule.

The handwritten text, addressed to interim party chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and seen by Dawn, said that the meeting “unanimously” proposed to nominate Mr Gandapur as the acting provincial president in the absence of Junaid Akbar, calling the ex-CM “the right man for the right job”.

The Oct 14 meeting, which according to one participant was held via Zoom and WhatsApp, was attended by around 55 provincial lawmakers. Their four-pronged agenda included party organisation issues; the status of negotiations with the government; the party’s plan for further protests; and legal issues.

The main outcome that invited derision from Mr Raja, however, was the resolution demanding that Mr Gandapur be appointed the acting provincial president immediately.

This prompted the secretary general to take a dig at “the narrative” regarding a possible announcement by a group of party MPAs, nominating a new provincial president without permission from their jailed leader Imran Khan, or the party’s political committee. He put the number of these dissidents at 68.

Ali Amin Gandapur

The secretary general accused the group of cutting off contact with Sohail Afridi and his team in the final days of the protest march, paving the way for state coercion, emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

He asserted that Ali Asghar, the party’s provincial general secretary, remained the acting provincial head and Mr Afridi continued to be the chief minister, in accordance with the law and Constitution. “Those spreading doubts — the snakes and the serpents — will be defeated,” he wrote while concluding his post on X.

Subsequently, an angry Mr Gandapur took to X to hit back at the secretary general’s claims; in a series of tweets and audio messages, he took strong exception to Mr Raja’s tone and tenor.

Demanding that he bring to an end “the spectacle” that had been made of the party, the former KP CM said that the secretary general had no right to accuse others of conspiracy, or call them names like “snakes and serpents”.

“Do you understand this? We know how to make others understand if they don’t get this,” he said in an angry tone.

Accusing Mr Raja of “hiding” during the party’s protest movement, he asked what sacrifices he had rendered for the party, and demanded the secretary general apologise for his remarks.

“At a time when the party is facing unprecedented political challenges, levelling vague accusations and using mocking language against your own elected representatives does not befit responsible leadership,” he wrote on X.

“I don’t know who has fed Salman Akram Raja and what the purpose of his tweet was”, Mr Gandapur continued. He also wondered why Mr Raja and Barrister Gohar did not attend parliamentary party meetings, despite repeated invitations to discuss the fallout of the decisions they had taken, which had brought the party to this juncture.

“If the parliamentary party of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa wants to seek a constitutional and political solution to the current crisis through consultation within itself, who has given a few individuals the authority to label these elected representatives as traitors, conspirators, or undemocratic?”

Incidentally, this is not the first time that both men have taken to social media to air their internal party grievances. In 2025, ahead of a nationwide protest, Mr Gandapur and then-PTI Punjab organiser Aliya Hamza Malik had become embroiled in a similar argument over social media.

At the time, the argument had prompted a censure from the jailed party founder, who had strictly instructed senior officeholders and junior members alike to avoid expressing “internal differences on social media, electronic media, print media, or any other platform”.

“Publicly airing internal matters or individual concerns before the media is entirely unacceptable,” Imran Khan had said at the time.

The latest exchange between the two party leaders also harkened to an outburst from MPA Mashal Yousafzai — former spokesperson to Bushra Bibi — who has blamed the former chief minister and a few other party leaders for the failure of the protest march and subsequent imposition of governor’s rule.

Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

World.title: Saudis intercept more drones as conflict with Houthis spirals
World.content:
• Coalition downs six drones launched towards cities, including Madina, as interception debris kills two • Rebels deny ‘deep operations’ in Saudi territory

• Iran says Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’

• Macron arrives in Riyadh for ‘surprise solidarity visit’

RIYADH: As the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement continues to escalate, the Saudi-led coalition on Wednesday said it had intercepted six drones launched towards the kingdom, including in the Madina region.

“Four drones launched towards the kingdom have been intercepted and destroyed,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X, adding in a second post that the interceptions took place in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern region as well as Madina.

Al-Malki, who did not specify who was behind the launches, later said drones had been intercepted, also in the eastern region. The Houthis denied having targeted the kingdom, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying their forces had not carried out any “deep” operations in Saudi territory.

The Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility “resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others”. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border.

Within Yemen, the Houthis claimed an attack on Wednesday on a military camp near the airport in the southern city of Aden, where the Yemeni government is based.

“Our armed forces were able to target the Saudi enemy’s operations room in the Badr camp in Aden with a ballistic missile,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a statement.

A government military source and a local official told Reuters the group also attacked Riyan airport in the southeastern coastal city of Mukalla. “The Houthis used missiles and drones to target a military base housing forces from the Saudi-led coalition at Al Rayyan airport,” one of the officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP. Saree said the group had targeted “military equipment transported by the Saudi enemy via military cargo planes to Al Rayyan airport”.

Egypt to support Saudis

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen,” state-linked media reported.

Al-Qahera News, which is closely linked to state intelligence and is to broadcast a speech by Sisi, reported that he also said “the stability of our brothers in the Gulf concerns Egypt’s national security”. The speech itself has not yet been aired by Wednesday night.

Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week.

Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Iran warns against interference

However, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Mr Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”.

The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July.

Macron meets MbS

Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Riyadh in a surprise “solidarity” visit, and met Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

Macron is the first Western leader to visit since the Houthis intensified their attacks on the kingdom this month.

The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president.

Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

World.title: ‘Letting roots of Pak-India conflict fester invites more danger’
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Failure to address the underlying disputes that engender crises between Pakistan and India could lead to more dangerous confrontations in the future, a former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee warned on Wednesday.

“Terminating a crisis without addressing its root causes only sets the stage for the next, more dangerous conflict,” retired Gen Zubair Mahmood Hayat said at the concluding session of the second Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference, organised by the Strategic Vision Institute (SVI).

Ex-CJCSC warns against ignoring Kashmir dispute, Indus treaty suspension

He said that in the subcontinent, the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir could not be wished away or reduced to an administrative matter. “Similarly, water cannot be converted from a shared necessity into an instrument of power and pressure,” he said while stressing the need for resolution of the Kashmir dispute and restoration of the Indus Waters Treaty.

Gen Hayat warned that repeated crises between the nuclear-armed neighbours could become increasingly dangerous if unresolved disputes, diminishing restraint and the absence of sustained political dialogue continued to undermine regional security.

Referring to the May 2025 conflict, he said Pakistan had demonstrated its military capabilities and political control through a calibrated response that denied India a unilateral fait accompli without pursuing an unlimited war.

“The larger lesson is not that conflict between two nuclear-armed neighbours can be made routine; it is that there is no tested and certified safe space for war,” he said, warning that future crises would involve different leaders, emerging technologies and shorter decision-making timelines, heightening the risk of miscalculation.

He said South Asia lacked an inclusive regional security framework, effective crisis-management mechanisms and sustained political dialogue. “The region lives between deterrence that prevents the worst and disputes that repeatedly regenerate danger,” he said.

Gen Hayat warned unverified allegations could trigger conflict before the facts were established, with a future confrontation potentially arising from an accident rather than a deliberate state decision. He cited the continuing Operation Sindoor in this context.

Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

World.title: PTI asks govt to ‘rebuild trust’ if it is serious about talks
World.content:
• Demands reversal of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency measures, release of political prisoners and Imran’s access to his personal physicians

• Claims party’s ‘popularity’ still intact despite ‘coercion’

ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Wednesday called on the government to take confidence-building measures (CBMs) to pave the way for meaningful dialogue, demanding the reversal of what it described as “unlawful” measures, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and release of political prisoners.

In a statement, PTI Central Infor­mation Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said meaningful negotiations required concrete action rather than political statements. “If the government was genuinely serious about dialogue, it should take steps to build trust,” he added.

Mr Akram demanded the reversal of measures the party considered unlawful, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate and release of political prisoners whose continued detention, he said, could not be legally justified.

He also called for the protection of PTI founder Imran Khan’s constitutional and fundamental rights, including lawful meetings with his lawyers and family, fair and timely proceedings in his and his wife’s cases, and medical treatment under the supervision of his personal physicians in accordance with applicable court orders.

Mr Akram condemned raids on homes, detentions and pressure on elected representatives and party workers in Punjab and KP, alleging that these actions were intended to intimidate political opponents.

PTI’s ‘popularity’

Rejecting Information Minister Attaullah Tarar’s remarks about the party’s political standing, Mr Akram challenged all ruling coalition parties to contest elections against the PTI under a single banner. He said they would suffer a “crushing defeat in a free and fair contest, even today”.

On Tuesday, Mr Tarar had said a formal ban on the PTI was no longer needed after the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in KP, arguing that the party had “lost po­­w­er” in the province because of security and counterterrorism failures.

Mr Akram said the government’s use of “coercive measures and political pressure” had failed to diminish the PTI’s public support. He described the party as Pakistan’s “leading federal political force” and its founder, Imran Khan, as the “only leader enjoying widespread public support across the country”.

Rejecting governor’s rule and the emergency in KP, he described the measures as an “attempt to undermine the province’s electoral mandate”. He said the party’s strength stemmed from its connection with the people rather than its control of government offices.

He added that no “handpicked administration should be allowed to dictate” the political future of around 50 million residents without respecting their democratic choices and constitutional rights.

Mr Akram insisted that decisions concerning the province’s governance, resources, and future must involve its elected representatives and local population.

Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

World.title: Draft auto policy revs up hopes for cheaper vehicles
World.content:
• PHEVs may see price reductions of over 20pc under proposed tax changes

• Petrol, hybrid vehicles may become around 8-10pc cheaper

• Parts makers warn rising CBU imports, lower tariffs to hurt local industry

KARACHI: The draft Auto Policy 2026-31 could trigger one of the biggest shake-ups in the country’s automobile market, with prices of some vehicles potentially falling by more than 20 per cent.

However, the prospect of cheaper cars may create an unusual predicament, as buyers are likely to hold back purchases in anticipation of lower prices, causing anxiety among automakers over the value of their existing inventory.

According to Topline Securities, the new draft maintains the 1pc general sales tax (GST) rate on battery electric vehicles (BEVs), while setting rates at 9pc for plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) and 6pc for range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs). The earlier draft had proposed a uniform 1pc GST across all new energy vehicles (NEVs), while the previous policy imposed rates of 8.5pc to 12.75pc on PHEVs.

This points to the government’s priority to incentivise the rollout of NEVs, particularly BEVs.

Preliminary industry estimates suggest conventional petrol vehicles could become approximately 8-10pc cheaper, while hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) may see reductions of around 9pc. PHEVs could benefit even more, with estimated price reductions exceeding 20pc.

Among BEVs, models with import values below $15,000 could see reductions of approximately 22pc compared to around 8pc for higher-priced BEVs. However, REEVs may become around 3pc more expensive under the proposed tax structure.

The new draft proposes reducing tariffs on localised completely knocked-down (CKD) parts to 15pc by FY31 from 25pc previously. Topline Securities said the reduction could be detrimental to the local vendor industry, adding that the benefits were likely to be passed on to consumers amid intense competition.

Parts makers sound alarm

Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (PAPAAM) Chairman Abdur Rehman Aizaz said the new auto policy amounted to a “conspiracy to destroy several industries”.

He said rising imports of new and used cars were already hurting the developed local auto parts industry, which now faced the threat of closures because of government policies.

Mr Aizaz pointed out that imports of completely built-up (CBU) new cars rose to 2,407 units in September from 391 in August, while imports of used cars increased to 2,454 units from 1,185 over the same period.

He said every new or used imported vehicle reduced potential volumes for the country’s 1,200 local auto parts manufacturers. Locally produced parts accounted for approximately Rs1.5 million of the value of each domestically assembled vehicle, he added.

On that basis, the 4,861 CBU vehicles imported in September represented an estimated Rs7.3 billion in lost revenue for local parts manufacturers, Mr Aizaz said.

Industry representatives said the GAC Aion UT, currently priced at around Rs6.4m, could fall to Rs5m-Rs5.2m. Higher-priced electric SUVs such as the BYD Atto 3 and GAC Aion V, priced at around Rs9m, could also see meaningful reductions.

They said popular petrol and hybrid models could become more affordable as well. Industry estimates indicate potential savings of around Rs600,000 to Rs800,000 on selected variants of the Honda HR-V e:HEV, Haval Jolion and Toyota Corolla Altis.

The biggest absolute reductions could emerge in the PHEV segment. A Jaecoo J7 PHEV, priced near Rs10m, could potentially fall to around Rs8m, while the Kia Sorento PHEV, which has already witnessed substantial price adjustments, could face further downward pressure from changes in GST and import duties.

Sania Irfan of Topline Securities said the new draft proposed a zero per cent automotive development levy (ADL) on fossil fuel-driven vehicles below 1,000cc, 2pc on 1,000-2,000cc vehicles and 10pc on those above 2,000cc, replacing the earlier draft’s rates of 4.5-5.5pc across engine categories.

Kalbe Ali in Islamabad also contributed to this report

Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

World.title: Lahore Gymkhana’s low rent attributed to ‘decades of oversight failures’
World.content:
LAHORE: A special committee of the Punjab Assembly, chaired by MPA Samiullah Khan, came down hard on decades of government oversight failures after Lahore Gymkhana Club Chairman Salman Siddique conceded that the annual rent of Rs5,000 paid for over 100 acres of prime state land in the provincial capital was wholly inadequate.

Appearing before the committee alongside members of the club’s management, Mr Siddique expressed surprise at the nominal rate given the vast acreage involved and the club’s vastly improved financial footing. Contrasting the institution’s current financial standing with its constraints during the 1990s, he admitted that the club should be paying at least Rs10 million annually, while expressing willingness to cooperate with the ongoing inquiry and share records.

Committee members noted that this admission from the club’s own top leadership underscored the urgency of determining why successive state authorities allowed such a massive concession to persist without meaningful scrutiny. They stressed that the onus rested squarely on public institutions mandated to protect state land, enforce lease terms, and ensure transparent usage.

During the session, the member colonies of the board of revenue revealed that then chief minister Sardar Muhammad Arif Nakai, who was also a member of the club, had verbally directed the fixation of a token Rs5,000 annual rent for the lease extension in 1996, bypassing proper land valuation and relevant legal principles. Perturbed by how a mere verbal instruction could underpin such a major agreement, lawmakers demanded the complete documentary record detailing the legal authority and approval process behind the 1996 lease deed.

PA body constitutes fact-finding committee to frame specific queries, verify records, and present comprehensive report within 10 days

Emphasising that the land ultimately belongs to the people of Punjab, the committee was presented with estimates valuing the prime property between Rs76 billion and Rs218 billion. Members questioned the state’s failure to secure a fair public return on an asset of this scale and firmly rejected any notion that the club’s internal corporate governance shielded it from state oversight, maintaining that institutional autonomy cannot supersede accountability for public property.

Touching upon structural approvals, Mr Siddique affirmed that while the club fulfills its corporate and tax obligations under the Companies Act 2017, he has struggled to locate internal records regarding official building sanctions.

In response, lawmakers called for strict verification of sanctioned building plans, statutory permissions, and compliance with lease terms, raising safety concerns over structures lacking documented approvals.

On the issue of an independent state audit, Mr Siddique noted that the matter remains pending before the Supreme Court and assured adherence to its eventual verdict, a position echoed by management committee member Tasneem Noorani.

The panel also explored proposals aimed at broader public utility, such as opening the club’s cricket ground to the general public or relocating the facility near the Ring Road, while questioning why public funds were ever spent on an exclusive recreational club occupying state land.

To take the probe forward, the committee directed the Lahore Development Authority, Parks and Horticulture Authority, Federal Board of Revenue, and other relevant bodies to submit detailed jurisdictional reports.

Furthermore, a fact-finding committee headed by the Advocate General Punjab, comprising officials from the Board of Revenue, Metropolitan Corporation Lahore, Law department, Agriculture department, and the deputy commissioner, had been assigned to frame specific queries, verify records, and present a comprehensive report within ten days.

Concluding the session, the chairperson directed that legal questions stemming from the proceedings be forwarded to the high-powered Law Reforms Committee, headed by Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan, for joint deliberations aimed at fixing responsibility for oversight lapses and ensuring the lawful use of public land.
